title: Hezbollah rebuilds military capabilities, upgrades FPV drones ahead of possible Israel war - report
body: Hezbollah is preparing to rearm and rebuild its terror capabilities in the event of an escalation with the IDF amid rising regional tensions, sources told Beirut-based independent news outlet Al-Modon on Monday.Al-Modon is managed by the Qatari-based Fadaat Media Group, and often takes a critical stance against the Iran-backed Shi'ite terror group, while calling for a pro-Arab consensus."If a large-scale war breaks out, it will reach Lebanon. Israeli is waiting for any opportunity for military escalation against Hezbollah, as it is working to convince Washington of the need to renew the war against Iran. Just as Tehran is anticipating the possibility of war against it, Hezbollah is preparing and equipping itself," the report said.According to the outlet, the Iranian proxy terror group takes "Israeli threats seriously and is dealing with messages conveyed through diplomatic channels indicating that Israel will not abandon its military escalation and is waiting for the appropriate timing."Sources told the outlet that Hezbollah is "anticipating" war and "has succeeded in taking advantage of the extended ceasefire period to rebuild its military capabilities in southern Lebanon, both south and north of the Litani River."Lebanese Armed Forces seize truck transporting Hezbollah explosives planned for FPV drone improvementsThe sources also linked Hezbollah's rebuilding of militarist terror capabilities to the interception of a truck that was transporting explosive materials from the Bekaa Valley to Beirut.The Jerusalem Post reported on Sunday that the Lebanese Armed Forces seized a truck at a checkpoint in the Bekaa Valley, which was carrying hundreds of kilograms of explosives belonging to the terror group, including TNT and C4.Two suspects admitted to receiving the explosives from a Hezbollah commander in Baalbek, with instructions to transport them to Beirut, the Post reported at the time.Sources told the Lebanese outlet that the terror group uses the materials found in such trucks to develop first-person view (FPV) drones, which have been upgraded to carry between four and six kilograms of explosives, compared with the previous payload of 2.5 kg.Hezbollah terrorists have also succeeded in extending the length of the FPV's cables from 20km. to over 30km., meaning that the terror group can attack targets from a further distance, the sources said.The terror group has also continued to work towards reinforcing its capabilities by increasing military deployments in villages and towns adjacent to the Yellow Line, including in some areas south of the Litani River, particularly in the vicinity of Nabatiya, the report noted.The terror group has also taken security precautions in anticipation of possible Israeli assassination attempts targeting terror leaders and officials, the report said. This included the evacuation of many apartments and offices in Beirut's southern suburbs, including the Hezbollah stronghold of Dahiyeh.Beirut has not taken enough steps towards disarming Hezbollah terrorists, Israel believes - reportThe outlet also highlighted that Israeli believes the Lebanese state has not fulfilled its duty towards the framework agreement surrounding Hezbollah disarmament. In this context, Israel has sent messages to Lebanon that it will launch a large-scale military operation against Hezbollah terrorists, including expanding military operations into new areas, the outlet reported.Israel may also resort to imposing an air, land, and sea blockade on Lebanon as a ramification for Beirut's failure to disarm the terror group and prevent Hezbollah from joining an escalated conflict.Negotiations reportedly include exploring the deployment of military forces from Italy, Switzerland, and Jordan to aid in removing Hezbollah's weaponry, according to Al-Modon.However, conditions for reaching an agreement are not in place, as Hezbollah refuses to hand over weapons, and the LAF does not want to enter into a confrontation with the Iranian proxy, the report said.The terror group is also betting on developments in the escalated conflict in Yemen between the Houthis and the Saudi-led coalition forces, the report stated.Danielle Greyman-Kennard contributed to this report.

title: Jerusalem court upholds 5-year suspension for gynecologist Guy Rofe over patient exploitation
body: The Jerusalem District Court rejected an appeal by gynecologist Guy Rofe to shorten or cancel the five-year suspension of his medical license, the Health Ministry announced Tuesday.The court found that Rofe used his position as a treating physician to pursue intimate relationships with two patients, mixing medical advice with sexual messages. It also upheld findings that he withheld medical records from investigators and continued advertising himself as a practicing gynecologist despite his suspended license.“I will examine you as a gynecologist and as a lover,” he wrote to one patient, according to the judgment. She was a 19-year-old soldier whom he treated while serving as a military doctor in the reserves.In messages to the second patient, he interspersed discussions of blood tests, pregnancy, and contraception with comments about her appearance and about his sexual fantasies.During an examination, the judgment said, he told her, “Maybe don't get dressed, I don't think there's any need,” and placed a hand on her knees.Rofe facing charges of rape, indecent actsThe decision means Rofe remains barred from practicing medicine and cannot present himself to the public as a licensed, practicing physician.Rofe also faces a separate criminal prosecution on charges of rape by deception and indecent acts by deception against a soldier who came to him for treatment. According to the indictment, he performed sexual acts under the guise of a medical examination. Those charges remain pending; the five-year suspension rests on disciplinary findings concerning different incidents.The judgment does not specify whether the soldier mentioned in the disciplinary case is the same woman involved in the criminal prosecution.Rofe's license was initially suspended on November 29, 2024, in connection with the criminal proceedings.The disciplinary complaint at the center of the latest ruling was filed on September 4, 2025. It contained four counts: two concerning his conduct toward the patients, identified as “A” and “D”; one concerning his refusal to provide medical records for five patients; and one concerning his continued online advertising.Retired judge Amnon Straschnov, acting under authority delegated by the health minister, adopted the disciplinary committee's findings on all four counts, except the allegation concerning Rofe's refusal to hand over WhatsApp correspondence.On April 20, Straschnov ordered the five-year suspension. The committee's majority had recommended three and a half years, while its minority favored at least 10 years or permanent revocation.Straschnov found the majority's recommendation insufficient given the harm to public trust, the misleading advertising, and Rofe's persistent refusal to cooperate with oversight authorities.Rofe appealed, seeking to have the decision canceled and the case returned to the committee or the suspension reduced to no more than six months.He argued that he had been denied a fair opportunity to defend himself because hearings proceeded in his absence, despite his having reported illness and a family event.The court found, however, that Rofe had missed two hearings and failed to submit a written defense. The committee then gave him further opportunities to respond and offered to arrange another hearing around dates he proposed. He did not provide them.“A doctor who chooses to turn his back on the disciplinary proceedings and deliberately cause prolonged delays cannot now complain that the proceedings were decided in his absence,” Judge Nimrod Flax wrote in the October 8 judgment.Rofe also challenged the findings concerning the patients. Regarding patient A, he disputed the existence of a special relationship of trust and dependence, citing her withdrawal of a criminal complaint, the closure of that investigation for lack of guilt, and the time elapsed since 2018. That investigation was distinct from the pending criminal prosecution.Regarding patient D, he argued that she had initiated the sexual conversations, that no physical contact had occurred, and that no emotional harm was proven.Flax rejected Rofe's attempt to compare his conduct with less serious disciplinary cases. The judgment described “a continuing and systematic pattern of conduct” involving violations of professional boundaries, refusal to supply medical records, and misleading advertising during suspension.Accused of withholding medical recordsThe Health Ministry argued that Rofe's appeal presented a partial account and concealed his repeated disregard of the committee's decisions. It said his continued advertising violated both the law and court decisions.Rofe argued that protection against self-incrimination entitled him to withhold medical records. He also maintained that investigators already possessed most of the information and that his refusal had not harmed their inquiries.The court rejected that defense.Medical records, it held, are documents doctors must create and preserve by law, rather than personal material protected against self-incrimination in these disciplinary proceedings. Records for three patients had still not been supplied.His refusal “directly undermines the Health Ministry's ability to exercise oversight and obstructs the proper examination of complaints by additional patients,” Flax wrote.The court also rejected Rofe's argument that he had not actually treated patients while advertising himself as an active physician. The advertising itself misled the public, it said, regardless of whether treatment took place.Rofe's continued conduct despite explicit court decisions, Flax wrote, “casts a heavy shadow over [his] very fitness to work in a professional field governed by ethical rules.”The Health Ministry described the ruling on medical records and self-incrimination as a first in Israel. It said it would continue monitoring compliance with the suspension and maintain a policy of zero tolerance toward conduct that harms patients or undermines public trust.The five-year disciplinary suspension remains in place independently of the outcome of the criminal prosecution.

title: Argentina files international case against Israeli-led oil project in UK's Falkland Islands
body: Argentina's government said on Tuesday it had filed a request for provisional measures with the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea seeking to halt British-authorized hydrocarbon activity near the Falkland Islands.The request aims to prevent the United Kingdom from exploiting hydrocarbon resources on the continental shelf of the Northern Falklands Basin, the government added in a statement.The Argentine request follows an earlier approval on Tuesday by UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband for the Sea Lion field, a new Israeli-led oil-field development in the area, The Telegraph reported.Israeli oil company Navitas Petroleum confirmed Miliband's approval, with the company leading the project, according to the report.Argentina sanctions companies, individuals linked to Israeli-led projectIn September, Argentina began sanctions proceedings against more than 60 companies and people linked to the offshore oil drilling project, a move UK officials have strongly pushed back on.British Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State for Overseas Territories Uma Kumaran called the Argentine sanctions "unacceptable," saying that "the Falkland Islands are British and they have the right to develop their natural resources as they see fit."Also in September, Argentina's government announced that it will file a criminal complaint against Navitas for operating in the Falklands.

title: Iranian matchmaking app removed by Google after allowing girls as young as 12 to register
body: Major platforms have removed the Iranian matchmaking app “Adam and Eve” after an investigation found that girls as young as 12 could register, according to announcements from Google, Meta, and the US-based Human Rights Activists News Agency (HRANA).Although the app has maintained that it is only available to adults over the age of 18, HRANA found in its investigative report, Child Marriage in the Digital Age, that children as young as 12 could register. The platform's search system also allowed users to filter prospective spouses by age, including girls as young as 13.The app has also publicly posted about the marriage of a 16-year-old bride to a 23-year-old man, who met through the platform.The Jerusalem Post also accessed the app's website and reviewed profiles advertising girls as young as 15 for marriage. However, a closer examination of one profile revealed that the girl was in eighth grade, indicating that she was likely 13 or 14. The profile also displayed a green notice, indicating parental approval.Although Google and Meta confirmed this week that they would remove the app, Iranian digital rights organization Filterbaan had warned in July last year that "Adam and Eve," alongside several Telegram channels, was facilitating child marriages.An investigation published by Filterbaan at the time found that nearly 17% of the profiles posted on Adam and Eve in the six months before the report's publication belonged to individuals under the age of 18.A whistleblower within the app's administration also told Filterbaan that, beginning in July 2023, the app's director, Hossein Asghari, had directly ordered that minors' profiles be published and presented as part of an “Islamic marriage and an Islamic-Iranian lifestyle.”The youngest child known to have married through the app at the time of Filterbaan's investigation was just 11 years old.Under Article 1041 of Iran's Civil Code, the minimum marriage age is 13 for girls and 15 for boys. However, marriage below those ages is permitted with a guardian's consent and “consideration of the child's best interests, as determined by the competent court.”“The exploitation of children is a horrific crime, and we work aggressively to fight it on and off our platforms,” a Meta spokesperson told HRANA. “We investigated the information provided by HRANA and identified external links to underage marriage services. We have removed these entities from Meta platforms.”Google removed the app for 'violating policies'Google separately told the organization that “the app was removed from Google Play on October 9 for violating our policies.”Despite global efforts to combat child marriage, the practice remains widespread. UNICEF's child marriage data portal reports that one in five young women worldwide married before their 18th birthday. Meanwhile, Iran's Statistical Center recorded approximately 25,900 marriages involving girls under the age of 15 in 2022.Licensed by the Iranian regime, "Adam and Eve" is part of a broader expansion of matchmaking services operating with government authorization. HRANA reported that Iran had only one licensed matchmaking platform in 2020, but that number had risen to more than 200 by early 2025.Efforts to raise Iran's minimum marriage age gained momentum throughout the 2010s, with proposals to set the minimum age at 16 for girls and 18 for boys and require court permission for marriages involving children over 13. However, government policy shifted in 2021, following Ebrahim Raisi's appointment as president, toward enabling and encouraging child marriage.The proposed Prohibition of Child Marriage Bill was subsequently removed from the government's agenda, despite efforts by the then-vice president for Women and Family Affairs to secure its approval by the executive branch of the Islamic Republic.

title: Hamas praises Nobel Peace Prize winner Navi Pillay over genocide allegations against Israel
body: Hamas praised the awarding of the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize to South African jurist Navi Pillay in a statement issued on Friday, citing her role in advancing accusations of genocide against Israel and calling for international legal action against Israeli officials.The terrorist organization welcomed the Norwegian Nobel Committee's decision to honor Pillay, a former UN high commissioner for human rights who chaired a commission of inquiry that concluded Israel had committed genocide in the Gaza Strip.In its statement, Hamas described the award as "an important step toward international justice," praising Pillay's involvement in investigating Israel's military operations in Gaza and calling for further international legal action against Israeli officials.The statement followed the announcement of Pillay as the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize laureate, a decision that prompted sharp criticism from Israel's political leadership.Hamas said the award represented international recognition of what it described as crimes committed by Israel against Palestinians, pointing specifically to the September 2025 findings of the UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry chaired by Pillay.The commission's report concluded that Israel had committed genocide in Gaza, an allegation rejected by Israel, which has maintained that its military operations targeted Hamas following the terrorist organization's October 7, 2023, massacre."The findings of the Independent International Commission of Inquiry, which was chaired by Pillay, concerning the crimes committed in the Gaza Strip, as well as the conclusion of its report issued in September 2025 that the crime of genocide had been committed, underscore the gravity of what our people have endured," Hamas said.The terrorist organization called on the international community to pursue Israeli officials through international courts, demanding an end to what it characterized as impunity for alleged war crimes.UN inquiry into Gaza genocide allegationsThe controversy surrounding Pillay stems in part from a September 2025 UN commission report, which determined that Israel had committed four of the five acts of genocide defined by the 1948 Genocide Convention. The commission alleged that Israeli actions demonstrated an intent to destroy Palestinians in Gaza.The commission, established in 2021, was tasked with investigating alleged violations of international law in Israel and the Palestinian territories. Pillay chaired the panel alongside commissioners Chris Sidoti and Miloon Kothari.Israel rejected the findings, accusing the commission of relying on inaccurate information and failing to adequately account for Hamas's conduct during the war. The Foreign Ministry denounced the report as fabricated and accused its authors of acting as proxies for Hamas.The war began when Hamas-led terrorists invaded southern Israel on October 7, 2023, killing approximately 1,200 people and abducting more than 250 others into Gaza. The massacre triggered Israel's military campaign against the terrorist organization.Pillay, who previously served as president of the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda and as a judge at the International Criminal Court, was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for her broader career advancing international law and accountability for international crimes.The Norwegian Nobel Committee said its decision recognized her efforts to promote peace and international legal principles, rather than specifically endorsing the conclusions of her Gaza investigation.Hamas, however, placed the commission's allegations against Israel at the center of its response, using the Nobel announcement to renew its demands for international legal proceedings against Israeli officials.In its statement, the terrorist organization also praised Pillay's earlier work defending anti-apartheid activists in South Africa and her service on international tribunals, presenting those roles alongside her involvement in the Gaza inquiry.Herzog condemns Nobel decision as 'moral erosion'President Isaac Herzog sharply criticized the awarding of the Nobel Peace Prize to Pillay during a ceremony honoring Israel Bonds on Monday, describing the decision as an "affront to any life-affirming, peace-loving people."According to remarks covered on Tuesday, Herzog condemned the Nobel Committee for recognizing Pillay, whom he accused of advancing false allegations against Israel."Awarding the Nobel Peace Prize to one of the leading proponents of the genocide lie is a cynical decision which celebrates a shameful display of moral erosion," Herzog said.His remarks came amid broader criticism from Israeli officials, including Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who accused Pillay of spreading false accusations against the Jewish state."The Nobel Prize committee has lost its moral compass," the Prime Minister's Office said in response to the announcement."It has awarded its highest honor to a bigot who built her career around inventing and propagating blood libels against the only Jewish state."The contrasting responses highlighted the dispute surrounding Pillay's work, with Hamas explicitly endorsing the UN investigation's findings while Israeli leaders rejected both the report's conclusions and the Nobel Committee's decision to recognize its former chairwoman.Hamas concluded its statement by renewing its call for international action against Israeli officials accused of crimes in Gaza.

title: High Court challenges law excluding women from Israel's Chief Rabbinate elections
body: The High Court of Justice last month made a small but consequential decision that has the potential to affect how chief rabbis and members of the Chief Rabbinate Council are chosen in the State of Israel.The court issued a conditional order requiring the respondents to explain why legislation passed in December 2024 should not be interpreted as requiring the chief rabbis to appoint both men and women as representatives in the electoral assembly – or why the provision restricting eligibility for those appointments should not be struck down.The petition was filed on December 19, 2024, ahead of elections to the Chief Rabbinate Council. Submitted by six women with advanced religious education, Bar-Ilan University's Rackman Center, and Na'amat, it argues that the amendment passed earlier that month effectively prevented women from being appointed to the electoral assembly's rabbinic contingent.The case concerns the body that chooses the chief rabbis and the council's elected members rather than membership in the council itself.Why doesn't the Chief Rabbinate ordain women?Under the Chief Rabbinate Law, the electoral assembly comprises 150 members: 80 rabbinic representatives and 70 public representatives. Most seats are linked to specified offices, such as rabbinic posts, local government leadership, and religious councils. Ten of the rabbinic representatives are appointed by the chief rabbis, in consultation with the religious services minister and with government approval.Those 10 appointments are at the center of the dispute.In an earlier Rackman Center case, the court ruled on January 14, 2024, that the chief rabbis must consider appointing women with suitable education in Torah and Halacha (Jewish law) to those seats. Justices Dafna Barak-Erez and Isaac Amit formed the majority, against Justice David Mintz's dissent.The ruling did not require the appointment of particular women or their ordination as rabbis. It rather held that, for this electoral role, the statutory term “rabbis” was not confined to people formally ordained by the Chief Rabbinate.On May 19, 2024, however, the Chief Rabbinate Council adopted a decision saying that women could not be appointed as rabbis and that even considering such appointments was forbidden under its interpretation of Jewish law. The decision, cited in the petition and reproduced in the state's response, argued that considering a woman would itself recognize the possibility of her holding a rabbinic role.The Knesset subsequently passed Amendment No. 8 to the Chief Rabbinate Law on December 4, 2024. It defined a “rabbi” eligible for one of the 10 appointments as someone ordained by the Chief Rabbinate after passing its required written examinations or holding a certificate of eligibility for specified rabbinic posts.Because the Chief Rabbinate does not ordain women, the petitioners argue, the new definition closed the route the court had recognized.A separate ruling has since changed women's access to the rabbinate's examinations. On July 14, 2025, a unanimous panel, in a judgment written by Supreme Court Deputy President Noam Sohlberg, ruled that the Chief Rabbinate could not bar women from taking its exams.The court explained that the examinations serve purposes beyond qualifying candidates for rabbinic office: Recognition of religious learning can also carry employment and salary benefits. Denying women access was therefore unlawful discrimination. That ruling did not, however, settle their eligibility for the electoral appointments challenged in this case.At a High Court hearing last month, September 14, the petitioners' lawyers emphasized that distinction: Passing examinations would not by itself satisfy a law requiring ordination. They argued that women's expertise in Jewish law was being excluded from the assembly's rabbinic representation because of their sex.The state's response argued that the amendment must be considered as a whole. Alongside the disputed qualification requirement, it introduced a minimum of 31 women among the assembly's public representatives.The state maintained that reserving the 10 appointments for rabbis recognized by the Chief Rabbinate served a legitimate purpose and that the broader increase in women's representation supported the amendment's constitutionality. The Knesset joined that position. The petitioners argued that additional public-representative seats did not remedy the exclusion of women as religious scholars.Gov't argues petition would suspend statutory election arrangementsThe government also argued that the petitioners' request to halt the council elections pending a judgment would effectively suspend the statutory election arrangements.Justice Gila Canfy-Steinitz rejected that interim request on December 31, 2024, citing the caution required before suspending legislation ahead of a ruling on its merits.The September conditional order leaves the substantive challenge open. The respondents must submit their formal answers by December 15.

title: Indigenous women challenge Islamist oppression, call for cross-community solidarity
body: The same radical Islamist forces behind the October 7 attacks, in which more than 1,200 people were killed, are also responsible for attacks on the Druze in Syria and the mass murder and oppression of Iranians and Hindus in India and Kashmir, according to six women from Indigenous communities. They spoke at the panel, Asia & the Middle East: Conversations Across Communities, hosted by Indigenous Bridges on Monday night.Hindu activist and regional analyst Kavya K, known online as “Kavya Speaks”; Israeli Druze activist Rania Dean; Kurdish speaker and educator Schilan Kurdpoor; Iranian human rights activist Honey Montzemi; and Native American and Jewish Indigenous rights activist Lani Anpo shared their experiences of oppression and silencing by Islamist forces with Ateret Shmuel, the Jewish director of Indigenous Bridges.Despite hailing from different countries, including Iran, the United States, Israel, and India, the women said they shared experiences of gender-based violence, genocide, forced assimilation, silencing, and intimidation.Each said she had been accused of Islamophobia and subjected to death threats or doxxing for speaking about her community's experiences.They also emphasized the need to build alliances among Indigenous communities to overcome their minority status and more effectively confront what they described as the oppressive forces of political Islam.Both Kurdpoor and Kavya said radical Islamist forces often target women first because attacks on women also threaten families and the transmission of cultural traditions between generations.Kavya argued that the targeting of women had led Hindu communities to adopt new gender-based restrictions, keeping women out of public life for their own protection. She contrasted these restrictions with what she described as the historically prominent role of women in Hindu communities.As an example of women's power and status in Hindu religious tradition, she cited the Hindu goddess Kali, who defeated the demon Mahishasura when the male gods could not.Shmuel noted how it was the Kurds who were able to weaponize the misogynistic beliefs of Islamic State against the group. The ISIS fighters believed that being killed by a female combatant would prevent them from entering paradise and receiving the rewards promised to martyrs, including the 72 virgins described in popular accounts of the group's ideology.Aware of this, Kurdish fighters in Rojava established the Women's Protection Units (YPJ), an all-female Kurdish military force operating in northern Syria. Kurdpoor recounted how the women used battle cries to signal their presence, sometimes prompting ISIS fighters to flee. She also described the role of women in the broader Kurdish-led military effort and their acceptance within the Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF).Kurdpoor discussed the role of ethnic cleansing and the restrictions on indigenous languages. She argued that restricting a community's language creates a disconnect between individuals and their cultural heritage, citing restrictions in Turkey and limits on Kurdish-language education in Iran. She also highlighted the continuing struggle to learn and preserve the language in Syria, describing it as central to the Kurdish community's cultural survival.Dean said that the Druze had historically spoken Aramaic before adopting Arabic, which she described as part of a broader effort to blend in with the surrounding occupying Arab population and protect Druze communities. She noted that the community's historical efforts to assimilate had failed to ensure its safety, pointing to the July 2025 massacres in Sweida, continued attacks on Druze communities, and the ongoing siege of villages in southern Syria as evidence that conformity had not provided protection.Dean also welcomed the growing use of Bashan, the biblical name for Sweida and the surrounding area, as it signaled that her community was moving away from what she described as failed attempts to secure peace with its occupiers through assimilation into their society. She condemned the labeling of Druze calling for freedom and self-determination as “separatists,” a term several speakers said had been used to discredit or suppress calls for freedom by Indigenous communities in the region.Beyond their shared experiences of oppression and Islamist colonial occupation, the speakers also expressed concern about what they saw as a growing trend of Western women supporting regimes that would strip them of the rights and freedoms they currently enjoy.Secular leftists paved way for Iran's 1979 Islamic RevolutionMontazemi noted that secular leftists had helped pave the way for Iran's 1979 Islamic Revolution, only to pay for it with their lives in the years that followed. She expressed concern at seeing women on social media proudly displaying the Islamic Republic's symbols while wearing tank tops, clothing that would result in their arrest in Iran.She pointed to Western women who had traveled to Syria to marry ISIS members, arguing that they had surrendered their rights in the process. Montazemi said more needed to be done to understand the appeal these groups held for women.Explaining the importance of the event to The Jerusalem Post, Shmuel said, “Indigenous nations across Asia, the Middle East, and Africa face the same violent colonialism, yet our stories are routinely spun for Western audiences to portray Islamists as the victims and Indigenous communities as the cause of the conflict. We see this in Western reporting on attacks against Druze, Hindu, Kurdish, Persian, Jewish, Yezidi, Bahá'í, and other Indigenous communities.Also, there is a sinister reason for this narrative: to manipulate the Western public into sympathizing with Islamist jihadi groups, paving the way for their expansion into the West,” she said.Shmuel indicated her hope that the panels would provide a greater understanding to the global community of communities too often silenced and an understanding that “the safety and sovereignty of Indigenous communities across Asia, the Middle East, and Africa are deeply intertwined.”The panel was the first in a series of events addressing the issue of Indigenous solidarity to be hosted by Indigenous Bridges. For more information, visit: https://indigenousbridges.com/

title: IAI and SIG SAUER conduct successful live‑fire test of FIRE STORM 250 armed UAS
body: WASHINGTON - Israel Aerospace Industries (IAI) and SIG SAUER have completed a live‑fire demonstration of the FIRE STORM 250, the Apus 60 VTOL tactical unmanned aircraft equipped with SIG SAUER's MICROLIGHT Remote Controlled Weapon Station (RCWS) and the new M250 machine gun. Defense & Tech by The Jerusalem Post understands that the test, conducted ahead of the AUSA 2026 exhibition in Washington, took place in Israel and showed the platform's ability to detect, identify, and engage targets while hovering over a simulated battlefield.During the trial, the UAS loitered over the test area and used its onboard camera to identify targets before it fired in both single‑shot and semi‑automatic modes. Engagements were carried out from different altitudes and ranges to assess accuracy, stability, and safety under varied conditions.While it is still a functional prototype, the companies said the live-fire test validated the system's core concept of pairing airborne surveillance with stabilized, remotely controlled firepower to give small units organic close‑support capability.The FIRE STORM 250 is built for long‑duration overwatch and armed reconnaissance. Powered by a multi-fuel internal-combustion engine, it can remain airborne for up to three hours and be refueled in the field, avoiding battery‑charging delays and specialized logistics. Its vertical take-off and landing (VTOL) configuration allows launch and recovery from forward positions without runways or aviation support. 200 rounds at 200 metersSIG SAUER's M250 airborne light machine gun can be configured to carry 200 rounds of either 7.62×51 millimeters or 6.8×51 mm. ammunition, depending on customer requirements. It has a targeting range of 400-600 meters at an altitude of 200 m. The MICROLIGHT RCWS brings the system's total combat weight to 53 pounds, including the gun and ammunition.Sensor feeds and fire‑control data are fused into a single targeting picture, giving operators real‑time imagery, tracking information, and engagement options. Operators control the platform by using advanced control algorithms that maintain shooting accuracy even while hovering and moving. “One of the most dangerous positions is in a turret, and the main idea is to keep the soldier out of the line of fire,” Mike Joslin, defense product manager at SIG SAUER, told D&T at AUSA. “Rather than the soldier holding the gun, he holds the interface that controls it.”Nevertheless, the platform's architecture keeps a human in the loop, with operators receiving real-time sensor imagery, target-tracking data and engagement options, and authorizing each use of fire.Sali Okanin, SIG SAUER's Israel general manager, said the test highlights how lightweight weapons can expand what small unmanned aircraft can do. "FIRE STORM 250 brings together the most advanced technologies in the world, including IAI's drone platform and SIG SAUER's MICROLIGHT RCWS mounted with the M250 machine gun to deliver a new level of operational flexibility,” he said, adding that the platform has “greater range than legacy systems and weight savings that not only provide squad-level benefits but also make drone capabilities possible."It is intended to be deployed with small tactical units and support missions including persistent overwatch, intelligence gathering, force protection, border defense and special‑operations surveillance.Joslin explained to D&T that multiple FIRE STORM 250 aircraft can operate together to maintain continuous day‑night coverage, provide advance observation along movement routes, and support maneuvering forces during operations and extraction.“Our concept of operations is that with the platform's flight time, you can have loitering support with more en route to provide constant support,” he said.Moshe Levy, executive vice president and head of IAI's Military Aircraft Group, said the demonstration reflects a shift in how tactical unmanned systems are being designed. “The next generation of unmanned systems will be defined not only by autonomy, but by how effectively they integrate sensing, decision-making and action within the operational environment,” he said. “FIRE STORM 250 brings these capabilities into a single operational loop, enabling tactical forces to extend their reach and maintain continuous awareness while retaining human control over engagement decisions,” he added. “The firing test demonstrates the potential of this approach in a realistic operational scenario."The futureThe collaboration between IAI and SIG SAUER, one of the world's largest weapons manufacturers, comes as it expands its line of unmanned aerial platforms. “Drones are the future,” said Ryan Scott, director of Advanced Concepts at SIG SAUER. Scott, a 22-year US Army Veteran with over a decade in unmanned systems with the Army, explained that the 250-year-old company has been investing in drone design and development for the past several years.The company's new direction “shows our innovative capabilities to support our troops.”Along with FIRESTORM, SIG SAUER displayed its fixed-wing SCYTHE platform, the SABER quadcopter with the M-HORNET 22 LR payload attachment. It also displayed the prototype XRAY-9 counter-UAS platform.According to Scott, “If Israel wanted our drones, we would sell them.”Joslin echoed Scott's feeling towards Israel, telling D&T that “there is no same amount of passion as Israel defense tech companies. Serving is embedded in the culture.”

title: 'Focus on Hamas, not me': Winter accuses Netanyahu of prioritizing political survival over security
body: People of Israel party chairman Brig.-Gen. (res.) Ofer Winter called on Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to focus his efforts on aid trucks entering Gaza, illegal weapons across Israel, and expanding IDF enlistment rather than attempting to weaken Winter's party ahead of the elections."Prime minister, I think you've gotten confused again," Winter said, responding to Netanyahu's reported call to continue attacking his party politically."Instead of dealing with the People of Israel and the electoral threshold, which doesn't seem to be working out so well for you because we're simply rising, focus on reducing the percentage of trucks entering Gaza every day as protection money for Hamas."Winter also accused the government of failing to address the widespread circulation of illegal weapons in Israel."Perhaps you should also focus on reducing the percentage of illegal weapons circulating throughout the country under this government. And perhaps you should also try to increase the percentage of people serving in the IDF," he continued.Netanyahu fights to gain three Knesset seats The remarks came after Netanyahu delivered two central messages to Likud lawmakers during a faction meeting on Sunday, ahead of the upcoming elections.According to the meeting account, Netanyahu called for increased voter mobilization in traditional Likud strongholds and efforts to recover about three Knesset seats he believes the right-wing bloc is losing to Winter's party and the Reservists/Economic Party list, headed by Yoaz Hendel and Yaron Zelekha.Netanyahu reportedly urged Likud members to continue targeting Winter politically as part of the party's election strategy.The dispute comes amid growing concern within Likud over Winter's potential impact on the right-wing bloc. The party has sought to prevent votes from being lost to smaller right-wing factions, particularly those at risk of failing to cross the electoral threshold.Anna Barsky contributed to this report.

title: Does Saudi Arabia have any good options to deal with the Houthis? - analysis
body: The deadly Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia over the last week have put pressure on Riyadh to respond.Saudi Arabia has carried out airstrikes on the Houthis in support of the Yemeni government forces over the past month. However, Riyadh has appeared reticent to respond in a massive way to the Houthi attacks. Rumors are swirling in the region about what might come next. Analysts tend to portray the Saudis as facing an uphill struggle with the Houthis.Does Saudi Arabia really have no good options? Various recent reports have discussed different aspects of what Riyadh may be weighing in terms of what comes next.For instance, there is the question of the US supporting Saudi Arabia. The US and many countries have condemned the attacks. However, US President Donald Trump has left media guessing as to whether the US will do more. The US appears to be supporting Saudi Arabia in terms of intelligence and targeting, according to the BBC.The Houthis have threatened a "swift and painful" response if the US does intervene. "If the US becomes involved in the aggression against Yemen, we will not deliberate over the decision to respond; rather, there will be a swift and painful response targeting the US and all its interests in the region," Houthi political bureau member Mohammed Al Bukhaiti told the AFP.All of this must weigh on US-Saudi coordination. There are questions about how a widening war in Yemen could also lead Iran to operationalize militias in Iraq.Who should Saudi Arabia ally with to minimize spread of war in the Middle East?Saudi Arabia has seen this before. It intervened in Yemen in 2015 to back the Yemeni government against the Houthis. The Houthis widened the war with ballistic missile and drone attacks on Saudi Arabia. In 2019, Iran directly attacked Saudi Arabia. Militias in Iraq also targeted Saudi Arabia. Therefore, Riyadh knows exactly what is at stake.Meanwhile, there are questions about whether tensions in Yemen could lead to renewed fighting with Iran. Reports indicate that Israel could be involved in strikes on Iran again, or even on the Houthis.There is intense interest in this among Saudi Arabia's allies in Turkey and Pakistan. Those countries joined an alliance with Saudi Arabia over the last few months.However, Turkey would likely not want to be on the same side as Israel fighting alongside Saudi Arabia. Anadolu media in Ankara noted that Riyadh had so far rejected Israel's “bid to join fight.” It is not entirely clear if Israel wants to get deeply involved again in Yemen.Israel already carried out strikes on Yemen in 2024-2025 in response to numerous attacks by the Houthis on Israel. The Houthis also attacked commercial ships they claimed were linked to Israel. They seized the Galaxy Leader, only releasing the crew in 2025. They tried to make the ship into a kind of tourist attraction. The Galaxy Leader finally partially sank in April 2026, the Maritime Executive noted.How did Saudi Arabia get into tensions with the Houthis?Further context might help explain how Riyadh got here.Saudi Arabia intervened in Yemen in March 2015, leading a coalition against the Iranian-backed Houthis after the group seized Sanaa and advanced toward Aden. The intervention developed into a prolonged conflict involving airstrikes, ground fighting and Houthi missile and drone attacks on Saudi territory. A UN-brokered truce in April 2022 significantly reduced hostilities, and although it formally expired that October, a fragile period of relative calm followed.That ceasefire has come under increasing pressure in 2026. Saudi strikes on Sanaa in July marked a renewed escalation, while the Houthis subsequently launched an offensive toward Bab el-Mandeb, the strategic strait connecting the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden. It's worth recalling that Saudi Arabia and the Yemeni government did not want Sanaa airport used by Iran to fly in Iranian advisers to the Houthis.Saudi-backed Yemeni forces launched a counteroffensive in October, supported by coalition airstrikes, to recover territory near Bab el-Mandeb and Mocha. The Houthis also escalated attacks on Saudi airports, including Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport, where an October 10 strike killed 12 people and wounded 309. Riyadh vowed a firm response.The conflict has also expanded beyond Yemen. On September 11, Saudi Arabia's East-West oil pipeline was struck by drones that Saudi and Iraqi authorities said originated in Iraq. Riyadh temporarily shut the pipeline, a crucial alternative to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. The attack highlighted growing concerns about coordination among Iran-backed terrorist groups across the region and the potential vulnerability of Saudi energy infrastructure.On October 12, JINSA President and CEO Michael Makovsky spoke to Fox News about the latest Houthi attacks. “It's very important that the [Saudi] Crown Prince be successful [in combating the Houthis], and it's vital for US national security. But he's alienated or distanced himself from a few key countries that could have been helpful here. I mean, he had a very well-known fight with the Emiratis, who were effective ... against the Houthis. ... He's kept a distance from the Israelis, who have ... [been] very effective at hitting the Houthis, and, at times in this war, he's been rather cool to the United States,” Makovsky said, according to a synopsis of the discussion released by JINSA.He added, “I'd like to see the Saudis work with the Israelis, the Emiratis, and the US to deal with the Houthi threat. It is not only a threat to the Saudis, of course, but affects the whole world because of [the Houthi threat] to international commerce. ... There has to be an international coalition.”Thomas Juneau, a Professor at the University of Ottawa, who focuses on Iran and Yemen and is a former Department of National Defense analyst in Canada, noted on October 11 on X that “Saudi Arabia faces no good options with the Houthis. Military escalation was inevitable and is likely to continue–but it will hurt Saudi Arabia more than the Houthis. Negotiations are inevitable too–though not in the short term. The Houthis hold stronger cards, and they know it; their goal will be to extract maximal concessions from Saudi Arabia, which remains reluctant to pay this very high price.”Game theory can help Saudi Arabia face its Houthi dilemmaMight game theory help us understand the dilemma for Saudi Arabia in confronting the Houthis? The challenge is assessing how this spectacle connects with Iran, Israel, the United States, Iranian-backed militias in Iraq, Turkey and Pakistan.The central problem is that Saudi Arabia may be militarily stronger than the Houthis, but military superiority does not necessarily translate into strategic leverage. The Houthis can impose high costs on Saudi Arabia without defeating its armed forces. Riyadh, meanwhile, must consider how its response affects not only Yemen but its economic security, regional alliances, and relations with Iran. This is what is called an “asymmetric” conflict.This creates several overlapping strategic dilemmas. Saudi Arabia faces three calculations it has to make at the same time. It has to examine how it might deter more attacks, it has to manage its alliances, and it has to look at the regional context and potential escalation. Game theory does not provide a clear answer, because the outcomes depend on uncertain information, different objectives, and the decisions of several independent actors. Nevertheless, it might be helpful to model this problem more because Saudi Arabia is in a difficult position, but it has many options.Saudi Arabia can weather the storm. It has done so in the past. It has a naturally cautious leadership, like most Gulf countries. The West tends to prefer quick solutions, and Western media appears to think that the lack of an immediate large response, like “shock and awe,” means nothing is happening. However, this illustrates the differences in calculations. The Iran war, for instance, has proven to be longer and more complex than many thought. This reflects differences in thinking between Washington, Jerusalem, Riyadh, Ankara, and other places in the region.

title: Lassa fever spreads across 119 LGAs as death toll hit 268
body: The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) has recorded 1,138 confirmed cases of Lassa fever and 268 deaths across 24 states, with the case fatality rate rising to 23.6 per cent. The figures were contained in the agency’s Lassa Fever Situation Report for epidemiological weeks 39 and 40, covering September 21 to October 4, 2026. According to the report, the cumulative case fatality rate of 23.6 per cent was higher than the 18.6 per cent recorded during the corresponding period in 2025, indicating an increase in the proportion of confirmed cases resulting in deaths. The NCDC disclosed that the disease had spread across 119 Local Government Areas (LGAs) in 24 states, with Bauchi, Ondo, Taraba, Benue and Edo accounting for 88 per cent of all confirmed cases recorded during the reporting period. It also identified people aged between 21 and 30 years as the most affected age group. However, the agency reported no new Lassa fever infections among healthcare workers during the two epidemiological weeks under review. A breakdown of the figures showed that Nigeria recorded three new confirmed cases in week 40, covering September 28 to October 4, compared with 13 cases reported in week 39. The three new infections were recorded in Bauchi and Benue states, bringing the cumulative number of confirmed cases to 1,138 and deaths to 268 by the end of week 40. For week 39, which covered September 21 to September 27, the NCDC recorded 13 new confirmed cases, an increase from the 11 cases reported in week 38. The new infections during week 39 were reported in Ondo State, bringing the cumulative number of confirmed cases to 1,134 and deaths to 267. The case fatality rate for week 39 stood at 23.6 per cent, compared with 18.5 per cent recorded during the corresponding period in 2025. The NCDC’s situation report provides periodic updates on confirmed cases, fatalities, affected states and LGAs, as well as the distribution of infections across different age groups. Lassa fever is an acute viral haemorrhagic illness primarily transmitted to humans through contact with food or household items contaminated by the urine or faeces of infected rodents. The disease can also spread from person to person through contact with the bodily fluids of an infected individual, particularly in healthcare settings where appropriate infection prevention and control measures are not implemented. The NCDC advised members of the public to maintain proper environmental sanitation, store food in rodent-proof containers and avoid contact with rats to minimise the risk of infection. The agency also emphasised the importance of preventive measures to limit exposure to infected rodents and reduce the spread of the disease.

title: OPEC again revises downward global oil demand growth outlook in 2026
body:
MOSCOW, October 13. /TASS/. The Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) has revised downward its international oil demand growth forecast for 2026.
The figure is expected to grow by 0.2 mln barrels per day (bpd) and the demand will stand at 105.72 mln bpd, OPEC said in its October report. The organization expected one month earlier that the global demand will grow by 0.4 mln bpd in 2026.
The decline by about 0.2 mln bpd is expected in OECD countries, while non-OECD nations are expected to show growth by 0.4 mln bpd.
OPEC at the same time increased its outlook for 2027. The organization now expects the global oil demand to grow by 2.6 mln bpd annually. The increase by 0.5 mln bpd is projected in OECD countries, and by about 2 mln bpd in non-OECD countries.

title: Anti-drone netting to be installed over modular town for displaced persons in Zaporizhia – regional administration
body:

title: Alleged forgery: Police arrest, release Okorocha
body: Police authorities on Monday night detained former Imo State Governor Rochas Okorocha at a hotel in Abuja following allegations of criminal conspiracy, forgery and impersonation. Okorocha was taken into custody at the Reiz Continental Hotel before being released on bail after roughly an hour of questioning, according to Nigeria Police Force (NPF) spokesperson Aniete Iniedu, who spoke with Channels Television. Iniedu stated that the former governor has been instructed to present himself at Force Headquarters on Tuesday for additional interrogation as detectives proceed with their inquiry. Law enforcement moved to arrest Okorocha after he repeatedly failed to respond to official invitations. Police initially summoned him to Force Headquarters on September 2, but the date was moved to September 8 following a request by his legal team. Okorocha subsequently missed the rescheduled appearance. The police action comes in the wake of formal petitions submitted by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to both the police and the Department of State Services (DSS) regarding a document shared on social media, which the election umpire labelled a fictitious All Progressives Congress (APC) senatorial primary result. The Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC) in Imo State, Chukwuemeka Ibeziako, petitioned the security agencies in separate letters dated October 5 and October 8, 2026. Ibeziako requested an investigation into the circulating document, which portrays Okorocha as the winner of the APC primary for the Imo West senatorial district. According to the REC, the online document directly contradicts the certified report submitted to INEC national headquarters, which confirms sitting Imo Governor Hope Uzodimma as the legitimate winner of the primary. In his October 5 letter to the DSS state director, Ibeziako noted that his attention had been brought to the online document, reaffirming that the authentic report, dated May 18, 2026, officially designated Uzodimma as the elected Imo West candidate. Warning that the spread of the fraudulent material threatened to trigger a breakdown of law and order within Imo State, Ibeziako urged immediate action by security operatives. He reiterated the complaint in a follow-up letter to the Imo State Commissioner of Police on October 8. The post Alleged forgery: Police arrest, release Okorocha appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Storm to bring up to 60 millimetres of rain to parts of Ontario, Quebec
body:
Some Ontarians and Quebecers will need to grab those umbrellas Tuesday as parts of both provinces could see up to 60 millimetres of rain depending on where people live.
In Ontario, eastern parts of the province are under special weather statements with Environment Canada forecasting a low pressure system will move eastward bringing showers and thunderstorms.
The agency warns local rainfall amounts could range from 40 to 60 mm, with Kingston, Peterborough, Picton, Parry Sound and Haliburton among those affected.
There is also the possibility of severe thunderstorms forming, along with heavy rainfall, this afternoon.
The stormy weather is expected to clear from west to east this afternoon or early this evening, Environment Canada said.
Next door in Quebec, special weather statements and yellow rainfall warnings are in effect for southern parts of the province due to a “nearly stationary” warm front that’s associated with a low pressure system moving south of the border.
According to Environment Canada, the Bois-Francs and Eastern Townships areas could see 30 to 50 mm between Tuesday morning and late Wednesday night or early Thursday morning.
Yellow warnings are also in place in the Montreal, Vaudreauil and Monteregie areas from Tuesday morning until the evening.
In those areas, the rainfall could reach 40 to 60 mm, with the agency warning water will likely pool on roads and in low-lying areas. Visibility could also be suddenly reduced at times.

title: E. Equatoria bans candidates from renting houses, citing misconduct, teenage pregnancies
body: The caretaker Minister of General Education in Eastern Equatoria State, Ibwaha Lucy Allam, has warned schools against allowing Primary Eight and Senior Four candidates to leave school premises and rent houses for private examination preparations ahead of the national examinations slated for November. She said the ministry does not permit candidates to rent houses outside school compounds, particularly where boys and girls stay together under the pretext of preparing for their final examinations. The minister told Radio Tamazuj that she is concerned about what she described as an unacceptable practice, warning that it could expose learners to misconduct and other risks during the examination period. “I want to make this information very clear: I have seen students moving from school to rent houses outside,” she stated. “The ministry does not accept this movement. It is abolished, and we do not want it to happen.” Ibwaha questioned the purpose of allowing boys and girls to rent houses together, arguing that the arrangement could undermine students’ discipline and expose them to risks instead of helping them concentrate on their studies. The minister urged parents to advise their children against leaving school to rent accommodation for examination preparations, emphasizing the need for proper supervision during this critical period. She also said examinations for lower classes would begin before those of Primary Eight and Senior Four candidates, with the ministry planning to give the examination classes their turn the following month. Meanwhile, parents in Torit have welcomed the minister’s position, citing concerns over teenage pregnancies, indiscipline and the difficulty of monitoring children living in rented accommodation. Afaf Millo, a parent in Torit, said parents could find it difficult to know what their children were doing when they lived away from home, even when the stated purpose was examination preparation. “They should stay at home so that I can monitor my child as a mother,” she said. “I will know how to guide her, ensure she follows the school timetable and balances studying with household responsibilities.” She argued that studying at home under parental supervision could help learners remain disciplined and avoid negative peer influence associated with unsupervised group living. Another parent, Jane Dudu, also welcomed the minister’s directive, saying she would not allow her child to rent a house in the name of preparing for examinations. “Last year, many of our children became pregnant because of that. We do not know who impregnated them there,” she stated. “We do not want children sleeping in rented places in the name of examination preparation. It should not happen in Eastern Equatoria.” The parents called on school administrators to enforce the ministry’s directive and urged families to take greater responsibility for supervising candidates throughout the examination period. The warning comes as schools in Eastern Equatoria prepare learners for the upcoming Primary Eight and Senior Four examinations, which mark important transitions in South Sudan’s education system. The post E. Equatoria bans candidates from renting houses, citing misconduct, teenage pregnancies appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

title: Titus Glover criticises Mahama’s appointment of Afi Agbenyo as EC Deputy Chairperson
body: The National Organiser of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Titus Glover, says Ghanaians will ultimately judge President John Dramani Mahama’s administration over its decisions, including the appointment of Emelia Afi Agbenyo as a Deputy Chairperson of the Electoral Commission (EC). Speaking on Adom FM’s Dwaso Nsem , Mr Glover criticised the appointment, arguing that it raised concerns about political neutrality in state institutions. “They can appoint whoever they want to the Electoral Commission. Ghanaians will make a decision on December 7,” he said. Mr Glover accused the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC) of applying inconsistent standards in its criticism of previous EC officials. He recalled concerns raised by the NDC about former EC Deputy Chairperson Dr Bossman Asare and the Commission’s Director of Information Technology, arguing that the party’s position on the current appointment appeared inconsistent with its earlier criticisms. “They accused Bossman Asare of being an NPP member without substantial evidence and made so much noise about him and the Director of IT. But now, we have an NDC member as a Deputy Chairperson of the Electoral Commission,” he stated. The NPP National Organiser warned that perceived political influence over state institutions could undermine public confidence in their impartiality. “We are now politicising every state institution. If you are not affiliated with the ‘green’ party, you cannot benefit from anything,” he added. Mr Glover’s comments come amid ongoing political debate over Afi Agbenyo’s appointment and concerns raised by the NPP about her alleged political affiliations and the Electoral Commission’s neutrality.

title: Letters to the editor: Readers question Trump's Russian diesel deal and US sanctions policy
body:
President Donald Trump (R) walks toward Russian President Vladimir Putin (L) to shake hands during a joint press conference at Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson in Anchorage, Alaska, U.S. on Aug. 15, 2025. (Jae C. Hong / AP)
This week's letters come from readers questioning the Trump administration's decision to purchase Russian diesel fuel amid rising prices in the United States. An American reader argues the deal benefits Russian President Vladimir Putin at Ukraine's expense, a scholar questions whether a U.S. sanctions bill will meaningfully pressure Moscow, and a British reader raises concerns about Washington's turn to Russian oil.
Got an opinion on anything you've read in the Kyiv Independent? Send it to letters@kyivindependent.com — your letter may appear in our Letters section.
U.S. President Donald Trump's MAGA Republican Party is projected to lose the midterm elections in a few weeks, and much of his power and support within the government could evaporate.
Trump needs a scapegoat for the crippling rise in diesel prices in the United States . He has now decided that scapegoat will be Ukraine and President Volodymyr Zelensky .
The diesel "deal" Trump announced a few days ago is nothing but a calculated act of gaslighting aimed at Americans and a wholesale admission that he has always been on Team Russia.
Trump says the deal will give the United States 1.8 million tons, or 14 million barrels, of diesel over the next 90 days, with another 3 million tons next year if Russia can supply it.
This figure is so minor in real terms that it would keep American trucks and industry running on diesel for a mere six days. Donald Trump has simultaneously destroyed American credibility, sided with the enemy, and sold out Ukraine for a pittance.
Karl Frost, United States / Germany member
The Lindsey Graham bill in the US, passed by Congress on Sept. 16, was celebrated internationally as a landmark Russian sanctions bill. Ukraine supporters who cheered this seem not to have fully appreciated that most Democrats voted against it.
Despite appearances, legally, the bill does not mandate Russia-related sanctions. The legally consequential aspect of the bill is authorizing discretionary tariff powers for the president with no meaningful oversight.
The bill identifies two categories of tariff targets: the top five importers of Russian oil and the top five facilitators of Russian sanctions evasion.
There is language in the bill "mandating" these tariffs. However, the bill gives the president arbitrary, discretionary powers to make exceptions. In other words, the president is not actually mandated to impose these tariffs.
Trump already had the power to sanction Russia, which he was not using, so there is no reason to think this further permission to tariff Russian oil consumers will be used, especially in light of his announcement that the U.S. would buy diesel fuel from Russia to offset fuel price increases caused by his war with Iran.
Unlike the "importer" tariffs, which do have relatively objective criteria, the "facilitator" tariffs are based on presidential interpretation. The Supreme Court has repeatedly affirmed, for example in Dalton v. Specter , that where a statute grants such pure executive discretion as spelled out in the bill, courts will decline to review the factual basis behind the president's determination. The president could theoretically designate any nation currently locked in a trade dispute with the U.S., including allies of Ukraine , as a "facilitator of sanction evasions," slap them with 100% tariffs, and face zero judicial review.
This is the central concern raised by Democrats. As U.S. Representative Don Beyer stated , "This bill would do more harm than good for America and for Ukraine . Giving (Trump) this power when he has shown us over and over again what he will do with it would be an incredible mistake."
Mostly no, at least not directly, except for dropping illusions. This matters because the bill is being presented as a tool to pressure Russia and support Ukraine. Trump already declines to use his existing sanctions powers, so there is little reason to expect this one to pressure Russia, and it could actually backfire on Ukraine.
I am a U.K. citizen living in the South West of England. I have a 23-year-old diesel car and am now paying 2 pounds per liter ($2.65).
I am appalled by the descent of the U.S. to the level of barbarism shown by its leaders: resorting to shouting down opposition when they have no reasoned argument and using personal insults against journalists who ask pertinent questions. But back to diesel.
Several weeks ago, Mr. Trump was castigating Ukraine for attacking Russian oil and petrochemical facilities. In the current circumstances, these are appropriate targets, in contrast with Russia's attacks on homes and civilian infrastructure. His "argument" was that Ukraine was causing a global diesel shortage through this strategy, while failing to acknowledge the sanctions he had imposed on Russia.
Ordinary Russians queuing for fuel learned more about their leaders' war from these shortages than from any other source. Mr. Trump had conveniently forgotten that he had contributed to the shortage by attacking Iran, which discovered it could hold the whole world to ransom by closing the Strait of Hormuz, creating shortages of all fuels and many other oil-based products.
Suddenly, Mr. Putin is America's savior, agreeing to export "millions of barrels" of oil to the US! Where has this oil appeared from? Is it the result of lifting sanctions on the shadow fleet? Is Ukraine no longer attacking Russian oil facilities? Maybe these are magic oil wells?
Any story that will last long enough for Mr. Trump to tell it to voters ahead of the midterm elections appears on his antisocial media sites.
Editor's note: The letters published in this section reflect the views of their authors alone and do not purport to represent the position of the Kyiv Independent.
