title: Iran fortifies nuclear sites, rebuilds missile arsenal as it prepares for the next war - analysis
body: Satellite images show that Iran is fortifying various locations as it may be preparing for renewed war, The Wall Street Journal reported on Monday.“Iran is fortifying its defenses, rallying loyalists and threatening a wider, harsher response against the US and its Gulf allies as it prepares for potential American attacks after the midterms and seeks to deter them,” the article noted.This comes amid a flurry of other reports suggesting that the US or Israel could return to fighting Iran.Maariv said over the weekend that the United States had pressured Israel to carry out strikes against Iran. Both Israel and the US have upcoming elections. Any strikes could affect the elections.PBS reported on Sunday that “Iran has continued to reject a deal with the US. The head of Iran's Supreme National Security Council says Tehran finds the latest response from the United States 'insufficient' as efforts at negotiations to end the war and fully open the Strait of Hormuz limp along.”The picture being painted is of an Iran that continues attempting to rebuild its missile and drone program.Netanyahu said Iran can no longer produce ballistic missilesIn March, Israel's prime minister said that the Islamic Republic could no longer produce ballistic missiles due to its hammering by US and Israeli strikes. There was also an optimistic assessment about how many Iranian launchers had been destroyed and how many missiles were “corked” in their depots by collapsing routes to the missiles.In April, The New York Times reported that Iran was repairing its missile bunkers. The regime has shown it can rebuild capabilities.The WSJ report noted that “Iran has also reinforced protection around its nuclear sites and other security-related bunkers. Last month, it built passive defense measures such as makeshift dirt mounds around its Pickaxe Mountain and Natanz nuclear sites to impede any attempted raid by ground forces, according to Vantor satellite images analyzed by the Institute for Science and International Security, a Washington, DC, nonprofit.”The report quoted Behnam Ben Taleblu, senior director of the Iran program at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies. “In both word and deed, the Islamic Republic is actively preparing for the next war,” Ben Taleblu said.Iran is a huge country, around 75 times the size of Israel and 150 times the size of Lebanon. Israel has struggled to defeat Hezbollah in Lebanon and remove all its threats. This illustrates the challenge of locating all the Iranian threats. The new report at the WSJ is concerning in this respect.“Satellite images show Iran is strengthening sensitive locations, including nuclear sites and border areas, to make them more resilient to attacks. The government is also preparing Iranians for renewed war, sending paramilitary forces to read war stories to kindergartners, advertising training in firing shoulder-mounted anti-aircraft missiles, and holding rallies,” the report added.It also said that Iran is prepared to defend against various types of airstrikes. It has likely learned some lessons from the 12 Day War in June 2025, as well as the round of strikes that began in February 2026 and lasted until May.Iran continues to threaten shipping via the Strait of Hormuz. The US has been working to make sure that ships can pass the Strait. It is trying to make sure that the crisis with Iran doesn't affect energy prices too much. However, all the levers the US has tried to pull still leave the conflict with Iran as an open-ended problem.The WSJ noted that “Iranian officials have hinted that their forces could conduct land incursions into neighboring countries, according to people familiar with the warnings.”With US forces having withdrawn from Iraq on September 30, this could give Iran some opportunities. It could try to infiltrate via Iraq or use Iranian-backed militias in Iraq to conduct more attacks. Those militias have already attacked a key pipeline in Saudi Arabia.While US Central Command (CENTCOM) and Saudi Arabia carried out retaliatory strikes in July, there is reticence in Riyadh to confront the militias in Iraq and the Houthis at the same time.Could renewed strikes produce different results?This is why the WSJ report is important. It notes that “Tehran has separately warned Arab officials that it could strike regional targets, including Saudi oil facilities, in the event of a renewed conflict, some of the people said.”Saudi Arabia is already weighing how to deal with the Houthi threat, which has targeted Saudi airports in recent days, killing and wounding people.The question now is whether a return to fighting by the US or Israel will lead to better results than in the past.Iran is seeking to rebuild; this means increasing its drone arsenal as well. The regime has had some success in attacking US bases in the region. It can read the same media reports as everyone else about how those attacks damaged facilities and airplanes and caused the US to reposition assets.

title: GCB customers call for more frequent engagement with bank leadership
body: Customers of GCB Bank PLC have called for more direct engagement with the Bank’s leadership while sharing feedback on their business needs, growth ambitions and banking experiences during a Customer Town Hall led by Managing Director, Farihan Alhassan. The engagement, held as part of GCB’s Customer Service Month 2026 activities, brought together customers and senior management for an open discussion on service delivery, business growth and ways the Bank can better support customers. Participants shared their experiences, concerns and expectations, while offering suggestions on how GCB could enhance its products, services and customer interactions. A recurring recommendation was for such engagements to be held more frequently and extended to a broader cross-section of customers, underscoring the value customers place on direct access to the Bank’s leadership. The session also highlighted the impact of strong relationship management on customer experience. Several customers took the opportunity to commend their relationship managers for their responsiveness, professionalism and commitment to understanding and supporting their business needs. Speaking at the event, Farihan Alhassan, Managing Director of GCB Bank PLC, reaffirmed the Bank’s commitment to placing customers at the centre of its operations. “Our customers are at the centre of everything we do. Their feedback helps us improve, innovate and serve them better. We value their trust and will continue to listen, learn and go the extra mile to exceed their expectations,” he said. Chief Marketing, Communications and Customer Experience Officer Cynthia Eyram Ofori-Dwumfuo said the Town Hall demonstrated the Bank’s commitment to ensuring customers have a direct voice in shaping their banking experience. “The insights shared by customers are invaluable. They help us understand what matters most to them and guide how we strengthen our services, relationships and overall customer experience,” she said. The Customer Town Hall forms part of GCB’s expanded Customer Service Month celebration, held under the global theme, “The Extra Mile.” For the first time, the Bank has extended its traditional Customer Service Week activities throughout October, creating more opportunities to appreciate customers, gather feedback and reinforce a culture of customer centricity across the organisation. Other activities planned for the month include customer appreciation engagements at branches, customer education sessions, Executive Committee customer interactions, Patrons Appreciation Day and the GCB Aerobics Fiesta. The Town Hall reflects GCB’s commitment to maintaining open dialogue with customers and ensuring their views remain central to the Bank’s efforts to continuously improve service delivery, strengthen relationships and support the growth of the businesses and communities it serves.

title: Kyiv Calls WP’s 4-Point Peace Plan ‘American PR’
body:
Ukraine has rejected the characterization of a reported four-point peace proposal as a joint US-European plan, saying the ideas reflect the position of only part of the American administration’s negotiating team.
Dmytro Lytvyn, communications advisor to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, responded on Tuesday, Oct. 13, to an opinion column in The Washington Post by columnist David Ignatius.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
“It is not ‘the US and European countries,’” Lytvyn told journalists.
“This is an outline of the vision of some members of the US team at the meeting in Florida, which was attended by Americans, Ukrainians and Europeans. Good PR by the Americans,” he added.
Lytvyn did not say that Ukraine had accepted or formally rejected the individual proposals outlined in the column.
Citing an unnamed US official familiar with the negotiations, Ignatius wrote that American officials were attempting to develop a broad package offering postwar economic and security benefits to both Ukraine and Russia in exchange for territorial compromises.
“We need to make the problem and the solution bigger to help both sides see what the postwar situation would be – and then make concessions,” the official said.
The ideas were discussed during a six-hour meeting in Florida on Friday, Oct. 9, hosted by Trump’s presidential envoys, son-in-law Jared Kushner and personal friend and golf partner Steve Witkoff.
The talks included Ukrainian officials and representatives of the UK, France and Germany. The meeting was held at the Shell Bay Golf Club in Hallandale Beach, a development personally owned by Witkoff.
The newspaper described four proposed components.
The first component would establish a framework for financing Ukraine’s postwar reconstruction, reportedly involving the World Bank and investment company BlackRock.
The funds would be used to rebuild destroyed regions, restore the Ukrainian economy and support the families of soldiers who were killed or wounded.
According to the US official cited by the newspaper, negotiators asked Kyiv to provide detailed estimates of its financial needs and assurances that reconstruction funds would be protected from corruption and postwar profiteering.
The column said Ukraine had not yet supplied the requested figures but was expected to do so within days if the negotiations continued.
The second component would provide Ukraine with security commitments from the US and European countries.
The unnamed official described the proposed guarantees as equivalent to NATO’s Article 5 collective-defense clause, with Western countries pledging to respond militarily if Russia attacked Ukraine again.
Russia would separately negotiate agreements with European states addressing its claimed security concerns. The column did not explain what concessions or restrictions those agreements could involve.
The third component would seek to integrate the Ukrainian, Russian and European economies through an energy agreement.
One option reportedly discussed was a pipeline carrying Russian oil and gas to Europe, with Ukraine and Russia sharing the profits.
Such an arrangement would provide Moscow with long-term access to the European energy market while potentially lowering energy prices in Europe, according to the White House official.
The proposed agreement would also establish conditions and a timetable for lifting existing economic sanctions against Russia.
No details were provided about which pipeline might be used, who would operate it or how revenues would be divided.
The fourth and most politically difficult component would involve a ceasefire along the existing front line, described by negotiators as the “line of control.”
Russia would abandon its original objective of conquering all of Ukraine but retain control of the Ukrainian territory it occupies when the ceasefire begins, including parts of the Donbas.
For Ukraine, this would mean tolerating continued Russian control without necessarily granting legal recognition to Moscow’s annexation claims.
The column noted that establishing such a line would be complicated by daily battlefield movements.
The discussion also covered Ukrainian attacks on Russian oil refineries, although this was not presented as one of the plan’s four components.
Kushner and Witkoff reportedly asked Ukraine to halt those attacks and warned Kyiv that Trump intended to conclude his diesel arrangement with Russia.
The Trump administration had previously pressed the Ukrainian delegation to stop striking Russian refineries , arguing that the attacks were contributing to higher fuel prices.
Zelensky later proposed a reciprocal “diesel deal” under which Ukraine would stop targeting Russian energy infrastructure if the US guaranteed protection for Ukraine’s electricity system.
The four-point proposal has not been published as an official document, approved by the participating governments or presented as an agreement accepted by Russia.
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: Downed drone crash injures one, damages houses in Malekhiv – official
body:
One person was injured and private residential houses were damaged as a result of a downed Russian drone crashing in the village of Malekhiv, Lviv district, Head of Lviv Regional Military Administration Maksym Kozytskyi reported.

"According to preliminary information, during an air alert that lasted in Lviv region from 15:04 to 15:31, a downed enemy drone fell in the village of Malekhiv, Lviv district. Private residential houses were damaged. All specialized services are working on site," Kozytsky noted in a post published on Tuesday.

He later added that one injured person had been reported: "As of this hour, one injured person is known."

title: One man killed, two injured in FPV drone strikes on civilian cars in Kharkiv region
body:
On Monday at around 10:00, a Russian FPV drone struck a car traveling on a road near Kuryazhanka (Kharkiv region), killing the driver.

"A 53-year-old driver, a resident of the settlement of Korotych, died as a result of the strike," the press service of Kharkiv Regional Prosecutor's Office reported.

In addition, in the afternoon on the road between Cherkaska Lozova and Derhachi, a Russian FPV drone attacked a car, injuring two men.

Pre-trial investigations into war crimes have been initiated (Article 438 of the Criminal Code of Ukraine).

title: Ukrainian strikes kill 52 Russian residents, including 5 children, over past week — envoy
body:
LUGANSK, October 13. /TASS/. Attacks by Ukrainian forces over the past week claimed the lives of 52 Russian civilians, including five children, while more than 270 people, including 11 minors, were injured, Rodion Miroshnik, Ambassador-at-Large of the Russian Foreign Ministry, told TASS.
"Over the past week, 326 civilians fell victim to shelling by Ukrainian Nazis: 274 civilians, including 11 minors, were injured, and 52 people, including five children, were killed," the diplomat noted.
Miroshnik said that 96% of the total number of casualties, or 312 people, were injured in attacks by enemy drones. "The largest number of civilian casualties over the week was recorded in the Belgorod, Bryansk, Zaporozhye, Kursk and Kherson regions, as well as the Donetsk and Lugansk People’s Republics," he said.
In total, Kiev fired approximately 8,500 munitions of various types at Russian territory over the past seven days, the source told the agency.

title: Mastercard research: Nigerian SMEs among global leaders in crypto, stablecoin and cybersecurity adoption
body: Nigerian small businesses lead 18 markets in crypto, stablecoin and cybersecurity adoption, Mastercard Dreamonomics report finds More than a third of Nigerian SMEs (34%) accept cryptocurrency, over twice the next-highest market, and 83% are excited about what AI can do for their business Eight in 10 Nigerian SMEs (81%) say cyber protection is a high priority, with 47% already using cybersecurity tools, the highest of the 18 markets surveyed Nigeria’s small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) are among the most advanced adopters of new payment methods and cybersecurity tools in the world, according to Mastercard’s new Dreamonomics report . Nigeria’s business owners rank highest of 18 global markets surveyed for accepting cryptocurrency, paying business expenses in both cryptocurrency and stablecoins, and using cybersecurity tools to protect what they are building. The Mastercard research shows that 34% of Nigerian SMEs now accept cryptocurrency as payment, well above the global average of 13%. Just over a fifth (22%) use cryptocurrency to pay business expenses, compared with 7% globally. Stablecoins are following the same path, with 23% of Nigerian SMEs accepting them, and 11% using them to settle business expenses, the highest of any surveyed market. Gabriel Swanepoel, executive vice president and division president, Africa at Mastercard, said: “Nigerian entrepreneurs have always been quick to put new technology to work when it helps them serve a customer or pay a supplier, and this research shows how far that instinct now reaches. Digital assets, AI and cybersecurity are already part of how many Nigerian businesses run from day to day, which gives the country a real opportunity to shape how the next generation of payments serves small businesses. Mastercard wants to make sure that momentum is built on trust, security and simplicity, so it keeps growing.” Key insights for Nigeria from the Dreamonomics report Security built in from the start. Nearly half of Nigerian SMEs (47%) already use cybersecurity tools such as antivirus software and firewalls, the highest of any surveyed market and above the global average of 37%. Cyber protection is a priority. Protecting the business from cyber threats is a high priority for 81% of Nigerian SMEs. Trust in financial providers. More than four in 10 (45%) would be very interested in cybersecurity services, software or risk assessments from their financial provider, the highest of any market surveyed. Optimism about AI. More than eight in 10 (83%) are excited about the possibilities AI opens up for their business, well above the global figure of 70%. AI that protects the business. Nearly six in 10 (59%) are interested in AI-powered fraud and security protection from their financial provider, the highest of the 18 markets and well ahead of the 41% global average. Tools that work together. The vast majority (82%) say it is critical that their business tools are connected and work well together. A strong appetite for growth. Half of Nigerian SMEs (51%) prioritize predictability over fast growth, compared with 68% globally, and 31% say they avoid risks to keep their finances predictable, against 54% globally. Both figures are the lowest of all 18 markets, placing Nigerian entrepreneurs among the most growth-focused in the study. The Dreamonomics results build on the Nigeria edition of the Mastercard SME Confidence Index released earlier this year, in which every SME surveyed (100%) agreed that digital and online payments are important to growing their business. They also arrive as Nigeria’s digital asset landscape continues to take shape. In August, the Central Bank of Nigeria opened applications for the second cohort of its Regulatory Sandbox Programme , which includes a dedicated track for virtual asset service providers covering areas such as fiat-backed stablecoin payments, giving companies a way to test new solutions under regulatory supervision. Mastercard is already supporting that momentum in Nigeria. Mastercard and Busha, a pan-African digital asset exchange, brought Mastercard Crypto Credential to Nigeria, enabling eligible users to send and receive supported digital assets using a verified alias such as an email address or phone number in place of long blockchain addresses. The collaboration brings added trust and simplicity to the kind of digital asset transfers a growing share of Nigerian SMEs already make. As small businesses prepare for what growth may demand next, Mastercard brings the connected system of insights, tools and solutions to help SMEs power every payment, protect every step and propel every dream — support for the realities of running and growing a business today. Globally, the Dreamonomics report finds that SMEs are redefining growth as steady, well-protected momentum, with 68% prioritizing stability and predictability over fast growth, 89% wanting to adopt more digital tools and 71% naming protection from cyber threats as a priority. More insights from the report are available here . About the report The Dreamonomics report is based on an online survey conducted by Hypothesis on behalf of Mastercard among more than 6,000 owners and senior decision-makers of SMEs with fewer than 250 employees across 18 markets, including Nigeria, in February and March 2026. About Mastercard Mastercard powers economies and empowers people in 200+ countries and territories worldwide. Together with our customers, we’re building a resilient economy where everyone can prosper. We support a wide range of digital payments choices, making transactions secure, simple, smart and accessible. Our technology and innovation, partnerships and networks combine to deliver a unique set of products and services that help people, businesses and governments realize their greatest potential. www.mastercard.com

title: Dark Signals: The death trap of non-functioning traffic lights along Asokwa-Aputuogya Road
body: The Asokwa-Aputuogya Road, one of the busiest corridors in the Kumasi Metropolis, has turned into a death trap for motorists and pedestrians due to non-functioning traffic lights along the stretch. A field assessment by JoyNews and Adom News revealed that only 14 out of the 95 traffic lights mounted at eight major intersections along the stretch are functioning. Francis Mensah reports that the non-functioning traffic lights pose a great road safety risk, with the situation already contributing to the loss of 20 lives at some intersections. Crossing any section of the Asokwa-Aputuogya road is one not for the faint-hearted. A sight not missed on the already dark stretch is malfunctioning traffic lights. Anyone crossing the road here could have used the traffic lights for easy passage, but here the pedestrians stand, sticking their necks out to fight for the right of way on the busy stretch. When the contractor completed the dualization of the first phase of the Lake Bosomtwe Road from Asokwa to Aputuogya, they erected 95 traffic lights. But over the years, the poles have failed to serve their purpose. The news team assessed the state of traffic lights along the route. Out of the total, 14 poles have functioning lamps, representing 14.74% functionality, leaving over 85% of the installations non-operational. At six critical intersections, namely Dompoase-Aprabong Junction, Fanko Junction, Agogo Hospital Junction, Atonsu High School Junction, Ahinsan Bonsuom, and Ahinsan Filling Station Junction, all traffic lights mounted on poles were non-functional. Additionally, some of the poles were damaged and had collapsed onto the ground. At Brewery Junction and from the Kumasi City Mall-KFC Junction to the Asokwa Police Station, the situation was slightly better, with some lights working while others remained non-functional. Our assessment revealed not a surprising reality, but a situation which underscores the fatalities recorded on the road. The malfunctioning traffic lights are taking a heavy toll on road safety. The intersections, which are supposed to be controlled, have become free-for-all zones. Commercial drivers, private motorists, motorcyclists and pedestrians all compete for space, leading to severe road hazards, including major vehicle crashes and pedestrian knockdowns. Drivers, residents and traders along the stretch say the situation has persisted for almost a year now. Despite several complaints, the faulty lights have not been repaired, raising questions about maintenance and monitoring by the responsible authorities. Authorities Aware, But No Action Checks by JoyNews reveal that authorities are not unaware of the looming danger. In January 2026, the Asokwa Municipal Chief Executive, together with the Municipal Roads Engineer and the Ashanti Regional Urban Roads team, inspected the Atonsu Market to Ahinsan Bonsuom stretch. It aimed to assess congestion and the state of traffic lights on the Asokwa Interchange–Atonsu corridor. Despite that high-profile inspection, the lights remain dead. On March 23, 2026, the situation worsened when the area experienced a significant traffic jam that left motorists stranded for hours. In a dramatic scene, the Municipal Chief Executive for Asokwa, Amoh Kamel, had to take matters into his own hands, personally directing traffic to ease the heavy congestion on the same stretch. The intervention, while praised by motorists, highlighted the failure of the automated system meant to do exactly that job. Some residents and road users who ply the stretch expressed frustration, saying accidents have increased along the road. “This place is very dangerous. I have personally witnessed many accidents here, involving cars, motorcycles, tricycles and trucks almost every week. Some victims have lost their lives while others sustained injuries,” lamented Fustian Osei, a trader at the Ahinsan Filling Station Junction. “We struggle to cross the road, especially the schoolchildren. Since the traffic lights are not working, drivers and riders do not stop for us. You have to look left, right and centre before crossing, otherwise you could be knocked down,” a pedestrian at Ahinsan Bonsuom said. Drivers who ply the Aputuogya-Asokwa route daily say near-misses and crashes have become common at these junctions, especially at the Dompoase-Aprabong Junction. “There is a slope at the Dompoase-Aprabong Junction and many heavy-duty trucks use this stretch. So, when a truck is descending the slope and gets to the intersection, and vehicles from the other side fail to stop to allow it to pass, it sometimes loses its brakes and rolls backwards, which often leads to accidents,” a driver explained. The Assembly Member for the Atonsu Electoral Area, Francis Asare Sarfo, disclosed that the Oforikrom Municipal Assembly is aware of the non-functioning traffic lights. According to him, the delay in fixing the faulty signals is due to the fact that the road has not yet been officially handed over to the Assembly by the contractor upon completion. Deaths at traffic intersections The role of traffic lights in controlling the flow of vehicles and coordinating pedestrian crossing at intersections is to prevent accidents and reduce congestion. Available data on road crashes in Greater Kumasi from the Building and Road Research Institute of the Council for Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR-BRRI) shows that a significant number of accidents occur at intersections. According to the Location Type by Crash Severity report, a total of 408 crashes were recorded at intersections in 2024. A breakdown shows that 20 of the crashes were fatal, 172 victims sustained serious injuries, and 216 escaped the carnage with lacerations. The Deputy Director of the CSIR-BRRI, Prof. Williams Ackaah, says non-functional traffic lights along the Asokwa-Lake Road expose motorists and pedestrians to high risk at intersections. “Look at the number of traffic lights that are not functioning. That’s not good. It means we are not getting the benefits we are supposed to get from the traffic lights. This can result in road crashes and road congestion,” he said The National Road Safety Authority (NRSA) has confirmed that most traffic lights along the corridor are non-functional, highlighting its attendant consequences. According to the Ashanti Regional Director of the Authority, Kwasi Agyenim Boateng, an audit of the road has been conducted and a report on the faulty traffic lights submitted to the Department of Urban Roads. He admitted that any casualties or accidents recorded at intersections where the lights are not functioning should be blamed on the authorities responsible for ensuring the lights are operational. “Most of the traffic lights on that stretch are not working, and as road users, we must acknowledge it. As the road safety authority, we have reported the issue to Urban Roads, which is the responsible agency. Its director has assured us that efforts are underway to get the contractor back on site to fix the lights,” Mr. Boateng admitted Deliberate Turn off? While some link the faulty traffic lights to mechanical failures, others suspect that lights at certain intersections have been deliberately turned off to ease traffic flow and reduce congestion. “We have been informed that some of the non-functional traffic lights were not faulty but were intentionally switched off. According to our sources, this decision was taken because the lights were contributing to heavy vehicular congestion on that stretch, rather than easing traffic flow,” a resident, Adom Helena said The Ashanti Regional Director of Urban Roads, Ing. Naeem Iddrisu, attributed the non-functioning of many traffic lights to mechanical faults but also admitted that some had been deliberately switched off because they were not communicating effectively with the rest of the lights. “Indeed, some traffic lights were deliberately switched off. For instance, the one at the Coca-Cola/Atonsu Market was in good working condition, but it was deactivated around 2003/2004 because it was not synchronizing effectively with the other traffic lights” Prof. Ackaah expressed deep concern over reasons that may account for the deliberate switching off of the lights. According to him, some of the traffic lights along the stretch have improper signal timings which, instead of improving traffic flow, worsen congestion, compelling traffic officers to switch them off for manual control. He warned that regardless of the justification, turning off traffic lights without effective alternative control measures heightens the risk of crashes, particularly for pedestrians and motorcyclists. Contractor yet to hand over road project Assembly Member for the Atonsu Electoral Area, Francis Asare Sarfo explained that until the formal handover is done, maintenance, including repairs of traffic lights, remains the responsibility of the contractor. Mr. Asare Sarfo further revealed that the Municipal Chief Executive (MCE) has held several engagements with both the project consultant and the contractor to ensure the defect is rectified, but the issue persists. Meanwhile, Urban Roads blamed the situation on a combination of factors, including erratic power supply, vandalism, and the theft of cables and other essential components of the traffic lights. Ing. Naeem Iddrisu explained that after the contractor completed construction and moved into the maintenance phase, it was discovered that a significant number of cables from the controllers had been stolen, rendering the lights inoperative. “The challenge has been that after the contractor finished the construction and started the maintenance phase, we realized that many of the cables in the controller had been stolen. We have different types of traffic lights – largely two types. We have solar traffic lights; those don’t need a major controller. But those fed by ECG or the national grid, like the one that was stolen, normally require a controller to regulate them” Prof. Ackaah therefore urged residents and road users to remain vigilant and assist in safeguarding the traffic lights against theft. He further advocated for the deployment of technology to enhance monitoring of the installations. But until the contractor officially hands over the project, how are authorities protecting lives on the road? The MTTD and road safety authority say they deploy officers to intersections where the traffic lights are not working daily. “We have therefore deployed MTTD officers and road safety campaigners to these intersections where the traffic lights are not functioning, and they are there on a daily basis to manage traffic flow and ensure the safety of motorists and pedestrians,” the NRSA director said. But our checks revealed a rather opposite account. From both ends of the road, no officer was sighted on the ground when we visited both at night and during the day. Residents want the traffic light fixed soon The Ashanti Regional Director of Urban Roads, Ing. Naeem Iddrisu, disclosed that arrangements are being made by the government to compensate the contractor for the stolen cables and vandalized components to enable him to return and restore the traffic lights. However, the contractor has yet to agree to the terms and has not provided a definite timeline for completing the repairs. “I have consulted the contractor, and he keeps giving me assurances that he will come, yet he has failed to provide me with a timeline to return to site to fix the traffic lights for us. So, I am still engaging him on the issue.” Road users are calling on the Department of Urban Roads, the Ministry of Roads and Highways and the Asokwa Municipal Assembly to, as a matter of urgency, rehabilitate all faulty traffic signals and put in place a regular maintenance plan for the corridor. From the Kumasi City Mall-KFC Junction to Dompoase-Aprabong Junction, ninety-five poles stand, but 85 percent are without functional bulbs. What is left is the will to fix them. But must it cost lives before authorities fix the lights? Pedestrians and motorists await the red, gold, and green bright colours on the stretch. End

title: Landlords Pay Rent as insecurity triggers housing crisis in Kaduna
body: Repeated kidnappings and attacks in communities on the outskirts of Kaduna metropolis are forcing residents to abandon their homes for rented apartments in the city. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the development is driving up rents and threatening the investments of low-income homeowners. From Baban Saura to Danhon II in Millennium City at the outskirts of Kaduna, residents who spent years building their houses are increasingly choosing to relocate rather than risk abduction and ransom demands. “I rented a self-contained apartment for N600,000, and many people say I got it cheap because houses are now very expensive in the city,” said Yakubu Dahiru, who abandoned his home in Danhon II community to Malali following attacks in his community. “The insecurity is no longer in the villages; the bandits are coming closer to us, and it is better to leave than to be abducted and then forced to sell the house to pay ransom,” he said. Dahiru said he had not returned home since the attack on his community last year and had been unable to find anyone willing to rent or guard the property because of fear. Residents in new layouts across Kaduna North, Kaduna South, Chikun and Igabi Local Government Areas are increasingly abandoning their properties to move to areas they consider safer locations within the metropolis. For more than a decade, such layouts provided affordable homeownership opportunities for lower-income earners who purchased plots and gradually developed their houses. The opening of the Eastern Bypass in Kaduna encouraged the growth of these settlements, according to an estate surveyor. Umar Mohammed, a Kaduna-based estate surveyor, said market women and people engaged in menial jobs had invested in the layouts because land was relatively affordable. However, insecurity is now forcing some homeowners to sell their properties at unfavourable prices or leave them unoccupied. Saidu Hamza, a resident of Danhono II, said he relocated his family to Ilorin in Kwara after an attack on his community and had put his three-bedroom house with an adjoining two-bedroom apartment up for sale. “With the security situation in the area, the price I am being offered is not very encouraging, and I could not leave my family there knowing the place is unsafe,” he said. The displacement has also increased demand for accommodation in Kaduna metropolis, with estate agents reporting substantial rent increases. Maiunguwa Ibrahim, an estate agent operating around Kurmin Mashi, Gwamna Road and Badiko, told NAN that rents for some three-bedroom apartments along Gwamna Road had risen from between N1.2 million and N1.5 million to between N3 million and N3.5 million. Mohammed attributed the increase to a shortage of available apartments amid the influx of residents fleeing insecure communities. The situation compounds Nigeria’s housing challenge, with the World Bank’s Nigeria Affordable Housing Project 2018 estimating a national housing deficit of 17 million units and an annual requirement of about 700,000 housing units over 20 years. Security sources told NAN that the scattered nature of houses in new layouts, inadequate fencing, limited security posts and proximity to forested areas made some communities vulnerable to attacks. The concerns have been reinforced by recurring abductions in Millennium City and neighbouring areas, including the kidnapping of two journalists two years ago More recently, gunmen reportedly killed a man identified as Sikiru in Baban Saura community and abducted his wife, Hafsat, their 14-year-old son, Abdulsalam, and six other persons. Hafsat and her son are still in captivity, according to a family member. In Millennium City, a couple and their six-month-old daughter were abducted from Alrahus Estate on October 6. The husband, Ahmed Abubakar Zakka, appealed for help in a viral video, saying the kidnappers demanded N300 million ransom. Amnesty International Nigeria has also warned that residents of Millennium City face persistent threats from armed men, with some families abandoning their homes and others suspending their children’s education. Meanwhile, the Kaduna State Police Command on Monday said it had arrested 12 suspects, including eight suspected kidnappers and four alleged informants, during operations in Millennium City and Maraban Rido. The command said the Kaduna State Government had released three additional armoured personnel carriers to strengthen security operations in the affected areas. Retired Capt. Abdullahi Umar, a security commentator, urged the government to support neighbourhood watch initiatives and strengthen collaboration between security agencies, traditional rulers and community leaders. He said community vigilance could complement security operations, particularly in settlements where the number of deployed personnel was insufficient for the size of the area. The growing displacement highlights how insecurity is extending beyond physical attacks to affect housing affordability, household investments and livelihoods, leaving residents paying rising rents while their own homes remain abandoned. (NAN)

title: NAF Air Crash: Reps seek independent probe, audit of military aircraft after fatal crash
body:
The House of Representatives has called for an independent investigation into the fatal Nigerian Air Force aircraft crash that claimed the lives of some military personnel.
It also called for a comprehensive audit of military aircraft and their maintenance systems.
The House made the call on Tuesday during plenary after Alhassan Usman (APC, Kano) moved an urgent motion on the incident, urging the federal government to strengthen aircraft maintenance, ensure adequate funding for the military and improve operational safety.
The motion followed the crash in Ondo State, which prompted search-and-rescue operations involving local divers and security agencies. No survivors were reported.
Mr Usman said the loss of military personnel underscored the need for sustained investment in military aviation infrastructure, aircraft maintenance and the logistical support required to keep military aircraft operational and safe.
He expressed condolences to the families of the deceased and the Nigerian Air Force, describing the incident as a painful loss to the country.
Mr Usman raised concerns about inadequate funding, shortages of spare-parts and logistical constraints, warning that these could undermine aircraft maintenance and compromise operational safety.
He urged the federal government to provide adequate resources for the military and ensure the timely release of approved funds for technical inspections, maintenance and other operational requirements.
Mr Usman also called for a comprehensive review of Nigerian Air Force aircraft and maintenance systems to establish whether the required safety standards and inspection procedures were being followed.
He asked the House committees responsible for the Air Force, aviation and defence to investigate the circumstances surrounding the crash and conduct an audit of military aircraft to identify safety gaps and recommend corrective measures.
Contributing to the debate, Donald Ojogo (APC, Ondo) supported the motion but called for an independent investigation into the crash, saying the circumstances surrounding the incident required further scrutiny.
“I want to plead that, because of the various claims and counterclaims that have come on the heels of this very important and unfortunate incident, there is a need for us to institute an independent probe,” Mr Ojogo said.
He added that the proposed investigation should not prevent the Nigerian Air Force from conducting its own inquiry.
Mr Ojogo also commended local divers, personnel of the Nigerian Navy at its Forward Operating Base in Igbokoda and the Ondo State Emergency Management Agency for their efforts at the crash site.
He said the agencies and local volunteers had made selfless efforts to locate and recover the victims, but no survivors were found.
The lawmaker further said the aircraft crashed near a densely populated part of Igbokoda, suggesting that the pilot’s actions may have prevented greater casualties on the ground.
“We have to give kudos to the pilot of the aircraft,” he said, adding that the crash occurred close to a densely populated community.
Mr Ojogo also backed calls for a comprehensive audit of military aircraft and urged the government to ensure adequate and timely funding for the armed forces.
Babajimi Benson (APC, Lagos) also supported the motion, describing the crash as a painful reminder of the risks military personnel face while carrying out their duties.
“Everyone lost to the tragedy, not only for the families that have been bereaved by their death, but also for the Nigerian Air Force and our country as a whole,” Mr Benson said.
He extended his condolences to the leadership of the Nigerian Air Force, the families of the deceased and other personnel affected by the incident.
Mr Benson called for a thorough investigation, saying the circumstances surrounding the crash must be established.
Following the debate, Speaker Abbas Tajudeen referred the motion to the House committees on Air Force, Aviation and Defence for further legislative action.
The lawmakers also observed a minute’s silence in honour of the deceased.
The crash occurred on 5 October when a Nigerian Air Force ATR-42 aircraft plunged into a swamp in Igbokoda, the headquarters of Ilaje Local Government Area of Ondo State, killing all 25 people on board, according to a PREMIUM TIMES report published on Tuesday.
A week after the incident, divers and rescue teams were still searching for the victims’ remains and the aircraft’s black box, which could provide investigators with critical information about the circumstances leading to the crash.
The search operation had recovered fragments of the aircraft and human remains, although the impact of the crash and the muddy terrain had made recovery and identification difficult.
The crash also raised concerns about possible water pollution in Igbokoda, where residents rely on the river as a major source of water. A rescue operator reported the presence of aviation fuel and oil in the water around the crash site.

title: Russia cuts oil production by 38,000 bpd in September, OPEC says
body:
MOSCOW, October 13. /TASS/. Russia reduced its crude oil production by 38,000 barrels per day (bpd) month-on-month in September to 8.643 million bpd, according to the latest report by the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC).
In September, Russia's production quota under the OPEC+ agreement stood at 9.949 million bpd, factoring in voluntary output caps. Consequently, Russia's oil production for the month was 1.306 million bpd below its targeted allocation, excluding the compensation schedule.
Currently, oil production in Russia is capped under the OPEC+ agreement. From early 2024 through March 2025, Russia's baseline production quota - including voluntary restrictions -stood at 8.978 million bpd. This figure did not account for obligations to compensate for past overproduction during the voluntary restriction window.
In April 2025, Russia began gradually scaling up its output month-on-month in accordance with the OPEC+ roadmap. In September 2025--a year ahead of schedule--OPEC+ nations completed the phase-out of voluntary cuts totaling 2.2 million bpd and began unwinding another 1.65 million bpd in supply curbs to return the curtailed volumes to the market. By September 2026, these countries had completed the restoration of this volume to the market. For the remainder of the year, previously approved baseline quotas will apply to all OPEC+ countries without additional restrictions, fixing Russia's quota at 9.949 million bpd.

title: Character.AI files for bankruptcy, will sell some assets to Disney for $20M
body:
Chatbot platform Character.AI said on Monday it has filed for bankruptcy in the U.S. and has agreed to sell some assets for US$20 million to Walt Disney.
The generative AI platform has faced mounting legal challenges over its chatbots. Earlier this year, Character.AI and Alphabet’s Google settled a lawsuit by the mother of a 14-year-old Florida boy who killed himself after the startup’s chatbot allegedly encouraged him to do so.
Kentucky has sued the company, saying its chatbots encouraged users to cut, starve or kill themselves, while Pennsylvania filed a lawsuit alleging its chatbots posed as doctors.
According to Character.AI’s proposal, Disney will be a “stalking-horse” bidder — an initial prospective buyer — for a non-exclusive perpetual license to some intellectual property. Other bidders can top Disney’s offer.
Character.AI expects to close the sale of all its assets by late November or early December. Character Technologies, its U.S.-based owner, listed estimated assets and liabilities of between $50 million and $100 million, according to a court filing.
Disney will help the platform in the transition, using staff it has hired from Character.AI. The platform’s services would continue meanwhile, but would be shut down if it can’t find a buyer, the company said.
Two former Google employees founded Character.AI in 2021. In 2024, Google licensed its technology and rehired the founders.
The Financial Times reported in May 2024 that Meta and Elon Musk’s xAI were competing to partner with Character.AI. In July 2024, Musk denied a media report that xAI was considering buying the company.
In September 2025, Disney sent Character.AI a cease-and-desist letter, demanding it stop using Disney’s copyrighted characters without permission. Character.AI said it had removed them.

title: US should not have eliminated Iran’s leadership — Trump
body:
WASHINGTON, October 13. /TASS/. The United States might have overdone it in Iran by eliminating its leadership because now Washington cannot understand who it is dealing with, President Donald Trump said.
"They got no leadership and that’s the problem. We might have gone too far with the leadership, we don’t know who the hell we are dealing with," he told Republican supporters in Ohio, as broadcast by CNN .
The United States and Israel started a war with Iran on February 28. In June, Washington and Tehran signed a memorandum of understanding providing for an immediate cessation of hostilities on all fronts, including in Lebanon. However, on the night of July 8, the United States resumed large-scale strikes against Iran, accusing it of violating the agreements on the Strait of Hormuz. About 25% of the world’s oil trade and about 20% of liquefied natural gas are transported through it. Subsequently, the US administration effectively signaled a shift away from the use of large·scale military force against Iran and towards an attempt to economically strangle it through sanctions.

title: Rep. Ilhan Omar’s residence searched as part of ongoing criminal investigation: DOJ
body:
The search comes three weeks before the midterm elections.
Democratic Rep. Ilhan Omar's Washington, D.C.-area residence was searched early Monday morning, a Department of Justice spokesperson said, as part of an ongoing criminal investigation.
Sources tell ABC News that the investigation relates to Omar's immigration paperwork. Omar, who was first elected to the House in 2018, is the first Somali-American in Congress.
In recent history, the Justice Department's practice has been to advise prosecutors not to take any overt investigative steps against members of Congress or candidates within 60 days of an election. The midterm elections, during which Omar is up for reelection, take place in 22 days, with early voting starting in Minnesota later this week.
Omar came to the U.S. as a refugee when she was a child and has been living in the country since she was 12 years old. She is a U.S. citizen.
"Today in the Washington, D.C. area, Homeland Security Investigations executed a judicially authorized search warrant secured by the Department of Justice," a DOJ spokesperson said. "This enforcement action is part of an ongoing federal criminal investigation."
Omar released a statement on social media on Monday, saying she is "ok" and that the search at her residence is "an attempt to target political enemies and weaponize federal law enforcement."
"I will not be silenced," she wrote in the statement.
It's unclear whether Omar was at her D.C.-area residence at the time of Monday's search.
White House border czar Tom Homan confirmed the investigation in an interview with Fox News on Monday, but offered few details. Homan said he didn't want to get ahead of Attorney General Todd Blanche on any matter related to the investigation.
"I can confirm that a search warrant was executed this morning, signed by a judge. Department of Justice is leading the investigation along with Department of Homeland Security," Homan said. "There is an investigation. I won't get into the specifics of the criminal investigation."
Omar, who represents Minnesota's 5th Congressional District, has been a central political target for the administration and its broader efforts to cast the Somali community as criminal and un-American.
"How about Ilhan Omar? She comes from Somalia. She comes from Somalia. They don't have a government. They don't have police. They don't. All they have is crime and squalor. And she comes into our country, and she says, 'My constitution allows me.' She's talking about our constitution, what they've done to Minnesota, these people from Somalia, what they've done to Minnesota, should never be allowed. And let's see what happens. JD Vance and our people are looking at it very strongly," Trump said during a rally on Saturday.
In social media posts earlier this year, Trump also said Omar "should be in jail" and "sent back to Somalia."
Trump's remarks directed at Omar have drawn criticism, and Omar said earlier this year that Trump's rhetoric has led threats against her to "skyrocket."
The White House referred all comment requests to the Department of Justice.
Vice President JD Vance, who the administration has tasked with leading the so-called "anti-fraud efforts" said during a White House briefing in May that the administration was going to look into Omar for immigration fraud allegations.
Omar has previously denied any wrongdoing and has not been charged with a crime.
Last month, Homan confirmed in an interview with Fox News that DHS was looking into Omar, but wouldn't disclose the extent of those allegations noting that it was part of an "ongoing criminal investigation."

title: FG seeks arrest of suspect in attack on FMC Abeokuta worker
body:
The federal government has called on the Nigeria Police Force to immediately arrest and prosecute the suspect who allegedly stabbed a health worker at the Federal Medical Centre (FMC), Idi-Aba, Abeokuta, Ogun.
The Minister of State for Health and Social Welfare, Iziaq Salako, made the call in a statement issued on Monday night by the Assistant Director, Information and Public Relations, Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, Ado Bako.
Mr Salako condemned the reported stabbing of Lawal Olasunkanmi, a medical laboratory scientist at the hospital, describing the attack as “barbaric and unacceptable”.
“No grief, frustration or dissatisfaction with care can justify violence against a health worker performing his lawful duties.”
The minister said the ministry would follow the case to ensure that the alleged assailant was brought to justice.
He said the incident reinforced the urgency of implementing measures directed by the ministry on 5 August to strengthen the protection of health workers in federal tertiary health institutions.
According to him, the measures include strengthened security arrangements, violence-prevention teams, incident reporting, collaboration with law-enforcement agencies and improved complaint-handling procedures.
“These safeguards must translate into effective protection for health personnel across health facilities,” he said.
Mr Salako also appealed to health workers, who had embarked on industrial action at FMC Abeokuta, to return to work immediately in the interest of patients and the wider public.
He urged the workers to allow security authorities to carry out their duties and pursue the investigation.
The minister further urged the hospital management to ensure that the injured staff member received appropriate medical care and support while strengthening security arrangements in line with federal government directives.
He extended the government’s condolences to the family of the deceased patient, stressing that the loss of a loved one deserved compassion and appropriate attention.
Mr Salako urged anyone dissatisfied with the care received at the hospital to use its formal complaints mechanism.
He said that such concerns could be examined fairly and addressed on their merits without recourse to violence.
The minister reiterated that protecting health workers was essential to safe and uninterrupted healthcare delivery.
According to him, health facilities must remain safe environments where personnel can perform their duties without fear of violence and patients and their families can seek care with confidence.

title: SSPDF: Soldiers who want to stand for elections must resign
body: The South Sudan People’s Defence Forces (SSPDF) has said officers and men who want to contest in the 22 December General Elections must resign their commissions and leave military service. The directive was contained in a press statement titled “Resignation from Military Service, a prerequisite to contest in December 2026 General Elections” put out by SSPDF Spokesperson Maj. Gen. Lul Ruai Koang on Tuesday afternoon on his Facebook page. “This brief statement serves to inform all our servicemen/servicewomen that the highest leadership and command of SSPDF has given approval to those aspiring to contest in the forthcoming December 22, 2026 General Elections to do so under the following strict and mandatory conditions,” the statement reads in part. “First and foremost, an aspirant must write and tender a duly written resignation letter to SSPDF’s Assistant Chief of Defence Forces for Administration, Personnel and Finance.” “And finally, upon successful receipt of the resignation letter, the SSPDF command will release you without further unnecessary delays,” the statement added. Gen. Ruai said the command wishes aspirants good luck in advance. On 31 December 2021, President Salva Kiir Mayardit issued Republican Order No. 27/2021 banning active-duty military and regular forces from participating in politics and community leadership. The order prohibits active officers and NCOs across regular forces from engaging in politics and restricts community leadership and social media misconduct. Interestingly, President Kiir, even after the order, has often appointed soldiers to political positions. The post SSPDF: Soldiers who want to stand for elections must resign appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

title: Protecting Nigeria’s oil and gas assets through coordination and accountability, By Chido Onumah
body:
A Common Framework for Protecting National Assets
The signing and launch, on 12 October, of the Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for Government Security and Intelligence Agencies and Other Stakeholders under the Nigerian Oil and Gas Industry-Wide Security Architecture gives Nigeria a common framework for protecting hydrocarbon assets. It connects security operations with economic recovery, environmental protection and public accountability. For operators and relevant stakeholders, the task is to translate its provisions into understood responsibilities, credible public information and constructive community participation.
The NSA’s Message on Coordination and Implementation
National Security Adviser , Nuhu Ribadu , placed these priorities at the centre of his remarks. He described crude oil theft, pipeline vandalism and illegal refining as threats to production, the environment and national security. Sustained progress, he emphasised, requires unity of purpose, clarity of roles and operational discipline. The SOP provides a practical basis for reducing friction among institutions and consolidating gains achieved through collaboration across government and industry.
Ribadu identified implementation as the decisive test. He urged agencies, operators and partners to disseminate the provisions to commands, formations, field operatives and relevant personnel. His insistence on professionalism, information sharing, respect for mandates and adherence to law establishes the standard against which implementation should be assessed. Personnel must understand the requirements, and supervisors must ensure that they guide everyday decisions.
Defence Leadership on Clear Roles and Operational Order
The Minister of Defence, General Christopher Musa (rtd), endorsed the initiative, describing the launch as “another milestone” and “a step in the right direction.” His assessment reflects the importance of giving participating institutions an agreed operational reference. Protecting petroleum infrastructure requires sustained cooperation among defence, intelligence and law enforcement institutions, working with operators, regulators and communities.
The Chief of Defence Staff, General Olufemi Oluyede, explained the practical value of that reference. “Every agency understanding what to do, how to go about it, and when to do it, aligning with its boundaries, ultimately brings about orderliness,” he said. His observation captures a central purpose of the SOP: enabling institutions to act together while respecting their respective mandates.
NNPC Limited on Production Gains and Institutional Alignment
Mr Bashir Bayo Ojulari, Group Chief Executive Officer of NNPC Limited, connected security to national revenue, investor confidence, operational continuity and host-community wellbeing. Recalling the crisis preceding the architecture, he said national crude oil and condensate production had fallen to approximately 950,000 barrels per day in August 2022, with unavailable trunklines and substantial differences between injected volumes and terminal receipts.
Ojulari reported more than 10,000 illegal refining sites deactivated, close to 7,000 illegal connections removed, over 2.4 million barrels of stolen crude recovered and more than 3,700 suspects apprehended. He also reported production above 1.7 million barrels per day and improved trunkline availability. These figures illustrate the gains he attributed to collaboration, while reinforcing the need for reliable reporting that distinguishes apprehensions from prosecutions and convictions.
While affirming NNPC Limited’s support, Ojulari proposed a 60-day period for stakeholders to refine certain provisions and secure institutional alignment. He explained that company responsibilities would undergo established internal approval processes, including Board consideration where required. His proposal complements the SOP’s periodic review mechanism, under which proposed changes pass through the Office of the National Security Adviser ( ONSA ) in consultation with relevant stakeholders.
The Commandant-General of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, Ahmed Audi, reaffirmed the corps’ responsibility for safeguarding oil and gas assets. He disclosed that several officers found guilty of misconduct in the Niger Delta had been dismissed. His remarks underline the importance of internal discipline: public confidence depends on the conduct of personnel entrusted with protecting national assets.
Private Surveillance Partners on Technology and Knowledge Sharing
Private surveillance contractors are also central to implementation. Captain Warredi Enisuoh, Executive Director, Operations and Technical, Tantita Security Services Nigeria Limited, argued that the manual should reach beyond the immediate participants. He called for its distribution to institutions of learning to benefit future generations, widening understanding of infrastructure protection and the responsibilities that accompany it.
Enisuoh noted that the operational gains cited at the launch had been achieved before the manual was available and expressed confidence that the SOP would support further improvements. He also described Tantita’s command and control centre as having the capacity to monitor beyond Nigeria’s exclusive economic zone. He pledged to use that capability to support implementation and share information with Nigerian security forces.
Institutional Mandates and Supervision of Contractors
The SOP gives these commitments operational substance. It preserves participating institutions’ rights and obligations under the Constitution and their establishing laws and agreements. Contractors contribute surveillance, intelligence, community engagement and technology under government security supervision. Their overt operations must be undertaken jointly with government security agencies, enabling complementary contributions while retaining public authority over enforcement.
Arrest Procedures and Protection of Suspects’ Rights
Its scope extends beyond those physically stealing oil to storage, transportation, marketing, sponsorship and financing of stolen hydrocarbons, alongside connivance and failure to report specified offences. Effective enforcement must therefore investigate the networks sustaining theft. Arrest procedures require verification, documentation and reporting through the Command-and-Control Centre, with contractors handing arrested persons or assets to designated government authorities as soon as practicable.
Records of exhibits, witness statements and physical or digital evidence support investigation and prosecution. Equally important, the SOP expressly recognises arrested persons’ freedom from torture and degrading treatment, information about reasons for arrest, the right to silence, access to legal representation and humane custody conditions. These safeguards strengthen lawful enforcement and the credibility of investigations.
Coordinated Patrols and Responsible Use of Surveillance Technology
The document regulates night patrols, movement along pipelines and unmanned aerial vehicles. Joint planning and operational briefings reduce confusion, while drone operations require relevant permissions, safe flight procedures and coordination with aviation and security authorities. Secure data handling, equipment controls and training help ensure that technology supports operations responsibly.
Recovery and Evacuation of Petroleum Products
Procedures for evacuating recovered crude oil and refined products assign coordination and oversight to ONSA, security protection to relevant agencies, and verification responsibilities to regulators. Environmental authorities oversee relevant compliance. Final inspection compares delivered products with recorded quantities and quality at recovery, while reporting and legal oversight support lawful forfeiture and accountability.
NFIU on Compliance and Measurable Outcomes
Hafsat Bakari, chief executive officer and director of the Nigerian Financial Intelligence Unit, described the framework as a technical and compliance milestone. She called for a legal and monitoring structure, supported by feedback mechanisms to assess implementation and address gaps. Her emphasis on outcomes reinforces the NSA’s message that adoption must produce measurable improvements.
Public Communication and Community Participation
Strategic communication and community engagement will help sustain implementation. The SOP assigns media coverage of arrested vessels to designated government bodies and NNPC Limited, supporting coordinated, verified information. Operators and contractors must also engage communities. Accessible communication, responsible civil society partnerships and opportunities to report concerns can strengthen cooperation while protecting investigations.
Implementation should combine training with oversight and sustained industry cooperation. Monitoring should track infrastructure reliability, environmental compliance, prosecution outcomes and lawful conduct. Feedback from personnel and communities can identify gaps requiring correction. Participating institutions should explain responsibilities and communicate verified progress.
Sustaining Cooperation for Security and Economic Recovery
The NSA’s closing message offers confidence in sustained cooperation. Thanking stakeholders, Ribadu expressed his conviction that, working together, we will strengthen Nigeria’s oil and gas infrastructure security and support increased production, environmental protection and economic recovery. Guided by professionalism, information sharing and respect for mandates, the SOP provides a firm foundation for securing these gains for Nigerians.
Chido Onumah is special adviser to the National Security Adviser on Strategic Communication and Civil Society Liaison.

title: Leonardo DRS Strengthens Dismounted Soldier Modernization
body:
ARLINGTON, Va., Oct. 13, 2026 — Leonardo DRS, Inc. announced today that it has received a $63 million production order from the U.S. Army for its next-generation Family of Weapon Sights – Individual, or FWS-I, thermal weapon sight system. The order was placed under the Army’s existing indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity, or IDIQ, contract for advanced, battlefield-proven, thermal weapon sight systems supporting dismounted soldiers. FWS-I is a lightweight, uncooled thermal imaging system designed to wirelessly integrate with solider-worn vision devices, including the Enhanced Night Vision Goggle–Binocular, or ENVG-B, and the Integrated Visual Augmentation System, or IVAS. This wireless connection allows soldiers to view thermal imagery from the weapon sight through their helmet-mounted display, enabling rapid target acquisition without needing to shoulder the weapon. Maintaining situational awareness provides a critical advantage in complex, high-threat environments. “Modernization at the tactical edge depends on giving soldiers the information they need without adding unnecessary complexity,” said John Baylouny, president and chief executive officer of Leonardo DRS . “The FWS-I production order reflects the Army’s continued focus on advanced sensing, connected soldier systems and mission-ready capability. DRS is proud to support that mission by delivering practical technologies designed to help soldiers detect threats, make decisions faster and Own the Edge™.” As adversaries employ more sophisticated concealment techniques and operate in low-visibility conditions, thermal weapon sights can help soldiers identify and assess potential threats across a range of operational environments, including urban terrain, dense foliage, smoke, fog and darkness. at close and extended ranges. FWS-I uses thermal imaging to help soldiers detect heat signatures in conditions where camouflage, lighting, or weather may reduce the effectiveness of traditional visual observation. “This cutting-edge technology ensures soldiers will have the most advanced weapon sight systems on the battlefield today, ” said Jerry Hathaway, senior vice president and general manager of Leonardo DRS Electro-Optical Infrared Systems. “FWS-I combines advanced uncooled thermal imaging with soldier-worn display integration to help improve target acquisition and situational awareness for dismounted soldiers. We are proud the U.S. Army continues to trust DRS to deliver this vital capability that enhances survivability and effectiveness in multi-domain operations.” FWS-I features uncooled infrared technology designed to provide rugged thermal imaging performance without the need of cryogenic cooling. Its clip-on design provides flexibility for use across multiple weapon platforms. The wireless link to soldier-worn systems ensures speed, accuracy, and situational awareness without compromising mobility. The award builds on DRS’s long-standing relationship with the U.S. Army and its experience in electro-optical and infrared, or EO/IR technologies. In addition to FWS-I, DRS provides a broad range of EO/IR technologies supporting mounted and unmounted operations, airborne platforms, and aircraft survivability. Source: Leonardo S.p.A. FWS-I uses thermal imaging to help soldiers detect heat signatures in conditions where camouflage, lighting, or weather may reduce the effectiveness of traditional visual observation. “This cutting-edge technology ensures soldiers will have the most advanced weapon sight systems on the battlefield today, ” said Jerry Hathaway, senior vice president and general manager of Leonardo DRS Electro-Optical Infrared Systems. “FWS-I combines advanced uncooled thermal imaging with soldier-worn display integration to help improve target acquisition and situational awareness for dismounted soldiers. We are proud the U.S. Army continues to trust DRS to deliver this vital capability that enhances survivability and effectiveness in multi-domain operations.” FWS-I features uncooled infrared technology designed to provide rugged thermal imaging performance without the need of cryogenic cooling. Its clip-on design provides flexibility for use across multiple weapon platforms. The wireless link to soldier-worn systems ensures speed, accuracy, and situational awareness without compromising mobility. The award builds on DRS’s long-standing relationship with the U.S. Army and its experience in electro-optical and infrared, or EO/IR technologies.
