title: Reps speaker warns lawmakers against 2027 campaign distractions, unveils 100-day legislative plan
body:
The Speaker of the House of Representatives, Abbas Tajudeen, has proposed a 100-day legislative programme to fast-track pending bills and committee reports, warning lawmakers against abandoning their legislative duties for political campaigns ahead of the 2027 general elections.
Mr Tajudeen announced the proposal on Tuesday in Abuja in his welcome address as the House officially resumed plenary after its annual recess.
He urged members to improve attendance at plenary and committee sittings and prioritise major bills and urgent national issues.
He said the programme would require committees to clear outstanding reports within defined timelines, while Tuesdays and Thursdays would be devoted to major legislative business.
“We must remain focused,” the speaker said, warning that the increasing demands of the political season must not undermine the responsibilities lawmakers owe their constituents.
“Our constituents elected us for a full term, and they deserve a full term of service,” he said.
Mr Tajudeen said the 10th House had entered its fourth and final phase, making it necessary for lawmakers to assess their performance and complete outstanding legislative priorities before the end of the Assembly.
He also proposed the publication of a comprehensive legislative scorecard and legacy report before the end of the Assembly to enable Nigerians to compare the House’s commitments with its performance.
Providing an account of the House’s performance, Mr Tajudeen said lawmakers had received 2,747 bills and passed 363 by the middle of June 2026.
He said the rate of passage increased from about seven per cent in the first session to approximately 26 per cent in the third session.
The House also processed hundreds of motions and public petitions during the period, according to the Speaker.
However, he cautioned against measuring legislative performance solely by the volume of bills passed, arguing that the ultimate test should be the impact of legislation and oversight on Nigerians.
“A law must solve a problem. A motion must lead to action. An investigation must protect the public interest. Oversight must improve the management of public resources,” he said.
Mr Tajudeen added that an internal assessment of the House’s performance against its Legislative Agenda showed that it had completed between 65 and 70 per cent of its principal milestones.
He urged lawmakers to use the remaining period to conclude priority legislation, strengthen oversight and ensure that outstanding proposals did not expire without consideration.
The speaker identified the conclusion of the constitutional review process as one of the House’s immediate priorities, specifically mentioning the proposed state police and reserved seats for women bills.
He said the bills and other outstanding constitutional alteration proposals required sustained engagement with the Senate and the State Houses of Assembly.
The state police proposal seeks to introduce a policing structure that would allow states to establish their own police services, while the reserved seats proposal seeks to increase women’s representation in legislative institutions.
Mr Tajudeen also urged the Executive to submit the Medium Term Expenditure Framework for the 2027 budget promptly to give lawmakers sufficient time to scrutinise the fiscal proposals ahead of the next appropriation process.
He said timely submission would help the National Assembly conduct a thorough review and lay the foundation for the passage of the budget within the required timeframe.
The Speaker further disclosed that the House would give attention to bills and requests transmitted by President Bola Tinubu, including the National Research Development Fund Bill and a request for the domestication of the Geneva Conventions and their relevant protocols.
According to him, the proposed domestication of the international humanitarian law instruments would strengthen protections for civilians, wounded persons and prisoners during armed conflicts.
He commended the president for transmitting the request, describing it as significant to Nigeria’s national and diplomatic interests.
Mr Tajudeen also urged lawmakers to protect the integrity of the electoral process as political activity intensifies ahead of the 2027 general elections.
He said the Electoral Act must be faithfully implemented and the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) given the lawful support required to perform its duties.
He added that public institutions involved in the elections must act with neutrality, competence and restraint.
The speaker acknowledged that political realignments and defections had occurred across party lines but urged members not to allow partisan interests to undermine the work of the House.
“Whatever our political affiliations or personal ambitions, we remain members of one House. We are bound by one Constitution and one oath. The campaign must never become more important than the country,” he said.
He called on lawmakers to maintain regular attendance at plenary and committee sittings, insisting that legislation and oversight must continue despite the approaching elections.
Mr Tajudeen also called for greater accountability in the management of public revenue, particularly at the sub-national level, following what he described as improvements in government revenues.
He said increased resources available to federal, state and local governments should translate into better roads, stronger schools, safer communities and more effective healthcare.
The speaker cited economic indicators, including growth above four per cent, a decline in inflation to 15.39 per cent in August from 23.14 per cent a year earlier, and external reserves of $54.7 billion in September.
He also said Nigeria recorded a trade surplus of more than N20 trillion in the first half of 2026, nearly twice the figure recorded during the corresponding period in 2025.
While acknowledging these developments, he said the gains must translate into improved living conditions through affordable food, productive employment, accessible credit and dependable public services.
He also cited new investment commitments in ports, power, agriculture and industry, including the proposed $7 billion Gateway Deep Seaport and Blue Marine Economic Zone, as potential sources of jobs and increased exports.
Mr Tajudeen, however, said the government must address continuing security and humanitarian challenges.
He expressed concern over reports of abducted schoolchildren in Borno, attacks and displacement in parts of Ondo, as well as flooding and erosion in Enugu and Abia during the recess.
He called for prompt relief for affected communities and lasting protection against further attacks and disasters. He also said security agencies should receive the necessary support while remaining accountable for the resources and authority entrusted to them.
The speaker said the House would continue to scrutinise the implementation of the 2025 Appropriation Act following the extension of its capital component to 31 December.
He said the extension, approved by the House on 29 September, was intended to protect ongoing projects and prevent the waste of public investment.
However, he warned that the decision must lead to faster implementation and measurable results rather than further delays.
“The extension must produce faster implementation and measurable results. It must not excuse further delay,” he said.
He added that the House would continue to examine budget releases, implementation timelines and project performance.
Mr Tajudeen also urged cooperation among the legislature, executive and judiciary, while emphasising the constitutional independence of each arm of government.
He thanked members of the House, including the Minority Caucus, for their contributions to the institution and called for continued cooperation in the final phase of the Tenth Assembly.
He said the remaining months should be used to complete priority legislation, strengthen oversight and demonstrate that the House had fulfilled its mandate to Nigerians.

title: Russians attack truck and warehouse in Khmelnytskyi region
body:
Serhii Tiurin, head of the Khmelnytskyi Regional Military Administration, reported the incident on Facebook , according to Ukrinform.
"During the day, the enemy attacked the Khmelnytskyi region. Air defense forces were operating. As a result of the Russian attack, a truck and the facade of a warehouse building on the premises of one of the region's businesses were damaged," the official reported.
According to him, no deaths or injuries had been reported.
As Ukrinform previously reported, four patients at a medical facility in the Khmelnytskyi region were injured in an attack by Russian strike drones .

Apple just announced its long-rumored smart home hub, the HomeView , during its “Welcome Home” event taking place today. As part of the event, it showed a video featuring the new device , and if you want to see it for yourself, you can watch it right here.
The HomeView is a 7-inch square display. It costs $299 and comes in two versions: one that mounts to a wall, and another that sits atop a small speaker base. It can be used to show smart home controls, pull up information with Siri AI, take video calls, and show footage from HomeKit Secure Video cameras. It’s also a Matter controller and a Thread Border Router.
Apple CEO John Ternus also shared a short video of the HomeView in a post on X , showing some of the different “faces” users can choose from.
The HomeView will be available for preorder starting today, with four color options, including silver, starlight, rose pink, and space gray. It starts shipping on November 13th.
Apple has been rumored to be working on a smart home display of some kind for a long time . The company originally planned to launch one in 2024 with an AI-powered upgrade to Siri, but had to change plans after it delayed Siri’s upgrade, Bloomberg reported . Apple finally launched its Siri AI overhaul alongside its OS updates last month .

title: Bandits kill Immigration official, burn corpse
body: The Nigeria Immigration Service (NIS), Niger Command, has confirmed the death of an officer attacked by bandits during a surveillance operation in Niger. ​‌⁠‌‍⁠⁠‍​‍​⁠‌​‌‌‌​ The Command’s Public Relations Officer, DSI Mukhtar Abubakar, confirmed the incident in a statement issued in Minna, the state capital, on Monday. Abubakar said Assistant Superintendent of Immigration I (ASI I), Ibrahim Babagiwa, and an inspector were attacked in Woko village, Tungan Waya axis. He said the incident occurred on October 6 when the officers embarked on a surveillance operation along the Tungan Waya-Woko axis. During the attack, Babagiwa was killed, while the inspector sustained machete injuries but managed to escape, the statement said. Abubakar added that the inspector was currently stable and responding to treatment. He said Babagiwa’s remains were discovered burnt two days after the attack, and he had since been buried according to Islamic rites. He reiterated the command’s commitment to combating irregular migration and addressing other security challenges along Nigeria’s international border. The spokesperson also reaffirmed the command’s resolve to discharge its statutory responsibilities in spite of the prevailing security challenges. (NAN)

title: Pope Leo diagnosed with lung cancer, Vatican says
body:
The pope had the lower lobe of his right lung removed during surgery Tuesday.
Pope Leo XIV has been diagnosed with lung cancer and underwent surgery to have the lower lobe of his right lung removed, the Vatican said on Tuesday.
In a release from the Holy See Press Office, Dr. Luigi Carbone and Prof. Stefano Margaritora explained that the pontiff underwent a minimally invasive camera-guided surgical procedure.
"The intraoperative histological examination confirmed the diagnosis of lung adenocarcinoma, as suspected by the preoperative tests," the press release read.
"The Holy Father was in the operating room for about three hours; the surgery itself lasted approximately 90 minutes. The surgery was successful, and there were no complications," the release continued.
During an intraoperative evaluation, a pathologist rapidly freezes, slices and analyzes a tissue sample while the patient is still on the operating table to provide the surgical team with immediate feedback.
The release said the Pope woke up "as expected" and returned to his room on the 10th floor.
Earlier on Tuesday, the Vatican said the procedure was "successfully completed."
"The procedure was successfully completed, on schedule and as planned, and the Holy Father has returned to his room," the Vatican press office said in a statement.
The pontiff departed the Vatican on Tuesday for Agostino Gemelli University Hospital in Rome.
"As announced, Pope Leo XIV has been admitted to the Agostino Gemelli University Hospital," the Vatican press office said in a statement at the time. "This afternoon, he will undergo surgery for a lung nodule performed by the thoracic surgery team led by Professor Stefano Margaritora."
Video posted by Vatican News on Tuesday featured Pope Leo arriving at the hospital, shaking hands and greeting staff.
The Rosary prayer was recited in the hospital chapel Tuesday evening, attended by Cardinal Baldassare Reina, the Vicar General for the Diocese of Rome.
"Together, let us raise our prayer that the Lord may sustain our bishop, Pope Leo, and bring comfort to all those who are hospitalized here," Reina said. "May Mary, Health of the Sick and Mother of the Church, accompany our prayer and teach us to remain steadfast in love."
His recovery at the hospital in Rome was expected to last about a week, the Vatican said on Sunday
"The doctors think it is opportune to intervene," Pope Leo, 71, said at the time.
A lung nodule, also known as a pulmonary nodule, is a small mass of dense tissue on the lung, according to the American Lung Association (ALA). Leo on Sunday said the nodule was discovered by doctors in "a very initial phase" and that it was "well localized."
Nodules can be caused by a variety of factors including scar tissue, lung irritants, inflammatory conditions, current or past infections, or cancer. Most nodules are benign, according to the ALA. They are diagnosed with imaging tests including an X-ray or a CT scan.
Depending on the size, appearance, growth and cause of nodules, they can be either be monitored regularly by a physician or treated with medication or surgery.
Lung adenocarcinoma is the most common subtype of non-small cell lung cancer, accounting for roughly 40% of all lung cancer cases, according to the National Cancer Institute.
Adenocarcinoma is found on the outer part of the lungs. It is more likely than other lung cancers to be found before it has spread because it grows more slowly, the LCFA said.
Cardinal Pietro Parolin, the Vatican's secretary of State, said that as he listened to Leo's announcement on Sunday, he was "struck by his serenity," according to Vatican media.
"We are confident," he reportedly said. "And of course we all accompany him with our prayers and our affection."
Gemelli Hospital, which is formally the Policlinico Universitario Fondazione Agostino Gemelli, is the largest hospital in Rome.
It's the primary medical facility commonly used by popes, including Leo's immediate predecessor , Pope Francis, who died in 2025 at the age of 88.
Leo, a Chicago native and the first American pope, who was previously Cardinal Robert Prevost, was elected the church's 267th pontiff in May 2025.

title: More than 220K cast advance votes in 2026 Toronto election, city says
body:
More than 220,000 people cast ballots during advance voting in the upcoming Toronto municipal election – a new record.
The City of Toronto said Tuesday that 222,550 eligible voters went to the polls during the six days of advance voting, which began on Oct. 6 and ended on Oct. 11.
The city said 36,743 voters cast ballots on Oct. 6, 31,018 voters did on Oct. 7 and 28,666 voters turned out on Oct. 8.
On Oct. 9, 33,579 voters headed to the polls, and 39,181 voters followed suit on Oct. 10. Oct. 11 saw the highest turnout of all the advance voting days with 53,363 voters casting ballots.
The advance turnout for the 2026 election surpasses figures seen in previous advanced votes.
The city said 129,745 advance votes were cast in the 2023 mayoral by-election, compared to 115,911 advanced votes in the 2022 election, 124,299 advanced votes in the 2018 election, 161,147 advanced votes in 2014 and 77,365 advance votes in 2010.
The next time Torontonians can vote is between 10 a.m. and 8 p.m. on Oct. 26 – election day.

Getty Images intends to file for bankruptcy and go private as part of a restructuring agreement after its plans to merge with rival stock platform Shutterstock fell through earlier this year. On Monday, Getty announced it had secured $533 million from the Getty family and Charles Koch’s investment firm to cut its debt and take the company private, outlining plans to undergo a prepackaged Chapter 11 process “in the coming weeks.”
The restructuring effort is expected to be wrapped up by the end of this year, with no anticipated impact on content contributors, partners, customers, or employees globally. Once completed, the company will be entirely owned by Getty family affiliates ⁠and Koch Equity Development. The agreement serves to rescue the financially struggling platform, which had more than $1.3 billion of debt as of June 30th according to regulatory filings. Bloomberg reported in September that Getty had entered a 30-day grace period for operations after failing to make interest payments on its unsecured notes.
This follows Getty walking away from a $3.7 billion transaction with Shutterstock in July in response to restrictions imposed on the merger by a UK regulator. This upended a decision granted by the US Department of Justice in February, which gave the agreement “ unconditional antitrust clearance .” Both Getty and Shutterstock face ongoing pressure from generative AI services that enable users to quickly generate custom images instead of locating stock and paying licensing fees. Getty has its own AI generator , but competition is fierce and the company hasn’t clearly laid out how it’ll “support its future growth.”
“Getty Images is uniquely trusted around the world as the unparalleled leader in premium visual content,” said Getty co-founder Mark Getty. “This transformational transaction is underpinned by the strength of the business and the significant growth potential we see ahead.”

title: Insecurity ‌‌forces Kaduna residents from homes, triggers rent hikes
body:
Repeated kidnappings and attacks in communities on the outskirts of Kaduna metropolis are forcing residents to abandon their homes for rented apartments in the city.
The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the development is driving up rents and threatening the investments of low-income homeowners.
From Baban Saura to Danhon II in Millennium City at the outskirts of Kaduna, residents who spent years building their houses are increasingly choosing to relocate rather than risk abduction and ransom demands.
“I rented a self-contained apartment for N600,000, and many people say I got it cheap because houses are now very expensive in the city,” said Yakubu Dahiru, who abandoned his home in Danhon II community to Malali following attacks in his community.
“The insecurity is no longer in the villages; the bandits are coming closer to us, and it is better to leave than to be abducted and then forced to sell the house to pay ransom,” he said.
Mr Dahiru said he had not returned home since the attack on his community last year and had been unable to find anyone willing to rent or guard the property because of fear.
The NAN reports that residents in new layouts across Kaduna North, Kaduna South, Chikun and Igabi Local Government Areas are increasingly abandoning their properties to move to areas they consider safer locations within the metropolis.
For more than a decade, such layouts provided affordable homeownership opportunities for lower-income earners who purchased plots and gradually developed their houses.
The opening of the Eastern Bypass in Kaduna encouraged the growth of these settlements, according to an estate surveyor.
Umar Mohammed, a Kaduna-based estate surveyor, said market women and people engaged in menial jobs had invested in the layouts because land was relatively affordable.
However, insecurity is now forcing some homeowners to sell their properties at unfavourable prices or leave them unoccupied.
Saidu Hamza, a resident of Danhono II, said he relocated his family to Ilorin in Kwara after an attack on his community and had put his three-bedroom house with an adjoining two-bedroom apartment up for sale.
“With the security situation in the area, the price I am being offered is not very encouraging, and I could not leave my family there knowing the place is unsafe,” he said.
The displacement has also increased demand for accommodation in Kaduna metropolis, with estate agents reporting substantial rent increases.
Maiunguwa Ibrahim, an estate agent operating around Kurmin Mashi, Gwamna Road and Badiko, told NAN that rents for some three-bedroom apartments along Gwamna Road had risen from between N1.2 million and N1.5 million to between N3 million and N3.5 million.
Mr Mohammed attributed the increase to a shortage of available apartments amid the influx of residents fleeing insecure communities.
The situation compounds Nigeria’s housing challenge, with the World Bank’s Nigeria Affordable Housing Project 2018 estimating a national housing deficit of 17 million units and an annual requirement of about 700,000 housing units over 20 years.
Security sources told NAN that the scattered nature of houses in new layouts, inadequate fencing, limited security posts and proximity to forested areas made some communities vulnerable to attacks.
The concerns have been reinforced by recurring abductions in Millennium City and neighbouring areas, including the kidnapping of two journalists two years ago.
More recently, gunmen reportedly killed a man identified as Sikiru in Baban Saura community and abducted his wife, Hafsat, their 14-year-old son, Abdulsalam, and six other persons.
Hafsat and her son are still in captivity, according to a family member.
In Millennium City, a couple and their six-month-old daughter were abducted from Alrahus Estate on 6 October.
The husband, Ahmed Zakka, appealed for help in a viral video, saying the kidnappers demanded a N300 million ransom.
Amnesty International Nigeria has also warned that residents of Millennium City face persistent threats from armed men, with some families abandoning their homes and others suspending their children’s education.
Meanwhile, the Kaduna State Police Command on Monday said it had arrested 12 suspects, including eight suspected kidnappers and four alleged informants, during operations in Millennium City and Maraban Rido.
The command said the Kaduna State Government had released three additional armoured personnel carriers to strengthen security operations in the affected areas.
Abdullahi Umar, a security commentator, urged the government to support neighbourhood watch initiatives and strengthen collaboration between security agencies, traditional rulers and community leaders.
He said community vigilance could complement security operations, particularly in settlements where the number of deployed personnel was insufficient for the size of the area.
The growing displacement highlights how insecurity is extending beyond physical attacks to affect housing affordability, household investments and livelihoods, leaving residents paying rising rents while their own homes remain abandoned.

title: 80–90% of gold purchased and exported is now refined in Ghana– Sammy Gyamfi
body: The Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod), Sammy Gyamfi, says between 80 and 90 percent of the gold purchased and exported by the institution is now refined locally before shipment. He said the development was helping Ghana retain more economic value through job creation, refining fees and the use of silver, a by-product of gold refining, to support the country’s fabrication industry. Speaking before the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) on Tuesday, October 13, Mr Gyamfi said GoldBod was on course to meet and potentially exceed its 2025 gold purchase and export targets, while substantially surpassing its foreign exchange generation performance for the year. He said increased local refining was changing Ghana’s approach to adding value to its mineral resources, noting that refining gold locally before export was not the norm before the establishment of GoldBod. “I’m happy to report to this Honourable Committee that, as we speak, about 80 to 90 per cent of the gold we purchase and export is refined here locally,” he said. Mr Gyamfi said the shift was creating employment opportunities for young people, as local refineries operated around the clock to process gold. “That means jobs for the teeming unemployed youth, because these refineries are operating 24/7, employing Ghanaians,” he said. He added that local refining was helping to retain money within the Ghanaian economy, as fees that would otherwise have gone to overseas refining destinations were now being paid to domestic operators. The development, he said, was helping Ghana benefit beyond the extraction and export of raw gold by retaining more of the economic value generated along the gold supply chain. Silver by-products support local industry Mr Gyamfi also highlighted the benefits of retaining silver, a by-product of gold refining, within the country. He said the silver recovered during the refining process was being sold to generate foreign exchange and used to support Ghana’s fabrication industry. According to him, the approach was helping the country derive additional value from its mineral resources while supporting related industrial activities. By refining more gold locally, Ghana can retain the fees associated with processing the metal and benefit from the by-products, rather than allowing those economic opportunities to accrue to foreign markets. Mr Gyamfi described the developments as progress towards strengthening local participation in the gold value chain. “So, so far, much better,” he told the committee.

title: Bulgaria Summons Russian Ambassador After Drone Attack Sinks Ship, Leaving 11 Missing
body:
Eleven sailors were missing at sea on Tuesday from a ship sunk by a drone attack off the coast of Bulgaria, possibly the second deadly sinking of a cargo vessel in the area in a week, prompting Bulgaria to summon Russia's ambassador.
Two cargo ships were hit by drones overnight and one was sunk, Bulgarian officials said. Bulgaria stopped short of explicitly accusing Russia of carrying out the attacks but Prime Minister Rumen Radev said their outcome "benefits the Russian Federation."
There was no immediate comment from Moscow on the incidents.
"This is absolutely unacceptable — another attack in the immediate vicinity of Bulgarian territorial waters," Radev said in a televised address.
The attacks were also condemned by Ukraine and the EU.
"The Black Sea has become another front of escalation of the Russian war in Ukraine," European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said on X. "Those responsible should be held accountable."
Ukraine's Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said on X on Tuesday that the strike "once again demonstrates Moscow's deliberate disregard for civilian lives."
"The Black Sea is a lifeline for global food security. Russia is attacking it to weaponize hunger and hold the world hostage," he said.
Speaking with von der Leyen and NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte by telephone on Tuesday, Radev urged their support to bolster his country's maritime and airspace surveillance, the Bulgarian government said in a statement.
NATO will continue to adjust its military presence on its eastern flank "as needed," Rutte said.
Bulgarian officials said five crew members had been rescued but 11 were still listed as missing from the ship which sank off the coast of the village of Krapets. President Iliana Iotova identified the vessel as the Guinea-Bissau-flagged cargo ship HS Dignity and said a search and rescue operation was ongoing.
Another ship, the Chelsea 3 sailing under a Maltese flag, was also hit by three drones overnight, Bulgarian officials said. All crew from that ship — seven Ukrainians and eight Azerbaijanis — were rescued and none seriously injured.
A week ago nine Syrian sailors and one Egyptian were lost at sea from a ship that sank when hit by drones in Bulgaria's Black Sea exclusive economic zone. Another ship was also hit that night but the crew was rescued.
After meeting Radev in Sofia, Russian Ambassador Eleonora Mitrofanova said she had no information from the Russian Defense Ministry about attacks on commercial vessels in the Black Sea but did not rule out they could be a provocation by a third party, the Bulgarian government said.
More than four and a half years into the war that Moscow launched with its full-scale invasion in 2022, Black Sea shipping has increasingly been drawn into a prolonged battle of economic endurance.
Ukraine and Russia are both among the world's largest exporters of grain.
Russia has been bombing Ukraine's Black Sea ports, forcing Ukraine to rely increasingly on river ports on the Danube and shipping routes close to the coasts of NATO members Bulgaria and Romania.
Ukraine, for its part, has increasingly targeted Russian grain-exporting ships in other parts of the Black Sea and the Azov Sea at the mouth of the Don River.

title: Gov Oyebanji Sacks Directors-General, Technical Advisors Ahead Of Second-Term Inauguration
body: Ahead of the second term inauguration, the Governor of Ekiti State, Biodun Oyebanji, has removed all Technical Advisors and Directors-General (DGs) of government agencies with immediate effect. The affected officials are to submit their handover notes to the Office of the Secretary to the State Government. This was contained in a statement signed and made available to journalists by his Special Adviser on Media, Yinka Oyebode. The statement continues, “The disengagement, which came barely 24 hours after the dissolution of the State Executive Council, marks the completion of the disengagement process for political appointees serving in the administration, except for a few whose appointments have been retained in view of the nature of their assignments. “Governor Oyebanji expressed appreciation to the affected DGs and TAs for their support, commitment and contributions to the administration as well as the development of Ekiti State. “He wished them success in their future endeavours”. The post Gov Oyebanji Sacks Directors-General, Technical Advisors Ahead Of Second-Term Inauguration appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Man City: Maresca questions critics of Anfield celebrations after 3-0 win
body: By Adegboyega Adeleye Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca has questioned criticism of his players’ celebrations after their 3-0 victory over Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday, insisting the team had every reason to celebrate the result. According to the BBC, Maresca defended the celebrations at a news conference on Tuesday ahead of Manchester City’s Champions League clash against Paris Saint-Germain, following criticism directed at the club after its guilty verdict over breaches of Premier League financial rules. “We won 3-0 at Anfield; what do you want us to do?” Maresca said. “Even if it was 1-0, it would be exactly the same. We work every day to win games. It’s the only thing that we can think of. The rest is just things from outside that we need to deal with.” City’s victory over Liverpool was their first match since the verdict, which the club has appealed. The celebrations at the final whistle attracted criticism amid the continuing scrutiny of the club’s financial case. Captain Rúben Dias also defended the players’ reaction, saying they should be free to express their emotions after matches. “I very much stand by the manager’s words,” Dias said. “I think we will enjoy it just as much and celebrate however it feels in the moment. It will be a show of how much it means to us.” Dias added that the players remained calm and trusted the club despite the ongoing legal process. Maresca said the situation had been more difficult for Manchester City supporters than for the players and staff, acknowledging the criticism the club’s fans had faced from rival supporters. “Probably it has been more tough for our fans than for the players or for me because it’s more complicated,” he said. “If I am an Arsenal fan or United fan and you are a City fan I say ‘hey, my friend you cheat.’ So it is probably more tough for them, but we were happy inside the changing room. We were very happy celebrating the three points because it is very difficult at Anfield.” Manchester City are preparing to host reigning European champions Paris Saint-Germain at the Etihad Stadium, with Maresca describing the fixture as a major test for his side. “We need the perfect performance because they are the best team in Europe,” he said. “They have won the past two Champions Leagues. We need the perfect game but, doing our best, I think we can beat them and be happy at the end.” The post Man City: Maresca questions critics of Anfield celebrations after 3-0 win appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Senate probes Ondo aircraft crash
body: …Asks Air Force leadership to provide budgetary provisions for the maintenance of the aircraft By Henry Umoru, Abuja The Senate has begun a probe into the penultimate Monday tragic crash of a Nigerian Air Force (NAF) aircraft in the Igbokoda area of Ilaje Local Government Area, Ondo State, which resulted in the loss of military personnel and other passengers on board. Consequently, the Senate has mandated its Committees on Air Force and that of Aviation to, as a matter of urgency, carry out an oversight visit to the crash site, interface with the Nigerian Air Force NAF authorities, and conduct a holistic audit of the serviceability and airworthiness of aircraft in the presidential and military fleet. Resolutions of the Senate on Tuesday were a sequel to a motion on the tragic crash of Nigerian Airforce Aircraft in Igbokoda, Ondo State, resulting in the loss of 32 lives, sponsored by Senator Osita Ngwu, APC, Enugu West. The upper chamber also urged the Nigerian Air Force and the Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau (NSIB) to conduct a thorough, transparent and comprehensive investigation into the immediate and remote causes of the crash and make its findings public. The Senate then directed the leadership of the Nigerian Air Force to make available to it through the relevant Senate committee the budgetary provisions for the maintenance of the aircraft and to establish the amount provided and whether it was sufficient to prevent the incident, as such provisions were made. It also unanimously adopted the additional prayer by Senator Adams Oshiomhole, APC, Edo, and seconded by Senator Titus Zam, APC, Benue North-West. The Upper Chamber has also urged the Federal Government to prioritise funding for regular maintenance and replacement of ageing military aircraft to safeguard lives of the country’s gallant personnel. The Senate observed a one-minute silence in honour of the passengers and crew members who lost their lives in the ill-fated aircraft. The Upper Chamber condoled with the President and Commander-in-Chief, the Chief of Air Staff, the Nigerian Air Force, the Government and the families of the victims of this national tragedy. Earlier in his presentation of the motion, Senator Ngwu said that “the Senate notes that on Monday, 5th October 2026, a Nigerian Air Force ATR-42 aircraft with tail number NGR 931, carrying 25 passengers and 7 crew members, crashed close to the Naval Base in Igbokoda, headquarters of Ilaje Local Government Area of Ondo State, while on a routine mission from Benin City to Lagos; “Further notes that this crash, involving military personnel and some civilian passengers, is one of the deadliest military aviation accidents in Nigeria in recent years and has intensified scrutiny of flight safety and operational readiness; “Aware that the air traffic controllers lost contact with the aircraft at about 0813 GMT (that is 9:13 am, local time) and all efforts to reach it on radio proved abortive before the wreckage was located following an immediate search and rescue operation by the Nigerian Airforce in collaboration with other relevant authorities; “Recognise that the Nigerian Air Force plays a crucial role in national defence and intelligence; therefore, operational readiness, serviceability and airworthiness of its aircraft are of strategic importance; “Worried that recurring military air crashes have claimed the lives of gallant officers, raising serious concerns about maintenance culture, ageing fleet, operational safety protocols and airworthiness of military aircraft; “Concerned that without a transparent, thorough and independent investigation, lessons will not be learnt to prevent future occurrences.” The post Senate probes Ondo aircraft crash appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Rodrigo Duterte appears again at ICC hearing ahead of November 30 trial
body: MANILA, Philippines – Former Philippine president Rodrigo Duterte made another appearance before the International Criminal Court (ICC) ahead of his full-blown trial slated to start on November 30. Duterte, who’s facing three counts of crimes against humanity over his war on drugs, attended the Trial Chamber III’s fourth status conference on his case on Tuesday, October 13. This is the second time that the former president has personally appeared before the court since his arrest in March 2025. On September 16, Duterte attended the chamber’s third status conference , marking his first personal appearance before the court. Play Video A status conference is held by the chamber to allow parties to discuss matters related to the case before proceeding to a full trial. This is done to iron out details such as the schedule and the list of witnesses and evidence, among others. During Tuesday’s hearing, Presiding Judge Joanna Korner disclosed the schedule of Duterte’s trial: 10 am to 11 am 11:30 am to 12:30 pm Lunch break: 12:30 pm to 1:30 pm 1:30 pm to 2:30 pm 3 pm to 4 pm Apart from lunch, there are 30-minute breaks between sessions, given the experts’ recommendation of no sitting for more than an hour for Duterte due to his age and condition. Recently, the Trial Chamber III ruled that Duterte is fit to stand trial. Citing experts’ analysis, Duterte was unanimously found have the capacity to understand: instructing counsel in preparing and conducting the defense the charges the purpose and consequences of the proceedings following the course of the proceedings, including the nature and implications of entering a plea the evidence Must Read Rodrigo Duterte fit for trial, says ICC Discussion on evidence Once again, the prosecution’s volume of evidence was brought up during the hearing, specifically by Presiding Judge Korner. Trial prosecutor Julian Nicholls explained that they had restructured their list based on the most important ones, including the “non-negotiables.” Korner flagged the inclusion of newspaper clippings — called by the court as secondary sources — in the prosecution’s 5,000 documents. Nicholls explained that they included them because the clippings will provide context and corroborate the allegation of killings committed during Duterte’s mayoral reign in Davao City. Defense lawyer Peter Haynes again complained about the prosecution’s “over 18,000” datasets, saying the material had been “literally dumped” on them. Later, Korner inquired why the defense did not take up the prosecution’s offer to review the documents and spreadsheet. At one point, the prosecution and defense also entered into an argument after the defense accused the prosecution of using artificial intelligence (AI) in reviewing the evidence. “But the dataset, yeah, Mr. Nicholls, I think, is saying they haven’t been read by a lawyer, and certainly I haven’t read them. You will have noticed from the filings and with the artificiality that we have to deal with this by not naming anybody, there have been three institutions that have had those documents,” said Haynes. “One of them is an institution that is very resourceful in terms of both human resources and money, and it took a team of people from that institution one year to review the dataset. That’s how big it is. And they did it humanly. The prosecution [hasn’t] done it humanly. They’ve effectively passed it through an AI machine,” Haynes added. “I have to object. That is completely untrue. He keeps saying that. We have gone through this dataset by analysts. We’ve gone through all of it, lawyers some of it, page by page, human, manual, 100%. Keep saying that. It’s not true,” Nicholls said in response. Play Video The defense also had a motion, requesting that the prosecution’s evidence be refiled and a 10,000-document limit be imposed. Presiding Judge Korner ruled that the motion was “at the moment refused,” explaining that an arbitrary limit could cause the prosecution to violate disclosure obligations. Disclosure of evidence is done in the proceedings to allow the legal counsel of the accused to prepare a proper defense. Nicholls explained during the trial that the prosecution can stipulate or agree to the fact that the drug war deaths were around 3,400. He said that this was actually lower than the number of deaths reported by the Duterte administration itself. There were 7,884 alleged drug suspects killed, as of August 31, 2020, based on the Philippine National Police’s count. However, several human rights groups said there could be around 27,000 to 30,000 victims if vigilante killings were to be included. Haynes argued with Nicholls about the number, saying that the figure was not all drug-related. However, the prosecution insisted that deaths were all related to Duterte’s drug war. – Rappler.com

title: Dichemso M/A teachers go house-to-house to get absent pupils back to class after strike suspension
body: Teachers at Dichemso M/A School in Kumasi have begun visiting the homes of absent pupils to encourage parents to send their children back to school following the suspension of the teachers’ strike. Despite the resumption of classes, pupil attendance remained low on the first day, leaving some classrooms partially empty and raising concerns about the loss of instructional hours. Teachers boycotted the classroom for two weeks, demanding better service conditions. But they now face a different battle after returning to work. In an interview with JoyNews , the Headmistress of Dichemso M/A School, Helena Amponsah, said teachers had made efforts to contact absent pupils, with some responding to the calls while others had yet to return. “In fact, we even went and also sent some of the students to go and call them, and some reported while others did not. We presume that they have not gotten the news or heard the news. So we hope that from tomorrow going they may come to school,” she said. According to the headmistress, all teachers had reported for duty, adding that the school had resumed lessons and organised morning classes to help pupils return to their academic routine. To address the lost contact hours, she said the school plans to introduce additional lessons and extend teaching hours to cover topics missed during the strike. “We are going to definitely make up to them by doing extra classes, morning classes, afternoon classes, and night classes, to make up to them for all the lost lessons and topics,” she said.

title: Israel must set red lines on Turkish presence in Syria to avoid confrontation, think tank argues
body: Israel needs to draw more limited red lines on Turkish activities in Syria instead of the more aggressive approach it has taken since the old Syrian Assad regime fell in December 2024, the Institute for National Security Studies think tank argued.On August 17, Israel struck an emerging Turkish position at the Abu al-Duhur base in Syria, leading to a high-profile diplomatic conflict with Israel on one side and the US, Turkey, and Syria on the other.Last Friday, the IDF targeted a vehicle near the Lebanese-Syrian border carrying Yusuf Ali al-Hassoun, who may be associated with Iran's terrorist handlers.Since early 2025, INSS has repeatedly warned that an indefinite stay in Syria was not the answer. It stressed that Israel needs to engage in dialogue with Syria about long-term security arrangements, or it stands to lose many of its gains since the fall of Assad.The IDF destroyed most of the former regime's high-profile sea, land, and air military threats. In a similar vein, the military set up a buffer zone in southern Syria to make it harder for potential terrorists or jihadists to initiate an invasion.INSS's most recent report was authored by researcher Amal Hayek and former IDF intelligence adviser Carmit Valensi. It recommended that Israel take a more nuanced approach in Syria, and it split the “restoration of Syrian infrastructure and the establishment of a Turkish presence” into multiple components.“A distinction should be made between technical assistance, training, and the rehabilitation of facilities for the Syrian state on the one hand – and the establishment of independent Turkish command-and-control infrastructure, on the other,” the think tank noted.Valensi confirmed that the findings of the report still held following recent events in Syria. “From an operational standpoint, there is little practical difference between the deployment of Turkish radar, electronic warfare, or air defense systems in northern Syria and their deployment in southern Turkey or northern Cyprus,” he said.“Their coverage ranges are similar, and the presence of such systems in northern Syria, therefore, does not in itself constitute a redline warranting the use of Israeli force,” the report noted.'Turkish navy has inherent advantage in eastern Mediterranean,' INSS arguesAccording to INSS, these same principles of nuance apply to the maritime domain. “The Turkish navy enjoys an inherent advantage in the eastern Mediterranean, and a limited presence along the Syrian coast would not fundamentally alter the balance of power,” the report read.INSS's position clashes with the navy's. The navy wants to be more aggressive in confronting Turkish naval expansion in the Mediterranean, and it seeks to expand Israel's submarine fleet from six (with the recently incorporated INS Drakon) to eight.INSS's recommendations are partly due to its assessment that, even if Turkey assisted Syrian leader Ahmad al-Sharaa, “the relationship between Ankara and Damascus is more complex than is sometimes perceived in Israel and is not free of tension.”INSS wrote that “evidence of this can be found in a series of structural changes recently implemented by Damascus in the ranks of the Syrian army, indicating an intention to reduce the autonomy of these forces and the extent of Turkish influence over them.”For example, “as of August 2026, the Turkish military presence in Syria is undergoing a process of reorganization. Ankara is gradually downsizing some of the smaller outposts and facilities it established during the years of war – particularly in areas where the security situation has changed – and transferring authority and responsibility to Syrian state institutions.”Israeli security officials have said that these are cosmetic changes designed to fool the West. However, some Mossad officials have expressed willingness to test whether Syria's new regime may choose stability over conflict with Israel.Notably, INSS warned that Israel's national security could be harmed if the state is seen as reluctant to give Syria a chance. With that said, INSS still believes that Israel must draw red lines when necessary.INSS wrote that central and southern Syria are critical areas and that “while Turkey justifies its presence in northern Syria as necessary to prevent threats to its territory, the establishment of Turkish bases farther inside the country – in central Syria, and even more so in the south – is not dictated by such security needs.”Furthermore, the INSS report said that such a Turkish presence “would also bring potential friction closer to the Israeli front and constitute a problematic shift in the regional balance.”Israel should focus on thwarting terror elements in Syria, INSS saysIn addition, the report said that Israel must avoid the “entrenchment of terror proxies in southern Syria. Israel should focus on thwarting terrorist elements – particularly Hamas – and preventing them from enjoying freedom of action or safe haven under Turkish or Syrian auspices in the southern region adjacent to Israel's border.”In other words, INSS is less tolerant of jihadist elements – particularly Hamas – getting anywhere close to Israel's border in southern Syria than it is of Turkey increasing its presence in northern Syria.It added, “Turkey's presence and influence in Syria are an established reality that is unlikely to disappear through the use of military force alone.” In that sense, “Israel's challenge is not to eliminate Turkish involvement altogether but rather to contain and balance it.”Moreover, “relying exclusively on military force and striking targets of marginal operational value, without a parallel diplomatic track with Damascus, jeopardizes Israel's security interests and could drag the parties into a direct confrontation that neither side desires.”Therefore, “Israeli decision-makers must combine focused military deterrence with direct and indirect dialogue, utilize deconfliction mechanisms, and clearly define the areas in which Israel is prepared to allow Syria to rebuild its capabilities – before the situation deteriorates into dangerous regional escalation.”INSS said that “blanket Israeli opposition to any process of Syrian military rehabilitation could prove counterproductive, pushing Damascus toward greater dependence on Ankara.”Moreover, “the broader regional and diplomatic context should be taken into account. Damascus is currently drawing closer to Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates, and gaining growing legitimacy from the United States and European countries.”In early 2025, Valensi and other security officials suggested that Israel formulate a list of conditions (such as demilitarized zones in Syria) that could lead to it withdrawing from some or all of the buffer zone.When the IDF first took over the buffer zone in Syria, IDF officials told The Jerusalem Post that the military's presence was temporary and would end once it was clear that Syria's new leadership had no intention of invading Israel.Despite Sharaa's background as a jihadist, he has given no hint of action against Israel for nearly two years.INSS reported, “Israel's actions are increasingly perceived as seeking to destabilize Syria, and in this context, Israel is, at times, even compared to Iran. In this framework, greater attention may be directed toward the issue of the Golan Heights, as recently raised by [US Special Envoy for Syria Tom] Barrack, while regional – and particularly international – pressure could intensify for Israel to withdraw to the lines established under the 1974 Separation of Forces Agreement, possibly even without significant political concessions in return.”INSS's conclusion should raise some alarm bells. Israel maintains its buffer zone in Syria for its own safety and, if needed, to gain security concessions from Damascus.However, Israel has made no concession offers to Syria for two years now. This could lead the Trump administration, which supports Sharaa, to force a withdrawal, resulting in few gains for Israel.

title: Rada proposed to legalize veterans' right to wear military uniform after discharge without special permits
body:
Members of Parliament propose that the Verkhovna Rada of Ukraine grant veterans the right to wear military uniforms after discharge from service without separate permits or additional approvals.
According to draft law No. 16130 dated October 7, the right will arise from the day of discharge from military service or, if the relevant status is granted later, from the day it is granted, taking into account the transitional provisions of the law.
Persons who already hold the relevant status on the day the law enters into force and have been discharged from military service will acquire this right automatically on the day it enters into force.
Information regarding this right is expected to be displayed in the veteran's electronic ID, including in the Diia application.
The Ministry of Veterans Affairs noted that male and female veterans will be able to wear the uniform of the military formation or state body where they served, or, if it no longer exists, the uniform of its successor.
At the same time, certain restrictions are provided: military uniforms and insignia cannot be used to impersonate an active-duty service member or to create a false impression of one's position or official authority.
"The fundamental approach of the draft law is to give veterans the opportunity to wear military uniforms without unnecessary bureaucracy while simultaneously preventing its use for deception," the ministry added.
The document was developed by a group of MPs with the participation of experts from the Ministry of Veterans Affairs.

title: Meet Dr Hazel and Nhyira: Mother and daughter called to the Ghana Bar
body: It was a double celebration for Dr Hazel P. Berrard Amuah and her daughter, Adwuwa Fynna Nhyira Berrard Quayson, as the two joined Ghana’s legal profession on the same day, marking a remarkable milestone in their family’s history. The mother and daughter were among the newly qualified lawyers called to the Ghana Bar on Friday, October 9, becoming Barristers and Solicitors of the Supreme Court of Ghana. Their shared achievement has attracted admiration, particularly as Dr Hazel adds the legal profession to an already extensive career in corporate leadership, human resource management, insurance and business consultancy. For Dr Hazel, the call to the Bar represents another chapter in a professional journey spanning more than 28 years, during which she has held senior executive positions and received several local and international recognitions. She previously served as the first female Chief Executive Officer of Prudential Life Insurance Ghana, a position she held until April 2024. An accomplished business leader and international public speaker, Dr Hazel has worked across 22 countries in West and Central Africa, building expertise in human resource management, organisational development, business strategy and leadership. Her professional accomplishments have earned her numerous honours, including Ghana Woman Professional of the Year in 2018, HR Practitioner of the Year in 2019, Africa HR Personality of the Year in 2020 and the Global Leadership Award in 2021. She has also received recognition for business leadership, corporate social responsibility and her contributions to human capital development. Beyond her corporate achievements, Dr Hazel has an extensive academic and professional background. She holds advanced degrees in business administration, master’s degrees in Bilingual Translation and Organisational Development, and professional qualifications in insurance and executive coaching. She is a chartered insurer, a member of the Chartered Insurance Institute in the United Kingdom and a Henley-certified coach. Her academic and professional interests have also taken her into teaching, having served as visiting faculty at the China Europe International Business School Africa and as an adjunct lecturer at the University of Ghana Business School. Dr Hazel is also an author whose publications include Winning in the Jungle , People Factory , Dolphins Don’t Swim in Lakes , Where Power Lies , Global Passport and 50 Lessons and Blessings . She has additionally contributed to academic publications addressing leadership, performance management and business strategy in developing economies. Outside her professional commitments, she founded People Factory Limited in 2009, a consultancy specialising in leadership, business strategy and human capital development. That same year, she established the Reach Out and Share Foundation, a non-governmental organisation dedicated to supporting less privileged and underserved communities. Her daughter, Nhyira Berrard Quayson, now begins her own journey in the legal profession, sharing with her mother the distinction of having been called to the Bar at the same ceremony. While both have reached the same professional milestone, their admission to the Bar also represents the beginning of separate careers in a profession that demands dedication, integrity and a commitment to justice. For Dr Hazel, who has spent decades building a career across several disciplines, the achievement reinforces the value of continuous learning and the pursuit of new professional opportunities. Their story is also a reminder that education and professional ambition need not be confined to a particular stage of life. What makes the occasion particularly memorable is that mother and daughter can now celebrate not only their individual achievements but also a professional qualification they have attained together. As the two embark on this new chapter, their shared accomplishment stands as an inspiring example of determination, lifelong learning and the special bond between a mother and her daughter.

title: US lists Nigeria among 14 countries facing military aid cuts
body: The United States has listed Nigeria among 14 countries facing potential cuts to military assistance over the recruitment and use of child soldiers, a designation that could affect defence cooperation, military training and weapons sales. The designation was contained in the US State Department’s 2026 Trafficking in Persons (TIP) Report, published on October 11, which identified Boko Haram and the Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) as armed groups continuing to recruit, abduct and use children in Nigeria. The report covers the period from April 1, 2025, to March 31, 2026, and places Nigeria on the Child Soldiers Prevention Act (CSPA) list alongside Afghanistan, Burma, the Central African Republic, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Ethiopia, Iran, Russia, Rwanda, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, Venezuela and Yemen. Under the CSPA, countries on the list may face restrictions on certain forms of US security assistance and the commercial licensing of military equipment, subject to applicable exceptions, a presidential waiver or other provisions under the law. The report stated that the restrictions would take effect from October 1, 2026, and apply throughout the relevant fiscal year unless an exemption or waiver was granted. “The CSPA prohibits assistance to governments that are identified in the list under the following authorities: International Military Education and Training, Foreign Military Financing, Excess Defence Articles, and Peacekeeping Operations, with exceptions for some programs undertaken pursuant to the Peacekeeping Operations authority. “The CSPA also prohibits the issuance of licenses for direct commercial sales of military equipment to such governments,” the report stated. The designation comes amid continued security cooperation between Washington and Abuja, including joint efforts to combat terrorism and other security threats in Nigeria. According to the report, Boko Haram and ISWAP continue to recruit, abduct and use children as young as 12 in various roles, including as cooks, domestic workers, spies, porters, messengers, bodyguards, checkpoint guards, armed combatants and suicide bombers. The groups reportedly operate across Nigeria, Cameroon, Chad and Niger, subjecting children to physical and sexual abuse and forced drug use. “Boko Haram and ISIS-West Africa continue recruiting, abducting, and using—including through force, fraud, and coercion—child soldiers as young as 12 years old as cooks, domestic workers, spies, porters, messengers, bodyguards or guards at checkpoints, ‘morality police,’ armed combatants, and suicide bombers in attacks in Nigeria, Cameroon, Chad, and Niger; these children are subjected to physical and sexual abuse and forced drug use,” the report stated. The report also raised concerns over the abduction and exploitation of women and girls in northern Nigeria, including forced labour, domestic servitude, sexual slavery and forced marriage. It alleged that Boko Haram had kidnapped thousands of women and girls and forced some into marriages, while punishing girls who refused to marry by compelling them to become suicide bombers. Beyond insurgent groups, the report said criminal gangs in southern Nigeria recruit children for forced criminal activities, including kidnappings and robberies, while exploiting some in sex trafficking. It also identified forced labour in agriculture and mining as a concern involving criminal gangs in the north-west. Apart from the child-soldier designation, the report said Nigeria had failed to meet the minimum standards for eliminating trafficking for the 15th consecutive year, although it acknowledged some improvements in government funding and victim support. The US State Department expressed concern over alleged official complicity in trafficking crimes, stating that the Nigerian government did not report investigations, prosecutions or convictions of public officials allegedly involved in such offences during the reporting period. “The government did not report any investigations, prosecutions, or convictions of government employees allegedly complicit in trafficking crimes or provide details or other actions taken against complicit officials from previous years,” the report stated. It added that “corruption and official complicity in trafficking crimes remained significant concerns.” Vanguard News The post US lists Nigeria among 14 countries facing military aid cuts appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Black Star Fashion Week: Can Ghana turn the runway into a tourism attraction?
body: Fashion has always been a powerful expression of identity. Through clothing, textiles, colours and craftsmanship, societies tell stories about their history, values and aspirations. Today, fashion is also a tourism asset, capable of attracting visitors, generating international media attention and creating economic opportunities across the creative industries. Ghana’s maiden Black Star Fashion Week (BSFW), announced by the Black Star Experience Secretariat at the Office of the President, presents an opportunity to explore this connection. More importantly, it raises a question about how the country can use fashion, alongside music, food, heritage and the arts, to strengthen its identity as a destination. Scheduled for November 4 and 7, 2026, the initiative will bring together industry engagement in Accra and a fashion showcase at Royal Senchi. With several established fashion events also taking place in the final quarter, Ghana has an opportunity to build a more coordinated fashion tourism proposition. From Accra to Senchi The structure of Black Star Fashion Week is particularly interesting because it goes beyond the conventional fashion show. The first event, the Black Star Fashion Summit, takes place in Accra on November 4. It is designed to bring together designers, fashion entrepreneurs, industry leaders, investors, buyers, manufacturers, policymakers and media professionals for discussions on the business and future of Ghanaian fashion. The programme includes keynote addresses, panel discussions, fireside conversations, masterclasses, industry presentations and practical workshops. The subjects range from entrepreneurship, branding and digital marketing to textile innovation, manufacturing, fashion finance, export readiness, e-commerce, artificial intelligence, sustainability and intellectual property. These are important conversations for an industry seeking to move beyond individual creative talent towards sustainable businesses, stronger manufacturing capacity and international market access. A particularly notable component is the 16-Region Designer Programme, through which emerging designers will interpret their regions using local identity, heritage, materials, craftsmanship and contemporary design. Five designers will be selected, with one advancing to the flagship showcase at Senchi. This creates an opportunity to present Ghana not simply as a country with talented designers, but as a destination with diverse regional cultures and creative traditions. The second event, at Royal Senchi on November 7, shifts the emphasis from industry dialogue to a wider cultural and fashion experience. The Black Star Fashion Show will be accompanied by a Fashion Village featuring designer showcases, retail, textiles, artisan experiences, brand activations, beauty, technology, food and beverage, tourism and lifestyle experiences. Music, dance, craft, storytelling, heritage and visual arts will also contribute to the programme. The event will include recognition of outstanding contributors to the fashion industry, alongside networking and business engagements connecting designers and creative enterprises with potential buyers, investors, manufacturers and retailers. This combination is significant from a tourism perspective. It creates room for visitors to engage with fashion as part of a broader Ghanaian cultural experience, rather than as a runway spectacle alone. The Accra-Senchi format also offers an opportunity to extend the visitor experience beyond the capital. However, that will require deliberate planning. Transport, accommodation, curated excursions and information about nearby attractions must be incorporated into the visitor proposition if the event is to generate wider tourism benefits. The opportunity beyond Black Star Fashion Week Black Star Fashion Week does not enter an empty space. Ghana already has fashion platforms with established audiences, industry relationships and distinctive identities. Glitz Africa Fashion Week, scheduled for November 10 to 13 in Accra, will bring together designers, manufacturers, textile producers, artisans and creative businesses. Its 2026 theme, Sustainable by Design: Shaping Africa’s Fashion Future, places sustainability, manufacturing, entrepreneurship and market access at the centre of its programme. Rhythms on Da Runway returns on November 28, combining fashion, live music and cultural expression. Its theme, UNBOUND, will broaden representation on the runway, including people of different abilities, backgrounds and body types. The programme also creates opportunities for young people to learn from established practitioners and explore careers in the creative industries. Accra Fashion Week, meanwhile, has an established record of bringing Ghanaian and other African designers, models, buyers and international fashion enthusiasts together. Its previous programming has included cultural tours of Accra, illustrating how fashion events can connect visiting industry professionals with the destination itself. These events should be seen as complementary platforms, not competing attractions. Black Star Fashion Week offers a national identity and policy framework, while the established events contribute their own creative communities, commercial relationships and audiences. Turning fashion into destination marketing The challenge is to connect these platforms to a recognisable Ghanaian tourism story. The Black Star Experience Secretariat, Ghana Tourism Authority, Creative Arts Agency and event organisers could develop a coordinated fashion tourism programme that attracts international buyers, fashion journalists, influencers and visitors from the diaspora. This could include fashion-themed itineraries, designer studio visits, textile and craft trails, shopping experiences, cultural excursions and opportunities to meet artisans. Packages could connect the November events, encouraging visitors to stay longer rather than travel in and out for a single show. The 16-region concept also deserves attention beyond the runway. The designers selected for Black Star Fashion Week could become ambassadors for their regions, with their collections providing a starting point for stories about local textiles, traditional craftsmanship, food, festivals and attractions. International promotion should communicate these experiences well ahead of the events, while partnerships with hotels, airlines, tour operators and travel media could help turn interest into bookings. Success must also be measured beyond attendance and publicity. International visitor numbers, length of stay, visitor expenditure, media reach, retail sales and business opportunities for local designers would provide a clearer picture of the tourism and economic impact. Ghana has the creative talent and cultural diversity to make fashion a distinctive part of its destination identity. Black Star Fashion Week provides an opportunity to organise that story around a national platform, while established events can sustain the momentum. The ultimate ambition should not simply be to put Ghanaian designers on the runway. It should be to give the world more reasons to visit Ghana, experience its culture, buy its creations and discover the places and people behind them. That is how fashion can become more than a showcase. It can become a reason to travel.

title: Qatar Emir condoles Tinubu over military plane crash
body: Qatar’s Amir, Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al-Thani, has sent a message of condolence to President Bola Tinubu over the deaths of passengers and crew members in a Nigerian Air Force aircraft crash in Ondo State. The Deputy Amir, Sheikh Abdullah bin Hamad Al-Thani, and the Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs, Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al-Thani, also sent separate messages of condolence to the Nigerian president. The Qatar News Agency (QNA) reported that the three Qatari leaders sent cables of condolence to Tinubu over the victims of the crash. The agency, however, did not disclose further details of the messages. The crash occurred on October 5 when a Nigerian Air Force ATR-42 aircraft went down in a swampy area near the Nigerian Navy’s Forward Operating Base in Igbokoda, headquarters of Ilaje Local Government Area of Ondo State. The aircraft was on a routine mission from Benin City, Edo State, to Lagos when the accident occurred, according to the Nigerian Air Force. The Air Force initially activated search-and-rescue operations following the crash. It later said 25 people were aboard the aircraft, comprising five crew members and 20 passengers, and confirmed that there were no survivors. The figure differed from the initial account by Aviation Minister Festus Keyamo, who said 32 people were aboard, comprising 25 passengers and seven crew members. Following the tragedy, Tinubu declared three days of national mourning and directed that flags be flown at half-mast across the country. Tinubu also ordered a thorough investigation into the cause of the crash. The Nigerian Air Force has since begun efforts to recover the aircraft’s flight data recorder and cockpit voice recorder, which investigators hope will help establish the circumstances surrounding the accident. Qatar’s condolence message comes amid efforts to deepen its diplomatic and economic relations with Nigeria and other African countries. In May 2025, President Tinubu welcomed fresh investment initiatives from Qatar, particularly in agriculture and food security, and reaffirmed Nigeria’s commitment to strengthening bilateral cooperation. The Qatari government also expressed interest in expanding collaboration in other critical sectors. Qatar has also engaged regional institutions on cooperation in peace, security, regional integration and development. In September 2026, the Qatari ambassador to Nigeria, Yousef Mohammed Ahmed Al-Hail met the president of the ECOWAS Commission, General Birame Diop in Abuja to discuss ways to strengthen cooperation between Qatar and the West African regional bloc. These engagements reflect Doha’s wider efforts to strengthen diplomatic, economic and development ties across Africa, with Nigeria serving as an important partner in its engagement with West Africa.

title: Interns paid as little as 500 euros a month, while unpaid placements become more common
body:
The share of internship advertisements offering unpaid positions has risen from 4.5% to 7.3% in recent years, according to job search service Duunitori.
Duunitori analysed more than 14,000 internship advertisements published on its service for Yle, covering the period from 1 January 2023 to 28 September 2026.
In 52 percent of the advertisements, employers did not disclose the salary or state whether the internship was unpaid.
The proportion of advertisements explicitly offering unpaid internships also increased. Between January and September in 2023 and 2024, unpaid positions accounted for 4.5 percent of advertisements. For the same period in 2025 and 2026, the figure rose to 7.3 percent.
Unpaid internships were particularly common in human resources and recruitment, as well as marketing and communications.
Public-sector employers were significantly more likely to disclose internship salaries and offer paid internships.
Among advertisements that disclosed a monthly salary, the most common range was between 1,500 - 2,000 euros.
Insurance company Lähi-Tapiola is advertising a full-time internship in debt collection services on Duunitori. The fixed-term position lasts at least three months, is linked to the applicant’s studies and starts in November. The advertised salary is 500 euros a month.
Susa Nikula , Director of People and Culture at Lähi-Tapiola, says the company has paid interns such salary for several years.
"We would certainly have a lot of people coming to us even without compensation, because the internship is part of their studies and young people need it. However, it is good to pay some kind of salary for the internship."
The company has also considered whether the amount is sufficient.
"We have sometimes wondered whether 500 euros is too little. On the other hand, I know companies that take interns on for free," Nikula added.
Lähi-Tapiola takes on around 150 interns across Finland during the winter season.
Lotta Viljamaa , a recruitment expert at Duunitori, says the lack of salary information is a broader problem in job advertisements, not just those for internships.
"Of course, not mentioning the salary is a fairly big problem in job advertisements. Applicants then don’t know what they will be paid or what they are applying for," Viljamaa says.
She says this partly reflects the fact that people in Finland do not tend to discuss salaries very openly.
Those looking for internships want greater transparency, Viljamaa says. Advertisements should make clear whether a position is paid and, if so, how much it pays.
In September, Yle reported on a Ukrainian student who had spent a year and a half looking for an internship. Finding placements has become more difficult in some fields, including business.
Nikula says Lähi-Tapiola has also seen increased competition for internships and jobs.
"More people are applying for internships and jobs now than before. It’s always great that there is interest and that we are able to offer internship positions," she says.

title: Nuremberg Airport briefly closed after Corendon flight squawks hijack code
body: Nuremberg Airport suspended operations midday on 13 October 2026 after Corendon Airlines flight XR456 (Boeing 737-800, 9H-CXD) from Corfu transmitted squawk 7500. The pilot was briefly unreachable by radio. Eurofighter jets escorted the aircraft, which landed safely at 10:16 UTC. Police sealed the site and checked the plane. They later issued an all-clear: no danger, passengers and crew unharmed. The airline attributed the code to a short radio system fault over Croatian airspace around 09:00 UTC and stated no actual emergency occurred. Operations resumed around 13:30 local time. Investigations continue into the technical cause. An unrelated overnight report of a possible drone was not confirmed. The post Nuremberg Airport briefly closed after Corendon flight squawks hijack code appeared first on Greek City Times .
