title: Kazakhstan to Hold Early Maslikhat Elections This November
body: The Astana Times provides news and information from Kazakhstan and around the world. ASTANA – Kazakhstan will hold early elections for local representative bodies, known as maslikhats, on Nov. 29, the Central Election Commission announced at an Oct. 13 meeting. The elections will fill 3,447 seats across 228 maslikhats at the regional, city and district levels, Deputy Chair of the Central Election Commission Mukhtar Yerman said. Of the total seats, 668 will be in regional maslikhats, 626 in city maslikhats and 2,053 in district maslikhats. The commission presented a draft resolution setting the election date for Nov. 29. Under Article 101, paragraph 3, of Kazakhstan’s Constitutional Law on Elections, early elections must be called by the Central Election Commission no later than two months after the early termination of a maslikhat’s powers. Maslikhats are elected by residents of their respective administrative and territorial units through universal, equal and direct suffrage by secret ballot. Deputies serve five-year terms. Earlier, President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev signed a decree on the early termination of the powers of maslikhats at all levels. The post Kazakhstan to Hold Early Maslikhat Elections This November appeared first on The Astana Times .

title: 2027: INEC unveils QR code for PVCs collection in Lagos
body: By Olayinka Ajayi The Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, has intensified efforts to ensure that residents who registered for their Permanent Voter Cards, PVCs, get them timely with the launching of a QR code to assist them locate designated collection centres. Briefing newsmen on preparations for the 2027 elections on Tuesday, the Lagos Resident Electoral Commissioner, REC, Professor Ayobami Salami, noted that PVCs for those who registered between January 5 and July 26, 2026 are not available presently. According to him, “PVCs are currently available for persons who registered between August 25, and December, 10 2025 as well as those who registered between 201l and 2022 but have yet to collect their cards.” “PVCs for persons who registered between January 5 and July 26,2026 are not yet available. The collection of their cards will be announced through official channels in due course. “NEC Lagos State Office has also provided a QR code to help voters locate designated PVC collection centres. I encourage eligible voters to collect their cards promptly and safeguard them, as the PVC remains essential for accreditation on Election Day,” he noted. Salami revealed plans by the commission to ensure that vote-buying won’t be tolerated in next year’s election saying “The Commission is strengthening election risk-management measures and collaborating with the EFCC, ICPC, NEIU and Federal Ministry of Justice to address vote buying, illicit campaign financing and other electoral offences. “Engagement with political parties on financial reporting, auditing and campaign finance compliance will be intensified between 28th October28,2026 and 1st January 1,2027. “I appeal to political parties, candidates, and their supporters to conduct their activities peacefully and in accordance with the law. “The increasing spread of misinformation, disinformation, deepfakes and A-generated content poses a serious challenge to public confidence in elections. “I therefore, urge media organisations to verify electoral information through official INEC channels before publication, particularly information concerning electoral procedures, Commission decisions and election results. “Unofficial projections and privately collated figures must not be presented as results formally declared by authorised electoral officials. “The Commission values your partnership in ensuring accurate and responsible reporting. “The Media Accreditation Portal is expected to become operational before the end of October 2026, with further guidelines to be communicated through official channels. “Preparations are equally advancing for the recruitment, training and deployment electoral personnel.” Professor Salami also revealed a planned Mock accreditation and election simulation exercise in November to fully test the readiness of the commission. “Mock accreditation and election simulation exercise is also scheduled for November 2026, to further assess readiness. “Equally important is the logistical preparation required for the elections. Nationwide, personnel and materials will be deployed across 176,846 Polling Units and 8,809 Registration Areas, supported by over 100,000 vehicles and approximately 4,000 boats. “Sensitive materials are expected to reach local government areas 72 hours before Election Day, with deployment to Registration Area Centres and Super Registration Area Centres Completed by 4:00 p.m. on the eve of the election. “In Lagos State, our preparations take account of population density, traffic conditions, riverine communities and other logistical challenges. “Attention is being given to transportation, storage, electoral facilities, personnel deployment and contingency arrangements to ensure that polling units are rowdy to commence activities as scheduled,” he said. Speaking on voter education and accessibility measures, Professor Salami said; “Voter education and inclusive participation also remain our priorities. “Through the VEP 2027 Election Project Plan, the Commission is expanding grassroots engagement, particularly among women, young people and persons with disabilities. “Activities include community meetings, engagements with tertiary institutions, public debates, mobile cinema and collaboration with the National Orientation Agency. “Accessibility measures include Braille materials, EC30 posters, magnifying glasses and sign-language interpretation at State Collation Centres. “In Lagos State, voter education will continue across communities, markets, educational institutions, religious organisations and other relevant platforms. Improvements are also being made to electronic result transmission and management. “Security remains integral to these arrangements. The Nigeria Police Force, as the lead agency, continues to coordinate with other security and intelligence agencies through the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security (ICCES).” The post 2027: INEC unveils QR code for PVCs collection in Lagos appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Tinubu Transmits NDLEA Reform Bill, Two Others To Senate
body: President Bola Tinubu has transmitted a series of bills to the Senate for consideration, including proposed legislation to reform the legal framework governing the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA), amend the Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau Act, and establish a National School of Government, among others. The bills, in accordance with the provisions of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, were conveyed by the President of the Senate, Sen. Godswill Akpabio. One of the proposals, the NDLEA Bill 2026, seeks to establish a consolidated legal framework for the operations of the NDLEA. The bill is expected to strengthen the agency’s powers, including its capacity to investigate individuals suspected of involvement in illicit drug-related activities. The Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau Amendment Bill 2026 seeks to amend the existing 2022 Act to reposition the bureau as an independent authority and expand its mandate. The proposed amendment also seeks to transfer supervisory oversight of the bureau to the Presidency, alongside changes to its administrative structure. President Tinubu also transmitted the National School of Government Bill (ASCON) 2026, which seeks to repeal the Administrative Staff College of Nigeria Act and establish a National School of Government. The proposed institution is intended to serve as a national centre for governance training, public sector capacity development and institutional strengthening. The President equally transmitted a bill seeking to domesticate the four Geneva Conventions of 1949 and their two Additional Protocols of 1977, which provide for the protection of victims of armed conflict, as well as the Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court, providing for the enforcement of punishment for genocide, war crimes, crimes against humanity and aggression. The post Tinubu Transmits NDLEA Reform Bill, Two Others To Senate appeared first on Channels Television .

title: NNPC’s profit after tax rises to N431bn in August – Report
body:
The Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC Ltd.) says it recorded a 54.5 per cent increase in Profit After Tax (PAT), rising from N279 billion to N431 billion in August 2026.
NNPC Ltd. made this known in its monthly operations and financial report for the month of August 2026.
According to the report, revenue for the period stood at N3.74 trillion as against N3.09 trillion recorded in July.
It said the company also recorded a 19.89 per cent increase in cumulative statutory payments, from N7.91 trillion for January to July, amounting to N9.49 trillion from January to August.
The report puts the average crude oil and gas production figures for the period at 1.69 million barrels per day (bpd) and 7,680 million standard cubic feet per day, respectively.
On the state of infrastructure, it said there was 100 per cent availability of upstream pipelines, while the OB3 and Ajaokuta-Kaduna-Kano (AKK) Gas Pipelines stood at 100 per cent and 95 per cent completion, respectively.

title: Number of injured in Russian strike on educational facility in Rivne rises to 25 – police
body:
As a result of an enemy strike on an educational institution in Rivne, 25 people have already been injured, three more are currently being examined by medics, and two casualties in serious condition are undergoing surgery, the press service of Rivne region police reported.

"The number of injured as a result of an enemy strike on an educational institution in Rivne has risen to 25 people. Three more are currently being examined by medics. Two people in serious condition are undergoing surgery," the agency noted in a report.

According to police, all necessary emergency services continue to work at the scene.

Earlier, 21 injured persons were reported.

title: Ghana sends 61 health workers to Grenada under Labour Export Programme
body: Ghana has deployed some sixty-one health workers to the Caribbean nation of Grenada under an arrangement with the country. The government of Ghana’s Labour Export Programme seeks to tackle the Caribbean nation’s shortage of skilled healthcare professionals, while seeking job opportunities for Ghanaian health workers. These health workers will serve in different medical facilities under two-year renewable contracts. Ghana’s Chief of Staff, Julius Debrah, charged the workers to be professional and ethical as they serve as ambassadors of Ghana. “Your certificate or your qualification may open the door for you, but your character will determine how long the door will be kept open,” Dr Debrah said. The Minister of Labour, Jobs and Employment, Emmanuel Kwadwo Agyekum, advised them to respect the terms of their contract at all times. “Go and work well, don’t mess up. Try and raise the flag of Ghana. Be professional. Professionalism is key. This is what we expect from you,” he said. The Minister revealed that the government is planning to deploy additional health workers to Germany and other Caribbean nations. The Labour Export Programme seeks to create employment opportunities abroad for Ghanaians and also help recipient nations to tackle their health sector staff shortages.

title: Russia's President, UAE counterpart touch on Russian-US diesel supply agreements — Kremlin
body:
MOSCOW, October 13. /TASS/. Russian leader Vladimir Putin and President of the United Arab Emirates Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan touched upon the issue of agreements on Russian diesel fuel supplies reached between Moscow and Washington in their telephone conversation, the Kremlin’s press service said.
"During the exchange of views on the international agenda, the agreements reached following the telephone call between Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump regarding the supply of Russian diesel fuel were touched upon, as well as the prospects for settling the crisis situation in the Persian Gulf zone," the Kremlin said.
The two leaders have agreed to continue their communications, the Kremlin added.

title: Oyebanji sacks heads of agencies, technical advisers as second term begins
body:
Ekiti State Governor Biodun Oyebanji has disengaged all directors-general of government agencies and technical advisers in his administration, completing a fresh round of changes involving political appointees ahead of his second term.
According to a statement on Tuesday by the governor’s Chief Press Secretary, Olayinka Oyebode, the decision takes immediate effect, with the affected officials directed to submit their handover notes to the Office of the Secretary to the State Government.
The statement, however, noted that a few appointments had been retained because of the nature of the officials’ assignments.
“The disengagement, which came barely 24 hours after the dissolution of the State Executive Council, marks the completion of the disengagement process for political appointees serving in the administration, except for a few whose appointments have been retained in view of the nature of their assignments,” the statement said.
Mr Oyebanji thanked the affected officials for their support, commitment and contributions to his administration and the development of Ekiti State, wishing them success in their future endeavours.
The latest decision follows an earlier round of changes announced on 27 September, when the governor dissolved boards, commissions and parastatals and terminated the appointments of political aides.
The latest disengagement comes as Mr Oyebanji prepares for his second term, with his inauguration scheduled for Friday, 16 October.
Mr Oyebanji, the All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate, won his re-election in the 20 June governorship election with 319,224 votes winning across the state’s 16 local government areas, defeating his closest challenger, Oluwole Oluyede of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), who polled 40,543 votes.
His victory made him the first incumbent governor in Ekiti State to win re-election, securing a second consecutive term in office.

title: Kyiv Mayor pushes back against claims of Kyiv heating disruption
body:
Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko called accusations that the city was disrupting the heating season groundless and said the city authorities were preparing for its start amid continued Russian attacks.
"Groundless accusations are being made that the heating season is allegedly being disrupted, and these are being spread by media outlets linked to the central government," Klitschko wrote in the caption to a video address released on Tuesday.
He also said there were attempts to remove heads of territorial communities from office on contrived pretexts. Klitschko said that, as head of the Association of Ukrainian Cities, he believed such actions were aimed at weakening local self-government and replacing elected leaders with appointed heads of military administrations.
"I would like to remind everyone that attempts are being made to destroy local self-government and remove 300 heads of communities. As head of the Association of Ukrainian Cities, I can say that 300 city mayors are being removed from office for various contrived reasons, made up on the spot, and replaced with heads of military administrations," Klitschko said in the video address.
He emphasized that he had been elected by Kyiv residents and noted that he was doing everything possible to live up to their trust. According to him, voters would be able to assess how well he had succeeded in the next elections.
Klitschko also rejected the accusations against him as groundless and noted that the city authorities regularly provide information about preparations for the heating season. "But, excuse me, given the intensity of the shelling, the power outages, the destruction of the electricity supply system and the ongoing damage to infrastructure, the mayor of the city is not responsible for air defense," he said.
As reported, an Interfax-Ukraine correspondent said that the Verkhovna Rada had supported a motion by MP Mariana Bezuhla to summon Klitschko. A total of 151 MPs voted in favor of the decision at Tuesday's session, while eight voted against.

title: Cineplex posts record $45.1M box office revenue for September
body:
Cineplex Inc. says its box office revenue totalled $45.1 million in September to set a record for the month, up from $37.7 million a year earlier.
The movie theatre company says the result brought its third-quarter box office revenue to a record $215.7 million, up from $159.5 million in the same quarter last year.
The increase came as third quarter box office revenue per patron topped $14 for the first time as moviegoers increasingly chose premium formats.
Cineplex says Spider-Man: Brand New Day and the Odyssey helped drive the results as both movies generated exceptional attendance across its premium offerings.
It says September also benefited from the performance of Resident Evil.
Cineplex CEO Bill Walker says the consistency over the past several quarters, including a record-setting third quarter, reflect the appeal of the theatrical experience.

title: Kyrgyzstan Rejects European Migrant Resettlement Proposals
body: Kyrgyzstan has repeatedly rejected proposals from several European countries to accept migrants from Afghanistan and African countries, Foreign Minister Jeenbek Kulubaev said on October 13. In exchange, those countries had offered employment opportunities for Kyrgyzstan’s skilled workers. He said Bishkek would not negotiate on those terms. Kulubaev did not specify which countries had made the proposals or how many migrants Kyrgyzstan had been asked to accept. No European government has publicly confirmed such an offer. On October 1, the Council of the European Union adopted new rules for returning foreign nationals who have no legal right to remain in its member states. The rules allow countries to establish migrant return centers outside the bloc under agreements with third countries. Such arrangements must comply with international human rights protections, including the prohibition on sending people to countries where they face persecution or ill-treatment. Similar arrangements have been discussed elsewhere in Central Asia. On May 7, Austria and Uzbekistan signed an agreement to cooperate on deportations during a visit by Austria’s foreign and interior ministers to Tashkent. The deal also provided for greater cooperation on legal employment opportunities for skilled workers from Uzbekistan. Unlike the proposals described by Kulubaev, the Austrian arrangement envisaged Uzbekistan as a potential transit route for Afghan nationals being returned from Austria, rather than a place of resettlement. Kyrgyzstan is reassessing its own approach to labor migration. According to Kulubaev, growing numbers of its citizens are choosing Turkey and the United States as destinations for work. South Korea and Japan are also interested in recruiting workers from Kyrgyzstan, particularly staff to care for elderly patients in hospitals. Bishkek has reduced the organized placement of its citizens in long-term jobs abroad while continuing to facilitate seasonal employment. Kulubaev said Kyrgyzstan also faces labor shortages at home. Kyrgyzstan’s Ministry of Labor, Social Security, and Migration said 736,600 citizens had worked abroad so far in 2026, compared with 798,400 during the whole of 2025. Russia remains the main destination, with more than 472,000 citizens of Kyrgyzstan living there in March. Approximately 70,000 were working in Kazakhstan, 60,000 in the U.S., 35,000 in Turkey, and 20,000 in Germany.

title: B.C. party leaders make campaign stop at Vancouver trade board ahead of election
body:
The leaders of British Columbia’s three major political parties will pitch their plans to business leaders in Vancouver with less than two weeks to go before the provincial election.
NDP Leader David Eby, Conservative interim leader Lorne Doerkson and Green Party Leader Emily Lowan are slated to speak at an event this afternoon hosted by the Greater Vancouver Board of Trade.
The leaders won’t debate each other, though each will address attendees.
That will be followed by a question-and-answer session with board president Bridgitte Anderson.
The board says the event is designed to allow people to hear directly from the leaders as they present their vision for the province and discuss their priorities for B.C.’s future.
A televised leaders’ debate is set for Wednesday ahead of election day on Oct. 24.

title: Russia raised issue of participation in World Bank procurements — Deputy PM
body:
BANGKOK, October 13. /TASS/. Russia supports a non-discriminatory and non-politicized approach to the participation of its companies in World Bank procurement procedures and has raised this issue during meetings with its leadership, Deputy Prime Minister Alexey Overchuk told reporters.
"Of course, we confirmed our interest in Russian companies participating in World Bank procurement procedures. Here, we advocate for a non-discriminatory and non-politicized approach towards Russian companies," he said.
"We have just held corresponding meetings with the bank's leadership, where we raised this issue," Overchuk added.

title: Central banks should avoid reacting too strongly to headline inflation – IMF
body: The International Monetary Fund has urged central banks to avoid reacting too strongly to high-frequency movements in headline inflation, particularly when those movements are driven by volatile energy prices. According to the Fund, they should, however, respond if higher inflation starts feeding into expectations or wage setting or if technology-driven activity starts strengthening pass-through from headline to core inflation. “Where the post-pandemic inflation episode may have weakened confidence in the monetary policy framework, central banks should be quicker to respond to signs of such feedback from inflation to expectations or stronger pass-through. Indeed, not arresting a drift in inflation expectations in response to the current shocks can be costly when shocks of similar nature arrive in the future because it puts the credibility of monetary policy on the line”. The Bretto Woods institution warned that should the adverse demand effects from the war or materialisation of financial risks eventually dominate—weakening growth materially, softening labor markets, and consequently reducing underlying inflationary pressures—scope for monetary policy to pivot toward easing could emerge. “Any such easing should be gradual and data dependent and remain consistent with returning inflation to target”. Central Banks worldwide are engrossed with inflation targeting policy to address rising inflation. This is done by largely reducing money supply in circulation, but increasing the cost of borrowing. The IMF continued that central banks should explain clearly how incoming data alter the balance of risks, what would justify a change in the policy path, and how they are distinguishing between first-round relative price effects and broader inflationary pressures. This it believes can reduce the risk that households, firms, and financial markets will misread conditional policy guidance as unconditional promises. With fiscal costs rising and electoral pressures intensifying in many countries, central banks may face renewed calls to accommodate higher public borrowing or tolerate inflation above target. The Fund advised that ensuring legal and operational independence of central banks and shielding monetary policy from political interference and fiscal dominance are therefore essential.

title: eTranzact appoints five directors after ownership change
body:
eTranzact International Plc has appointed five new directors following a change in its majority ownership structure.
The company disclosed this in a statement issued on Tuesday, following the transfer of 5.17 billion ordinary shares, representing 56.18 per cent of its issued shares, to Trademarks Global Concepts Ltd.
The shares were transferred by Access Bank Plc, Meristem Trustees Ltd., acting as trustee for Accelerex Holdings, and eTranzact Global Ltd.
The company said the transaction resulted in the resignation of five directors, comprising three Non-Executive Directors and two Independent Non-Executive Directors.
The outgoing directors are Chuma Ajene, Benjamin Dabra, Afolabi Oladele, Binta Max-Gbinije and Emeka Onwuamaegbu.
The new appointees are Akinwunmi Akinfemiwa, Olatunde Akande and Doron Grupper as Non-Executive Directors, while Omobola Hollist and Mustapha Ajenifuja were appointed Independent Non-Executive Directors.
According to the company, the new directors bring experience in corporate leadership, banking, development finance, governance, legal advisory, infrastructure, energy, investment management and business transformation.
It said the appointments were expected to strengthen the board’s strategic oversight and support the company’s long-term objectives.
The company added that it had obtained approval from the Central Bank of Nigeria for the appointments and was updating its records with the Corporate Affairs Commission.
The ownership transition follows changes in the company’s shareholding structure, with Trademarks Global Concepts Ltd. emerging as its majority shareholder.
eTranzact provides electronic payment processing services and operates in Nigeria’s digital payments industry.
The company said it remained committed to strong corporate governance, operational excellence and sustainable value creation for shareholders and other stakeholders.

title: Russia remains open to those who sincerely share its values — historical society chairman
body:
MOSCOW, October 13. /TASS/. Russia is open to all foreigners who share and respect its values and culture, according to a welcoming address by Russian Historical Society Chairman and Foreign Intelligence Service Director Sergey Naryshkin to participants of the Third International Catherine Forum.
The address was read out by Ruslan Gagkuev, chairman of the board of the Russian Historical Society and executive director of the History of the Fatherland Foundation.
"Today, Russia is open to everyone who shares its spiritual and moral values, respects the culture and traditions of the peoples inhabiting our country, and seeks to build their future here," Naryshkin noted. "I am convinced that the proposals developed here will help continue a centuries-old tradition through which people from different countries have found a new homeland in Russia."
According to the chairman, over the centuries Russia has attracted people from all corners of the world, "who found opportunities here for work, creativity and self-fulfillment." "The ability to unite representatives of a wide variety of peoples while preserving the diversity of their traditions and cultures has been and remains a key foundation of Russian statehood, our civilizational advantage and an integral part of our national character," he added.
"This characteristic was particularly evident during the reign of Catherine II. In response to her call, tens of thousands of people from German lands, Switzerland and the Netherlands moved to Russia. As we approach the 300th anniversary of the empress’s birth, it is encouraging that this year’s Catherine Forum is revisiting this historical experience, which remains relevant to this day," the Russian Foreign Intelligence Service director concluded.
The Catherine Forum is an international public and government platform dedicated to Russia’s civilizational development, traditional spiritual and moral values, and international humanitarian cooperation.
The forum is being held for the third time this year. Its agenda focuses on integrating foreign nationals moving to Russia, attracting highly qualified foreign specialists, reducing barriers for people relocating to the country, supporting Russian-speaking communities abroad, public diplomacy and Russia’s image in the international media landscape.
TASS is the informational partner of the forum.

title: Iran and Russia targeting Britain with hybrid methods, UK spy chief says
body:
Russia is “escalating” its hybrid warfare efforts against Europe and its allies as the country’s stalled invasion of Ukraine becomes more costly, the U.K.’s spy chief warned Tuesday.
Ken McCallum, the head of the UK’s MI5 agency, said in a public speech that Vladimir Putin’s Kremlin remains “aggressor number one” in terms of state threats targeting the U.K.
“This means Russia is using tactics that stop short, though sometimes not much short, of conventional conflict. A cyber attack on Polish energy infrastructure. A misfired attempt to use an explosive-laden drone to destroy a cargo plane in Germany. A thwarted assassination attempt in the U.S.,” McCallum said.
“It’s no accident that Russian aggressors are trying to unsettle other European homelands at a time when their military progress in Ukraine is minimal and horrifically costly.”
McCallum said that his agency, which is mandated to safeguard the U.K.’s domestic security, now devotes roughly equal attention to foreign state aggression as terrorism — which he noted is a dramatic shift from the post 9/11 stance of Western security agencies.
McCallum’s warning joins a recent chorus from European politicians, suggesting Russian sabotage and interference operations have increased as the war in Ukraine drags on despite U.S. assurances of an “energy ceasefire.”
Last week, EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas told reporters that in recent weeks Europe has seen a spike in “sabotage attempts and airspace violations” attributed to Russia, putting lives at risk.
“Russian missiles and drones violated Moldovan airspace again over the weekend. And this is completely unacceptable,” Kallas told reporters while standing beside Moldovan Prime Minister Vasile Tofan.
It also comes as NATO’s supreme allied commander in Europe, U.S. Gen. Alexus Grynkewich, gave a speech warning against any conventional incursions into the defensive alliance’s territory.
Speaking in Warsaw Monday, Grynkewich said he does not view military conflict in Europe as “imminent or inevitable,” according to French public broadcaster France24.
“If someone is foolish enough to attack us, we will fight. We will stop the attack and deny them the ability to achieve their objectives, whatever those may be … We will, in short, ensure any attack against any ally proves utterly futile.”
In its most recent public report, the Canadian Security Intelligence Service (CSIS) listed the Russian Federation among the countries attempting to interfere in Canadian domestic affairs, behind the People’s Republic of China and Iran.
Russia’s efforts have been aimed at undermining the Canadian government — and people’s — support for Ukraine, the agency suggested.
“Hostile Russian state actors, and those working on their behalf, have carried out several information and malign influence operations against Canada, exploiting various contentious social topics aimed at discrediting the Government of Canada’s position on Ukraine by polarizing segments of both political and public spectrums,” the agency’s annual public report read.
“As part of this, Russian state-linked actors often hide behind networks of proxies who amplify the Kremlin’s messaging or generate their own versions using powerful new technologies, such as artificial intelligence (AI) and social media.”
CSIS noted that, like MI5, the agency has been forced to “reprioritize its operations” in order to counter the activity of “foreign intelligence services and their proxies” who have targeted people in Canada, including thwarting one “potentially lethal” operation.
McCallum noted that Russia’s hybrid tactics do not suggest “a great power with a strategic upper hand” — but said they must be taken seriously.
“The whole aim of hybrid tactics is to intimidate us, so let’s not fall into that trap. But we do need to be resilient to them,” McCallum said.

title: Ukraine Delays $2.3 Billion in Payments as Treasury Cash Runs Short
body:
Ukraine has pushed about Hr.39 billion ($876 million) of spending to the end of the year and left a further Hr.46 billion ($1.03 billion) in payments unprocessed on the Single Treasury Account, Finance Minister Serhiy Marchenko told the Verkhovna Rada on Monday.
The unprocessed payments cover road repairs, the upkeep and development of administrative service centers, repairs of penal institutions, school bus purchases, current and capital repairs of housing, preparations for the heating season and the purchase of backup power, Marchenko told lawmakers.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
The government entered October in a liquidity crisis, Marchenko told lawmakers. Only defense spending, pensions, salaries and social benefits are being financed. Other expenditures have been either prioritized or put on hold until the Single Treasury Account recovers.
“… approximately Hr.39 billion pushed at the end of the year. In addition, as of today, there are Hr.46 billion in the state treasury allocated to the Unified State Budget, of which funds are earmarked for road repairs, the maintenance and development of administrative centers, the renovation of correctional facilities, the purchase of school buses, routine and major repairs to the housing stock, preparations for the heating season, and the purchase of backup power supplies,” Interfax-Ukraine quoted the finance minister.
He added that the government has also suspended Hr.18 billion hryvnias ($404 million) in budget refunds of value-added tax (VAT) to taxpayers. Together, the three categories he named amount to Hr.103 billion ($2.3 billion).
A VAT refund is the money the state returns to a registered business when the tax it paid on its purchases exceeds the tax it owes on its sales.
On Sept. 15, the government submitted a 2027 budget of about $162 billion, but Marchenko warned that Ukraine will run short of cash before the end of 2026.
The government had already adopted a decision allowing the Treasury to limit the opening of appropriations for non-priority expenditures starting in October if the Single Treasury Account lacks sufficient resources to make all planned payments. The decision remains in effect until the end of the year, according to the government’s website.
Marchenko stressed that the government is seeking domestic resourc es and has stepped up the work of a task force to reduce the shadow economy. According to him, the group will prepare proposals to prevent the artificial splitting of businesses, counter illegal production and sales of tobacco products, and bring the labor market out of the shadows.
The International Monetary Fund kept its forecast for Ukraine’s real GDP growth at 1.0 percent in 2026, with a pickup to 3.5 percent in 2027, in its October World Economic Outlook.
Olena Hrazhdan is the Business Reporter at Kyiv Post, covering Ukraine’s markets, business, and economic policy. While she reports broadly on economic issues, her core focus is banking, finance, monetary and fiscal policy. Olena previously wrote for leading Ukrainian business media and became a Fellow of the International Monetary Fund’s Journalism Fellowship in 2024.

title: Catholic Church shuts institutions in Benue community, gives reasons
body:
The Catholic Diocese of Gboko has ordered the temporary closure of its institutions in Ihugh, Vandeikya Local Government Area (LGA) of Benue , following repeated attacks, arson and destruction of church properties.
The decision was announced in a pastoral letter and decree signed by the Bishop of the diocese, Most Rev. William Avenya, and the Diocesan Chancellor, Rev. Fr. Marcellinus Wende, dated 12 October.
The affected institutions, according to the pastoral letter, are St. Winifred Girls Secondary School, St. Thomas Hospital, St. Winifred Nursery and Primary School and St. Winifred Parish, all in High.
The decree directed the withdrawal of pastoral agents, including priests and consecrated persons, citing persistent security threats to church personnel, students, teachers, medical workers and other members of the community.
The diocese expressed deep concern over the repeated burning of students’ hostels at St. Winifred Secondary School, which it said occurred on 28 October 2025; 10 and 15 May 2026; and 11 October 2026.
The decree also cited recurring burglaries at St. Winifred Parish and repeated criminal incidents at St. Thomas’ Hospital, Ihugh, as part of what it described as a pattern of hostility towards church-owned institutions.
The letter recalled an incident during the reopening of St. Thomas’ Hospital on 21 June 2024, when some residents allegedly protested against the continued presence of Reverend Sisters in the community.
According to the diocese, the incidents had resulted in significant losses, fear and uncertainty, undermining the safety of people working in and benefiting from the affected institutions.
“The Church cannot, in conscience, continue to expose her priests, consecrated persons, teachers, medical personnel, students and patients to danger,” the letter stated.
The diocese, however, said the decision followed several efforts to resolve the crisis peacefully, including dialogue with the host community, traditional rulers, community elders and relevant civil and security authorities.
“The attacks have continued, and no assurance of lasting safety has been secured,” the letter stated.
The diocese explained that its schools, hospital and parish in Ihugh were established to serve the common good, irrespective of religious affiliation or origin.
The letter also said the withdrawal was therefore a painful but necessary measure to protect lives and prevent further destruction of church properties.
On the implications of the decision, the diocese said affected pupils and students would, as far as possible, be assisted to continue their education in other Catholic schools within the diocese.
The decree said the Director of Catholic Education Services would provide further details on the arrangements.
Patients receiving treatment at St. Thomas’ Hospital would also be referred to other health facilities, with particular attention to those requiring urgent medical care.
The diocese further assured affected staff members that they would be treated with justice and charity, in accordance with the Church’s teachings on the dignity of labour.
Addressing Catholic faithful in Ihugh, the diocese urged them not to lose hope, stressing that the closure of church buildings did not diminish their faith.
The decree also clarified that the decision was not intended to condemn innocent members of the community or foster hostility towards the people of Ihugh.
“We bear no ill will toward our brothers and sisters, many of whom have known only the good that these institutions brought,” the letter stated.
The diocese, however, called on community leaders, traditional rulers, youth leaders, government officials and security agencies to work towards restoring peace and bringing those responsible for the attacks to justice.
The letter stated that the closure did not constitute a permanent departure, adding that the diocese could reconsider its return if there was genuine repentance, restitution and lasting assurances of safety for its personnel and properties.
The diocese also called on the faithful across its jurisdiction to intensify prayers for peace and reconciliation in Ihugh and other communities.
The letter directed all parishes to offer prayers and Holy Mass for peace and urged the faithful to observe Friday, Oct. 23, as a day of prayer and fasting for reconciliation.
The pastoral letter concluded with an appeal for divine intervention to restore peace and promote reconciliation among the people of Ihugh.
Meanwhile, the spokesman of Police Command in Benue, Aondogu Orchia, said the command has commenced a full investigation into the incident.
Orchia also said that despite the fire incident, no life was lost.

title: New robot that can prepare your meal in under four minutes arrives in Abu Dhabi
body: A new kitchen robot in Abu Dhabi can cook four hot dishes at once, with each meal ready in about four minutes. Circus Group’s CA-1 is being tested at First Clique in Paragon Mall with the catering company Royal Prestige. The German company says the Abu Dhabi installation is its first in the UAE and that it hopes to expand to hospitals, universities, shopping malls, petrol stations and airports, where fresh food can be harder to find. “The goal is to help people have great food in places where they normally don’t have food,” Michael Bassler, Circus Group shareholder, told The National. The CA-1 has 36 silos for solid and liquid ingredients, four induction plates and two robotic arms: one cooks and the other serves. Its current menu has 10 dishes, including chicken fajita, chicken biryani, lentil soup, chicken curry and pasta. Depending on the menu, the machine can make up to 50 hot meals or 100 cold meals an hour. One load of ingredients can produce up to 200 dishes with the current menu configuration. Ingredients are kept in temperature-controlled silos and usually replaced within 48 hours. “If you already have a restaurant, it’s a very good question: why do you need the CA-1?” Mr Bassler said. “The best locations we focus on are places where you have no food or really bad food.” 'Made with love' The company is looking at 24 hour sites such as petrol stations, central stations and airports. Mr Bassler said Abu Dhabi Airport’s VIP terminal would be a good fit. The Paragon Mall site is being used as a showroom where customers can try the meals. Mr Bassler said customers have been eating there for about two months. Sana Pathan, 24, from India, tried the quinoa salad and chicken biryani. “For something made by AI, I think this biryani is really fresh and it feels like it’s made with love,” she said. “It does really taste human-made.” She said she would like to see the technology in restaurants and public places, including beaches, sports centres and university campuses. Meals start at Dh40, with a chicken curry at about Dh48. Mr Bassler said the machine costs about Dh1 million. “The big goal is to find the best locations where the clients can make the money back,” he said. Circus Group has about 10 machines operating in Germany, including at Mercedes-Benz and Meta sites, and at a supermarket chain. It was founded five years ago and spent about four years developing the CA-1 before entering the German market around a year and a half ago. It also makes a smaller machine, the CA-A, for smoothies and protein shakes. “It’s like a small vending machine, just for fresh smoothies,” Mr Bassler said. The company is developing a larger version for military use. Circus Group is updating the CA-1’s software and visual recognition system to improve cooking and detect when food may be burning. Customers in Germany can order through touchscreen or, or speak to the machine for meal recommendations based on their dietary needs. Those options remain to be tested in Abu Dhabi. Not replacing people The robot does not remove the need for people to load ingredients, handle orders and serve meals. Dylan Frayne, Circus Group’s culinary research and development chef, develops and tests recipes before they are programmed into the machine. Asked whether the robot could replace his job, Mr Frayne said: “It hasn’t replaced my job. It’s given me a another job.” Mr Bassler said the CA-1 was meant to give people another way to get a quick, freshly cooked meal, rather than replace restaurants. “You will always have restaurants. You will always have chefs in restaurants,” he said. “We don’t replace anyone in this scenario. We offer an additional option for people to have fresh food that didn’t exist before.”

title: If Iran attacked, consequences to be extended beyond region
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 13 (MNA) – Warning US of wider consequences of war, Iran’s deputy foreign minister for Legal and International Affairs has said once US chooses military aggression against Iran, the consequences of war will be extended beyond the region.
Kazem Gharibabadi made the remarks in an interview with RIA Novosti on Tuesday, emphasizing that the US, in case of renewed aggression against Iran, its consequences will be extended beyond the region.
The situation is clear and that it is Washington that needs to adjust to the realities of the region and seek solutions based on diplomacy, he underlined.
Gharibabadi warned that repeating past mistakes by resorting to military scenarios and threats would lead to consequences that would reach well beyond the region, adding that the US must now decide which path to adopt.
The Iranian deputy foreign minister said that Tehran has always maintained a constructive approach toward diplomacy and negotiations, while remaining prepared for any possible scenario.

title: Former political rivals Notley, Kenney to unite at event ahead of separation vote
body:
Former premier Jason Kenney, who co-founded Alberta’s governing United Conservative Party, says separatists have infiltrated it and are wielding an outsized influence.
Kenney, speaking to business leaders in Edmonton alongside his former political rival Rachel Notley, said Tuesday that after the province’s Alberta referendum separation vote the party will face a “reckoning.”
He said the UCP needs to decide whether it stands on its founding federalist principles, and if so, separatists need to be shown the door.
“There’s no doubt that those folks have infiltrated (the party),” Kenney said at an Edmonton Chamber of Commerce luncheon.
“They’re welcome to participate in democracy, but if their primary goal is separation, then they have to do it in a separatist party,” he said.
Kenney’s conservatives defeated Notley’s NDP government in 2019.
Kenney stepped down in the spring of 2022 after he receiving 51.4 per cent support in a leadership review , which came amid frustration in his party over COVID-19 restrictions.
Premier Danielle Smith took over as UCP leader in the fall of 2022 .
Kenney said Tuesday many of the same hard-right Albertans angered by COVID “conspiracy theories” became organized and have moved on to the next fight — separation.
Kenney’s comments come as advance polls open and Albertans vote on 10 questions in a referendum ahead of the final polling day Monday.
The key question asks whether the province should stay in Canada or hold a second, binding referendum on leaving the country.
Notley and Kenney have united in a campaign to keep the province from quitting Canada.
Kenney said it appears the majority of the UCP caucus is committed to Canada.
“But, there is clearly a problem that the folks who used to run these marginal separatist parties got tired of getting pummeled with one or two per cent of the vote,” he said.
He also pointed to Quebec, where he said it would be unthinkable to hold a referendum on secession without an explicit mandate from the people in an election.
“We should have at least as much respect for the democratic process here as Quebec separatists do there,” he said.
Notley agreed, saying the UCP needs to do some soul-searching to understand how “such a small tail on an otherwise completely respectable dog” has garnered the influence it has.
Speaking to reporters later Tuesday, Kenney said the UCP would not even exist as a party had loyalty to Canada not been agreed to by its founding parties.
“The commitment is clear, and separatists trying to infiltrate a federalist party are fundamentally dishonest and disrespectful of democracy,” he said.
He added that while as UCP leader, he invalidated some three dozen would-be candidates from running in the 2019 election because they had a record of advocating for separatism.
“You’re either for Canada, national unity, or you’re not, and if you’re still a citizen, you’re welcome to be involved in democracy. Go and do that in a separatist party,” said Kenney.
When asked to comment on Smith’s leadership, and willingness to accept separatism advocates in her caucus and party, Kenney declined to weigh in.
“I don’t want to be a Monday morning quarterback,” he said.
“When this is all over, I hope that the party that was elected twice as a federalist party, that was founded on federalist principles, will clearly be a federalist party.”
Notely, however, said the rest of Alberta is being “held hostage” by a small segment of the population.
She said Smith needs to eject members of caucus and cabinet who will not commit to staying in Canada.
“That’s exactly what the leader should do, and in failing to do that she is abdicating her obligation to Albertans and to Canadians.”
Smith has repeatedly said she will vote in favour of staying in Canada.
Despite some of her caucus members supporting separation or declining to say where they stand, Smith has emphasized that her party and government take the position that they support staying in Canada.
Smith has said every political party has a range of diverse views, but the majority view wins the day.

title: US Intelligence Still Flows to Ukraine, Sybiha Says
body:
Ukraine continues to receive intelligence from the US, Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said on Tuesday, Oct. 13, following concerns that Washington may have suspended the cooperation.
Speaking at the Warsaw Security Forum, Sybiha was asked about the absence of an advance air raid warning before Russia’s overnight ballistic missile attack.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
“You are probably asking me if we are receiving intelligence data from the American side. Yes, we continue this cooperation,” Sybiha said, according to The Guardian .
Sybiha did not disclose what types of intelligence Washington continues to provide or whether the scope of the cooperation has changed.
Sybiha confirmed that the air raid alert during Monday night’s Russian attack was activated late but said this was caused by the weapons Moscow used rather than an interruption in US intelligence sharing.
“It is also true that yesterday’s attack, or nighttime attack, the red alert was launched with a delay, but this was because of the special type of weaponry used by the Russian side,” he said.
Ukraine’s Air Force said it had not received prior information about the launches. The ballistic missiles were detected only after the attack was already underway.
Russia targeted Kyiv with approximately six ballistic missiles at around 10:10 p.m. on Monday, striking transport and warehouse facilities in several districts.
The attack came after a Russian drone struck a residential high-rise earlier in the day. Russian missile and drone attacks across Ukraine from Monday into Tuesday killed two women and injured nine people in Kyiv .
Ballistic missiles travel at extremely high speeds and follow trajectories that significantly reduce the time available to detect them, activate alerts, and reach shelter.
Questions over intelligence sharing emerged after reports that US officials had threatened to restrict military support unless Ukraine stopped striking Russian oil refineries.
During talks in Miami, US presidential envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner reportedly warned Ukrainian negotiators that Washington could suspend intelligence sharing if Kyiv continued its long-range attacks on Russia’s energy infrastructure.
A person familiar with the discussions also told Reuters that the US had raised the possibility of restricting weapons procurement through the Prioritized Ukraine Requirements List (PURL).
The reported threat followed US President Donald Trump’s calls for Ukraine to halt attacks on Russian refineries amid rising global diesel prices.
An assessment of the possible suspension found that losing US intelligence would particularly affect Ukraine’s early warning against ballistic missiles, although European intelligence and Ukraine’s own surveillance capabilities could replace part of the lost coverage.
Sybiha’s statement indicates that the reported restrictions have not been implemented.
Sybiha also argued that Ukraine’s position in relations with its partners had strengthened significantly during the war.
“In less than two years, we have gone from a situation where you have no cards in your hands to a stage where we are told not to play our cards,” he said at the Warsaw Security Forum, according to Ukrinform .
“This is our real achievement and an important lesson that we have learned,” Sybiha added.
He said Ukraine was defending the idea of freedom on the battlefield and paying a high price for it.
According to the foreign minister, the future of Europe, the global security architecture, and the fate of international law are now being decided in Ukraine.
“Ukraine’s front line is Europe’s first line of defense,” he said.
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: Alleged Financial Misconduct: El-Rufai Arrives In Kaduna High Court For Resumed Trial
body: Former Kaduna State Governor Nasir El-Rufai has arrived at the Kaduna State High Court for the continuation of his alleged corruption trial in a suit filed against him by the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC). The former Governor arrived at the court at about 11: 59 a.m., ahead of the hearing on the substantive trial, accompanied by the Governorship Candidate of the African Democratic Congress, Isah Ashiru, amid tight security. The former governor’s appearance followed an order by the Presiding Judge, Justice Darius Khobo, directing the anti-corruption agency to produce him in court for the resumed hearing. The case had been adjourned on Monday after El-Rufai was absent from court following information that he had requested to consult his personal medical doctor to review medical test results At Monday’s sitting, ICPC lead counsel, Ayodeji Adedipe, told the court that the prosecution had expected El-Rufai to be present despite a request by the lead defence counsel, Paul Erokoro, SAN, for an adjournment to attend the swearing-in ceremony of a new set of Senior Advocates of Nigeria at the Supreme Court. Adedipe explained that he had communicated with the defence over the scheduling of the proceedings and agreed to an adjournment for Monday, while proposing that the case continue on Tuesday. Tuesday’s proceedings are expected to advance the substantive trial, which involves allegations of corruption and other financial offences linked to transactions and decisions during El-Rufai’s tenure as Governor of Kaduna State between 2015 and 2023. The resumed hearing comes days after the Court of Appeal in Kaduna dismissed El-Rufai’s appeal challenging the refusal of bail by the state high court. In its judgment delivered on October 9, a three-member panel unanimously held that the former governor had failed to establish fresh facts or special circumstances warranting interference with the lower court’s decision. The lead judgment, delivered by Justice Onyekachi Aja Otisi, affirmed the ruling of the Kaduna State High Court, which had refused El-Rufai’s second bail application on June 10. The appellate court also struck out a reply brief filed by the appellant on September 29, describing it as incompetent, and resolved the issue before it against El-Rufai. During the appeal, Erokoro argued that the offences against his client were bailable and did not attract the death penalty. He maintained that continued detention was affecting the former governor’s ability to prepare adequately for his defence. The defence also argued that detention made access to lawyers and witnesses difficult and could affect confidential communication between the defendant and his legal team. The ICPC opposed the appeal, insisting that the trial court had exercised its discretion appropriately and that El-Rufai had not established sufficient grounds for the appellate court to overturn the decision. The Court of Appeal, however, dismissed the appeal for lacking merit. The former Governor has been in the custody of ICPC since February 18, 2026. Tuesday’s proceedings followed a series of adjournments and legal applications that have delayed the progress of the case. The post Alleged Financial Misconduct: El-Rufai Arrives In Kaduna High Court For Resumed Trial appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Syrskyi says redeploying troops from Kursk would not have changed situation near Pokrovsk
body:
According to Ukrinform, Syrskyi made these remarks in an interview with BBC News Ukrainian .
"No, it would not have been better. The point is that in the Kursk sector, the offensive grouping consisted of only three understrength Air Assault Forces brigades and two assault battalions," he said in response to a question about whether the resources should instead have been directed toward defending the eastern front.
According to Syrskyi, only one brigade took part in the offensive at full strength. Two other brigades initially operated with two battalions each, while the 95th Brigade had just emerged from heavy fighting in the Toretsk sector before the operation.
Other units involved in the operation were tasked with consolidating and holding the captured territory. Their personnel strength stood at approximately 60–70% of full capacity.
"So, if they had been deployed in the Pokrovsk sector—and we consider the Pokrovsk sector to include two directions, Dobropillia and Pokrovsk—the Russians had nearly 100,000 troops concentrated there. Those two brigades, and then another brigade, would not have made any difference, given their technical condition," the former commander-in-chief explained.
He said Ukraine's military leadership chose the Kursk direction after assessing the entire front line.
In early summer 2024, Russia was advancing along 13 operational axes, with its forces enjoying a numerical advantage of between 4.5 and six to one in some areas. At the same time, Russian defenses in the Sumy region had weakened after troops were redeployed to the Kharkiv direction.
"But the defenses in the Sumy sector had been significantly weakened, and there were virtually no active troops there. That is precisely why I made the decision to launch the offensive operation, which was approved by the President of Ukraine," Syrskyi said.
According to him, within a month, Ukrainian troops had taken control of 1,273 square kilometers of Russian territory.
Russia redeployed approximately 70,000 troops to the Kursk region, and its offensive operations came to a halt across all operational and strategic directions except Pokrovsk.
"This effectively gave us the opportunity to prepare reserves, give our troops a respite, and restore the combat effectiveness of units that had suffered losses in such intense fighting," Syrskyi said.
He added that Russian defenses in the Kursk sector had been weak. Border-guard units consisted primarily of conscripts and were spread thinly along the front, with individual positions separated by 10–12 kilometers.
After the Ukrainian offensive began, Russian forces redeployed units in a chaotic manner. Those units entered combat almost immediately and suffered significant losses.
According to Russian figures cited by Syrskyi, on some days the casualty ratio in the Kursk sector was one to five, unfavorable to Russian forces.
As previously reported, Ukrainian forces launched an operation in Russia's Kursk region on August 6, 2024, crossing the state border near the towns of Sudzha and Korenevo.

title: 17.9m Affected as Nigeria Records World’s Highest Rise in Multidimensional Poverty
body: An additional 17.9 million Nigerians fell into multidimensional poverty between 2021 and 2024, the highest increase recorded by any country globally, according to a new report by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) and the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI). The 2026 Global Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI), published on Monday, showed that Nigeria’s progress in reducing poverty between 2018 and 2021 was reversed in the subsequent three-year period, with millions more people experiencing overlapping deprivations in basic necessities. Nigeria recorded a significantly higher increase than Afghanistan, where an additional 5.3 million people fell into multidimensional poverty during the country’s latest assessment period. “In absolute terms, the largest increase in the number of poor people is seen in Nigeria, where although poverty had decreased in the previous period (2018–2021), in the recent period (2021–2024), 17.9 million people became multidimensionally poor, followed by 5.3 million in Afghanistan,” the report stated. The findings place Nigeria among five countries that recorded increases in multidimensional poverty during their respective assessment periods, alongside Afghanistan, the Central African Republic, Guinea and Kyrgyzstan. The development highlights the scale of Nigeria’s poverty challenge, particularly as rising living costs, food insecurity and inadequate access to essential services continue to put pressure on households. It also raises concerns about the sustainability of previous gains in poverty reduction and the country’s progress towards the United Nations’ target of significantly reducing poverty by 2030. Poverty rate rises to 38.7% The report’s harmonised historical comparison showed that Nigeria’s multidimensional poverty rate rose from 33 per cent in 2021 to 38.7 per cent in 2024, an increase of 5.7 percentage points. The number of people affected increased from 72.21 million to 90.07 million over the period, while the country’s Multidimensional Poverty Index value rose from 0.175 to 0.208, indicating worsening deprivation. However, a separate national estimate for 2024 put the number of Nigerians living in multidimensional poverty at 113.32 million, representing 48.7 per cent of the population. The report explained that the higher figure was based on the latest survey without the adjustments applied to the harmonised historical comparison. The two estimates therefore reflect different approaches to measuring poverty and should not be treated as directly interchangeable. It also found that 28.7 per cent of Nigerians experienced severe multidimensional poverty, while another 18.1 per cent were vulnerable to falling into multidimensional poverty. “In Nigeria, poverty incidence declined from 2018–2021, then increased from 2021–2024,” the report stated. What multidimensional poverty means Unlike conventional poverty measures that focus primarily on income or expenditure, the Global MPI assesses poverty by examining overlapping disadvantages in health, education and living standards. Its indicators include nutrition, child mortality, years of schooling, school attendance, access to electricity, drinking water, sanitation, housing and basic household assets. Under the methodology, a person is classified as multidimensionally poor when they experience deprivation in at least one-third of the weighted indicators. The approach captures forms of hardship that income-based measurements may not fully reflect. For instance, a household may earn some income but still lack clean water, adequate sanitation, electricity or access to education and healthcare. The index is designed to help governments identify not only how many people are poor but also the nature and severity of the disadvantages they face, providing a basis for more targeted policies and interventions. Northern states face heavier poverty burdens At the subnational level, the report found substantial differences in the extent and causes of multidimensional poverty across Nigerian states. Kebbi, Yobe and Sokoto were among the states with the highest multidimensional poverty burdens, while Lagos recorded the lowest MPI value. The findings also showed that states with similarly high poverty levels could face different underlying challenges. In Yobe, nutrition and child mortality contributed more significantly to deprivation, while inadequate access to water and electricity were stronger contributors in Sokoto. The report said identifying such differences was essential to designing interventions that address the specific needs of affected communities rather than relying on a uniform approach to poverty reduction. The findings point to the importance of improving basic services, including healthcare, education, electricity, water and sanitation, particularly in communities where several forms of deprivation occur simultaneously. Africa accounts for more than half of global poverty Globally, the report estimated that 1.2 billion people, representing 18.9 per cent of the population covered by the index, lived in acute multidimensional poverty. Of these, 534 million experienced severe poverty, while another 952 million people were classified as vulnerable to multidimensional poverty. Sub-Saharan Africa accounted for 616 million people living in multidimensional poverty, representing more than half of the global total. Children bore a disproportionate share of the burden, with 617 million people below the age of 18 classified as multidimensionally poor worldwide. “Roughly one in every three children is multidimensionally poor, compared to one in seven adults,” the report stated. The findings underscore the disproportionate impact of poverty on children, particularly in households where inadequate nutrition, poor living conditions and limited access to education and healthcare reinforce one another.

title: Scientists call for international body to oversee advanced AI
body: Around 400 scientists, including AI pioneers Geoffrey Hinton and Yoshua Bengio, on Tuesday, October 13, called for an international body to oversee containment standards and incident reporting for advanced cyber-capable AI systems. The proposed body would set industry-wide containment standards and maintain a registry of significant security incidents, which the scientists said should eventually be made public. In an open letter, the researchers said frontier AI models should initially be air-gapped from external networks and subject to independent oversight, arguing that voluntary industry commitments are not enough. The proposal comes a month after Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Meta, xAI, and Nvidia signed a White House accord committing to voluntary safety measures without any formal enforcement mechanism. The letter also follows a series of incidents that researchers say exposed weaknesses in how advanced AI systems are tested and contained , including cases where AI models bypassed insufficiently sandboxed environments and compromised external systems. The signatories from 34 countries said organisations developing or testing cyber-capable models should immediately adopt high-assurance containment standards while governments work towards a more formal oversight regime. Policymakers are increasingly debating how advanced AI systems should be supervised. EU tech chief Henna Virkkunen told Reuters on Friday, October 9, that the bloc’s AI Act is sufficient to address risks from rogue AI systems. On Sunday, October 11, the Trump administration lifted its block on US labs giving Britain’s AI Security Institute early access to models for safety testing. Hinton and Bengio shared the 2018 Turing Award with Meta’s Yann LeCun, another leading AI researcher. LeCun did not sign the letter and has argued that recent security incidents primarily reflect engineering failures rather than existential AI risks. – Rappler.com

title: Iran more concerned with economic war than armed confrontation — Majlis speaker
body:
RABAT, October 13. /TASS/. Iran is more concerned with countering sanctions and economic pressure right now than with armed confrontation, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, Speaker of the Majlis, the Islamic Republic’s unicameral parliament said.
"Today, economic warfare is more important than military confrontation or cyber warfare," Ghalibaf said, as quoted by the Tasnim news agency. In his view, economic pressure is "the main axis of the war against Iran, and the main task of the country’s authorities is to make the right decisions and ensure stable state governance."
The speaker of the Iranian parliament noted that the Islamic Republic "carefully assesses past events, and both the government and the parliament are trying to cope with the situation." "At present," Ghalibaf added, "the most important priority in our decision-making is the well-being of Iranians and the armed forces." According to him, "the state must ensure that the normal living conditions of the population are the last sphere to suffer from the pressure of war and the sanctions imposed against Iran."

title: Russian forces destroy over 260,000 military drones in Ukraine operation — top brass
body:
MOSCOW, October 13. /TASS/. Russian forces have destroyed over 260,000 Ukrainian military drones since the start of the special military operation in Ukraine, according to the latest report released by Russia’s Defense Ministry.
"In all, the following targets have been destroyed since the start of the special military operation: 674 aircraft, 284 helicopters, 260,703 unmanned aerial vehicles, 672 surface-to-air missile systems, 31,216 tanks and other armored combat vehicles, 1,787 multiple rocket launchers, 36,713 field artillery guns and mortars and 74,402 special military motor vehicles," the ministry said in a statement.
The Ukrainian army lost roughly 1,285 troops in battles with Russian forces in all the frontline areas over the past 24 hours, according to the latest data on the special military operation in Ukraine released by Russia’s Defense Ministry.
The latest figures show that the Ukrainian army lost over 270 troops, a tank and a field artillery gun in the responsibility area of Russia’s Battlegroup North, roughly 230 troops and an armored combat vehicle in the responsibility area of the Battlegroup West and about 160 troops and four armored combat vehicles in the responsibility area of the Battlegroup South.
During the last 24-hour period, the Ukrainian army also lost roughly 345 troops and seven armored combat vehicles in the responsibility area of Russia’s Battlegroup Center, over 240 troops and an armored combat vehicle in the responsibility area of the Battlegroup East and about 40 troops and two field artillery guns in the responsibility area of the Battlegroup Dnepr, the latest figures show.
Russia’s Battlegroup North forces are fighting for the liberation of three communities in the Kharkov Region and tightening the ring of encirclement of Ukrainian troops in that area, the ministry reported.
"Battlegroup North units are tightening the ring of encirclement in the Kharkov Region and expanding the outer area of control. In the pocket of encirclement, they are fighting for the liberation of the communities of Nikolayevka, Varvarovka and Nefyodovka in the Kharkov Region," the ministry said.
During the last 24-hour period, the Ukrainian army lost roughly 60 troops, a motor vehicle and five ground robotic platforms in the pocket of encirclement, it specified.
Battlegroup North forces are expanding the outer area of control and continue battles for taking control of the settlements of Prikolotnoye, Kotovka and Gogino in the Kharkov Region, the ministry said.
Russia’s Battlegroup North forces inflicted more than 270 casualties on Ukrainian troops and destroyed an enemy tank and a field artillery gun in its areas of responsibility over the past 24 hours, the ministry reported.
In the Kharkov direction, Battlegroup North units "inflicted losses on manpower and equipment of two mechanized brigades, a motorized infantry brigade of the Ukrainian army and a territorial defense brigade in areas near the settlements of Velikiye Prokhody, Khotomlya, Pogoreloye, Russkaya Lozovaya, Tsirkuny and Veliky Burluk in the Kharkov Region," the ministry said.
In the Sumy direction, Battlegroup North units struck formations of two mechanized brigades of the Ukrainian army and two territorial defense brigades in areas near the settlements of Glukhov, Yuryevo, Barilovka, Maryino, Konotop and Nikolskoye in the Sumy Region and the city of Sumy, it said.
Overall, the Ukrainian army lost more than 270 personnel, a tank, eight motor vehicles, a field artillery gun and an electronic warfare station in the areas of responsibility of Russia’s Battlegroup North over the past 24 hours, it specified.
Russia’s Battlegroup West inflicted roughly 230 casualties on Ukrainian troops and destroyed an enemy armored combat vehicle in its area of responsibility over the past day, the ministry reported.
"Battlegroup West units improved their forward positions and inflicted losses on manpower and equipment of two mechanized brigades, an assault brigade of the Ukrainian army and two territorial defense brigades in areas near the settlements of Grushevka, Blagodatovka, Berezovka, Maliyevka and Osinovo in the Kharkov Region and Volchy Yar in the Donetsk People’s Republic," the ministry said.
The Ukrainian army lost an estimated 230 personnel, an armored combat vehicle, 17 motor vehicles, three artillery guns and four electronic warfare stations in that frontline area over the past 24 hours, it said.
Russia’s Battlegroup South inflicted roughly 160 casualties on Ukrainian troops and destroyed four enemy armored combat vehicles in its area of responsibility over the past day, the ministry reported.
"Battlegroup South units gained better lines and positions and inflicted losses on formations of two mechanized brigades, an airmobile brigade of the Ukrainian army and a marine infantry brigade in areas near the settlements of Kramatorsk, Semyonovka, Slavyansk and Nikolayevka in the Donetsk People’s Republic," the ministry said.
The Ukrainian army lost an estimated 160 personnel, four armored combat vehicles, 31 motor vehicles and an artillery gun in that frontline area over the past 24 hours, it specified.
Russia’s Battlegroup Center forces liberated 286 buildings in Dobropolye in the Donetsk People’s Republic and destroyed roughly 65 Ukrainian troops over the past 24 hours, the ministry reported.
"In Dobropolye in the Donetsk People’s Republic, assault groups of the 51st Army advanced in the town’s central and northwestern parts. Some forces jointly with marine infantry formations continued mopping up the town’s quarters they had seized and the territory of the Dobropolskaya coalmine," the ministry said.
During the last 24-hour period, Battlegroup Center units liberated 286 buildings, including three production structures and eliminated roughly 65 Ukrainian troops in Dobropolye, it said.
Russia’s Battlegroup Center inflicted roughly 345 casualties on Ukrainian troops and destroyed seven enemy armored combat vehicles in its area of responsibility over the past day, the ministry reported.
"Battlegroup Center units inflicted losses on manpower and equipment of two mechanized brigades, an airborne brigade of the Ukrainian army and two National Guard brigades in areas near the settlements of Liman, Verovka, Belozerskoye, Svyatogorovka, Vesyolaya Gora, Maryevka and Novoyavlenka in the Donetsk People’s Republic," the ministry said.
The Ukrainian army lost an estimated 345 personnel, seven armored combat vehicles, eight motor vehicles, three field artillery guns and a Grad multiple rocket launcher in the responsibility area of Russia’s Battlegroup Center over the past 24 hours, it specified.
Russia’s Battlegroup East inflicted more than 240 casualties on Ukrainian troops and destroyed an enemy armored combat vehicle in its area of responsibility over the past day, the ministry reported.
"Battlegroup East units continued their advance deep into the enemy’s defenses and inflicted losses on manpower and equipment of a mechanized brigade, an air assault brigade, two assault regiments of the Ukrainian army and a marine infantry brigade in areas near the settlements of Gavrilovka and Tarasovka in the Dnepropetrovsk Region, Dudnikovo, Zalivnoye, Blakitnoye and Volnyanka in the Zaporozhye Region," the ministry said.
The Ukrainian army lost more than 240 personnel, an armored combat vehicle, eight motor vehicles and an artillery gun in that frontline area over the past 24 hours, it specified.
Russia’s Battlegroup Dnepr eliminated roughly 40 Ukrainian troops and destroyed two enemy field artillery guns in its area of responsibility over the past day, the ministry reported.
"Battlegroup Dnepr units gained better lines and positions and inflicted losses on formations of a mechanized brigade and a mountain assault brigade of the Ukrainian army in areas near the settlements of Orekhov and Kushugum in the Zaporozhye Region," the ministry said.
"Up to 40 Ukrainian military personnel, 20 motor vehicles, two field artillery guns and two electronic warfare stations were destroyed," it said.
Russian forces struck Ukrainian military-industrial sites, transport infrastructure facilities and enemy deployment areas over the past 24 hours, the ministry reported.
"Operational/tactical aircraft, attack unmanned aerial vehicles, missile troops and artillery of the Russian groups of forces struck Ukraine’s military-industrial and transport infrastructure facilities used by the Ukrainian army, workshops producing unmanned aerial vehicles and their storage sites, and also temporary deployment areas of Ukrainian armed formations and foreign mercenaries in 142 locations," the ministry said.
Russian air defense forces intercepted and destroyed 883 Ukrainian unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) over the past 24 hours, the ministry reported.
"Air defense capabilities shot down 883 fixed-wing unmanned aerial vehicles," the ministry said.

title: C5+1 and the Forgotten Geography of Central Asia
body: In modern diplomacy, Central Asia usually means five post-Soviet states: Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan. But how fixed are the region’s boundaries, and who gets to define them? Should Central Asia be understood as the five states that have emerged as a distinct political space? A broader historical and cultural region that includes Afghanistan, parts of Iran, western China, and Mongolia? Or an even more fluid system of economic, transportation, and strategic ties? New details about the origins of the C5+1 format involving the United States bring us back to precisely this question. Frederick Starr, one of the most consistent proponents of the Greater Central Asia concept, recently wrote that including Afghanistan was considered during early discussions of the American regional mechanism. In that case, the formula could have been C6+1. What makes this episode interesting is not that Afghanistan supposedly almost became the “sixth country of Central Asia.” More importantly, even before C5+1 was launched in 2015, there were different ways of understanding the region: political, historical and civilizational, and strategic. Those differences persist today, while closer relations with Afghanistan and Azerbaijan have once again raised questions about Central Asia’s boundaries. Political Central Asia and the C5 Politically, the definition is relatively clear. After the collapse of the Soviet Union, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan gradually developed from a geographical grouping into a distinct political category.
