C5+1 reflects precisely this logic. The joint declaration adopted in Samarkand on November 1, 2015, established regular cooperation between the United States and the five Central Asian states. Afghanistan was part of the regional agenda but was not included in the format itself. The “five plus an external partner” model has since proliferated. Germany uses the Z5+1 formula, from the German Zentralasien . Similar regional mechanisms operate with Japan, South Korea, the European Union, China, India, Russia, Italy, the Gulf Cooperation Council, and other partners. The proliferation of these formats reflects the extent to which external partners increasingly treat the C5 as a regional actor in its own right, while the five countries themselves are also increasingly acting in that capacity. But political Central Asia is not the only way to view the region. As part of UNESCO’s multivolume History of Civilizations of Central Asia project, the region was understood much more broadly. This historical and cultural space included not only the five former Soviet republics but also Afghanistan, northeastern Iran, Pakistan, northern India, western China, and Mongolia. UNESCO specifically noted that these were not rigid political boundaries but an area shaped by long-standing cultural and historical ties. This does not offer a “correct” alternative map. Rather, it shows that the region’s political, historical, and civilizational boundaries do not necessarily coincide. It was against this background that Starr proposed the concept of Greater Central Asia in 2005. This represented a third, strategic way of viewing the region. His idea was less about redrawing the geographical map than about changing American policy. In Starr’s view, the five post-Soviet republics and Afghanistan should be considered within a broader economic and infrastructure framework. Security, trade, energy, transportation, and access to South Asia were too closely connected to be separated into different areas of policy. Almost a decade later, this logic found practical expression. A joint Kazakh-American expert report published in 2014, Looking Forward: Kazakhstan and the United States , explicitly proposed creating a “Central Asia Six Plus One,” a permanent mechanism involving the United States, the Central Asian countries, and Afghanistan. This was an expert proposal rather than an agreed intergovernmental format. There is no evidence in the report that the C5 governments had agreed to treat Afghanistan as part of a common political framework. According to Starr’s recent account, however, the idea of a broader format subsequently reached the diplomatic level and was discussed by senior U.S. officials. This is not a dispute over which definition is “more correct.” Each answers a different question. C5 describes the political identity of the five states; the historical and civilizational approach describes an area of long-standing ties; Greater Central Asia offers a strategic framework for policy and infrastructure. Problems arise when one level is presented as another. Afghanistan and the Limits of the C5 Today, the question is becoming relevant again, but without a Western military presence in Afghanistan and in a very different political environment. In April 2026, the first “Afghanistan-Central Asia Consultative Dialogue” took place in Kabul, with representatives of all five Central Asian states participating. The name of the format itself is telling: Afghanistan and Central Asia appear as two sides of the dialogue. Kabul, however, promotes a broader interpretation. Afghan authorities speak of “regional convergence” and seek to present Afghanistan not as an isolated territory but as a connecting space between Central and South Asia. This is primarily Afghanistan’s vision of a desirable regional architecture. The C5 countries are more cautious. They are interested in a stable Afghanistan, are expanding trade, and support transportation and energy projects. For now, however, this is more about involving a neighboring country in regional processes than about revising Central Asia’s political framework. Even within the C5, there are differences in emphasis. Uzbekistan offers the broadest formulation. In 2025, Shavkat Mirziyoyev stated that Afghanistan is “not a periphery, but a natural part of our shared region.” For Tashkent, its inclusion is closely tied to transportation and economic connectivity between Central and South Asia. Kazakhstan uses more cautious language but also consistently opposes the isolation of Afghanistan. Kassym-Jomart Tokayev’s statements emphasize the country’s reconstruction, its involvement in regional and international processes, and the development of trade, infrastructure, and transportation links. This approach is consistent with Kazakhstan’s broader foreign policy principle of rejecting the logic of a “zero-sum game.” Tokayev has proposed replacing the traditional “Great Game” with a model of mutual benefit that he calls “Great Gain.” Applied to Afghanistan, that approach points toward integration primarily through economics, infrastructure, and multilateral mechanisms rather than through formally redefining the region’s boundaries. Tashkent and Astana therefore agree that Afghanistan should not remain isolated. But Uzbekistan is prepared to use an almost geographical formulation of shared regional belonging, while Kazakhstan places greater emphasis on practical engagement. Azerbaijan and a Different Kind of Expansion Against this background, proposals to expand C5+1 into C6+1 by adding Azerbaijan are particularly interesting. The U.S. format has not yet made that change and continues to operate officially as C5+1. But the political basis for including Azerbaijan is very different from the earlier Six Plus One proposal involving Afghanistan. In November 2025, the heads of the Central Asian states decided to grant Azerbaijan full participation in the Consultative Meetings of the Heads of State of Central Asia. This was not an external expert model but a decision by the region’s own countries. There is also a practical logic behind it. The Caspian Sea, the Middle Corridor, energy links, and growing transportation connectivity are bringing Central Asia and the South Caucasus ever closer together. Afghanistan and Azerbaijan therefore cannot be viewed in the same way in the context of a possible “sixth place.” They represent two different paths of external connectivity for the C5. The Afghan direction is developing primarily through trade, security, infrastructure, and separate dialogue mechanisms. Azerbaijan, by contrast, has already been incorporated into one of Central Asia’s main political consultation mechanisms by a decision of the Central Asian states themselves. This is perhaps where the main conclusion lies. External powers, international organizations, and schools of thought can propose their own versions of Central Asia, narrower or broader, based on history, culture, security, or transportation connectivity. This is how both the Greater Central Asia concept and the Six Plus One idea emerged. However, the political character of the region is increasingly being shaped by the Central Asian states themselves: through their own mechanisms of cooperation, their choice of partners, and their decisions about whom they are prepared to include and in what form. The question of Central Asia, therefore, has never been solely about how many countries to place before the “+1” sign. Far more important is what different participants understand by the region itself and what kind of Central Asia they want to see. Perhaps the main change of recent decades is that the answer to this question is increasingly being determined by the region itself rather than from outside.

title: West’s aggression against Russia also aimed at China, British politician argues
body:
BEIJING, October 13. /TASS/. In its aggression against Russia using Ukraine as a proxy, the West is also taking aim at China, George Galloway, leader of the Workers Party of Britain, told TASS.
"I think the [Western] aggression against Russia mounted by NATO, through the proxy of Ukraine is also aimed at China," he said on the premises of the Russian Cultural Centre in Beijing. "It's aimed at the emerging world power, which is the BRICS, the SCO, the Global South - all those who challenge the unipolar moment and seek to alter it," he argued.
Even as Beijing has not been a party to the Ukraine conflict, the Chinese side "knows that the same forces seeking to weaken Russia, balkanize Russia, break Russia, also have ambitions in that regard for them," Galloway continued.
The British politician shared his impressions from a recent trip to China: "We've seen China up close and personal in different cities. I think we are fully grasped of China's emerged greatness, and therefore can fully understand why the West is anxious about China seeking to de-risk from China, as they put it, which really means they consider China an adversary."
According to Galloway, "Russia faced this, has emerged from this, and is on the point of victory over this." "This is useful as a lesson to everybody in the emerging world, the new world that is struggling to be born," the politician continued. "The West hegemony has lasted hundreds of years - this is Roman empire levels of domination and longevity. Nobody gives up an empire like that easily, but they [Western countries] will have to give up," he emphasized.
The leader of the British party said the public in the EU knows that the bloc is currently at a crossroads. "They have to decide whether to carry on down the road they've been traveling or take the opportunity of an off-ramp. And I hope they'll do so," he noted.
Thus, Galloway explained, the British economy "is in ruins" amid the Western aggression, French society "is in flames," the German government is "in a slow motion for huge things are happening," while "the Greeks are on the march." These negative trends are all related to the Ukraine conflict, the politician concluded.

title: NCDC reports 1,138 lassa fever cases, 268 deaths
body: The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) has reported 1,138 confirmed Lassa fever cases and 268 deaths across 24 states, with the case fatality rate standing at 23.6 per cent. The agency said this in a statement on Monday, citing its Lassa Fever Situation Report for epidemiological weeks 39 and 40, covering Sept. 21 to Oct. 4, 2026. The report showed that the cumulative case fatality rate of 23.6 per cent was higher than the 18.6 per cent recorded during the corresponding period in 2025. According to the report, 24 states have recorded at least one confirmed Lassa fever case across 119 Local Government Areas (LGAs) nationwide. It stated that Bauchi, Ondo, Taraba, Benue and Edo accounted for 88 per cent of all confirmed cases recorded during the reporting period. The NCDC also identified people aged between 21 and 30 years as the predominant age group affected by the disease during the reporting period. The report further indicated that no new healthcare worker was infected with Lassa fever during epidemiological weeks 39 and 40. In week 40, covering Sept. 28 to Oct. 4, the country recorded three new confirmed cases, a decrease from the 13 cases reported in week 39. The three new cases in week 40 were reported in Bauchi and Benue states, according to the situation report. The cumulative figures for week 40 showed that 1,138 confirmed cases and 268 deaths had been recorded, representing a case fatality rate of 23.6 per cent. In week 39, covering Sept. 21 to Sept. 27, the NCDC recorded 13 new confirmed cases, compared with 11 cases reported in week 38. The 13 new cases in week 39 were reported in Ondo State, bringing the cumulative number of confirmed cases to 1,134 and deaths to 267. The case fatality rate for week 39 stood at 23.6 per cent, compared with 18.5 per cent recorded during the corresponding period in 2025. The NCDC’s situation report provides updates on confirmed cases, deaths, affected states and LGAs, as well as the distribution of infections among different age groups. “Lassa fever is an acute viral haemorrhagic illness transmitted primarily through contact with food or household items contaminated by infected rodents’ urine or faeces. “The disease can also spread through contact with the bodily fluids of an infected person, particularly in healthcare settings where appropriate infection prevention and control measures are not observed. “Members of the public are advised to maintain good environmental sanitation, store food in rodent-proof containers and avoid contact with rats to reduce the risk of infection,” it said. (NAN) The post NCDC reports 1,138 lassa fever cases, 268 deaths appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Ex-Liverpool defender Carragher settles tax debt to avoid bankruptcy
body: By Adegboyega Adeleye Former Liverpool and England defender Jamie Carragher will not be declared bankrupt after settling an unpaid tax debt to HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC). According to the BBC, an insolvency judge, Nicholas Briggs, dismissed a bankruptcy petition against the 48-year-old at the Insolvency and Companies Court on Tuesday after the tax authority confirmed that the debt had been paid. The petition was issued in August, with HMRC representative Kevin Hassan telling the court in London that Carragher had settled the outstanding bill. No exact amount was disclosed during the hearing, although the debt was previously estimated at between £700,000 and £800,000. Carragher spent his entire professional career at Liverpool and was part of the team that won the UEFA Champions League in 2005. The former defender retired in 2013 after making 737 appearances for the Premier League club. Since retiring from football, Carragher has built a career as a television pundit, regularly appearing on Sky Sports and CBS Sports. The post Ex-Liverpool defender Carragher settles tax debt to avoid bankruptcy appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: More than 300 advance polls open across Alberta in historic referendum on separation
body:
Albertans — some sporting Canadian flags on their clothes — trooped to the polls Tuesday to decide whether the province should still be a part of Canada.
Elections Alberta opened the doors at just over 300 polling stations for the first of five days of advanced voting ahead of the official Alberta referendum polling day on Oct. 19.
It was a day of long lineups, short lineups, a few tech glitches and, for comic relief, a face full of stickers.
In Edmonton, one downtown polling station saw a lineup that stretched almost half a block after doors opened at 9 a.m., with voters spending anywhere between 30 minutes and an hour to cast their ballots.
Some Edmonton voters wore their vote on their sleeves by donning hats or sweaters with the Canadian flag. One of them was Christopher Hashmi.
“It is obviously a bad idea,” Hashmi said of separation, adding that he thought Alberta would only be more vulnerable to the interests of the United States and oil and gas companies if the province went its own way.
Lizzy Somerville said it was patriotism that inspired her to vote to stay in Canada. “Canada works better together,” she said.
For Samara O’Hagan, the issue of separation comes down to concerns over who has the rights to the land.
“I’m Indigenous, so it’s very important to me,” she said.
“It would just be totally wrong, essentially stealing land from Indigenous people. Alberta should not be able to do that.”
Premier Danielle Smith has put 10 questions to a vote, including whether Alberta should remain in Canada or hold a second, binding referendum on quitting Confederation.
Smith is urging Albertans to vote yes for the remaining nine questions that call for Alberta to take more control of immigration and to work with other provinces to wrest more power from the federal government through changes to the Constitution.
Somerville said she voted against all but one of the premier’s proposals. She voted yes to lobbying other provincial governments to garner support for abolishing the Senate.
She said the upper house was “useless” and that if abolishment wasn’t an option, she’d like to see the seats be subject to elections rather than the current appointment process handled by the prime minister.
Hashmi said he voted “no to the nine” — a slogan used by critics and third-party advertisers pushing against Smith’s referendum proposals. Hashmi said he would have considered voting yes to that but felt doing so would be a sign of support for Smith’s government.
“Is the unelected Senate bad? Yes, it sucks. It is an archaic and broken part of our Constitution,” he said. “But Danielle Smith and her government are a broken and archaic part of my day-to-day life.”
In Calgary, there was no line for voters in the afternoon at a northeast polling station.
Chris Pichette said outside the polling station that she voted for Alberta to have a binding separation referendum and that she hopes the majority of voters do the same.
Pichette said she’d like to see Alberta stop sending money to Ottawa. “We get nothing in return for it,” she said.
Another Calgary voter, Kevin Chow, decorated his face with “I Voted!” stickers in hopes that it would encourage others to cast a ballot.
Chow said no country was perfect but that everyone was trying their best to make Canada succeed.
Opposition NDP Leader Naheed Nenshi cast his vote in Calgary on Tuesday and encouraged all Albertans to vote to stay Canada and reject the premier’s other nine proposals.
Nenshi said he was concerned about voter apathy on the pro-Canada side and said motivated separatists would benefit from a low voter turnout.
“They will crawl over broken glass to vote, and I don’t want pro-Canada voters to see a long line and go, ‘Oh, we’ve got it in the bag,'” Nenshi said.
Smith’s office said the premier will vote at advance polls later this week and will vote to stay in Canada.
Michelle Gurney, a spokesperson for Elections Alberta, said the first day of advanced voting was going well, but that there were minor delays at 17 polling stations due to technology issues (see list below.)
The agency said in a news release that the issues were fixed and that affected polling stations would stay open later to make up for it.
The start of advanced voting comes after Elections Alberta saw record interest in special ballots for the referendum. Roughly 658,000 Albertans requested to vote by mail.
Gurney said that as of Monday evening about 60 per cent of those ballots had been returned ahead of the Friday deadline.
Elections Alberta list of 17 advance voting locations with extended hours on Tuesday
More information about what to expect when voting can be found here .
— With files from Karen Bartko, Global News and The Canadian Press reporter Bill Graveland in Calgary

title: UN chief pledges to support peace, civilian protection in W. Equatoria
body: The Special Representative of the Secretary-General (SRSG) and Head of the United Nations Mission in South Sudan (UNMISS), Anita Kiki Gbeho, has pledged to strengthen cooperation with Western Equatoria State’s caretaker government to promote peace, protect civilians and improve humanitarian access in conflict-affected areas. She made the assurance on Tuesday in Yambio after meeting Caretaker Governor Badagbu Daniel Rimbasa and state officials during her maiden trip to the state since being appointed SRSG. “I came to consult with the governor and the authorities to understand the priorities for the state and also to talk with my colleagues who are here on the ground. The governor has been clear. His priority is peace; it is to build peace in Western Equatoria and to ensure that Western Equatoria is an example in South Sudan,” she said. “We talked about several areas that he would want to see us work together. The first is protection of civilians: we talked about a protection of civilians plan for some of the hotspot areas and then how we can look at implementing it.” “He [governor] mentioned he has declared an amnesty, so how he can be supported to redouble efforts to dialogue with those who are still bearing arms. We also talked about access. Following the governor’s conference, there has been an improvement in access,” SRSG Gbeho added. She welcomed the state government’s commitment to working with the United Nations to ensure humanitarian organisations could reach vulnerable communities, particularly those facing the greatest difficulties. She was accompanied by a high-level UN delegation, including a deputy force commander, the mission’s Director for Protection and Civil Affairs, and a Protection Adviser. Gbeho said the delegation’s presence reflected the mission’s commitment to supporting the state government’s peace and stability efforts. Governor Rimbasa reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to working with UNMISS to strengthen civilian protection, improve humanitarian access and address security challenges. He thanked the delegation for visiting the state, saying the government was ready to work with the mission. “We are committed to the protection of civilians. We want to thank the United Nations very much, on behalf of the government and people of Western Equatoria State, for taking the time to visit our state. We will work together on the issues we have discussed, and we will keep in touch,” he said. The governor commended UNMISS for its civilian protection efforts in Tambura and other parts of the state, saying the mission’s presence had supported communities affected by insecurity. He pledged government support for UNMISS movements and patrols, adding that cooperation was necessary to address insecurity and improve the delivery of humanitarian assistance. The governor further praised the mission’s quick-impact projects and capacity-building programmes involving young people, women, civil society organisations and traditional leaders. Meanwhile, Western Equatoria State Minister of Agriculture Gibson Bullen Wande called on UNMISS to consider supporting road maintenance, saying damaged roads and potholes could restrict movement and worsen security challenges. “Poor road conditions make it difficult for communities and security personnel to reach certain areas, potentially complicating efforts to address insecurity,” he stated. The visit comes as the caretaker government seeks to strengthen cooperation with international partners on civilian protection, reconciliation, humanitarian access, and stability across the state. The post UN chief pledges to support peace, civilian protection in W. Equatoria appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

title: Kumasi: One injured, shops destroyed in Atasemanso fire in Kumasi
body: One person has been injured, and a pregnant woman left homeless after a fire destroyed four container shops and two rooms at Atasemanso in Kumasi, the Ashanti Regional capital. The blaze, which is suspected to have been triggered by a gas cylinder explosion, destroyed property and merchandise worth millions of cedis, including several bales of second-hand clothing, leaving traders and residents devastated. Residents described scenes of panic as the fire engulfed the structures, forcing people to scramble to safety while shop owners watched helplessly as their investments went up in flames. Speaking to Joy News, one woman, visibly distressed by the situation, said she had nowhere to spend the night following the incident. “We have nowhere to go. We don’t know where to sleep today. Help me,” she pleaded. For the traders, the losses represent a major financial setback, while residents who have lost their rooms now face the immediate challenge of securing alternative accommodation. The Assembly Member for Atasemanso, Abdul Samid, confirmed that one woman sustained injuries and was taken to Atasemanso Hospital for treatment. Preliminary investigations, he said, suggest that a gas cylinder explosion may have triggered the fire. According to him, the swift intervention of personnel from the Ghana National Fire Service (GNFS) prevented the fire from spreading to nearby houses. The Ashanti Regional Command of the GNFS says it will step up monitoring of markets and other locations identified as vulnerable to fire outbreaks. Arthur Arhin Mensah, the command’s Public Relations Officer, said officers would conduct patrols during the day and at night to improve surveillance and ensure compliance with fire safety regulations. Mr Arhin Mensah also urged the public to cooperate with fire officers during the exercise, as the Service steps up efforts to enforce safety requirements and reduce the risk of further incidents.

title: Oil-Contaminated Birds Found On Shore By Drone-Hit Russian Tanker
body:
Sea birds covered with oil were found on Monday dead and dying on Black Sea beaches dozens of kilometers from a tanker attacked and disabled by Ukrainian drones, contradicting official Russian statements the vessel was structurally intact and environmentally-threatening amounts of product had not leaked into local waters.Images published by the Anapa-based regional wildlife protection group Zhemchuzhnaya Reabilitatsionniy Tsenter (Zhemchuzhnaya Rehabilitation Center) on Sunday and Monday showed seagulls, grebes, pigeons and a white swans soiled with oil and needing treatment. Some of the birds had been found on local beaches unable to move, a worker said in an appeal for donations and volunteers to help with cleaning.
The local news platform Ostorozhno Novosti in a Sunday report showed rescue workers washing petroleum-based gunk from the feathers of seabirds and globs of congealed diesel oil washed up on the sea shore near the village Abrau-Dyurso, some 200+ km (124 miles) from the scene of the attack on a 100,000+ ton tanker off-shore the seaside resort city Sochi on Oct. 6.
Zhora Kavanosyan, a Sochi-based ecologist, in a Monday Telegram report said beach-walkers found some oil-covered birds near the villages of Lazarevsky, Sosnovka and the city of Gedzhelik, all seaside resorts in the heart of the the Black Sea’s “Russian Riveria” region.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
The damaging Ukrainian drone strike hit the Fiberia-flagged Aframax Rio 30 km (19 miles) off shore Sochi, setting the vessel ablaze and forcing the crew to abandon ship.
Sochi- and Krasnodar-based officials in the wake of the attack closed beaches temporarily but re-opened them the next day after declaring the fires aboard the Aframax under control and pollution to local waters minimal. For almost 24 hours after the attack, the tanker burned fiercely in waters off Sochi and beachgoers recorded burning oil flowing out of storage tanks into the sea.
Initially adrift, the vessel by Tuesday had been surrounded by oil containment buoys at an anchorage “beyond greater Sochi”, and “no evidence of oil slicks was visible”, a Transportation Ministry comment to Kavanosyan said. A report by the Russia-watch group Supernova+ said that the ship had been towed to the vicinity of the port Novorossiysk and work to empty the tanker’s bunkers had begun.
Geo-located social media video from Novorossiysk showed the ship completely blackened by fire, listing heavily to starboard and with forward decks nearly awash. Video recorded by local yachtsmen showed a charred Afromax anchored 2-3 miles (3.2 to 4.8 km) off shore the Novorossiysk resort village of Kabardinka.
Ukraine has accused Russia of using the Aframax as a shadow tanker to evade international sanctions on Russian crude oil and fuel exports. Marine traffic tracking platforms showed the vessel’s transponder had been turned off for almost a month and put its last tracked location, inaccurately, well to the south, off shore Georgia.
Russia’s Greenpeace branch in a Friday statement said the Aframax Rio following damaging hits by Ukrainian drones had spilled oil and potentially lost some of its structural integrity, and that the abandoned vessel drifting northwards parallel to the shore posed a serious threat to local wildlife and wetlands.
“Russian authorities’ claims that this incident did not result in environmental pollution are false…It can be said that this is serious pollution that will impact the ecosystems of the Black Sea,” the Greenpeace statement said in part. “[T]he threat of a major spill remains until all the contents are pumped out of the takes. The current condition of the ship’s hull is unknown, so it’s impossible to assess the likelihood of a further spill.”
In December 2024 two Russian tankers, the Volgoneft-212 and the Volgoneft-239, sank in the Kerch Strait, spilling most of their cargo into the sea over the winter. Thousands of birds died as a result along with at least 700 dolphins, Greenpeace tracking of those sinkings reported.
Ukraine in mid-July 2026 launched a martime drone strike campaign targeting Russian tanker traffic in the Black and Azov Seas, with shadow tankers thought by Kyiv to be assisting Moscow in evading international sanctions top priority targets for drone operators.
According to claims by Ukraine’s Unmanned Systems Forces (USF), since then through September, Ukrainian aircraft had hit or disabled 300+ Russian shadow tankers, of which 134 were hit in the Sea of Azov and 166 in the Black Sea.
Among the most spectacular attacks was a pair of November sea drone strikes that disabled the tankers Kairos and Virat off Turkey’s Black Sea coast, and a December 2025 aerial drone that hit the suspected shadow tanker Quendil in the central Mediterranean.Thanks to high oil prices and pressing Kremlin need for overseas cash earnings, Russian export of crude and petroleum products from its Black Sea ports has continued at reduced volumes. According to open source ship movement tracking platforms, Russian tanker traffic westward into the Black Sea escapes are roughly 1/3 pre-full-scale-war levels.
A Black Sea Grebe covered with crude oil rests on a beach near the Russian village Larzerovsky. (Image published by the Russian ecological researcher Zhora Kavanosyan on Oct. 11 on Telegram.)
A Black Sea Grebe covered with crude oil rests on a beach near the Russian village Larzerovsky. (Image published by the Russian ecological researcher Zhora Kavanosyan on Oct. 11 on Telegram.)
Stefan Korshak is the Kyiv Post Senior Defense Correspondent. He is from Houston Texas, is a Yalie and since the mid-1990s has worked as correspondent/photographer for newswire, newspapers, television and radio. He has reported from five wars but most enjoys doing articles on wildlife and nature. You can read his weekly blog on the Russo-Ukraine War on Facebook, Substack and Medium. His new book on the 2022 Siege of Mariupol is available on Amazon UK and Amazon US .

title: Wike admits working with APC to defeat PDP in 2024 Edo governorship election
body:
The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, has admitted collaborating with members of the All Progressives Congress (APC) to defeat his own party, the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in the 2024 Edo State governorship election, saying he has no regrets about his role.
Mr Wike said the alliance was deliberately formed to prevent former Governor Godwin Obaseki of Edo from installing a successor, acknowledging that the collaboration between sections of the PDP and the APC helped the ruling party win the election.
“I was behind it, and I don’t have any regrets about it,” he said.
According to T he Punch , the minister spoke on Monday at a stakeholders’ meeting of the Rainbow Coalition, a cross-party political platform mobilising support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election in 2027.
The admission reinforces Mr Wike’s history of working across party lines to influence electoral outcomes, including his role in the 2023 presidential election, when he and four other aggrieved PDP governors refused to support their party’s candidate, Atiku Abubakar.
In September 2026, Mr Wike disclosed how the G-5 governors devised strategies to prevent Atiku from benefiting from the PDP’s traditional electoral strength in parts of the South-south, particularly Edo and Cross River states.
Speaking on TVC’s Journalists’ Hangout, he said the group considered the PDP’s strength in the region a potential advantage for Atiku and deliberately sought to redirect votes to the Labour Party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, in some states.
“How did he win? When the G-5, we sat, we had our strategy. We said in Edo, PDP is stronger in the South-south. Our problem will be Atiku. Therefore, instead of Atiku to take it, let it go to the Labour Party. That was our strategy. Cross River, the same thing. That’s what we did,” he said.
Mr Wike also said Rivers State was deliberately treated differently because the group feared the political implications of Mr Obi winning the state.
“It was only Rivers that said, ‘No, we have a problem here in Rivers. Obi will not win here because if he wins, he sends a signal somewhere, people may not understand it.’ And we stopped…we stopped it,” he said.
The remarks offered a rare public account of the political calculations behind the G-5 governors’ opposition to Mr Atiku, despite their membership of the PDP.
The group comprised Mr Wike, then Rivers governor; Seyi Makinde of Oyo State; Samuel Ortom of Benue State; Okezie Ikpeazu of Abia State; and Ifeanyi Ugwuanyi of Enugu State.
The governors had demanded the resignation of the PDP’s then national chairman, Iyorchia Ayu, arguing that the party’s presidential candidate and national chairman should not both come from the North after eight years of northern leadership under President Muhammadu Buhari.
Their dispute with the PDP leadership continued into the 2023 general election, when Mr Wike openly maintained that his priority was the emergence of a southern president rather than the victory of a particular candidate.
Mr Tinubu, the APC candidate, won the presidential election, while Atiku finished second and Mr Obi third nationally.
In Rivers, where Mr Wike was governor, the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) declared Mr Tinubu the winner with 231,591 votes, against Mr Obi’s 175,071 and Mr Atiku’s 88,468.
However, PREMIUM TIMES later reviewed results uploaded to INEC’s Results Viewing Portal and found substantial discrepancies in Obio/Akpor Local Government Area, Mr Wike’s political stronghold. The newspaper’s review indicated that Mr Obi had won the state based on the polling-unit results it examined, although missing, illegible and improperly uploaded results limited the scope of the independent tally.
In March 2023, Mr Wike denied directing Rivers residents to vote against Mr Obi, saying he had urged them to support national unity. He also criticised the PDP leadership for failing to resolve the crisis that preceded the election.
Mr Wike’s latest admission concerns the September 2024 Edo governorship election, which the APC’s Monday Okpebholo won with 291,667 votes.
The PDP candidate, Asue Ighodalo, polled 247,274 votes, while the Labour Party candidate, Olumide Akpata, received 22,763 votes, according to INEC’s announced results.
Mr Wike said his opposition to Mr Ighodalo was not based on the candidate’s qualifications. Rather, he said, he wanted to prevent Mr Obaseki from retaining political influence through his successor.
He recalled that Mr Ighodalo visited his residence several times to seek his support, but he declined to back him.
“He came to my house more than three times. I said, listen, you’re a good candidate. But for this election, I’m sorry,” Mr Wike said.
He said he told Mr Ighodalo that supporting his candidacy would amount to returning Mr Obaseki to power indirectly.
“This election is between us and the man who is bringing you, Governor Obaseki, an ingrate person, ungrateful person. So returning you is like bringing him back. So I’m sorry. You have to fail. And he failed,” he said.
Mr Wike said the result showed that political alliances across party lines were an established feature of Nigerian elections.
“So when people say that nothing like coalition, they tell lies. The truth of the matter is that it has been there depending on how it is worked out,” he said.
He specifically credited the collaboration between PDP loyalists and APC members with Mr Okpebholo’s victory, saying former APC national chairman Adams Oshiomhole could attest to the alliance.
Mr Wike’s latest comments follow political manoeuvring ahead of the 2027 general election and disagreements within the APC over the Rainbow Coalition.
The minister has promoted the coalition as a platform through which politicians from different parties can mobilise support for Mr Tinubu’s re-election without necessarily abandoning their existing party affiliations.
Mr Wike remains a member of the PDP, despite serving in Mr Tinubu’s APC-led federal government. His support for the president has repeatedly put him at odds with sections of his party, which has struggled with internal divisions and questions over its political direction.
At Monday’s meeting, Mr Wike also declared himself coordinator of Mr Tinubu’s re-election campaign in the FCT and Rivers State.
Participants drawn from the PDP and APC reportedly agreed to work together for Mr Tinubu’s second term and support APC candidates for the FCT senatorial and House of Representatives seats.
The latest declaration further shows Mr Wike’s willingness to pursue electoral alliances across party lines, even when doing so means campaigning against candidates of the party to which he formally belongs.

title: One injured in drone strike on Kharkiv shopping center – mayor
body:
A Russian drone attacked a shopping center in the Shevchenkivsky district of Kharkiv, injuring one person, Kharkiv Mayor Ihor Terekhov reported.
"The Shevchenkivsky district is under enemy strike – a drone attacked the building of one of the shopping centers, one person was injured," Terekhov wrote on his Telegram channel.

title: Global economy proving resilient, growth projected at 3.1% in 2026 – IMF
body: The International Monetary Fund says the global economy is again proving resilient, but unevenly so and with rapidly narrowing margins of adjustment in the near term. According to its October 2026 World Economic Outlook, activity in the first half of 2026 held up better than expected despite the dragging war in the Middle East and continuing strains from trade tensions. It said the technology cycle has provided a demand impulse, driven by strong investment in artificial intelligence (AI). “The interaction of these forces—geopolitics and technology—has produced a split global economy: Favorable terms of trade or technology-related exports and investment give some countries a cushion, whereas others face higher import bills and weaker demand”. Meanwhile, global growth is projected at 3.1% in 2026 and 3.4% in 2027, unchanged for 2026 and revised moderately upward for 2027. This is relative to the projections in the April 2026 World Economic Outlook (WEO). Global headline inflation is also projected to increase to 4.7% in 2026 before easing to 4.1% in 2027, marking a cumulative upward revision of 0.7 percentage point with the temporary increase driven mainly by energy and food prices. World Trade Volume to Slow Again, the Bretton Woods institution said world trade volume growth is projected to slow in 2026 and stabilise in 2027, reflecting the drag from tariffs, adjustment in production chains, and continued strength in technology-related trade. Also, global imbalances are expected to decline only modestly over the medium term, as large fiscal deficits, limited domestic rebalancing, technology-driven capital flows, and differing demand compositions across major economies under current policies continue to sustain external gaps. It said the medium-term growth outlook remains lackluster by historical standards and uneven across countries, in part reflecting varying degrees of AI preparedness and robustness of the energy mix. Risks Skewed to Downside The IMF also stressed that risks are skewed to the downside. According to the Washington-based firm, a prolonged stalemate or further escalation in the Middle East could keep energy and food prices elevated and volatile, revive inflationary pressures, worsen fiscal and external balances, and weigh on growth. It said further disruptions to energy infrastructure, cyberattacks, or extreme weather events could amplify these effects. “As the Commodity Special Feature shows, price increases driven by physical supply disruptions have larger and more persistent macroeconomic effects than those driven by geopolitical risks. A reassessment of AI-related profitability and productivity prospects could sharply reduce investment, trigger equity market corrections, and tighten financial conditions, with spillovers to economies integrated into technology supply chains and stakes in technology stocks”, it added.

title: Two childcare workers questioned after toddlers found alone, nearly one km. from daycare
body: Police detained two daycare staff members for questioning on Monday after toddlers left a Petah Tikva childcare facility and were found riding toy cars on a nearby street without adult supervision, Israel Police announced on Tuesday.The women, Petah Tikva residents in their 40s and 50s, were released after questioning under restrictive conditions, police said on Tuesday. The announcement did not specify those conditions or identify the suspected offenses.The investigation began Sunday after police received a report of young children wandering alone near the facility. Officers arrived, located the toddlers, and arranged for them to be returned to their parents.Investigators have since taken statements, collected evidence, and used technological tools to examine the circumstances, the police said.Earlier reports by N12 News and Walla, drawing on a mother's account, described children aged about two leaving the daycare, with three reportedly reaching roughly a kilometer away. According to that account, the three crossed at a pedestrian crossing and reached an area near a busy road before a member of the public spotted them and called the police.The six children were all located and safely returnedBoth outlets reported that six children had left the premises and that all were located. The mother told N12 that about 15 minutes after dropping off her son on Sunday morning, the daycare manager called to say he had left the premises and staff could not find him. She described suddenly having to search for a child she had just entrusted to the facility's care.According to the account carried by N12 and Walla, one staff member was supervising more than 20 children in the yard while two others washed the floor. Another mother's search for a ride-on toy led to the discovery that the exit gate was open and children were missing.The mother's account described four children leaving on ride-on toys and two on foot. One girl was found on steps near the daycare's emergency gate and two other children in a public playground. She said the remaining three were located after a search lasting about 15 minutes.N12 and Walla further reported that municipal and supervisory officials, including personnel responsible for early childhood education in Petah Tikva, were informed. The mother called for a thorough examination of how the children had been able to leave and for measures to prevent another incident.

title: Accused Cornell University student asks for gag order
body:
Lawyers for Diego Sarabia are seeking to prevent public comments about the case.
Lawyers for one of the men named in a civil lawsuit brought by a former Cornell University student who alleged she was sexually assaulted at a school fraternity in 2024 is asking a New York judge to impose a gag order in the case, arguing the publicity surrounding the case risks tainting potential jurors.
Attorneys for Diego Sarabia on Monday asked for "narrowly tailored restrictions" that would prevent lawyers and parties in the civil case from commenting on the allegations outside of court.
"Since this action began, Plaintiff's counsel has repeatedly addressed the merits through widely disseminated media statements," the motion said. "These statements present disputed allegations and interpretations of evidence to the public before discovery and trial."
A then-undergraduate student identified only as Jane Doe made a complaint to campus police in November 2024, three weeks after the incident occurred, that she had been raped by a group of men at the Chi Phi fraternity house. She has filed a civil suit against the men and the university alleging that she had been drugged and raped.
No criminal charges have been filed, but an investigation by the New York attorney general is ongoing.
The case has rocked the university and started conversations about treatment of alleged sexual assault on college campuses across the country.
James Knox, an attorney for Sarabia, argued that a gag order would limit "possible juror prejudice" and prevent the potential release of sensitive information that could lead to " threats, doxing, intimidation, and extrajudicial contact." Knox also submitted to the court a list of what he described as "prejudicial statements" made by Thomas Giuffra, an attorney for Jane Doe.
"Plaintiff's counsel has been trying his case in the media since filing the lawsuit," the motion alleged. "A full cataloguing of the media tour he has engaged in would be far lengthier than necessary to establish the potential risks these statements are incurring upon the fair administration of justice in this case and upon the parties."
In a statement responding to the motion, Giuffra said, "The Defense has tried to rebut the claims in this case by engaging in a wholesale leaking of confidential documents, giving interviews calling Ms. Doe's story into question and calling her lawsuit immoral. These attempts to shift the narrative have not been successful."
"The Defense is now attempting to silence me and Ms. Doe because we have been so successful in rebutting their ineffectual attempts to undermine her story," the statement said. "Truth always wins out."
Sarabia is accused in the lawsuit of grabbing and kissing Jane Doe before "pouring lines of Ketamine all over her body and snorting them." He has denied wrongdoing, and according to Cornell documents reviewed by ABC News, he previously argued that the interaction was consensual.
Last week, a member of the Marine Corps who shares the same name as one of the defendants in the case asked the court to restrict some of the filings in the case because he and his family have been the subject of "continued and ongoing harassment, including death threats from members of the public."
Judge Phaedra Perry-Bond agreed to seal some of the filings on Friday, condemning what she described as "misguided vigilantism."
"This Court strongly condemns the reported acts of threats and doxing, which can only be characterized as brash, reckless, and ultimately dangerous internet vigilantism, " the judge wrote. "Our society has developed procedures and legal mechanisms over the course of centuries to ensure justice and due process are afforded to all. When certain actors decide to work outside those robust and developed frameworks, innocent people often get hurt. That is precisely what has happened here."
24/7 coverage of breaking news and live events

title: Raytheon says Coyote and KuRFS enter export market with Qatar and Jordan contracts
body: Both are components of the Army’s Low, slow, small, unmanned aircraft Integrated Defeat System, or LIDS. The contracts cover a mix of fixed-site and mobile configurations. KuRFS provides 360-degree threat detection, while Coyote kinetic and non-kinetic effectors engage individual drones and swarms. Raytheon said Coyote has achieved hundreds of combat intercepts. “LIDS provides a proven and cost-effective layer of defense that ensures allied forces have the protection they need against hostile drones,” said Tom Laliberty, president of Land and Air Defense Systems at Raytheon. “To stay ahead of rapidly evolving drone threats, Raytheon is accelerating production of the Coyote family of effectors — delivering a uniquely scalable, battle–tested solution that meets the surge in global demand.” The awards reflect growing demand for dedicated counter-drone defenses, including kinetic weapons that destroy incoming aircraft. Russia’s war against Ukraine and the recent U.S.-Iran confrontation in the Gulf have demonstrated the need for this equipment. Counter-drone systems serve both deployed forces and installations away from the battlefield. Their roles include protecting personnel, military bases, critical infrastructure and important government and civilian facilities. Iranian drone attacks that damaged sites in U.S.-allied Gulf countries have added urgency to regional procurement. The scale of that damage has highlighted the need for sufficient quantities of counter-drone weapons to defend against repeated attacks. RTX is investing in production capacity and new technology for the Coyote family. Upgrades include faster launch times, higher speeds and greater range at higher altitudes. Raytheon did not disclose the quantities ordered or delivery schedules. It also did not provide a breakdown of the $729 million among the three customers.

title: Jos primary school pupils learn on bare floors as poor facilities raise health concerns
body:
A concerned citizen has petitioned the government over the condition of facilities at Garba Daho Primary School in Jos North Local Government Area of Plateau State .
Pupils attend the school amid dilapidated classroom structures, inadequate furniture and poorly maintained toilets, raising concerns about their safety, health and learning conditions.
In a petition dated 13 October, Ismail Rabiu, an education stakeholder from Garba Daho Ward, urged the authorities to rehabilitate the school urgently, calling for improved classrooms, basic learning facilities and better sanitation.
Mr Rabiu appealed to the Plateau State Universal Basic Education Board (SUBEB), the Ministry for Local Government and Chieftaincy Affairs, and the Jos North Local Government chairman to inspect the school and take immediate steps to improve its condition.
When a PREMIUM TIMES’ reporter visited the school, they observed deteriorating classroom structures, cracked floors and inadequate furniture for pupils.
The school’s toilets were also in poor condition, raising concerns about hygiene and potential health risks.
The condition of the facilities highlights the challenges pupils face in accessing a safe and conducive learning environment, where damaged infrastructure and inadequate sanitation can undermine their wellbeing and ability to learn.
Mr Rabiu was concerned that the pupils lacked basic facilities, including desks, chairs and adequate teaching and learning materials.
He also urged the authorities to prioritise emergency repairs.
“Our children deserve to learn in dignity. Save them today,” Mr Rabiu said in the petition.
Mr Rabiu called on SUBEB and the Plateau State Government to conduct an on-site assessment of the school and determine the immediate interventions required to address its structural and sanitary problems.
The petitioner said addressing the school’s condition was necessary to protect pupils and provide them with an environment suitable for learning.
Mr Rabiu described Garba Daho as a major commercial centre in Jos, citing Terminus Market, Metal Market, Abuja Market, Yan Doya, Yan Kwalabe and Kasuwan Dare among the markets and commercial areas in the ward.
He also listed several financial institutions, the National Orthopaedic Hospital and other commercial establishments as part of the area’s economic importance.
Despite the community’s significance, he said the condition of the primary school required urgent attention from the relevant authorities.
Mr Rabiu stressed that his appeal was not intended to antagonise the local government leadership but to draw attention to the needs of children attending the public school.
He urged the Jos North Local Government chairman, SUBEB and the state government to ensure that pupils have access to functional classrooms, adequate furniture, essential learning materials and hygienic toilets.
The petition calls for a physical inspection of the school and prompt action to address the problems identified.

title: NDC targets all 6 parliamentary seats in Ahafo Region for 2028
body: The National Democratic Congress (NDC) in the Ahafo Region has declared its intent to sweep all six parliamentary seats in the region during the 2028 general election. Regional party executives say they’re poised to render the sole remaining New Patriotic Party (NPP) Member of Parliament in the region, Dr Gideon Boako, a one-term lawmaker. The party also expressed confidence in expanding its presidential vote margin beyond the 52.54 per cent secured by President John Dramani Mahama in the 2024 presidential polls. In the 2024 general elections, John Dramani Mahama led the NDC to a decisive victory in the region, polling 130,106 votes, representing 52.54 per cent to defeat the NPP’s Dr Mahamudu Bawumia, who garnered 113,851 votes, recording 45.98 per cent The NDC flipped three traditional NPP strongholds, namely Asutifi North, Tano South, and Asunafo North, adding them to its long-held strongholds of Asutifi South, represented by Collins Dauda, and Asunafo South, represented by Eric Opoku. The victory handed the NDC five out of the six seats in the region, leaving the NPP with only the Tano North seat, currently occupied by Dr Gideon Boako, Economic Adviser to former Vice President Dr Mahamudu Bawumia. Speaking at Yamfo in the Tano North municipality during the swearing-in ceremony of newly elected executives for the Yamfo College of Health chapter of the Tertiary Education Institutions Network (TEIN-NDC), party executives laid out their plans for the 2028 campaign. The Ahafo Regional Vice Chairman of the NDC, Joseph Baradoe, stated that the party nearly won the Tano North seat in 2024 but faced a few challenges at the time. He noted that the leadership has since resolved every obstacle and is putting potent measures on the ground to secure a full sweep in 2028. The Regional Vice Chairman emphasised that having successfully snatched three long-standing NPP constituencies with wider margins, taking the final seat is well within reach, charging student organisers and TEIN members to double their efforts in selling the party’s message. Adding to the call, the NDC Regional Youth Organiser, Sulemana Masahudu, criticised the incumbent MP’s performance, asserting that despite Dr Boako serving as the Economic Adviser to the former Vice President for eight years, key infrastructure, including road networks in his hometown, remained unaddressed. He argued that if development was not delivered while holding a key position in government, little could be expected now from him as an opposition MP. The Youth Organiser charged the youth across the region to exhibit commitment, hard work, and determination to retain the five NDC seats and claim the final one held by the NPP.

title: Nigeria vs Comoros Preview: Super Falcons eye third-round ticket in Olympic race
body:
The Super Falcons will look to finish the job against Comoros on Tuesday when both sides meet in the second leg of their second-round tie in the race to qualify for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games.
Nigeria head into the return fixture with a two-goal advantage after securing a 2-0 victory in the first leg on Friday, 9 October, and will be aiming to book their place in the third round of the African qualifying series.
The encounter will take place at the Remo Stars Stadium in Ikenne, Ogun State, with kick-off scheduled for 4:00 pm Nigerian time.
Interim head coach Augustine Eguavoen has the immediate task of guiding the 10-time African champions through the tie, with a meeting against Morocco awaiting the aggregate winners.
Michelle Alozie broke the deadlock three minutes into the second half of the first leg, before Uchenna Kanu doubled Nigeria’s advantage in the 60th minute, giving the Super Falcons a valuable cushion ahead of Tuesday’s showdown.
Although Nigeria remain firmly in control of the contest, Eguavoen’s side will need to combine defensive discipline with greater efficiency in front of goal to avoid giving Comoros any hope of mounting a comeback.
Super Falcons enjoy home advantage as Comoros return to Ikenne
Despite the first encounter being designated as Comoros’ home fixture, both legs of the qualifying tie are taking place in Nigeria.
Comoros do not have a CAF-approved stadium available to host the match, forcing the island nation to stage its nominal home leg on Nigerian soil. The return fixture will also be played at the Remo Stars Stadium, this time with Nigeria officially designated as the home team.
The arrangement means the Super Falcons have enjoyed the familiarity of playing in Nigeria across both encounters, although the first-leg victory still had to be earned on the pitch.
With the tie now returning to Ikenne, the Nigerians will hope to make the most of their advantage and complete qualification for the next round without unnecessary complications.
Nigeria secured the result they needed in the opening encounter, but their performance also highlighted areas that require improvement.
The Super Falcons created opportunities during the first half but struggled to convert their pressure into goals. They eventually found a breakthrough after the interval, with Alozie opening the scoring in the 48th minute before Kanu headed home from a Jennifer Echegini corner 12 minutes later.
The two goals provided Nigeria with a clean sheet and a commanding aggregate advantage, but the attacking wastefulness before the break was one of the talking points after the game.
Eguavoen acknowledged the team’s difficulties with the final ball and explained that the coaching staff addressed the issue during half-time.
Tuesday’s fixture offers the Super Falcons another opportunity to sharpen their attacking play while maintaining the defensive organisation that helped them keep Comoros at bay in the first leg.
Nigeria do not necessarily need another victory to progress. A draw or a win will be enough, while a one-goal defeat would also send them through on aggregate.
A two-goal loss would level the aggregate score and take the tie into the applicable extra-time and penalty-shootout procedures, while a defeat by three or more goals would eliminate the Super Falcons.
The challenge, therefore, is to remain composed, avoid defensive lapses and take advantage of the opportunities that come their way.
Comoros face a difficult assignment as they attempt to overturn a two-goal deficit against one of Africa’s most successful women’s national teams.
Their progress to this stage was emphatic. Comoros swept aside Sudan 30-0 on aggregate in the first round, winning the opening leg 17-0 before completing the rout with a 13-0 victory in the return fixture.
Those results demonstrated their ability to score freely, but the Super Falcons represent a significantly tougher test, with greater international experience and quality across the pitch.
Comoros head coach Yusuf Abdullah previously described the opportunity to face Nigeria as an important experience for his players, pointing to the value of the encounter for the development of women’s football in the island nation.
However, Comoros must now find a way to breach Nigeria’s defence while preventing the Super Falcons from extending their aggregate lead. An early goal could increase the pressure on the hosts, but the visitors will need a disciplined performance at both ends of the pitch to keep their qualification hopes alive.
Beyond securing progression, Tuesday’s match provides another important assessment of Eguavoen’s interim leadership as the Super Falcons pursue a second consecutive appearance at the Women’s Olympic Football Tournament.
Nigeria returned to the Olympics at Paris 2024 after a 16-year absence and are now seeking to make it to Los Angeles 2028.
The squad features established internationals such as captain Rasheedat Ajibade, goalkeeper Chiamaka Nnadozie, Christy Ucheibe, Kanu, Toni Payne and Alozie, alongside younger players seeking to establish themselves in the senior team.
Joy Igbokwe made her senior international debut in the first leg, while Janet Akekoromowei and Suliat Abideen also earned their first competitive senior caps during the encounter.
Their opportunities reflect the importance of building depth within the squad as Nigeria navigate a demanding qualification campaign.
Eguavoen must now decide whether to retain the starting lineup that delivered Friday’s victory or make adjustments to keep his players fresh and improve the team’s attacking output.
Whatever changes he makes, the objective remains straightforward: secure progression without allowing Comoros to turn the contest into a tense finish.
The winner of the Nigeria-Comoros tie on aggregate will advance to the third round of the African qualifying competition, where Morocco await.
The North Africans have already progressed after Congo withdrew from their scheduled second-round encounter, leaving Nigeria and Comoros to settle the remaining place in the next stage.
The Super Falcons must first complete their assignment in Ikenne before shifting their attention to Morocco and the next hurdle in their Olympic qualification campaign.
Africa’s qualifying series features five knockout rounds, with only two teams ultimately earning places at the Los Angeles 2028 Women’s Football Tournament.
For Nigeria, Tuesday’s match is about more than protecting a two-goal lead. It is an opportunity to maintain their momentum, build confidence under Eguavoen and move one step closer to another appearance on the Olympic stage.
With a place in the third round within reach, the Super Falcons will expect to finish the job against Comoros and keep their Los Angeles 2028 ambitions firmly on track.

title: Just 5 years in, interactive chatbot platform Character.AI files for bankruptcy
body:
Only five years into its journey, Character.AI, which lets users create AI characters and have conversations with them, has filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy, following a slew of lawsuits and struggles to scale its popular platform. In a court document , the company said it had assets and liabilities between $50 million and $100 million.
“Over the past year, Character.ai has taken meaningful steps to sustain and improve its business in the face of significant legal, regulatory, and operational headwinds. After a comprehensive review of the available alternatives, the board determined that this court-supervised sale process provides the Company with the best opportunity to maximize value for all stakeholders,” Character.AI CEO Colin Adams said in a statement.
The startup has also agreed to sell some of its assets to Disney for $20 million, as well as a non-exclusive perpetual license for its technology.
The company said Disney will provide transition services via former Character.AI employees who joined the entertainment giant last month alongside its former CEO Karandeep Singh Anand .
Adams said the company would continue operating during the sale process, which is expected to close in late November or early December. However, he did note that there isn’t yet a bid for the company’s assets or a buyer.
“We hope that the sale process will yield an actionable proposal that will allow continued operations of the Character.ai platform. If such a bid is unavailable, however, the platform will be wound down,” Adams wrote.
Character.AI has had a tumultuous five years. Founded by former Google engineers Noam Shazeer, a co-author of the landmark Transformer paper, and Daniel De Freitas in late 2021, the startup initially focused on training foundation models and developing an AI chatbot platform that lets people create custom characters they could chat with.
By September 2022, the startup reached unicorn valuation with a $150 million fundraise on the back of high demand for its platform, with the company saying at the time that its users had exchanged more than 2 billion messages with its bots in five months, and active users were averaging more than two hours on the platform daily.
In May 2023, the Character.AI’s apps attracted more than 1.7 million installs in their first week after launch. But about a year later, in August 2024, Google struck a $2.7 billion deal to license the startup’s models, and both Shazeer and De Freitas returned to the search giant . At that time, the startup’s general counsel, Dominic Perella, stepped in as interim CEO, and the company moved away from training foundation models to focus on growth.
Character.AI’s traction didn’t slow, however, with its platform recording 20 million monthly active users by October of that year.
But things got difficult after the startup was sued following the suicide of a 14-year-old Florida boy whose mother says he became obsessed with a chatbot on its platform. Soon after, Texas launched an investigation to assess if the platform conformed to child privacy and safety laws. The company subsequently settled some of these lawsuits , added more safety features, and banned minors from its platform.
In June of last year, the company appointed Anand, a former Brex and Meta executive, as CEO, and expanded its products to add AI video generation, and social feeds. The company has since tried to introduce new ways to spur user engagement via interactive storytelling formats as well as microdramas.
But the fact that the company had to file for bankruptcy shows that such changes couldn’t move the needle on sustainability for the startup.
It also shows that consumer-facing AI products are really hard to scale and monetize. Character.AI was one of the top apps in terms of time spent, according to analytics firm Sensor Tower. But high engagement can be a double-edged sword; AI costs rise the more people use the app, which consequently also increases the pressure to monetize users.
Character.AI has raised over $193 million in funding across multiple rounds from investors including Lightspeed, SV Angel, Greycroft, and a16z, according to PitchBook.

title: Embraer and LATAM Sign Component Pool Program Agreement for the E195‑E2 fleet ordered by the airline
body:
Santiago de Chile, Oct 13, 2026. Embraer and LATAM Airlines Group S.A. have signed a Component Pool Program agreement to support the introduction of 24 Embraer E195‑E2 aircraft ordered by the airline. In addition to the 24 firm orders, the LATAM Group also holds 50 purchase options.



The agreement will deliver comprehensive component support for LATAM’s E195‑E2 fleet under Embraer’s Pool Program, helping optimize aircraft availability as the airline expands its operations. The Pool Program covers more than 300 aircraft components across multiple systems of the E2 and includes advanced exchange services, repair and overhaul solutions, and a selected inventory of components at LATAM facilities in Brazil.

“This Component Pool Program agreement marks an important step as LATAM prepares to introduce the E195‑E2 into its fleet. Our objective is to deliver a robust and cost‑efficient support solution from day one, ensuring high aircraft availability and operational reliability as the airline prepares to advance its growth strategy. Embraer Services & Support is fully committed to providing the best-in-class services experience and long‑term value for LATAM,” says Carlos Naufel, President and CEO, Embraer Services & Support.



Embraer’s Pool Program offers comprehensive component support to airlines worldwide, leveraging the company’s technical expertise and extensive services network. The program delivers significant savings and economies in component repair and inventory holding costs, reduces warehousing needs, and operates within a framework of guaranteed performance levels. Embraer Services & Support provides a wide range of customized solutions designed to enhance the aftersales experience and support the growing global fleet of Embraer aircraft.

title: Ghana targets thousands of overseas nursing jobs under Labour Export Programme
body: The government is seeking to secure thousands of overseas employment opportunities for Ghanaian nurses as demand for skilled health professionals grows in several international labour markets. Minister for Labour, Jobs and Employment Emmanuel Agyekum says countries including Germany, the United States and Caribbean nations are seeking Ghanaian nurses to support their healthcare systems. He said the demand presents an opportunity to connect trained health professionals who have yet to secure jobs locally with employment opportunities abroad. Mr Agyekum made the remarks at a send-off ceremony for the second cohort of Ghanaian health workers travelling to Grenada under the government’s Labour Export Programme. He said the government intended to expand the initiative to enable thousands of qualified Ghanaians to work abroad. “We have demands coming from the USA, Illinois, that is Chicago, and other states. The state of Michigan and Germany as well. The demand is huge. I think we should be able to let thousands of people go out and work because the demand is huge,” he said. The minister also identified Grenada, the Bahamas and Antigua as destinations seeking Ghanaian health professionals. Mr Agyekum said the recruitment process was designed to be fair and transparent, with applicants required to complete the necessary forms and undergo the selection process before being considered for placement. He added that successful applicants receive support, including free accommodation and transportation, to ease their transition into their new workplaces. The minister also highlighted the potential financial benefits of overseas employment, citing Antigua as an example. “For example, in Antigua, a nurse makes close to about 2,000 dollars, and over time they make up to 2,500 and above,” he said. He did not specify the applicable salary scales, the experience required to reach the higher earnings or whether the figures referred to monthly pay. Meanwhile, Chief of Staff Julius Debrah, who represented President John Dramani Mahama at the send-off ceremony, urged the departing health workers to uphold Ghana’s reputation in their new workplaces. “I’ve been asked by the President to come and say goodbye to you. Please make sure you raise the flag of Ghana,” he said. He encouraged the nurses to remain professional, demonstrate commitment to their duties and represent the country positively wherever they worked. The Labour Export Programme forms part of the government’s efforts to create employment opportunities by connecting skilled Ghanaian workers with international labour markets. The government says expanding the initiative could help more trained health professionals secure jobs, although details of the total number of overseas vacancies, recruitment timelines and placements expected under the programme were not provided in the remarks.

title: Russians damage nine private homes in Lviv region
body:
The Lviv Regional Military Administration stated this on its website , according to Ukrinform.
During an air raid alert on October 13, Russian forces attacked the Lviv region with two jet-powered drones. Ukrainian air defense forces shot down both drones.
"Following the crash of one of the drones in the village of Murovane, in Lviv district, nine residential buildings were damaged. No people were injured," the regional administration said.
According to Maksym Kozytskyi, head of the regional military administration, the crash of the drone and the resulting fire caused significant damage to two houses in Murovane. Another seven homes sustained varying degrees of damage.
Infrastructure was also damaged. Three cars were burned, and two others were damaged.
"The most important thing is that no people were injured," Kozytskyi emphasized.
He urged residents not to ignore air raid alerts and to seek shelter every time the warning sounds.
As Ukrinform previously reported, two houses caught fire in one of the villages in the Lviv region after a downed Russian drone crashed there.

title: NAF Plane Crash: Senate, Reps To Probe Air Force Aircraft Maintenance
body: The Senate has resolved to investigate budgetary provisions for the maintenance of Nigerian Air Force aircraft following the crash in Igbokoda, Ondo State, which claimed 25 lives. The resolution followed a motion sponsored by the Chairman of the Senate Committee on Air Force, Sen. Osita Ngwu, who raised concerns over recurring military aircraft accidents and the need to strengthen aviation safety. Presenting the motion today at the resumption of plenary, Sen. Ngwu reminded that the Nigerian Air Force ATR-42 aircraft, with tail number NGR 931, crashed near the Naval Base in Igbokoda, headquarters of Ilaje Local Government Area of Ondo State, on October 5, 2026, while on a routine mission from Benin City to Lagos. The Senate, which expressed concern that recurring military aircraft crashes had resulted in the loss of military personnel, raised questions about aircraft maintenance, the condition of ageing fleets and compliance with operational safety standards. Lawmakers further underscored that the operational readiness and airworthiness of military aircraft were critical to national security, intelligence gathering and defence. They warned that a failure to conduct a transparent and comprehensive investigation into the circumstances surrounding the crash could undermine efforts to prevent similar tragedies. Consequently, the Senate urged the Federal Government to prioritise funding for the regular maintenance and replacement of ageing military aircraft to improve operational safety and protect the lives of military personnel. It also mandated its committees on Air Force and Aviation to visit the crash site, engage with Nigerian Air Force authorities and conduct a comprehensive audit of the serviceability and airworthiness of aircraft in the presidential and military fleets. The Senate further called on the Nigerian Air Force and the Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau to investigate the immediate and underlying causes of the crash and make their findings public. Like the Senate, the House of Representatives has resolved to carry out an investigation into the crash. Following a motion by the chairman of the House Committee on Airforce, Kabiru Rurum, the House also resolved to carry out an audit of the aircraft in the fleet of the Airforce while calling for improved funding to ensure maintenance. The post NAF Plane Crash: Senate, Reps To Probe Air Force Aircraft Maintenance appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Pius Hadzide explains why Sports Ministry always attracts scandals
body: Former deputy Sports Minister Pius Hadzide has explained why the ministry has become a hub for scandals. Speaking on JoyNews’ PM Express on Monday night, Hadzide first highlighted the limited power of the Minister in controlling the various agencies it works with. “There are peculiriaties at the Ministry that makes relationship management a little tricky. We work with stakeholders over whom we do not have total control. Such as the GFA, which is an independent association not an organ of state.” “The Minister’s influence over for instance the Ghana Football, or Swimming Federation is limited because they have their own rules and if you go in too much, you stand accused of interference. While in other Ministries, the Minister has full grasp of the agencies they work with.” The Ministry has a notoriously high turnover. Since 1979, the country has had 28 Sports Ministers. In that time, only 15 Finance Ministers have been appointed. More recently, the tenures have been marked by controversies at an alarming rate. For every two substantive Ministers, one tenure is marked by a visa racketeering, misappropiation, and other corruption allegations. That has been the case since 2001. “The other leg of the problem, which I believe is a blessing rather than a curse, is the sheer amount of work that journalists do in that area.” “You’ll find that there is dedicated attention to sports in this country. Across the other ministries, you dont find (spector-specific) programs like Agric programs or health programs (on radio or television) as much as sports journalists, like Muftawu Nabila Abdulai and Fentuo Tahiru, do.” “So their eyes are always on the ball so when a pin drops, they are able to notice that something has gone amiss.” “I suspect that if that was what was happening across other Ministries, the Sports Ministry would have paled into insignificance (presumably because the scandals from other Ministries would have been bigger).” He made the comments in the wake of the 2026 World Cup VISA scandal, which has already seen the NSA Director General suspended while calls for the sacking of the Sports Minister, continues to grow.

title: PM Orpo: Finland working on €60m fuel subsidy package
body:
The subsidy is intended to ease commuting costs and support professional transport amid high fuel prices.
Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo (NCP) says the government is continuing negotiations on a fuel subsidy for those struggling with high pump prices.
"It's narrowed down to around 60 million euros, which is what's being discussed now."
However, where that sum would come from remains open, according to Orpo. He noted that there's little financial elbow room at the moment.
He said the key priorities are easing commuter travel and supporting professional transport.
Orpo commented on the matter at an event held by the Finnish Association of Political Journalists on Tuesday.
At the end of last month, the PM's National Coalition Party floated a nine-billion-euro savings proposal, among other things it suggested two billion euros in savings by reforming the pension system.
In another savings proposal, finance ministry officials suggested raising the age of retirement to 70. But Orpo has characterised that as unrealistic and reiterated that on Tuesday.
According to Orpo, the National Coalition wants to examine unpaid periods within the pension system — that is, pension accrual during periods when individuals are unemployed or studying, for example.
"Removing those would significantly strengthen the pension system," Orpo said, adding that savings could also be made in pension system administration.
Orpo also said the length of people's working lives should be extended, by enabling young people to begin higher education sooner than they currently do.
The PM was also asked about suspected illegal logging at Google's Muhos and Kajaani data centre construction sites — and what his role was in that process.
"I haven't been involved in any permit processes whatsoever. I see data centres as a major opportunity for Finland when they're handled properly," Orpo replied.
According to him, not all of the planned data centre projects will move forward, but Google's project has the potential to offer major societal benefits.
Orpo also answered questions about data centre energy demands, and whether there will be enough electricity as more of the power-hungry facilities arrive.
He said the government has taken steps to strengthen the transmission grid so that planned investments in Finland can be accommodated.
According to Orpo, a number of other energy-intensive investments besides data centres are coming to Finland.
As an example, he pointed to a planned aluminium plant in Kokkola.
