"There's interest in Finland because we have clean energy," he said, adding that he believes new electricity will be generated as demand for it grows.
Orpo was also asked about US President Donald Trump positioning himself against Ukraine.
Last Friday, Trump announced that Russia had agreed to supply more than 300,000 tonnes of diesel fuel to US and world markets. To facilitate that move, the US is temporarily lifting sanctions on Russia for the deliveries.
Trump characterised his conversation with Russian President Vladimir Putin as very successful. Trump has also said that Ukraine should not bomb Russian oil refineries.
According to The Financial Times, Trump is also threatening to halt the supply of US weapons to Ukraine.
Orpo was asked what he thinks of Trump's actions and how Europe should respond.
"It really was a huge disappointment. A direct deal with Putin, which goes against everything we've done together—together with the United States. He's making a deal with Putin which is financing Putin's war."
According to Orpo, Europe must forcefully state its position to Trump. He says Europe needs to continue supporting Ukraine, while ensuring that support from the United States continues.

title: Drones Are Creating New Opportunities For The U.S. Army To Deceive Its Enemies
body: For more than a year, U.S. Army forces in Europe have been experimenting with new counter-drone capabilities, as well as tactics, techniques, and procedures to go with them, under the umbrella of what is dubbed Project Flytrap . In doing so, the service has also been gaining valuable new insights into how uncrewed systems can help shape the battlefield for friendly forces. It is particularly interesting to hear how the Army envisions using uncrewed platforms to open up new avenues for deceiving opponents. Army Col. Timothy Price, head of the 2nd Cavalry Regiment , discussed the use of uncrewed platforms for deception and other operational concepts that have emerged in the course of Project Flytrap during a talk yesterday. Price’s remarks came at the Association of the U.S. Army’s (AUSA) main annual convention, at which TWZ is in attendance . 2nd Cavalry Regiment, based in Germany, is a brigade-sized mechanized formation equipped primarily with variants of the Stryker 8×8 light armored vehicle . Stryker light armored vehicles assigned to 2nd Cavalry Regiment seen configured for a Project Flytrap event. US Army Sgt. Alejandro Carrasquel Price, by way of introduction, described modern battlefields full of uncrewed platforms in the air and on the ground as presenting new twists on long-standing problem sets. More specifically, he started by describing the typical approach to getting past a minefield or similar obstacle using an established framework called SOSRA, which stands for Suppress, Obscure, Secure, Reduce, Assault . “If we were going to breach a mined wire obstacle , the first step of SOSRA – suppress – would be the utilization of indirect fires, to get the enemy’s head down, and direct fire systems, so they would not maneuver on you, fix them in place, and you can make a decision about how you’re going to approach the problem,” the 2nd Cavalry Regiment commander explained. “The next step would be to obscure it. In the historical sense, obscurations used is [sic] smoke, to mask your movement to the point of breach, so the enemy doesn’t know what you’re doing. And then, of course, secure would be to establish frontside security, [and] allow your engineers to come up within this local security bubble. They’ll utilize some kind of line charge to open the breach, reduce it – that’s the ‘R’ – and then bring on a follow-on force of assault through.” “We were brought up around the old traditional mined wire obstacles that we had to physically breach. This is no different,” he added. “It’s just a multi-domain environment. So it’s built up of a combination of electronic warfare, kinetic UAS [uncrewed aerial systems] threats, and then counter-UAS threats, and then the network that holds [that all] together that forms the obstacle, which a unit has to maneuver through in order to maintain the offensive.” A briefing slide Col. Price showed at AUSA yesterday while talking about SOSRA on the modern ‘multi-domain’ battlefield. Jamie Hunter Within this environment, Col. Price described the suppression step of SOSRA as having a different kind of probing dimension, particularly to feel out an enemy’s uncrewed capabilities, as well as those in the electromagnetic spectrum. He also noted that brigade-sized formations like this no longer necessarily have all the required tools organizationally to ‘service’ that aspect of the mission. This is in part because what has to be suppressed, including ground control stations for enemy drones, might now be miles behind the front line. So, “what we have to do is allow the enemy to turn on their systems. How do I suppress them to allow division, or higher, to put an effect on them for suppression? It probably looks like flying small, attritable UAS [sic] into their security area” in the rear, he said. This, in turn, “cause[s] the enemy to do one of two things, either … go from passive to active with their EW [electronic warfare] systems, or to turn on radars to actually figure out what they’re seeing, which then forms the signature which higher headquarters can use to target.” Though Col. Price did not describe it as such, there is already something of a deception aspect to this step in fooling enemy emitters to switch on and expose themselves. This, as a general tactic , is also hardly new . Stimulating air defenses, in particular, is a key part of operations to gather intelligence on those capabilities , as well as to suppress and destroy them. Once you have categorized and geolocated an emitter, it is a logical step to then target it. The ultimate goal, with data being passed along a more deeply networked kill chain, is for the time it takes for fires to be brought to bear to be almost instantaneous. In 2020, then-Army Col. Scott Woodward, at the time commander of the 11th Cavalry Regiment, shared this annotated satellite image showing the electronic emissions signature of a battalion-sized element, underscoring how such signals exposed a unit to attack. US Army via X Regardless, deception comes far more into play in the obscure step, according to the 2nd Cavalry Regiment commander. “Obscuration is different, as well. So instead of trying to hide behind smoke as we maneuver through it, what is the deception plan, right? How am I trying to show the enemy a signature that says I’m going to breach over here when I’m actually going to breach here, right?” he asked rhetorically. “So, that’s probably the implementation of UGVs [uncrewed ground vehicles] with some kind of decoy emitter on top of them to pull the enemy’s eyes, resources, and time to a point that allows me to focus my assets and resources on the point of breach.” The use of uncrewed platforms as decoys is also not new , and even more complex concepts have emerged within the U.S. military in the past. Uncrewed systems have also been developed for military and other purposes over the years that are designed to mimic something else entirely, including for purposes of deception . This includes masquerading as birds and other animals . Back in 2019, TWZ was the first to report in detail on a Navy effort to develop and field an entire networked, cooperative electronic warfare ecosystem, at that time referred to as the Netted Emulation of Multi-Element Signature against Integrated Sensors, or NEMESIS. This was also a drone-heavy cross-domain concept intended to make many types of sensors over vast areas believe they were ‘seeing’ the same false fleets of aircraft and/or ships, and deceive and confuse the enemy on a grand scale. This, in turn, represented a massive leap in electronic warfare capabilities. An unclassified 2014 briefing slide with details about NEMESIS. Note the inclusion of drone boats among other uncrewed platforms in the associated graphic. USN An unclassified 2014 briefing slide with details about NEMSIS. Note the inclusion of drone boats among other uncrewed platforms in the associated graphic. USN There is also overlap here with reported sightings of what are now commonly called unidentified aerial phenomena (UAP), and that used to be called unidentified flying objects (UFO). As we have reported on repeatedly over the years , while some UAP sightings remain unexplained, many more have turned out to be drones . Adversaries have been using uncrewed capabilities for intelligence gathering and deception purposes against American interests at home and abroad, likely in part by exploiting UAP stigma for cover . We have talked in the past about how drones will be used in more and more exotic ways to confuse opponents. I don’t know what this is, or if it’s legit BUT remember we are in a new age of misdirection, decoy and guile. Specifically using low end drone technology. There are more ways to stimulate an enemy air defense system, distract a populous, assess the flow of public info from a… https://t.co/wW7YVlbayB — Tyler Rogoway (@Aviation_Intel) September 21, 2026 When it comes to UGVs, specifically, 2nd Cavalry Regiment , as well as units elsewhere across the U.S. Army , have been experimenting with various designs in recent years. The service has been trying for years to expand its operational use of UGVs, in general, but has faced repeated setbacks . “It’s also spectral camouflage . So how are we controlling our heat and thermal signatures on our vehicles and our people?” Price continued. “It’s basic soldier discipline issues. It’s how we use our radios. It’s where we’re talking, where we’re not. But that’s what obscuration looks like.” A Soviet-designed 2S3 self-propelled howitzer as seen through a thermal camera, offering a good example of how heat signatures can put forces at risk. CI Systems As a reminder, Project Flytrap’s primary focus has been on counter-drone capabilities, which come into play heavily during the secure stage. “There’s multi-layered assets on top of that to allow that convergence for our success at the point of breach. I’m going to focus on our corner, our part of the battle, right?” he said. “So, I’m looking at active and passive electronic warfare systems – that can either, one, find [threats], let me know that I’ve got some kind of system flying or operating against me and, then, if it’s an active system, take some kind of effect to maybe cut a downlink and disrupt that system – all the way down to the individual soldier with a shotgun.” As mentioned, the ‘obstacle’ to be ‘reduced’ at the end of this is not necessarily something as simple as a minefield surrounded by barbed wire anymore. Now it could be enemy one-way-attack drone capabilities preventing holding up an advance. Col. Price, in turn, described friendly kamikaze drones as part of the equation for breaching past those threats. Decoys and deception have a continued role to play in this phase. “This is where, at the brigade level, we introduce one-way attack munitions to try to destroy the C2 [command and control] network that the enemy is using to operate this reconnaissance/strike complex” that is standing in the way, he explained. “There’s layers to it, right? Like they’ve got a close side to this that’s the local part of this reconnaissance/strike complex. They’ve probably got a theater level that the Corps [the U.S. Army’s command echelon above divisions] and higher is trying to target as we are forcing people to turn on systems to communicate. But at the regiment level, I’m looking at one-way attack munitions, focused on C2 nodes, headquarters, and ground control stations that [sic] I can disrupt their ability to put lethal effects on me as we begin to open the breach.” The U.S. Army is in the process of fielding a variety of weaponized drones, including loitering munitions and designs capable of releasing grenades and other small bomblets. A member of the 2nd Cavalry Regiment holds a small quadcopter drone in one hand and a simulated bomblet in the other during an exercise in 2025. US Army During a question-and-answer session that followed his remarks, Col. Price was asked about whether lessons learned and other observations from Ukraine, and specifically that country’s recent Operation Vivaldi counteroffensive, had contributed to this evolving framework. “In terms of Vivaldi, I’m not an expert, so I’m not going to make any kind of estimations on how that worked or why,” he said in response. “But I will say, if you look at the focus of that operation, you can probably make the assumption that there was convergence of efforts across the different headquarters to enable success. So that’s how I would relate to the two.” “In order to be successful for a multi-domain breach, the tactical level requires my higher headquarters to be part of that solution to enable me with resources and capabilities that I don’t have in here at the brigade level,” he continued. “I would imagine it’s very similar in the other operational comparisons.” Though certainly true, in broad strokes, this response in some ways underscores how the U.S. Army continues to lag behind global trends in the use of uncrewed systems, as now typified by the ongoing war in Ukraine. Army leaders have been open about this continued reality in the past, despite efforts to try to reverse it. “We’re behind. I’ll just be candid. I think we know we’re behind,” Army Lt. Gen. Charles Costanza said during a panel discussion at AUSA last year, in response to a direct question at the panel from our Howard Altman. Costanza was talking about both the employment of drones and counter-drone capabilities, and highlighted work being done then under Project Flytrap, as you can read more about here . Another 2nd Cavalry Regiment Stryker configured for the counter-drone role seen during a Project Flytrap exercise. US Army Costanza was head of V Corps, a key component of the U.S. Army presence in Europe, at the time. He was removed from that post abruptly in August for reasons that remain unclear, but were reportedly tied to disputes between top Army leadership and Secretary Pete Hegseth. Secretary of the Army Dan Driscoll resigned last month, amid reports of months of friction with Hegseth about various policies . The Pentagon under Hegseth has launched a number of initiatives to accelerate the fielding of new uncrewed capabilities across the U.S. military, especially within smaller ground units. This now includes plans for a new Autonomous Warfare Command (AUTOWARCOM) unveiled last month. For units like the 2nd Cavalry Regiment, new drone-centric concepts of operations are already taking shape. Beyond using them for surveillance and as one-way-attack munitions, there is also a clear focus emerging on employing expanding uncrewed capabilities to deceive opponents and prevent them from making the best use of their own resources. Contact the author: joe@twz.com The post Drones Are Creating New Opportunities For The U.S. Army To Deceive Its Enemies appeared first on TWZ .

title: NBI files complaints vs Davao contractor linked to Dutertes
body: MANILA, Philippines – Weeks after starting its investigation into Genesis88 Construction Inc., the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) filed complaints against its owner, Glenn Escandor, and six others, including Genesis88 employees and former officials of the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) Davao City District Engineering Office. On Tuesday, October 13, the NBI filed falsification by public officer and graft complaints against Escandor and the following: Saturnino Bentulan – authorized managing officer, Genesis88 Benjamin Zosa – project engineer, Genesis 88 Roy Bohol – construction foreman, Genesis 88 Richard Ragasa – former district engineer, DPWH Davao City District Engineering Office Lilibeth Sarmiento – former assistant district engineer, DPWH Davao City District Engineering Office Roberto Mamaril – former OIC-chief, Construction Section, DPWH Davao City District Engineering Office The complaints came after the NBI started looking into the P1.9-billion flood control projects awarded to Genesis88, located in the district of Davao City Representative Paolo Duterte. Escandor, the Dutertes’ longtime friend, is the owner of the firm, based on Securities and Exchange Commission records obtained by Rappler in 2025. A Rappler investigation revealed that one in four flood control projects in Davao City was awarded to Genesis88. The years when it bagged the contracts coincided with the time when Rodrigo Duterte was president and when the younger Duterte was the lawmaker representing the 1st District of Davao City. Almost P2.9 billion (or P2,890,690,550.13) worth of contracts for flood control infrastructure from 2021 to 2023 went to the firm, based on figures from the Sumbong sa Pangulo website . This translated to a total of 35 projects — solo contracting and joint ventures with other firms included — in the region. Escandor was former president Duterte’s assistant for sports. He also owns the Escandor Development Corporation, which donated P19.923 million for the ads of Vice President Sara Duterte during the 2022 national elections, according to the Vice President’s Statement of Contributions and Expenditures seen by Rappler. – with reports from Jairo Bolledo/Rappler.com

title: APL says GoldBod terminated US$1bn Goldstream deal over failure to meet obligations
body: Africa Policy Lens (APL) says the Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) has terminated its memorandum of understanding (MoU) with Goldstream Global DMCC after the company failed to fulfil its obligations under an agreement announced as a proposed US$1 billion investment in more than 300 mines across Ghana. The disclosure follows a Right to Information (RTI) request submitted on August 11, 2026, by mining consultant and APL Senior Fellow Ing. Wisdom Edem Gomashie. According to APL, GoldBod’s response, dated August 26, 2026, confirmed that the agreement had been terminated because of Goldstream Global DMCC’s failure to perform its obligations. GoldBod also stated that the terminated MoU should not be treated as an ongoing commercial arrangement or as creating any current financial or operational obligation for the institution. However, the response, as cited by APL, did not specify which obligations the company failed to fulfil, when the termination took effect or whether the proposed investment advanced beyond the MoU stage. The agreement was signed on August 22, 2025, and publicly announced by GoldBod Chief Executive Officer Sammy Gyamfi at the Mining and Minerals Convention in Accra on September 9, 2025. At the time, Mr Gyamfi described the initiative as a major shift in Ghana’s mining sector, intended to increase national gold production, create thousands of jobs and empower mining communities. The programme was presented as part of efforts to move Ghana beyond raw mineral extraction towards greater domestic value retention. APL’s account says the Minerals Commission had released 10 blocked-out mineralised areas to GoldBod for the first phase, with additional areas expected to follow. The proposed investment was expected to support the development of more than 300 responsible mines across the country. The termination raises questions about the status of those plans and whether any preparatory work or financial commitments were made before the agreement ended. APL says the termination raises broader questions about due diligence, institutional oversight and transparency in major public-sector investment announcements. The organisation is asking GoldBod to explain what financial, technical and operational checks were conducted before the agreement was signed and what evidence was available regarding Goldstream Global DMCC’s capacity to mobilise the proposed investment. It also wants clarification on the specific obligations the company failed to meet, the steps taken before termination and whether any public institution incurred expenditure in anticipation of the project. Other questions concern whether the arrangement included proposed gold offtake rights or other commercial benefits for Goldstream Global DMCC, and what safeguards were established to protect Ghana’s interests. APL argues that GoldBod’s assurance that the terminated MoU creates no current financial or operational obligations does not establish whether the State incurred historical costs or made commitments before the agreement ended. “The public deserves to know whether the proposed commercial partnership created any financial exposure or obligations before its termination,” APL said. The organisation is calling on GoldBod to publish an account of the circumstances surrounding the termination, including the due diligence conducted, the obligations that were not fulfilled, the termination procedures and any financial or operational implications for the State. It is also urging the institution to release the executed MoU, relevant agreements, termination notices and associated records, subject to applicable legal exemptions. Beyond the Goldstream agreement, APL wants stronger institutional standards for major commercial arrangements involving public institutions. It says such agreements should be subject to appropriate due diligence, performance monitoring and timely public disclosure throughout their lifecycle, including when they are terminated. “Ghana’s mineral resources must be governed by more than ambitious investment announcements. They require verifiable commitments, rigorous oversight, transparent implementation and accountability when agreements fail to deliver,” APL said. The disclosure comes amid wider scrutiny of GoldBod’s operations. In August 2026, APL called for a forensic investigation into the institution following disclosures in an International Monetary Fund report concerning losses of more than US$1.7 billion associated with Ghana’s Domestic Gold Purchase Programme. The Ghana Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative (GHEITI) had also recommended the publication of the Goldstream MoU, noting that the agreement had not been disclosed. APL says the termination adds to concerns about transparency and accountability in the management of Ghana’s gold sector. The information cited by APL does not establish whether the proposed investment resulted in any financial commitments, whether public funds were spent or whether the company received any commercial rights before the MoU was terminated. The organisation says it will continue its investigative and policy reform series, The Gold Accountability Files , with further publications examining transparency, governance and institutional accountability in Ghana’s gold sector. APL says GoldBod has not yet responded to its demands for further disclosure.

title: Daily Insight for CEOs: Making better decisions under pressure
body: Insight. CEOs often make important decisions under pressure, particularly when markets shift, financial performance weakens, customers demand immediate responses, or unexpected risks emerge. Pressure can encourage rushed judgments, emotional reactions, and excessive reliance on assumptions. Effective CEOs remain calm, separate facts from opinions, assess the available options, and make timely decisions without pretending to have perfect information. Key Strategies: Separate verified facts from assumptions and incomplete information. Identify the most important risks and consequences of each option. Consult relevant experts and executives without creating unnecessary delays. Consider alternative scenarios before committing to a course of action. Establish clear criteria for reviewing or changing a decision as circumstances evolve. CEO Leadership Actions. Create a disciplined process for evaluating high-impact decisions. Encourage executives to respectfully challenge assumptions before decisions are finalised. Communicate decisions clearly, explaining the rationale and expected outcomes. Actionable Tip. When facing a difficult decision, ask: “What do we know, what are we assuming, what could go wrong, and what would cause us to change course?” Why This Matters? Pressure is an unavoidable part of executive leadership. The CEO’s ability to think clearly under pressure reduces avoidable mistakes, strengthens stakeholder confidence, and helps the organisation respond effectively to uncertainty. About the Author. Ernest De-Graft Egyir, CEO advisor, Thought Leader, and Founding CEO of Chief Executives Network Ghana, convenes the Ghana CEO Summit and served on Ghana’s Economic Dialogue Planning Committee.

title: Tokayev Dissolves Kazakhstan Local Councils Ruling Party Merger
body: Kazakhstan’s President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev signed a decree on October 12 terminating the powers of maslikhats, the country’s local representative assemblies. Snap elections must now be held by December 12. The move follows a decision in June 2026 to merge the Amanat party into the newly established pro-presidential Adilet party, which won August’s parliamentary elections . Most incumbent local deputies, however, were elected in 2023 under the Amanat banner, raising questions about their mandates as the party is absorbed into Adilet. Why Questions About Legitimacy Arose Tokayev first raised the prospect of early elections on September 24, speaking at the inaugural session of the Halyq Kenesi, or People’s Council of Kazakhstan. “The overwhelming majority of maslikhat deputies were elected from the Amanat party. That party no longer operates independently, having merged with the Adilet party,” Tokayev explained. He said the merger would soon raise questions about the legitimacy of much of the country’s local representative bodies once the legal procedures were completed. Under Kazakh law , deputies can lose their seats if the party through which they were elected ceases to exist. However, the decision to merge the parties did not, by itself, end their mandates. From Nur Otan to Adilet Amanat was previously known as Nur Otan and had been the main political support base of Kazakhstan’s first president, Nursultan Nazarbayev. Founded in 1999, the party underwent several name changes. The most recent came in March 2022, following the January unrest, when mass protests escalated into the largest political crisis in Kazakhstan’s post-independence history. Amanat voted on June 12 to join Adilet, which approved the merger two days later. The new organization inherited its regional branches, administrative apparatus, and extensive network of activists. Adilet itself had been registered only on June 1, just weeks before the merger. Adilet was headed by Aibek Dadebay, who had previously led President Tokayev’s administration. Following the August parliamentary elections, he became chairman of the Kurultai, Kazakhstan’s new unicameral parliament. In the August 23 elections, Adilet won 71.17% of the vote and 110 of the 145 parliamentary seats. Four other parties crossed the 5% electoral threshold but secured only 35 seats between them. Maslikhats and the New Parliamentary System Maslikhats are elected at the regional, city, and district levels. They approve local budgets, review territorial development programs, and hear reports from executive officials. In cases provided for by law, deputies may initiate a vote of no confidence in an akim, the head of a local administration. Kazakhstan, however, remains a unitary state with a strong presidential chain of command. The heads of regions and major cities are appointed by the president. Following constitutional reform, the Senate and Mazhilis were replaced by the unicameral Kurultai. On October 7, its deputies voted to establish a Council for Cooperation with Maslikhats. According to deputy Amirbek Ospanbekov, local representative bodies work directly with residents, understand regional conditions, and encounter the practical consequences of laws passed by parliament. The council is expected to involve maslikhat representatives in drafting legislation and gathering information about how laws are implemented locally. The decision was made five days before the maslikhats were dissolved. Parliament will now have to establish working relationships with the newly elected local assemblies. How Many Deputies Will Serve in the New Maslikhats? On October 2, the Central Election Commission revised the rules for determining the number of maslikhat deputies. The resolution took effect on October 7. The number of seats depends on the population of each region. Astana, Almaty, and Shymkent must have at least 30 deputies if their populations do not exceed 1.1 million. Two additional seats are allocated for every additional 200,000 residents. Regional maslikhats must have at least 26 deputies in regions with populations of up to 300,000. As the population increases, the number of seats also rises by two for every additional 200,000 residents. Elections Could Take Place on December 6 On October 12, Tokayev held the promised consultations with Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov and Kurultai Chairman Aibek Dadebay. The consultations were required under the Constitution before the president could dissolve the assemblies. The official election date has not yet been announced. Political analyst Andrey Chebotarev wrote that the elections “will most likely take place on Sunday, December 6,” since the legal deadline of December 12 falls on a Saturday. The final decision rests with the Central Election Commission. Adilet now enters the local elections with a significant advantage: the extensive regional network it inherited from Amanat. Whether the composition of the maslikhats will change significantly remains to be seen.

title: Weta rice farmers seek urgent support after floods destroy crops
body: Rice farmers in Weta of the Volta Region have petitioned the Ministry of Food and Agriculture for urgent financial support and the rehabilitation of the Weta Irrigation Scheme following floods that destroyed their crops. A delegation comprising chiefs, farmers and concerned youth presented the petition, calling for government intervention to restore production and help affected families recover their livelihoods. The farmers also requested an investigation into how World Bank funds earmarked for the redevelopment of the scheme had been used. Gideon Kokroko, a member of the concerned youth associated with the project, said 1,203 farmers had registered under the scheme and invested heavily in their farms before the floods struck. “So far, we have invested a lot in it, but the floods came and consumed everything,” he said. He appealed for immediate assistance to help farmers meet their basic needs while awaiting the next farming season. “We are appealing to the government, as a matter of urgency, to rehabilitate the project for us and provide financial support so that we can feed ourselves while waiting for the next farming season. We are suffering, and we are hungry,” he added. Deputy Minister of Food and Agriculture, John Dumelo, received the petition on behalf of the minister and assured the delegation that the government would address their concerns. He said the Member of Parliament for Ketu North, Edem Agbana, had informed him about the delegation’s request for a meeting. “What I can assure you is that it is something that can be done and will be done,” Mr Dumelo said. The delegation maintained that restoring the irrigation facility was essential to reviving farming activities. With more than 1,200 families affected, they also called for appropriate compensation to support their recovery. Mr Agbana pledged to continue engaging the relevant authorities to ensure the petition resulted in practical measures. “I have assured the delegation that I will continue to engage the relevant authorities and push for concrete, measurable action,” he said. He stressed that the response must include a clear rehabilitation plan, accountability for money committed to the scheme and measures to restore farmers’ livelihoods. “The concerns raised must translate into a clear rehabilitation plan, accountability for funds committed to the project, and a credible pathway towards restoring the livelihoods of affected farmers,” Mr Agbana added.

title: US, Canada, 8 other countries that allow Nigerians, other foreigners join their military
body: Foreign nationals seeking opportunities to serve in a foreign military can apply to join the armed forces of several countries, although eligibility depends on nationality, immigration status, military experience and the recruitment programme available. Countries such as France, the United Kingdom, Australia, Canada, Spain, the United States, Ukraine, Russia and New Zealand have provisions under which certain foreign nationals can serve in their armed forces. Israel also operates a special enlistment programme for eligible foreign volunteers. However, the rules differ considerably. While some countries accept foreign applicants without requiring permanent residency, others restrict recruitment to citizens of selected countries, permanent residents or experienced military personnel. For Nigerians considering military service abroad, understanding these differences is essential because being eligible to enlist does not automatically guarantee a visa, admission into the armed forces or permission to settle in the country. Here are nine countries, alongside Israel’s special volunteer programme, where foreign nationals may be eligible to serve in the military. 1. France France is among the best-known destinations for foreigners seeking to enlist in a foreign military through its French Foreign Legion. The Legion, a branch of the French Army, recruits men of different nationalities and allows eligible foreign nationals to apply without first becoming French citizens. According to the Legion’s official recruitment website, applicants must generally be older than 17 and younger than 40 when they report to a recruitment office. Candidates must also meet medical, physical and administrative requirements. Applicants from outside the Schengen area must present a passport, although the Legion does not arrange visas or exit authorisation on behalf of recruits. Unlike conventional recruitment into many national armed forces, the Foreign Legion has a specific recruitment system designed to accommodate foreign nationals. 2. United Kingdom The United Kingdom recruits eligible foreign nationals into its armed forces, including the British Army, subject to nationality and recruitment rules. Eligible applicants can include citizens of Commonwealth countries, a category that includes Nigeria, as well as Irish citizens and certain other groups. The British Army has historically recruited Commonwealth citizens and operates the Brigade of Gurkhas, which recruits eligible Nepalese applicants. However, Commonwealth citizenship alone does not guarantee admission. Recruitment availability, residency requirements, age limits, medical standards and the specific service or role can affect eligibility. The UK Ministry of Defence has also operated limited recruitment arrangements for Commonwealth applicants in specialist roles. Consequently, prospective applicants should check whether applications are currently open before making travel plans. 3. Australia Australia allows certain foreign nationals to apply to join the Australian Defence Force (ADF). Under eligibility arrangements introduced in 2024 and expanded from 2025, eligible permanent residents from the United Kingdom, the United States and Canada can apply. Eligible New Zealand citizens living in Australia can also apply. Applicants must satisfy additional requirements, including residency conditions, medical and physical standards, security checks and relevant citizenship rules. Australia also has an overseas lateral-entry pathway for eligible personnel with previous military experience whose skills can be transferred to the Australian Defence Force. This means Australia is not an unrestricted destination for anyone seeking to join a foreign military. Nationality, residency and previous service can determine whether an application is accepted. 4. Canada Canada permits eligible permanent residents, as well as Canadian citizens, to apply to join the Canadian Armed Forces. This creates a potential route for foreign nationals who have already obtained permanent residency in Canada. However, applicants must satisfy the armed forces’ recruitment conditions. The official recruitment website specifies that permanent resident applicants must provide evidence of three years of physical presence in Canada. Age, education, medical fitness, background checks and the requirements of the selected military occupation also apply. Therefore, Nigerians hoping to enlist in Canada generally need to establish the required immigration status and meet the applicable recruitment conditions before they can join. 5. Spain Spain allows certain foreign nationals to compete for places in its armed forces, particularly in enlisted soldier and sailor positions. However, eligibility is restricted to citizens of specified countries rather than foreigners generally. Spain’s 2026 recruitment documentation identifies eligible nationalities including Argentina, Bolivia, Colombia, Chile, Ecuador, Mexico, Peru, the Dominican Republic, Uruguay and Venezuela, alongside other listed countries. Equatorial Guinea and several other Spanish-speaking countries are also included. The number of places available to foreign applicants is limited, and candidates must satisfy age, education, criminal-record and other recruitment requirements. Nigeria is not among the nationalities listed in Spain’s 2026 recruitment rules for these foreign-applicant places. 6. United States The United States permits certain non-citizens to enlist in its military, but it does not generally offer ordinary enlistment to foreign nationals living overseas without the required immigration status. The US Army states that enlisted applicants must be US citizens or lawful permanent residents holding a valid Green Card, alongside other eligibility requirements. A Green Card provides permanent resident status, allowing eligible holders to live and work in the United States. Non-citizens who meet the requirements may subsequently qualify for an expedited naturalisation process through military service, subject to applicable law. However, military service is not a general visa programme, and a person cannot assume that applying to enlist will automatically provide permission to enter or reside in the United States. 7. Ukraine Ukraine permits foreign nationals and stateless persons to serve in its armed forces under military contracts. The country has recruited international volunteers during its war with Russia, including through its International Legion for the Defence of Ukraine. Ukraine’s official recruitment information states that foreign volunteers can serve as full members of the Ukrainian Armed Forces, with applicable service conditions, remuneration and benefits. Its foreign-national recruitment guidance says applicants must already be legally present in Ukraine to apply through the relevant Ground Forces recruitment route. Candidates are subject to background checks, medical examinations and other requirements. The official International Legion website also provides information for foreigners seeking to apply. However, prospective recruits must carefully consider the risks of military service in an active war zone, including the possibility of serious injury or death, as well as the legal implications of serving in a foreign armed force. 8. Russia Russia permits foreign nationals to enter military service under contract, subject to its laws and recruitment requirements. Russian legislation provides for foreign citizens and stateless persons to serve under military contracts. The legal framework has also been amended in recent years, including changes made in 2025. However, the existence of a legal route does not mean every foreign national is automatically eligible or that all recruitment offers are genuine. Anyone considering this option should independently verify the applicable law, contract terms, immigration requirements and consequences of military service. The risks associated with service during an international armed conflict also warrant particular attention. 9. New Zealand New Zealand operates an overseas recruitment pathway for certain applicants with military backgrounds. According to the New Zealand Defence Force’s overseas recruitment guidance, eligible candidates can include serving members of the armed forces of the United Kingdom, Australia, the United States and Canada who meet the applicable service-release conditions. The pathway also covers certain citizens of those countries who meet specified citizenship or residency criteria, provided they satisfy the relevant vacancy and rank requirements. This is principally a route for experienced military personnel rather than an open enlistment programme for all foreign civilians. Applicants must meet the Defence Force’s medical, security and professional requirements and obtain the necessary immigration status. 10. Israel: Special enlistment programme for foreign volunteers Israel provides a special route through which eligible foreign volunteers can serve in the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) without first becoming Israeli citizens. The IDF identifies Mahal as an enlistment programme for foreign volunteers interested in serving in military combat and support roles. This is different from unrestricted recruitment into the Israeli military. Applicants must meet the programme’s eligibility requirements, and participation depends on the applicable rules and recruitment arrangements. The IDF also operates other programmes for foreign volunteers that involve supporting military activities without necessarily becoming full-time soldiers. Prospective applicants should distinguish between formal enlistment and non-combat volunteer programmes before applying. What Nigerians should know before applying Although these countries provide routes for certain foreign nationals to serve, the requirements vary substantially. Nationality: Some countries accept applicants from specified nationalities, while others have broader foreign-recruitment systems. Immigration status: Canada and the United States generally require applicants to hold permanent resident status if they are not citizens. Australia’s eligibility rules also impose nationality and residency conditions. Military experience: Some overseas recruitment pathways, particularly in New Zealand and Australia, are designed for people who have already served in the military. Age and fitness: Applicants must meet the relevant age limits, medical standards, physical requirements and background checks. Legal consequences: Serving in a foreign military may have implications under the applicant’s home-country laws. Nigerians should seek reliable legal advice before signing a contract with a foreign armed force. Recruitment scams: Applicants should use official military recruitment websites and verify any offer before paying fees or sharing sensitive documents. Vanguard News The post US, Canada, 8 other countries that allow Nigerians, other foreigners join their military appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Rada introduces auctions to attract investment in fisheries, simplifies access to water bodies
body:
The Verkhovna Rada has passed as a whole the law On Stimulating the Economic Development of the Fisheries Industry (draft law No. 12384), aimed at increasing the investment attractiveness of the sector and developing aquaculture and mariculture.
As an Interfax-Ukraine correspondent reports, 275 MPs voted in favor of the decision at a meeting on Tuesday, with the required minimum being 226 votes.
The law establishes the legal framework for attracting investment through transparent auctions for fishery water bodies, internal sea waters, territorial sea, and the exclusive economic zone for the development of aquaculture and mariculture. To use such water areas, the requirement to allocate a land plot of the water fund and mark its boundaries on the ground is eliminated, allowing investors to operate within designated coordinates of the water space.
In addition, the document allows using state- or municipally-owned land plots with an area of up to 0.1 hectares located in coastal protective strips without changing their designated purpose to accommodate necessary equipment and temporary structures.
The law also defines a list of water bodies that cannot be subject to investment attraction: these include objects leased under the Water Code, drinking water intake reservoirs in the first zone of sanitary protection, objects of water users, natural reserve fund sites with prohibited activities, and objects with approved bioresource catch limits (except aquaculture). Such lists will be approved by the specialized authority based on investment proposals from state bodies, local self-government, and business.
A scientific and biological rationale will be developed for each object within the framework of investment attraction, and relations will be formalized through agreements on attracting funds for aquaculture development or fishery operation in specialized commercial fish farms. The document also introduces state control and monitoring over the execution of investment obligations to ensure the rational use of aquatic bioresources.
The document was registered in the Rada on January 8, 2025. It was passed in the first reading on May 13, 2025, after which parliamentarians referred it for a repeat second reading on July 1. The initiators of the document are Head of the Subcommittee on Economic and Financial Policy in the Agro-Industrial Complex of the Rada Committee on Agrarian and Land Policy Artem Chornomorov, Head of the Rada Agrarian Committee Oleksandr Haidu, Head of the Servant of the People David Arakhamia, First Deputy Head of the Servant of the People faction Andriy Motovylovets, and member of the Rada Budget Committee Anatoliy Urbansky (For the Future).

title: Trump cites violations of energy truce ‘on both sides’, his intent to compel Kyiv and Moscow to reach agreement
body:
U.S. President Donald Trump has stated that the agreements regarding an energy ceasefire are being violated by both sides, yet expressed confidence that the leaders of Ukraine and Russia aim to conclude a peace agreement.
Responding to questions from journalists before departing for a rally in Ohio, Trump commented on overnight strikes and the breakdown of the truce he had announced. Addressing reporters' remarks that Russia had violated the agreement, he noted: "There have been violations on both sides."
Commenting on Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's statement regarding support for the energy truce, contrasted with a lack of similar readiness from Vladimir Putin, Trump asserted that both leaders support the initiative.
He believes Putin wants to reach an agreement, and we need to ensure Zelenskyy wants to reach an agreement too. According to him, Putin and Zelenskyy want to reach an agreement, but they don't know how. However, he said, they will make them come to an agreement.
Trump also defended the agreement on Russian diesel fuel exports, which had drawn criticism in Kyiv and the US Congress: "My diesel deal with Russia is actually not a deal for me. It is a deal for the rest of the world."
On October 11, Trump announced that an energy truce had been reached between Ukraine and Russia. At the same time, on the evening of October 12 and into the night of October 13, Russian occupation forces launched massive strikes against Kyiv, Kharkiv, and other Ukrainian cities, attacking civilian and transport infrastructure with ballistic missiles and loitering munitions. President Zelenskyy stated his readiness to refrain from striking Russian energy facilities only on the condition of a genuine, mutual cessation of strikes by Moscow.

title: 5 killed in clash btw Iran security forces, terrorist element
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 13 (MNA) – The clashes erupted between Iran’s security forces and terrorist elements in Kourin, Zahedan on Tuesday which left five terrorists dead and one security officer was martyred.
Five terrorist elements were killed and one security force of the country was martyred in a fierce clash erupted in Kourin, southern Iranian city of Zahedan, Sistan and Baluchestan province.
The Quds Base of the Islamic Revolution Guards Corps Ground Force announced in a statement that the operation took place in the Kourin area of Zahedan, Sistan and Balouchestan Province.
The statement said the kidnapping team had abducted a construction project engineer in western Zahedan on Monday and intended to transfer him to a neighboring country.
Following the kidnapping, IRGC Ground Force personnel from the Quds Base used their intelligence capabilities to locate the team’s hideout in Kourin and launched a surprise operation against its members, the statement added.
Five members of the kidnapping team were killed during the operation, and the abducted engineer was freed.
One IRGC serviceman was martyred in the clashes, the statement added.

title: Committee approves building plans for permanent UAE embassy in central Israel
body: The Tel Aviv District Planning and Building Committee approved plans for a permanent United Arab Emirates embassy in Herzliya Pituah on Tuesday, six years after the signing of the Abraham Accords and the establishment of diplomatic relations between Israel and the UAE.The approved plan allows for the construction of a building of up to 15 stories to house the embassy's offices and residences for the ambassador and diplomatic staff.The approval clears the way for progress on the UAE diplomatic mission's permanent headquarters in Israel, at a time when regional tensions are affecting relations between the two countries.Herzliya planned as location for permanent embassy for months, mayor previously confirmed to 'Post'In October 2025, The Jerusalem Post reported that the permanent embassy would be built in Herzliya, after receiving exclusive confirmation from the city's mayor.“We welcome the fact that the building of the embassy of the United Arab Emirates in Israel will be constructed in Herzliya,” Mayor Yariv Fisher told the Post at the time.Herzliya has long-term plans to strengthen its ties with the countries of the Abraham Accords, “as well as with other nations that we all hope will join these agreements in the near future, in areas such as education, transportation, technology, tourism, and environmental quality: particularly initiatives that will strengthen understanding and the importance of coexistence and peace in the Middle East,” Fisher noted.“The process of locating the land was complex and included negotiations with various parties,” the Israel Land Authority told the Post last October.The ILA said at the time that the request to search for a permanent location had come from the Prime Minister's Office.Mathilda Heller contributed to this report.

title: Mahama commits GH¢200m in 2027 Budget to complete Police Hospital expansion
body: President John Dramani Mahama has announced the termination of the Police Hospital expansion contract after 22 years of delays, citing prolonged disagreements with the contractor and cost overruns. He said the government would take responsibility for completing the project, with about GH¢200 million to be provided in the 2027 Budget to bring the expanded facility into service before the end of that year. Speaking at the commissioning of a new 85-bed ward at the Police Hospital, President Mahama directed the Minister for Finance to provide the funds. “Following protracted disagreements and cost overruns with the contractor, I’ve asked the Minister for Finance to provide in the 2027 Budget approximately GH¢200 million that is required to complete the Police Hospital expansion,” he said. “The contract has been going on for 22 years. We have finally brought it to an end. We’re going to complete it ourselves.” The President said the completed expansion would add another 106 beds to the hospital, taking its total capacity to more than 300 beds. The expansion is expected to include a 12-bed intensive care unit (ICU), a new accident and emergency centre, 11 consulting rooms and four paediatric consulting rooms. It will also provide magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and computed tomography (CT) scan equipment, three general surgical theatres, a specialised orthopaedic theatre and an endoscopy unit. A mortuary with a capacity of 222 bodies is also planned as part of the expanded facility. President Mahama said the government aimed to complete the project and bring it into service before the end of 2027. At the event, the President also announced the donation of two new ambulances to the Police Hospital to support its emergency response and the delivery of services at the newly commissioned ward. The hospital expansion forms part of efforts to improve healthcare infrastructure and increase capacity to provide specialised treatment to police personnel and other patients. The GH¢200 million allocation is expected to be included in the 2027 Budget, while the government assumes responsibility for completing the long-delayed expansion.

title: Cargo Dragon spacecraft lifts off for ISS from Florida spaceport
body:
NEW YORK, October 13. /TASS/. The US company SpaceX launched a Falcon 9 rocket carrying the Cargo Dragon spacecraft to the International Space Station (ISS) on Tuesday. The launch was streamed on the website of the US National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA).
The spacecraft lifted off from the spaceport at Cape Canaveral, Florida, at 06:33 a.m. local time (1:33 p.m. Moscow time/10:33 a.m. GMT) on the 35th resupply mission to the orbital station.
Cargo Dragon will transport more than 2.8 tons of cargo to the orbiting outpost, including equipment for scientific experiments studying the effects of microgravity on heart tissue, as well as a set of solar arrays for the ISS.
The spacecraft is expected to dock automatically with the ISS on October 15. In mid-November, Cargo Dragon is scheduled to return to Earth carrying the results of scientific experiments and equipment for repair.

title: Jev handed our LLM the wrong page a tenth as often as our embeddings
body:
Here's a question from our test set. A caller rings a multi-trade maintenanceÂ company.
"Hi, I had a plumber round last week and there's a problem with what he did, it's still leaking. Who do I contact aboutÂ that?"
Our AI receptionist does what we built it to do. It searches the company's website for context and hands the closest matches to the language model. The closest match, according to our production embeddings, was a blog post called How to Find a ReliableÂ Plumber .
Which, if you think about it, is about the worst page you could hand an LLM while it's on the phone with one of the company's unhappyÂ customers.
It wasn't a one-off. In a test we ran at the start of October, our search handed the LLM a wrong page on a third of 168 caller questions. This post is about what we tried instead. A model that can't write a word, picking pages off a list. It handed our LLM the wrong page a tenth as often, 3% of the time against our search's 33%. It put the right page first 88% of the time, against 70%. And, the bit I didn't see coming, it knew when the website didn't have theÂ answer.
Sayora answers the phone for small businesses in the UK: plumbers, estate agents, electricians, bars. Most calls are routine. Bookings, messages, "are you open on Saturday?". The interesting ones are questions about the business itself. Is the valuation free? Do you fit water softeners? Can I bring theÂ dog?
The answers are usually on the business's own website, so today we fetch them the standardÂ way:
For a small site, we paste the homepage (or up to eight pages) straight into theÂ prompt.
For anything bigger, we cut every page into 1,200-character chunks with 200 characters of overlap, and embed them with OpenAI's text-embedding-3-large at 768Â dimensions.
On every caller turn, we embed what they said (plus a version with the turn before, for follow-ups) and inject the closest chunks scoring above a cosine similarity ofÂ 0.36.
It's the standard RAG recipe, and it works well enough that we shipped it. It also always buggedÂ me.
A small business's website isn't a pile of documents. Someone who knows the business has already organised it into pages, and each page is about one thing: boiler servicing, fees, the team, the Christmas menu. Shredding those pages into confetti and trusting cosine similarity to put the meaning back together always feltÂ backwards.
Keep pages whole, and write each one a shortÂ description.
Give the receptionist a tool. When it hits something it doesn't know, it says "let me check that for you" and callsÂ it.
The tool asks a model a multiple-choice question: which of these pages answers what the caller just said? "None of these" is one of theÂ options.
The best page or two go to the LLM. If the answer is "none", the receptionist says it doesn't know and passes the questionÂ on.
One lookup from the test, on an estate agent's 74-pageÂ site.
The model doing the picking is Jev, a decision model TypeSafe launched on 15 September. It doesn't generate text. You send it some state and some typed questions, and it sends back a choice with a probability for every option. A choice question takes up to 255 options and a request up to 64k tokens. It costs $0.042 per million input tokens, and output is free. On a 100-page site, that's about a twentieth of a cent perÂ lookup.
(New to Jev? I've written a plain-English introduction: What is Jev goodÂ for? )
The shape fits the job almost suspiciously well. The options are the pages, the state is what the caller said, and "none of these" is just another option. That last part turned out to matter more than theÂ ranking.
We took four of our customers' websites and removed the pages a page picker should never see. Individual property listings went, because a feed already covers those. So did near-identical "electrician in [town]" landing pages, because a coverage list answers "do you cover X?" better than a choice between 31 copies of the same page. ThatÂ left:
a multi-trade maintenance company, 232Â pages
Claude Haiku 4.5 read every page once and wrote a description: the title, the path, a 30-word factual summary and a few questions a caller might ask. About 100 tokens aÂ page.
Separately, Claude Opus 5.5 read the page text (never the descriptions) and wrote questions the way callers actually talk. That gave us 168 questions: 128 the sites answer and 40 they don't. A quarter of the answerable ones also got a follow-up form ("and how much is that?") after two turns ofÂ conversation.
Then nine pickers had a go at everyÂ question:
Jev: one choice question over every page on the site, plusÂ "none"
Jev with thinner descriptions: title and summary only, and titleÂ only
Embeddings shortlist, then Jev: the top 40 pages by embedding, then JevÂ picks
GPT-6 Luna: the same list, asked for up to three page ids, orÂ none
Embeddings on page descriptions: the same descriptions Jev read,Â embedded
Embeddings on chunks: our production retrieval, exactly as it runsÂ today
BM25: keyword search, on the descriptions and on the pageÂ text
Judging was pooled. For each question, every page that any picker ranked in its top three went to a judge (Claude Opus 5.5), which read the actual page text and decided whether a receptionist could answer from it. That's 1,668 judgements. No picker was graded against pages another picker chose. When the judge found an answer to a question we'd written as unanswerable, or nothing for one we'd written as answerable, the question switched sides. That happened sixÂ times.
A picker "hands over" its first two pages, unless it says none. The intervals below are a paired bootstrap overÂ questions.
Share of the 128 answerable questions where the picker's first page was one the judge said answersÂ it.
Jev put a right page first on 88% of the answerable questions, and in its top three on 95%. Our production search managed 70%. That's 18 points, with a 95% interval of 11 to 26. Or, if you prefer headline maths, 26%Â better.
The fairer fight is embeddings over the exact descriptions Jev read. That narrows the gap to 14 points (7 to 21), still well clear of zero. Keyword search came last, at 53% toÂ 57%.
Jev's lead over each alternative on the same 128 questions. Intervals that cross zero mean no clearÂ difference.
Ranking is only half the job. On a phone call, the worse mistake is handing the LLM a page that doesn't answer the question, because a fluent model will often build an answer out of it anyway. That's how a receptionist ends up quoting a guide's average prices as if they were the business'sÂ own.
A wrong page handed over means the picker returned pages and neither of the first two answers theÂ question.
At our production cut-off of 0.36, chunk search handed over a wrong page on 33% of all questions. It said the website didn't have the answer for just 9 of the 40 questions the sites can't answer. Jev handed over a wrong page 3% of the time and said "not on the website" for 38 of theÂ 40.
The obvious objection is that we should just raise the cut-off. So I swept it. Even tuning it on these same questions, which flatters it, the best chunk search managed 73% answered right end to end, and still handed over a wrong page 15% of the time. Jev, with nothing tuned, managed 90% and 3%. Jev's "none" isn't a threshold on a similarity score. It's an option the model weighs against every page, and itÂ shows.
That "none" is useful for more than safety, too. Every time it fires, we've found something callers ask that the website doesn't cover, which is exactly what a business owner wants to hearÂ about.
I read every question where chunk search put a wrong page first. Of the 39, 23 went to a generic guide or blog post. "Rewiring a house in the UK" for "will I get a certificate?". "How to find a reliable plumber" for the leak complaint. A long advice article shares more words with a caller's question than the business's own short page does, so it wins the cosineÂ contest.
Jev reads the list more like a person would. When it was wrong, it was usually wrong between near twins ("Certified electrician" instead of "Part P certificate"), and only one of its 16 wrong first pages was aÂ guide.
Six questions from the test. Questions and page names are lightly edited to keep the businessesÂ anonymous.
The last receipt is Jev's real weakness. It reads descriptions literally. The plumbing installation page does mention water softeners, but its description didn't, so Jev said "none" and meant it. Chunk search found the page because it reads the page text. Key cutting on a fees page and EV chargers on an electrical installation page failed the same way. The fix is on our side: descriptions have to name the specific things callers askÂ about.
Fair question. It's the first one I got asked. We gave GPT-6 Luna the same list and asked for up to three page ids, or none. OpenAI's new Decisions API is reportedly built on a tuned GPT-6 Luna. We don't have access to it yet, so this stands in for its judgement, not itsÂ speed.
Luna tied Jev on picking: 86% right first against Jev's 88%, a difference of 2 points with an interval of â4 to +7. But it was slower, at 0.66 s median and 1.27 s at p95 (reasoning effort low), against Jev's 0.28 s and 0.42 s. It was also less willing to say "none". It caught 80% of the unanswerable questions and handed over a wrong page 8% of theÂ time.
When Luna missed, it reached for something plausible. Asked about a kids' menu the bar doesn't have, it handed over the food menu, with full confidence. On a phone call, that's the receptionist reading the adult menu out to a parent and implying there's something for theÂ kids.
Some of the best numbers in the whole test came from using both. Embeddings shortlist 40 pages, then Jev picks among them: 88% right first, in 0.25 s. On the 232-page site, a shortlist of 100 got 95% right first and never handed over a wrongÂ page.
Embeddings are good at "somewhere around here". Jev is good at "this one". You don't have toÂ choose.
A choice question tops out at 255 options, so we checked whether that bites. Of the 449 business websites in our customer records, 353 publish a sitemap. The median has 14 pages, and 95% have 255 or fewer. Small businesses, it turns out, have small websites. WhoÂ knew.
Then we pushed it. For each question we built option lists of 16 up to 232 pages, filling them with the most similar pages first (from the same section of the site), so every extra option was a plausibleÂ distractor.
Each list holds the right pages plus lookalikes from the same section. Jev picked from the list; embeddings ranked the sameÂ list.
Accuracy drifts down as the list fills with lookalikes. On the biggest site, Jev went from 100% at 16 options to 92% at 232, and the right page stayed in its top three every time. Embeddings over the same lists fell from 89% to 74%. The electrician's site was the hardest for both, with dozens of near-duplicate serviceÂ pages.
Median time per Jev request against its input tokens, from a laptop in theÂ UK.
Time follows tokens, not options or questions. A 16-page list (about 2,000 tokens) took 0.23 s and a 232-page list (24,000 tokens) took 0.43 s. Across everything we measured, latency fits roughly 0.23 s plus 7 ms per thousand inputÂ tokens.
Past 254 pages you need more than one question, so we tried that on a site I know very well: The Podcast Host, with 1,253 pages. We packed a section question plus one page question per section into a single request: 553 described pages and 63,000 tokens, just under the cap, answered in 0.63 s. The extra questions cost no extra time. Only the tokensÂ did.
Answered right end to end: a right page handed over, or "none" when the site doesn'tÂ say.
Jev only knows what the description tells it. Page titles alone cost 9 points on the right page first and 16 points end to end. Title plus a one-line summary did as well as the full description with example questions, so the example questions can go. Writing the summaries cost about $0.002 a page with Claude Haiku, once per page and again only when a pageÂ changes.
On the phone, people don't repeat themselves. "And how much is that?" only makes sense with the two turns before it. We gave Jev those turns as state and the caller's last words as the question. It put the right page first 91% of the time, exactly the same as when we handed it a cleanly rewritten question. Our production search, which already widens its query for follow-ups, dropped from 78% toÂ 72%.
So the tool can take the caller's actual words. Nothing needs rewriting before it'sÂ called.
Picking the page was the easy bit. Reading real small-business websites broke something different almost everyÂ time.
Two sites didn't make it into the test atÂ all:
A used car dealer's host answers honest crawlers with an empty "202 Accepted" on every inner page. Our production scanner gets the same, which is why that customer's receptionist only knows their homepage. We don't dress our crawler up as a browser to get past bot protection, so the way in is the owner allow-listingÂ us.
An electrician's site was made with an AI site builder that draws everything in the browser. A plain fetch gets an emptyÂ shell.
The estate agent's page-builder site fooled our main-content extractor, which returned the cookie banner as the content of the valuation page, the team page and every "selling in [town]" page. Falling back to the page body minus every line repeated across the site recovered 49 of its 91Â pages.
The Podcast Host's CDN started answering 429 after a few minutes of six parallel requests. At one request every 1.2 seconds (its robots.txt asks search engines for one a second), all 1,253 pages came through clean in about 25Â minutes.
The questions aren't real calls. A model wrote them from page text. They sound like callers, but real call transcripts are the nextÂ test.
One model judged relevance. We checked five of its verdicts by hand where Jev and chunk search disagreed, and it was right all five times. The rest areÂ unchecked.
The sample is small. About 35 questions per site, so a single site's numbers can swing 15 points either way. Trust the pooled numbers and theirÂ intervals.
One run, one place. Every picker ran once, from a laptop in theÂ UK.
Our chunk search isn't the best embedding setup possible. A reranker, hybrid search or smarter chunking would close some of the gap. We tested what we actually run, plus embeddings over the same descriptions JevÂ read.
Jev is three weeks old. If we ship this, the embeddings shortlist stays in as theÂ fallback.
The big site is half done. We wanted The Podcast Host's 1,253 pages in the accuracy table. We ran out of API credit halfway through writing its page descriptions.Â Classic.
Real caller questions from transcripts, then a test on live calls. If it holds up, our receptionist reads a business's whole website instead of its homepage, the owner chooses which parts it can use, and every "not on the website" becomes a question for the owner to answer. We'd also like to put OpenAI's Decisions API through the same test once we can getÂ in.
If you've tried decision models for retrieval, or you think we've missed something obvious, I'd love to hear aboutÂ it.
"Right page first" and "Top 3" are out of the 128 answerable questions. "Answered right" covers all 168: a right page among the two handed over, or "none" when the site doesn't say. "Says not on site" is out of the 40 the sites don't answer. The embedding latencies are one query embedding plus an in-memoryÂ search.
Many Hands is written by the team building Sayora, an AI receptionist that answers the phone for UK small businesses. Give Sayora your business name and Sayora builds a receptionist from your website for you to talk to and test forÂ free.

title: Man who killed Russian tourist in Abkhazia could face life sentence but serve just eight years
body: Abkhazia: sentence in Russian tourist’s murder case The man accused of murdering Amina Bikbova , a Russian tourist in Abkhazia, will not be treated as a repeat offender, despite having previously been convicted of a serious sexual assault. The reason is that Edgar Abukhba was a minor at the time. Said Gezerdava , a lawyer and member of the NGO Centre for Humanitarian Programmes, told Caucasian Knot . It remains unclear what sentence the court will impose. “Part one of Article 99 of Abkhazia’s Criminal Code, which covers murder, provides for a maximum sentence of 12 years in a high-security prison. Part two is significantly harsher: it provides for a prison term of between eight and 15 years, life imprisonment or the death penalty. “However, there is a complication when it comes to calculating prison terms. On paper, the sentence could be 12 or 15 years. But under Abkhazia’s system for calculating prison terms, he may serve only eight years,” Said Gezer­dava said. The lawyer added, however, that judges he had spoken to said the court would have information about the previous crime and would take it into account when determining the sentence. The 26-year-old woman from Orenburg, Russia , was on holiday in the Abkhazian city of Gagra, where she met Edgar Abukhba, a 25-year-old local fruit seller. They exchanged messages on their phones for a couple of days. Then, on 24 September, Abukhba invited her for coffee, according to Amina’s friend. No one has seen her since, and she stopped contacting her family. Concerned about their daughter’s disappearance, her parents contacted Abkhazia’s Interior Ministry. A day later, the ministry announced that police had arrested a suspect in the Russian tourist’s murder. The suspect was Edgar Abukhba. On 27 September, reports emerged that Abukhba had been detained on suspicion of murdering Amina Bikbova, a 26-year-old tourist from Russia’s Orenburg region who had not contacted her family for three days. According to investigators, Abukhba confessed to killing her. On 29 September, a court in Gagra ordered him to be held in custody. In July 2019, Abukhba committed a crime against another Russian tourist. He raped and brutally beat her, leaving her incapacitated. He also stole her phone, money and jewellery. In 2021, a court sentenced him to nine years in prison, but he was released as early as February 2024. Abukhba has been charged with intentional murder. On 7 October, reports emerged that the case had been transferred from the district prosecutor’s office to the Investigative Department of Abkhazia’s Prosecutor General’s Office. Amina Bikbova’s father told Caucasian Knot that the Abkhazian authorities had helped the family transport Amina’s body. They buried her on 2 October. According to her father, the authorities in Russia’s Orenburg region provided no assistance. Conflicts involving tourists have occurred repeatedly in Abkhazia. The most recent incident to come to light took place on 26 August near Lake Ritsa, where tourists clashed with local residents. According to Abkhazia’s Interior Ministry, two tourists suffered soft-tissue injuries and concussions, while police took three Abkhazian residents to a police station. On 2 August, a woman from Cherkessk who was visiting Abkhazia on holiday was attacked in Sukhumi. She was taken to hospital with a concussion and other injuries. Russian tourists pelt Abkhaz Supreme Court judge with stones Russian tourist shot in Abkhazia over bare torso – why are local authorities covering it up?
