title: Riyadh keeps moving after deadly strikes, but schools go online and travellers reroute
body: Riyadh’s roads remain crowded, many offices are open and sporting events are continuing, even as deadly attacks on the Saudi capital’s airport have disrupted travel and forced schools to switch to remote learning. King Khalid International Airport, Saudi Arabia’s second-busiest after King Abdulaziz International Airport in Jeddah, will remain closed until midnight on October 17, according to a Notice to Air Missions issued on Monday, following a series of attacks by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthi militants. Operations at the airport have been suspended since an attack on Saturday that killed 13 people and injured more than 300, the deadliest in the kingdom in more than a decade. Another attack on Sunday killed one person and injured nearly a dozen others. The strikes have caused one of the most significant disruptions to Saudi aviation in years, adding pressure to an industry already grappling with conflict across the Middle East and higher jet fuel prices that are eating into profits. Despite the repeated attacks, Salman Al Dosary, Saudi Minister of Media, said on Monday life was continuing as normal. Streets full of cars The National spoke to five Riyadh residents about how the attacks had affected their daily lives. “The usual traffic is there. The streets are full of cars,” said Christina, a Lebanese citizen working in Riyadh on an events management project. “I’m working from the office and the roads look completely normal on my way to work.” Tony, another foreign resident, said his company has given employees the choice of working from home or going into the office. Some of his friends, however, have been told to work remotely. “We could hear loud explosions from time to time, but the situation was worse for those living near the airport,” he said. Several events, summits and conferences are scheduled to take place in Riyadh over the coming weeks, with most appearing set to proceed as planned. However, the Misk Foundation, a non-profit organisation established by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman to empower young people in Saudi Arabia, announced on Monday that this year’s Misk Global Forum would not go ahead, citing organisational and logistical challenges. Saudi Pro League football matches are also expected to continue and the Riyadh Racing Season is due to begin on Friday. Ahlam, a Saudi journalist, highlighted Saturday night’s Saudi Clasico between Al Hilal and Al Ittihad at the Kingdom Arena in Riyadh. The match took place as scheduled before a crowd of about 22,800, she said. Schools and travel hit Schools in Riyadh have been ordered to switch to remote learning for a week, according to an email sent to parents on Sunday citing instructions from the Education Ministry. It is the second time in less than a month that schools in the capital have moved online . The Houthis have warned of further strikes on Saudi airports. Late on Monday, they said they had targeted Riyadh’s international airport with a ballistic missile, shortly after Saudi Arabia said it had intercepted and destroyed a missile fired towards the capital by the militant group. The attacks represent a sharp escalation in the conflict between the Houthis and Saudi Arabia , which has long backed Yemen’s internationally recognised government. Riyadh has vowed to respond, while US President Donald Trump has said Washington is considering joining Saudi strikes against the rebels. Mr Trump condemned the Riyadh attack, saying it was unacceptable. “The Houthis are misbehaving very badly. No good,” the President said. He added that he would be speaking to Prince Mohammed. The airport closure has forced travellers to find alternative routes out of Saudi Arabia. Ahmed, who needed to travel for work, said he drove from Riyadh to Dammam, flew to Jeddah and then caught a flight to Paris. “The [King Khalid] airport is closed and I was travelling for work, so I had to take the longer route,” he said. Gap in public alerts Rami, another Riyadh resident, said he was concerned about the apparent gap in public alerts before the latest attacks. He said he had not received one for weeks, until they resumed on Monday. “I received one yesterday,” he said. “Before that, the last one I got was on September 19. And I’m not the only one who noticed the gap.” His account could not independently establish whether alerts had been issued to other residents. Messages seen by The National suggest public alerts had resumed by Monday. Early on Tuesday, residents also received a Civil Defence message urging them to update their mobile phone operating systems to the latest available version “to ensure that warnings are received”. The contrast between busy streets and the disruption to schools and air travel reflects the uncertainty facing residents as Saudi Arabia braces for further attacks, and the possibility of a wider conflict that could draw in the US. The interviewees’ surnames have been withheld at their request because of the sensitivity of the situation

title: President Sheikh Mohamed receives phone call from Russia’s Vladimir Putin
body: President Sheikh Mohamed and Vladimir Putin have spoken by phone, with the two leaders reaffirming the strength of ties between the UAE and Russia. Sheikh Mohamed and the Russian President held the call on Tuesday and discussed ways to deepen their countries' strategic partnership and advance shared interests, state news agency Wam reported. The two leaders reviewed regional and international issues of mutual concern, with developments in the Middle East featuring prominently in their discussions. Sheikh Mohamed and Mr Putin underscored the importance of reinforcing security and stability across the region, emphasising that such efforts are essential for the benefit of all countries and peoples in the Middle East. The call reflects the continued engagement between Abu Dhabi and Moscow at the highest levels of government, as both nations look to strengthen bilateral co-operation across key areas of shared interest. The UAE has maintained active diplomatic channels with Russia, with Sheikh Mohamed and Mr Putin having met on several occasions to discuss bilateral relations and pressing global issues. Tuesday's phone call signals both sides' commitment to sustaining that dialogue in an evolving regional and international landscape.

title: NUC introduces post-accreditation monitoring, admission checks to varsities
body: By Joseph Erunke, Abuja The National Universities Commission (NUC) is stepping up regulatory oversight of Nigerian universities, introducing fresh quality assurance measures targeting admission processes, academic standards, accreditation and institutional governance amid growing concerns over the quality and global competitiveness of university education. The Executive Secretary of the commission, Prof. Abdullahi Yusufu Ribadu, disclosed this on Tuesday in Abuja at the opening of the 2026 NUC retreat with vice-chancellors of all Nigerian universities. Among the measures being pursued by the commission are post-accreditation monitoring visits to universities, post-matriculation monitoring and carrying-capacity visits to improve admission processes, and the development of accreditation software to enhance transparency, data management and regulatory compliance. Ribadu also announced plans to develop a national artificial intelligence roadmap and policy framework for the Nigerian University System, alongside efforts to strengthen research commercialisation and translate university research into practical solutions for national development. The two-day retreat, which brought together vice-chancellors of federal, state and private universities, is themed “Enhancing Regulatory Compliance, Governance, Leadership, and Partnership in the Nigerian University System”. The renewed push for tighter oversight comes as Nigerian universities grapple with funding constraints, technological disruption, questions of academic quality and the need to produce graduates equipped with the skills required by a rapidly changing economy. Speaking at the event, the Minister of State for Education, Prof. Suwaiba Said Ahmad, said improving the university system required stronger compliance with regulatory directives, transparent institutional administration and closer collaboration between the NUC and university managements. Ahmad, who declared the retreat open, said universities could no longer rely on isolated institutional efforts or regulatory directives alone to overcome the challenges confronting higher education. She said sustained engagement between the regulator and university leadership was necessary to ensure coherent policy implementation and make institutions more responsive to national priorities and global developments. According to her, the growing influence of artificial intelligence, digital learning, data analytics, virtual laboratories, research and innovation requires universities to rethink their operations while safeguarding academic integrity, ethics and data protection. The minister stressed that vice-chancellors must demonstrate accountability in financial management, procurement, recruitment, promotion, admissions and examinations. She urged university heads to establish clear institutional visions, set measurable performance targets and create environments conducive to academic excellence. Ahmad said the retreat should go beyond discussions to produce practical commitments capable of delivering measurable improvements across the university system. She expressed support for the proposed communiqué and post-retreat monitoring mechanism, describing them as important instruments for ensuring that resolutions reached at the meeting translate into concrete institutional action. Ahmad similarly warned that the adoption of AI must be accompanied by safeguards for academic integrity, responsible use, ethics and data protection. In his address, Ribadu said the commission had strengthened its operational guidelines since he assumed office on December 23, 2024, as part of efforts to improve the quality and relevance of university education. He disclosed that the NUC had introduced post-matriculation monitoring and carrying-capacity visits to universities to improve admission processes and ensure institutions operated within appropriate capacity limits. The commission, he added, was preparing to institute post-accreditation monitoring visits to strengthen the implementation of quality assurance standards after academic programmes had secured accreditation. Ribadu also announced the development of new guidelines for the award and use of honorary doctorate degrees, including sanctions for universities that violate the rules. He said the NUC Policy Development Strategy Committee had completed a comprehensive review and produced Blueprint 2.0 for the Rapid Revitalisation of Nigerian University Education. The commission is also developing a 21st-century strategic plan and transitioning from the Annual Performance Evaluation system to a Performance Monitoring System pioneered by the Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation. Ribadu urged universities to strengthen institutional strategic planning, warning that sustainable improvements in academic standards required deliberate planning, effective leadership and continuous monitoring. The NUC boss said artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies were reshaping how knowledge was created, delivered and accessed, making digital transformation imperative for Nigerian universities. He disclosed that the commission had developed and deployed the e-NUC platform to automate its entire workflow, while accreditation software was being developed to improve the efficiency and transparency of quality assurance processes. He, however, cautioned that digital transformation must go beyond the acquisition of hardware and software to include institutional preparedness, staff capacity development, cybersecurity and appropriate policies. Ribadu also said the commission was developing a national AI roadmap and policy framework for universities, stressing the need to ensure that technological adoption was responsible, relevant and aligned with national development priorities. Beyond regulation and technology, Ribadu called for stronger collaboration between universities, government, industry and other stakeholders to ensure that research outcomes translated into products, services and solutions addressing Nigeria’s development challenges. He identified agriculture, healthcare, education, technology, manufacturing, the environment and the creative industry as areas where university research should have tangible economic and social impact. According to him, the commission had launched the ACE Alliance platform to strengthen collaboration among Nigeria’s 20 African Centres of Excellence and unveiled a four-volume compendium documenting research outputs from the centres. He also disclosed that the Tertiary Education Research and Application Services platform of the Tertiary Education Trust Fund had been integrated with the Nigerian Research and Education Network at the directive of the Minister of Education to encourage research collaboration. Ribadu said the commission was establishing a Research Commercialisation Division to strengthen the protection of intellectual property and the conversion of viable research findings into marketable products. He added that the NUC was working towards an international study tour for selected vice-chancellors to universities in Europe and Asia to examine global best practices in research commercialisation. Acknowledging the financial challenges confronting the university system, Ribadu said inadequate resources remained a major obstacle to institutional development. He urged universities to explore innovative resource mobilisation strategies, including partnerships with the private sector, alumni associations and development partners, while ensuring that such arrangements complied with regulatory requirements and institutional objectives. He disclosed that the NUC had established partnerships with development agencies, including the World Bank, the Agence Française de Développement and the African Development Bank, to attract additional support for university development. The commission, he said, would continue to work with relevant stakeholders to reposition Nigerian universities for excellence and global competitiveness. Retreat to produce an implementation roadmap. Ribadu said the retreat was convened to provide a platform for frank discussions on the challenges facing higher education, the effectiveness of existing policies and the practical steps required to improve institutional performance. He urged vice-chancellors to demonstrate integrity, accountability, courage and consensus-building in managing their institutions, adding that university leadership must be guided by institutional priorities and established due processes. Earlier, the Chairman of the Local Organising Committee and Director of Research, Innovation and Information Technology Transfer at the NUC, Lawal Mohammed Faruk, said the retreat was designed to strengthen relations between the commission and universities through strategic engagement. Faruk identified its objectives as strengthening regulatory compliance and quality assurance, advancing good governance and transformational leadership, and building strategic partnerships for the development of university education. The meeting is expected to culminate in a communiqué outlining agreed policy actions and institutional commitments, with a post-retreat monitoring and feedback mechanism proposed to track implementation. The post NUC introduces post-accreditation monitoring, admission checks to varsities appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Poroshenko responds to Trump's call for elections in Ukraine: if anyone needs new leader, it's Russia
body:
People's Deputy and leader of the European Solidarity party Petro Poroshenko responded to U.S. President Donald Trump's criticism of incumbent President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy and his statements regarding the need to hold presidential elections in Ukraine with a call to change the leadership of the Russian Federation.
"If anyone needs a new leader, it is Russia," Poroshenko said in a comment to Politico.
European Solidarity MP Mykola Knyazhytsky stated that Trump's calls to replace Zelenskyy actually reinforce the position of the Ukrainian head of state. " There’s no greater campaigner for Zelenskyy than Donald Trump... After every such conflict, Zelenskyy’s approval rating rises both in Ukraine and among our allies, particularly in Europe," he said.
Commenting on Trump's statements, Poroshenko added: " For me, the key question is simple: Are we any closer to a full and unconditional ceasefire? That is the only lens through which any move should be assessed."
As reported, the U.S. Department of the Treasury, by order of Trump, temporarily authorized supplies of Russian diesel fuel to the global market. Following this, on October 10, Trump accused Zelenskyy of strikes on Russian oil refineries and an unwillingness to end the war with Russia, expressing a desire "for Ukraine to get a new leader capable of reaching deals".
In response, Zelenskyy stated that Ukraine is ready to hold presidential elections if Putin agrees to a 60-day ceasefire.
European Commissioner for Enlargement Marta Kos stated that only Ukraine will decide the issue of elections and its future.
Poroshenko has previously repeatedly emphasized the impossibility of holding elections in Ukraine during wartime and criticized actions that could be construed as preparations for them, while advocating for the formation of a coalition government with opposition participation.

title: IOM, C. Equatoria prepare to launch durable solutions roadmap
body: The International Organization for Migration (IOM) revealed that it is working with the Central Equatoria State Government to launch a durable solutions roadmap to address the long-term needs of internally displaced persons (IDPs), returnees, refugees, and host communities. IOM South Sudan Deputy Chief of Mission Newson Michael made the remarks on Monday after meeting with Central Equatoria State Caretaker Governor Augustino Jadalla Kamilo Wani to discuss preparations for the anticipated launch of the roadmap in the coming weeks. “So it is looking at a process of three to five years as a guiding tool to help develop durable solutions for communities, for Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs), and for returnees,” Michael said. The IOM Durable Solutions Roadmap also refers to state- and area-based strategic plans developed in coordination with the national and local governments to help IDPs, returnees, refugees, and host communities transition away from crisis aid and toward long-term stability. In addition, it also focuses on ensuring sustainable Returns & Integration withSupport, safe, voluntary, and dignified returns, local integration, or relocation using a community-driven approach, and basic services and livelihoodsby restoring access to housing, land, and property (HLP) rights, healthcare, education, water, sanitation, and job opportunities. “So we are very grateful to be able to work so closely with the governor and with the government here to support this initiative and do the launch, which we are hoping will take place in the next few weeks,” Michael said. The roadmap is intended to guide efforts to address the challenges facing displaced populations and support their transition towards more stable and sustainable living conditions. Durable solutions generally involve helping displaced people return voluntarily to their places of origin, integrate into their current locations or settle elsewhere, while ensuring their safety, access to basic services and opportunities to rebuild their lives. The initiative is expected to provide a framework for coordinating efforts by the state government, humanitarian organizations and development partners in responding to displacement-related challenges. Central Equatoria State, which includes the national capital, Juba, hosts displaced people, returnees and refugees whose needs include shelter, livelihoods, access to essential services and peaceful coexistence with host communities. The anticipated launch of the roadmap is expected to mark a step towards strengthening the state’s long-term planning and coordination for displacement solutions. However, details of the roadmap’s specific activities, funding arrangements, and implementation priorities were not provided in Michael’s remarks. The planned three-to-five-year process is expected to serve as a guiding framework for developing durable solutions tailored to the needs of affected communities across Central Equatoria State. The post IOM, C. Equatoria prepare to launch durable solutions roadmap appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

title: Edo guber: I made sure Ighodalo lose because of Obaseki – Wike
body: Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, has admitted that he worked against Asue Ighodalo, the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) candidate in the 2024 Edo State governorship election, because he did not want former governor Godwin Obaseki to determine his successor. Wike said a political alliance involving members of the PDP and the All Progressives Congress (APC) contributed to the defeat of Ighodalo, who was backed by Obaseki, in the September 2024 governorship election. The minister spoke at a stakeholders’ meeting of the rainbow coalition in Abuja, where he argued that political coalitions had played significant roles in determining electoral outcomes in Nigeria. According to him, the collaboration between elements of the two parties was instrumental in ensuring that Obaseki did not retain political influence through a successor of his choice. “In the last election that took place in Edo State, the victory was as a result of the coalition between the legacy of PDP and the APC,” Wike said. He added, “We had to work together to make sure that the former governor, Governor Obaseki, did not produce his successor. And that is the truth. I was behind it, and I don’t have any regrets about it. So when people say that nothing like coalition, they tell lies.” APC candidate Monday Okpebholo defeated Ighodalo in the election, marking the end of Obaseki’s administration and its bid to retain power through the PDP candidate. Wike, a PDP member serving in President Bola Tinubu’s administration, said the outcome of the election illustrated how political alliances could influence electoral contests, irrespective of party affiliations. The FCT minister maintained that Okpebholo and Adams Oshiomhole, a former Edo governor and senator representing Edo North, could attest to the role the alliance played in the election. “The truth of the matter is that it has been there, depending on how it is worked out. So the governor today, Senator Okpebholo, will know sincerely that it was that coalition,” he said. Wike added that Oshiomhole could also confirm the contribution of the alliance to the PDP’s defeat in the state. “Senator Adams Oshiomhole will also attest to the fact that it was that coalition that made us to defeat the PDP, even though I’m a member of PDP,” he said. Explaining his decision to oppose Ighodalo despite being in the same party, Wike said his disagreement was primarily with Obaseki’s attempt to produce a successor. He described Ighodalo as a good candidate and disclosed that the former managing director of a bank had visited his residence more than three times to seek his support ahead of the election. However, Wike said he declined to back the PDP candidate because he believed supporting him would allow Obaseki to maintain his political influence beyond his tenure as governor. He recalled telling Ighodalo that his candidacy was acceptable to him, but that his association with Obaseki made it impossible for him to offer support. “He came to my house more than three times. I said, ‘listen, you’re a good candidate, but for this election, I’m sorry, because this election is between us and the man who is bringing you, called Obaseki, an ungrateful person, so returning you is like bringing him back, so I’m sorry. You have to fail,’ and he failed,” Wike said. The minister said he had no regrets about his role in the election, insisting that the Edo contest provided an example of how political actors could cooperate across party lines to achieve a shared objective.

title: Sikorsky Introduces Nomad™ 100 Fast Pack, a Containerized VTOL UAS Kit for Rapid Deployment in Austere Environments
body:
WASHINGTON, Oct 12, 2026. Sikorsky, a Lockheed Martin company, today introduced the Nomad 100 fast pack, a containerized vertical takeoff and landing uncrewed aerial system (UAS) kit designed to help customers rapidly deploy autonomous air capability from austere and infrastructure-limited locations.



The US Armed Forces require rapid expansion of autonomous platforms: compact, low-footprint solutions that can be deployed, sustained and repositioned quickly in contested environments. The fast pack delivers that capability in a single 20‑foot ISO container that houses four Nomad 100 aircraft, mission‑command software, power, communications and sustainment equipment, all designed for maximum mobility, rapid set‑up and minimal personnel requirements.

“Military leaders are challenging industry to expand the inventory of uncrewed aircraft, and Sikorsky is delivering proven autonomous air capability with speed and scale, offering field-ready solutions to deploy and sustain those systems where they are needed most.” said Rich Benton, Vice President and General Manager, Sikorsky. “By packaging aircraft, mission command, communications, power and sustainment into a single containerized system, we are making it easier to move, employ and reposition VTOL UAS capability with urgency and flexibility.”

Instant Offense:

 	In its planned configuration, two Nomad 100 aircraft can be mission ready in less than 15 minutes, with two additional aircraft available within four to six hours.
 	The containerized system is designed for runway independent launch from locations such as naval vessels, tactical vehicle staging areas and improvised landing zones.
 	Integrated communications, power, and sustainment equipment are designed to extend mission availability with reduced external support.
 	The kit is also designed for rapid movement between operating locations. Once a mission is complete, the container can be repacked, loaded onto a compatible transport vehicle and moved to a new site to support follow-on operations.

The Nomad 100 fast pack is designed to help customers close critical operational gaps where runway-independent launch, limited forward support and rapid relocation are mission priorities. Depending on customer configuration, Nomad 100 fast pack can enable missions including ISR-T, light attack, and contested logistics, giving operators multirole capabilities in challenging and dynamic environments.

Nomad 100 is part of Sikorsky’s Nomad family of systems, a runway-independent VTOL UAS family designed for austere operations across land and sea. Enabled by MATRIX™ autonomy, Nomad combines the vertical lift and hover characteristics of a helicopter with the speed, range and endurance advantages of a fixed-wing aircraft. Lockheed Martin continues to push the forefront of autonomy with a mission‑centric evolution that moves beyond simple “self‑fly” or “self‑drive” concepts to operator commanded systems that can plan, execute and adapt complex operations in a dynamic environment.

title: WWE Crown Jewel in Riyadh: Start time, matches, tickets and how to watch in the UAE
body: WWE is set to return to Saudi Arabia for Crown Jewel, with the annual wrestling event scheduled to take place in Riyadh on November 7, despite recent missile attacks on the Saudi capital. The show will feature some of WWE's biggest stars, including Roman Reigns, Sami Zayn , Liv Morgan and Chelsea Green , with two championship matches confirmed during Monday Night Raw on October 12. WWE has continued to promote the show, with no changes to the venue or date announced. Crown Jewel is part of Riyadh Season and continues WWE's partnership with Saudi Arabia, a partnership that began in 2018. The kingdom is also preparing to host WrestleMania 43 in 2027, which will be the first time WWE's flagship event has taken place outside North America. Here is everything you need to know about Crown Jewel 2026. When and where is Crown Jewel being held? Crown Jewel will take place on November 7 at Riyadh Season Stadium in the King Abdullah Financial District. What time will the event begin? The main show is scheduled to begin at 10pm Saudi Arabia time, which is 11pm in the UAE. How much do tickets cost? Tickets went on sale on October 2 through Webook. Prices range from 80 Saudi riyals to 600 Saudi riyals, depending on seating category. Availability and prices may change closer to the event. How can fans watch from the UAE? Crown Jewel will stream live on Netflix in the UAE and other international markets covered by WWE's streaming agreement. In the US, the event will be available through the ESPN app with an ESPN Unlimited subscription. Which matches have been announced? World Heavyweight Champion Roman Reigns will face WWE Champion Sami Zayn for the men's Crown Jewel Championship. Zayn won his first WWE Championship at Night of Champions in Riyadh in June, before losing it only nine days later. However, he recaptured the title for the second time on September 11. Women's World Champion Liv Morgan will take on WWE Women's Champion Chelsea Green for the women's Crown Jewel Championship. Their rivalry developed on Raw when Morgan dismissed Green's championship reign before Green lost a non-title match to Roxanne Perez. Both contests follow Crown Jewel's champion-versus-champion format, with separate titles awarded to the winners rather than either wrestler's existing championship being defended. Seth Rollins and Stephanie Vaquer won the respective men's and women's Crown Jewel titles at last year's event in Perth, Australia. More matches are expected to be announced in the coming weeks.

title: Police arrest four for alleged cultism, recover gun in Lagos
body:
The Lagos State Police Command has arrested four men suspected of cultism in the Lekki, Ajah and Elemoro areas and allegedly recovered a locally made gun from one of them.
According to a statement posted by the command’s spokesperson Abimbola Adebisi on X on Tuesday, the suspects were arrested between 2 and 9 October following intelligence reports.
They were identified as Arisekola Ojo, 32; Oluwatobi Oyewole, 29; Oluwaseyi Odunewu, 32; and Olumagba Ifatope, 29.
The police said the suspects were being investigated for alleged conspiracy and membership of an unlawful society.
The statement noted that the gun was recovered during a search of Mr Odunewu’s residence after information obtained from the suspects during questioning.
The command said investigations were continuing to identify and arrest other people allegedly involved in the case and recover additional firearms.
The arrests follow previous police operations against suspected cultists in Lagos. In October 2025, PREMIUM TIMES reported the arrest of five suspected cultists after a clash in the Onireke and Isashi areas left one person dead.
In July 2026, a report stated that police arrested 135 suspected cultists during coordinated raids across the state and recovered 26 firearms.
The Commissioner of Police in Lagos, Tijani Fatai, said the command would continue its efforts to dismantle cult groups and other criminal networks.
He urged residents to provide credible information to help the police tackle crime in their communities and warned suspected criminals to desist from unlawful activities.
The command provided the following emergency numbers for residents to report security concerns: 07061019374, 08065154338, 08063299264, 08039344870 and 09168630929. The number 08080193432 is for marine-related emergencies.

title: Du and etisalat unveil new services boosting UAE push towards 6G
body: UAE telecoms operators du and etisalat have unveiled new services to boost mobile phone communications as the nation accelerates its push towards 6G technology . Du said on Tuesday it has delivered commercial U6GHz connectivity on its 5G+ network, which will serve as a foundation for high-capacity services across homes, businesses and industries . U6GHz – the new spectrum for the next generation of mobile connectivity – is expected to enhance the cloud, artificial intelligence, digital experiences and connected environments. The U6GHz band was identified for international mobile telecoms in the Europe, Middle East and Africa region, several Asian countries, as well as China, Brazil and Mexico, according to global technology advisory Omdia. U6GHz combines a wide contiguous spectrum bandwidth with characteristics closer to that of existing bands than that of other higher candidate bands, making it the “sweet spot” that balances capacity and coverage, the UK-based research firm said. Placing U6GHz “into the hands of customers … [will be] unlocking new opportunities for consumers, businesses and emerging digital applications”, Saleem Alblooshi, chief technology officer of Dubai-based du, said in a statement. Separately, Abu Dhabi's etisalat said it has commercially launched a service that increase upload speeds to smartphones threefold. The company – which recently rebranded back from e& – is using 2x2 Mimo, a wireless technology that allows the transmission of two data streams between mobile devices and cellular base stations. That new capability is exclusive on compatible smartphones on etisalat UAE’s 5.5G network and will be useful in sending high-resolution photos, videos and large files faster, in addition to harnessing the abilities of AI-powered applications, the company said. “Mobile experiences are changing,” said Marwan bin Shakar, chief technology officer of etisalat UAE. “Smartphones are no longer primarily consuming content – they are creating, sharing and increasingly sending richer data to AI and cloud applications in real time. That changes what we need from the network. By bringing this capability … we are increasing upload capacity where it matters.” Last month, etisalat claimed it had launched the world’s first mobile network operating on U6GHz. Mr bin Shakar said this was key to “accelerating the nation's transition to the 6G era”. Sixth-generation technology , or 6G, will offer faster speeds and data transfers for users of smartphones, tablets, laptops and other devices. Though the announcement does not mean 6G cellular technology has officially arrived, the UAE telecoms company's U6GHz mobile network makes use of several innovations that “elevate the 5G-advanced experience” and pave the way for it to become standard. The announcements from du and etisalat are the latest in a series of developments in the UAE related to the eventual adoption of 6G. Last month, du and Khalifa University said they had carried out field trials for the new technology. In 2024, the UAE's Telecommunications and Digital Regulatory Authority announced plans to allocate 600MHz and 6GHz bands, a move that helped accelerate the development of 6G services in the Arab world's second-largest economy. South Korea's Samsung, one of the world's largest manufacturers of smartphones, has predicted widespread adoption of 6G networks by 2030, with “completion of standards and early commercialisation by 2028".

title: All Systems Go: Global PC App Ecosystem Ready for NVIDIA RTX Spark
body: NVIDIA RTX Spark is a new beginning for the PC — a reinvention combining the capabilities of a gaming PC, a creative studio and a personal AI supercomputer into a single superchip. With up to 128GB of unified memory and 1 petaflop of AI compute, RTX Spark delivers the full stack of NVIDIA RTX and CUDA technologies for creators, developers and gamers, while unlocking a new paradigm in personal computing via powerful local AI agents. Last week, NVIDIA and Microsoft announced that RTX Spark laptops will be available on Friday, Oct. 16 . Ahead of the launch, NVIDIA and its ecosystem partners are rolling out new software features and performance optimizations to expand what’s possible with local AI on RTX Spark. New and upcoming RTX Spark updates — among the thousands of apps, games and models available at launch — include: New agent features, models and tools that enhance local agents on RTX Spark: Updates to top agent apps including GitHub Copilot, Hermes, OpenClaw, Perplexity, Pi and WorkBuddy streamline setup on RTX Spark, improve security with OpenShell and Microsoft Execution Containers (MXC), and enable hybrid local and cloud AI routing. The NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B model, purpose-built for agentic AI on RTX Spark, releases on Thursday, Oct. 15. NVIDIA PAIR moves out of beta and adds llama.cpp support. Top creative apps optimized for RTX Spark: Up to 2x performance is coming soon to Adobe’s top apps. NVIDIA and Adobe have collaborated to rearchitect Photoshop for GPU-accelerated compositing and Premiere for playback, rendering, effects and more. The NVIDIA Broadcast 2.3 release brings new Video Super Resolution, Video Frame Generation, offline file processing and agent Model Context Protocol (MCP) controls to the app. NVIDIA RTX Video Frame Generation and high dynamic range (HDR) capabilities are available now in ComfyUI to accelerate AI generative video workflows. NVIDIA DLSS Ray Reconstruction will be available in Blender 5.3 in November to improve interactivity in the viewport. Developer tools are now ready for RTX Spark: Top developer frameworks are now available for RTX Spark, including PyTorch, Python and CUDA, as well as all CUDA libraries. GitHub Copilot, Pi and other coding agents are now optimized for RTX Spark. Llama.cpp adds support for decision models, and releases a Windows app. Hundreds of top games and anti-cheat are supported on RTX Spark, plus: A 2x faster DLSS 5 AI model arrives Friday, Oct. 16, and a new Performance Mode for DLSS Frame Generation is available today via the NVIDIA App beta . Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB, the third-generation small language model (SLM) for NVIDIA ACE AI game characters, releases Friday, Oct. 23. The latest RTX Remix update, including DLSS 5 support, releases on Friday, Oct. 23. Advancing Local AI Agents With New Apps, Models and Tools AI is changing the way people interact with PCs. Agent popularity skyrocketed this year, with projects such as OpenClaw and Hermes topping popularity charts on GitHub. Local large language models (LLMs) surpassed the intelligence threshold to power agents, with models like Qwen 3.8-Flash-Next catching up to frontier cloud models released just a few months ago. As a result, local LLM downloads are already 5x higher than all of last year. From models to agent harnesses to security to tools, NVIDIA is partnering closely with the local AI ecosystem to make RTX Spark the ideal hardware to run local agents. Local AI Agents Made Easy On RTX Spark From the first boot of RTX Spark, users will be greeted with a “Getting Started” screen to choose and install their agent app. These agents will come with new, secure sandboxing technology thanks to NVIDIA OpenShell and MXC. MXC delivers operating system-level security, while OpenShell makes it simpler for agents to adopt MXC and adds advanced capabilities such as credential protection and security monitoring. Hermes Agent will integrate granular OpenShell controls and MXC by the end of the month. OpenClaw and GitHub Copilot now support MXC. After installing an agent, setting up local AI is also now seamless in GitHub Copilot, Hermes Agent, OpenClaw, Perplexity, Pi and WorkBuddy. The apps will recommend an optimized local model and settings configuration for RTX Spark, and set it all up for users in a few clicks. Many users want the best of both worlds — local models for free iteration, and cloud models for frontier intelligence. NVIDIA Switchyard, an open source model router library, enables agents to intelligently route queries between local and cloud LLMs, allowing the user to minimize cloud usage but still obtain similar results to just running on cloud. Hermes will be adding Switchyard later in October, and other agents like Perplexity Computer and GitHub Copilot have integrated their own routing solutions. Software providers have made it simple for agents to connect to top Windows apps, with easy-to-use MCP libraries and command line interfaces (CLIs). NVIDIA has also now made available MCPs for its applications, including NVIDIA App, Broadcast, PAIR, Omniverse, RTX Remix and a large library of CUDA-X Skills . NVIDIA is also releasing AI playbooks for RTX Spark, available on Friday, Oct 16. Users can set up their first agent, build an AI chief of staff, configure their system for development or design a creative assistant. Meet Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B: Built for Local Agents on RTX Spark NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB, available Thursday, Oct. 15, is a new LLM purpose-built for running local agents on RTX Spark. This model is a 74B parameter, 9B-active-parameter mixture-of-experts (MoE) model, packed into 24GB using 2-bit quantization with advanced quantization-aware training techniques to retain quality. It aims to achieve the optimal balance between speed and intelligence, being faster than most popular dense models while smarter than most popular MoE models with a similar memory footprint. Users will be able to run Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B at launch through llama.cpp, vLLM, Ollama, Unsloth and LM Studio. It will also be directly accessible via agents such as Hermes and OpenClaw. Like other Nemotron models, Bolt 74B is fully open source — including training data, weights and recipes — so developers can fine-tune and customize their own agents. The Perfect PAIR Local AI doesn’t have to run on just one PC. NVIDIA PAIR , a personal AI router, is officially moving out of beta today, making it easier to tap into the total AI compute of compatible PCs on a local network. The free, open source software tool automatically discovers and connects devices, installs AI models and inference engines, and distributes AI workloads across available systems. The official release adds llama.cpp support, direct model downloads from Hugging Face, customizable inference engine settings and RTX Spark support, along with a variety of inference and user experience improvements. PAIR works on Windows, Linux and macOS. Developers can contribute to the open source project via Github — just one month after the initial PAIR release, the community has already contributed over 10 features and fixes to the release. Sparking Creativity RTX Spark brings over 130 accelerated apps, CUDA for fast video and image generation, and RTX technologies such as DLSS, NVENC and OptiX to advanced content creation workflows — all in a thin and light laptop with on-the-go performance. Adobe Accelerates Creative Applications for RTX Spark Adobe is optimizing its industry-leading creative applications, including Photoshop, Premiere and Substance 3D, for RTX Spark, delivering up to 2x faster AI, editing, color and effects across creative workflows. In Photoshop, GPU-accelerated compositing makes complex image editing faster and more responsive, with improvements to the Remove Tool and effects such as Light Leaks. Premiere accelerates demanding video editing tasks, including playback, rendering, color grading and AI-powered features such as Enhance Speech and Object Mask. Meanwhile, Substance 3D Painter speeds up texture creation workflows, from baking high-resolution mesh maps to opening, saving and exporting large projects. The updates will be rolling out in phases, with AI feature optimizations in Photoshop and Premiere now ready in beta, and with Adobe Substance 3D updates coming soon. Opt in to the beta to get access to the RTX Spark-optimized builds. Latest NVIDIA Broadcast Brings New AI Effects to Live and Recorded Content Available for download now, NVIDIA Broadcast 2.3 runs natively on RTX Spark, and adds new RTX Video Super Resolution and Frame Generation AI effects and Studio Voice profiles. A new Offline File Processor lets creators apply Broadcast effects to prerecorded content, with many effects running at higher quality since there isn’t a need to maintain real-time performance. The update also introduces a new MCP server and skill that lets local AI agents adjust effects, change settings and process files directly through the Broadcast app. RTX Video Brings Frame Generation and HDR to ComfyUI ComfyUI is expanding its RTX Video tools with two new nodes: RTX Video Frame Generation and RTX Video HDR. It’s also providing the ability to export EXR files, giving creators more ways to enhance AI-generated video. https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/comfyui_nvidia_vfx_nodes_explainer_4k48_v4.mp4 RTX Video Frame Generation increases video frame rates for smoother motion for GeForce RTX 40 Series GPUs and newer, while RTX Video HDR converts standard dynamic range (SDR) footage to HDR for greater flexibility in color grading. Combined with RTX Video Super Resolution, these tools enable creators to upscale, enhance and refine video within a single ComfyUI workflow. For example, creators can combine LTX 2.5 with RTX Video Frame Generation and HDR to transform a 1080p, 30 frames-per-second (fps) SDR clip into a smoother 60 fps HDR video exported as EXR files ready for color grading. Blender Adds DLSS 4.5 Ray Reconstruction Blender has released a beta version of its popular 3D editor, adding compatibility for RTX Spark. Download Blender version 5.3 to get access. Coming next month, Blender will also be adding support for DLSS Ray Reconstruction, allowing for real-time updates in the viewport so artists can navigate a scene while previewing it in real time. Code, Text and Deploy From RTX Spark Developers are moving from writing code to directing AI agents. This new development paradigm is requiring many to spread their work across their laptop, a cloud LLM and a cloud virtual machine, where they test and prototype. RTX Spark enables developers to work on one machine, running all their workloads and libraries, testing and prototyping, and deploying. They can now do so directly in Windows with the new Windows Developer Config, which enhances the user experience for devs and installs all the top developer tools — or via Windows Subsystem for Linux, where they can get access to the same packages they’ll use to publish to the cloud. Developer Tools Are RTX-Spark Ready NVIDIA has partnered with Microsoft to ensure that developer tools are ready for RTX Spark. Alongside RTX Spark, the community is releasing: The first PyTorch-CUDA build for Windows on Arm. The first Python build that is native by default on Windows on Arm, with Python 3.15. The first native Conda installer for Windows on Arm, with over 2,000 Conda packages. 97% of the top 15,000 Python wheels are ready, thanks to work with the ecosystem. NVIDIA will be working closely with the community to ready the remaining wheels. Development is now mostly done by agents. NVIDIA Skills — an open source GitHub repository that teaches agents how to use NVIDIA CUDA-X tools and libraries — lets users develop apps that are accelerated on NVIDIA technologies, even without knowing anything about CUDA. Coding Agents Are Ready for Local AI In addition to GitHub Copilot — one of the most popular coding agents, used by millions worldwide — adding support for MXC, it’s updating its model router HydraFusion with support for local models. This enables developers to use their local hardware to reduce token consumption while tapping into frontier intelligence. Microsoft is making coding models, such as MAI 1.1 Coding Flash, available locally , and adding llama.cpp as a backend to Windows ML — extending the supported models and enabling the latest NVIDIA performance optimizations. Get started with GitHub Copilot running locally when RTX Spark launches. Llama.cpp Adds Support for Decision Models, Releases a Windows App Decision models are the latest breakthrough in AI development. They give AI agents a near-instant way to make decisions, without lengthy reasoning loops. They can choose what to do next, from classifying requests to selecting the next action, up to 200x faster than traditional agents. Decision models are now supported in llama.cpp and Unsloth on RTX Spark and GeForce RTX GPUs. Llama.cpp is also releasing today Llama Windows , a Windows-native companion app for llama.cpp, enabling an easy-to-use user interface to download and run models locally, without having to go into the command line. This app, like llama.cpp, is optimized for RTX Spark. Learn more on the Hugging Face blog . Llama Windows runs from the Windows 11 system tray, with local models and recommended models from the Hugging Face Hub one click away. Game On: RTX Spark Launches With Hundreds of Top Games and DLSS 5 RTX Spark is ready for gaming, with hundreds of top titles available when laptops launch on Friday, Oct. 16, including CONTROL Resonant , Cyberpunk 2077 , Fortnite , Gears of War: E-Day , Genshin Impact , Hogwarts Legacy , Honkai: Star Rail , Marvel Rivals , NARAKA: BLADEPOINT , NBA 2K27 , World of Warcraft and many more. NVIDIA has worked to bring the full stack of RTX technologies, including DLSS, Reflex, Remix, G-SYNC and ray tracing, to the new platform, along with collaborating with game developers to enable anti-cheat support for popular multiplayer games. Learn more about gaming on RTX Spark . DLSS 5 Brings Neural Rendering to RTX Spark NVIDIA DLSS 5 with 3D-Guided Neural Rendering is also coming to RTX Spark on launch day. The technology uses AI to enhance lighting and materials with lifelike detail, making game worlds and characters more realistic while preserving developers’ artistic vision. A new, 2x faster DLSS 5 AI model debuts in NBA 2K27 on Friday, Oct. 16, boosting frame rates by up to 1.4x. The faster model will also power DLSS 5 in Hogwarts Legacy starting Thursday, Nov. 5, and Where Winds Meet in late November. DLSS 5 is also coming to NVIDIA RTX Remix on Friday, Oct. 23, so modders can add better materials, lighting and shadows to classic characters and environments, as shown from modder Sparkles/Kim2091 in her in-development project, Fallout 4 RTX . Read more about DLSS 5 on RTX Spark on GeForce.com. Game Agents Running Locally on RTX Spark Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB is the third-generation SLM for NVIDIA ACE, the suite of technologies for building in-game AI agents that deliver next-generation gaming experiences. The first-generation model was in a public beta earlier this year for PUBG , allowing players to team up with AI teammates, while the more efficient second-generation model previewed in Aniimo at Gamescom, turning standard creatures into voice-responsive companions. Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B combines natural conversation with multi-turn tool use, instruction following and grounding in application state to power fast local voice and device assistants, interactive characters and embedded interfaces. Designed for a low memory footprint and fast time to first token, this model enables responsive local experiences while leaving headroom for applications and other AI models. Its new conversational mode helps keep responses concise and speech-ready, and developers can turn reasoning on or off as needed. Starting Friday, Oct. 23, test drive the third-generation Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB inside SkyrimNET, an AI nonplayable character (NPC) modding platform by MinLL for The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim. SkyrimNET transforms every NPC into an unscripted, interactive character equipped with personal memory, voice and autonomy for dynamic conversations and context-aware quests generated on the fly. Now compatible with RTX Spark, SkyrimNET supports both cloud and local inference across multiple models, with the latest Nemotron models delivering best-in-class performance for efficient and fast in-game interactions. Download the build on GitHub . Accelerating Modding Workflows in RTX Remix As AI agents continue to help modders make their favorite classic games compatible with the RTX Remix renderer , NVIDIA is streamlining asset updates with a major overhaul to its AI-powered texture generation workflow. Launching Friday, Oct. 23, as part of Remix 1.6, ComfyUI Version 2 replaces complex REST application programming interface (API) node connections with a dedicated AI tools layout directly in the sidebar. This update allows modders and artists to generate physically based rendering materials natively inside RTX Remix with zero API setup required. A new batch processing feature makes it easy to scale beyond single-texture experimentation to full modding projects, while an intuitive presets system lets non-technical creators adjust key settings without touching the node graph. Subscribe to the NVIDIA Local AI newsletter . Follow NVIDIA RTX Spark on X , Instagram , TikTok and Facebook . See notice regarding software product information.
