title: Olympic champion Zakharova and NGO Sports Context challenge presence of Russian organizations in FIG
body:
Taras Samborsky, co-founder and expert at the Sports Context NGO and a specialist in legal and institutional sports matters, announced the submission of complaints to the Gymnastics Ethics Foundation (GEF) of the International Gymnastics Federation (FIG). These complaints document violations related to the presence of Russian sports organizations within the FIG and the inclusion of athletes from the temporarily occupied territories of Ukraine in their ranks.
"We prepared the documents and engaged not only legal specialists but also OSINT experts. We enlisted specialists to document unlawful actions committed by Russian organizations, specifically the Russian Gymnastics Federation, regarding the recruitment of athletes and organizations from the temporarily occupied territories. As of today, this package of documents, detailing the violations and our legal assessment, and prepared in compliance with all procedures set out in the FIG Code of Ethics, has been submitted to the relevant FIG body. The goal is to secure a legal assessment and a decision regarding the continued presence of Russian organizations within the International Gymnastics Federation," Samborsky said during a press conference at the Interfax-Ukraine agency on Tuesday .
Photo: Interfax-Ukraine / Oleksandr Zubko Photo: Interfax-Ukraine / Oleksandr Zubko Photo: Interfax-Ukraine / Oleksandr Zubko Photo: Interfax-Ukraine / Oleksandr Zubko Ukraine must adopt a systematic legal approach to preventing Russians from returning to international sport
According to him, the formal appeal was submitted by Olympic champion Stela Zakharova, Vice President of the Ukrainian Gymnastics Federation (responsible for artistic gymnastics), who initiated the separate filing. "We helped her compile the relevant package of documents," stated the co-founder of the NGO Sports Context.
Samborsky added that the document package has already been "accepted and is undergoing assessment by the International Gymnastics Federation," and that the organization is prepared to "bolster its position with additional documentation if necessary."
Zakharova, for her part, emphasized that the events unfolding in the temporarily occupied territories of Ukraine "cannot be viewed as unrelated to sports."
"When sports organizations, coaches, judges, athletes, or competitions from internationally recognized Ukrainian territory are incorporated into another state's sports system, a very specific question arises: whose sports system do they represent, and who should defend the Ukrainian gymnast's right to her own territory and jurisdiction? To me, the answer is obvious: first and foremost, we ourselves—people to whom Ukrainian sport has given the opportunity to compete, win, become Olympic champions, and work within national federations—must not only avail ourselves of these opportunities but also stand up for ourselves. That is precisely why my appeal to the GEF—the International Federation's Gymnastics Ethics Foundation—reflects not only a civic stance but also a professional responsibility," she said during a press conference.
According to the Olympic champion, "we are submitting facts and documents and requesting an assessment of them in accordance with international gymnastics regulations."
"I do not know what the final decision will be, and I believe it is wrong to predict it before the procedure concludes. But I know one thing for certain: if a protection mechanism exists, we must trigger it; if rules exist, we have the right to demand that they apply equally to everyone. Therefore, what matters to me is not just the act of filing the complaint, but the fact that we are changing our approach—moving beyond merely talking about the problem to professionally defending Ukrainian gymnastics by utilizing the international sports system itself," said Zakharova.
She also emphasized the importance of ensuring that Russian athletes are not admitted to FIG international competitions. "I took this step deliberately, fully aware that certain organizations might respond with actions that could be considered inappropriate. I understood that risk, but for me, the priority is ensuring that our sport has every opportunity to prevent their admission into international sports organizations. I hope that will happen," Zakharova said.
Samborsky described the goal of the appeal as enabling Ukrainian sports institutions to defend their rights and "create conditions under which the return of Russian and Belarusian athletes to the international sports arena would be, if not impossible, then extremely difficult."
"We are not currently asking international sports organizations to agree with Ukraine politically, nor are we asking for an exception for Ukraine or for an assessment of the political actions of the organizations and aggressor nations currently causing us harm. We are asking for an assessment, a legal assessment of the actions, taken by Russian sports organizations that violate the statutes of international organizations. That is precisely the foundation upon which we propose basing Ukraine's position..."

title: Dad’s Army/African Polistas crowned champions of 2026 Accra Polo Club Trustees’ Cup
body: Dad’s Army/African Polistas were crowned champions of the 2026 Accra Polo Club Trustees’ Cup after edging DSGHOB 6-5½ in a thrilling and closely contested final on Saturday, October 10. Patrons at the Accra Polo Club were treated to an enthralling display of polo as both teams traded goals in a pulsating encounter that went down to the wire. Starting with a half-goal handicap, DSGHOB were quickly pegged back as Dad’s Army/African Polistas, inspired by Dantani Sahnoon, scored twice in the opening chukka to take an early lead. L-R: Moses Armah – Special Guest of Honour and President of Medeama Sporting Club; Ricky Khubchandani – APC Member and tournament commentator; David Awuah-Darko – President of APC; Alhaji Yusif Ibrahim – APC Chairman of Trustees; Kwakye Dopoah-Dei – APC Trustee; Gerard Boakye – APC Entertainment Executive; and Fentuo Tahiru Fentuo – Special Guest of Honour, JoySports journalist and tournament guest commentator DSGHOB responded at the start of the second chukka to reduce the deficit, but Dad’s Army/African Polistas restored their advantage just before the break. DSGHOB refused to back down, with siblings Edward Osei Boakye and Gerald Osei Boakye Jnr combining with South African player Rattray to keep the contest alive and set up a dramatic finish. The fourth and final chukka proved to be a ding-dong battle, with DSGHOB repeatedly threatening to complete a comeback. They came within half a goal of drawing level before Dad’s Army/African Polistas restored their advantage. Just when it appeared the champions had sealed victory, DSGHOB struck again to cut the deficit to half a goal. However, the final whistle came before they could complete the comeback, handing Dad’s Army/African Polistas a narrow 6-5½ victory. The thrilling contest drew applause from the crowd, who witnessed an exciting showcase of skill, determination and competitive spirit. Sahnoon’s influential performance was recognised with the Most Valuable Player (MVP) award. He received a beautiful trophy from Accra Polo Club Trustees Chairman Alhaji Yusif Ibrahim, who had celebrated his 80th birthday just days earlier.

title: Mahama approves Integrated Basic Education Model, with funding expected in 2027 under GETFund formula
body: Education Minister Haruna Iddrisu says President John Dramani Mahama has approved plans to introduce an Integrated Basic Education Model that will bring kindergarten, primary and junior high school education together within a single school environment. The model is expected to receive funding allocations under the 2027 formula of the Ghana Education Trust Fund (GETFund), with the government planning to construct at least one model school in every district or region of the country. Speaking on Joy FM’s Super Morning Show on Tuesday, October 13, Mr Iddrisu said the initiative would provide a dedicated infrastructure to accommodate pupils from kindergarten through to junior high school. Under the proposed model, pupils would progress from kindergarten to Primary One through to Primary Six before continuing to junior high school within the same school environment. The infrastructure would include classroom blocks, a changing room, a laboratory and a Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM) room. “I have just gotten approval from President Mahama to introduce what we call the Integrated Basic Education Model,” he said. He explained that the arrangement would allow children to begin at kindergarten, progress through primary school and continue to junior high school without having to move to a different school environment. “What we are seeking to do is to have a new basic education model where the child starts kindergarten, moves to primary 1 to primary 6, and moves to junior high school within the same school environment, with a changing room as part of it, an ICT laboratory and a STEM room as part of it, in one dedicated infrastructure,” he said. Mr Iddrisu said the idea was inspired by a visit to Asuogyaman in the Asuogyaman Constituency, where he commissioned a school block. The Minister said the government expects to make allocations for the project under the 2027 GETFund formula, adding that preparations would be made to begin construction. “We expect that in the GETFund formula of 2027, we’ll make some allocations so that at least in each region of Ghana or in each district of Ghana, one of those model schools will be built,” he said. Addressing concerns that the introduction of a new education model could lead to frequent changes in the country’s education system, Mr Iddrisu said the initiative was focused on infrastructure rather than curriculum reform. He acknowledged concerns that repeated adjustments to the education system could negatively affect pupils as they progress through school. However, he stressed that the proposed model would not involve changes to the curriculum, but would instead provide a unified physical environment for basic education. Assemblies notified of approved model Mr Iddrisu further disclosed that he had written to the Minister for Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs to inform the relevant metropolitan, municipal and district assemblies about the approved basic education infrastructure model. According to him, copies of the letter had also been shared with the District Assemblies Common Fund and GETFund to ensure that the relevant institutions were informed of the government’s approved design.

title: NSCDC Gets New Commandant In Akwa Ibom
body: Jonathan Olariche has assumed duty as the 18th State Commandant of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, NSCDC, Akwa Ibom State Command. ‎Olariche, whose last place of assignment was the NSCDC Zonal Command Headquarters in Awka, urged officers and men of the command to rededicate themselves to delivering on the corps’ mandate by showing commitment to duty. ‎The commandant, in his maiden briefing to NSCDC personnel at the command’s headquarters in Uyo on Monday, vowed to protect critical government infrastructure, lives and property of residents. ‎Olariche, who titled his speech “Dawn of a New Paradigm,” said he would operate on a three-point agenda of leadership development, core mandate advancement, and capacity building and empowerment. ‎He solicited the cooperation of officers and men of the command to ensure the command achieves the three-point agenda and moves the corps forward. ‎“To my respected officers and men of the Akwa Ibom State Command, let me be clear: the achievement of this agenda requires an immediate and total shift in mindset. ‎“We cannot expect new results with old habits. I call on every officer, from the senior management down to the latest recruit, to embrace a spirit of discipline, dedication, and professional renewal. ‎“Align your attitude with this new paradigm. Let professionalism be your identity, promptness your tradition, and integrity your signature. This Command has a zero-tolerance policy on failure,” Olariche said. ‎The new commandant vowed to clamp down on perpetrators of crime, oil thieves, vandals targeting critical national assets and infrastructure, and criminal elements operating in the state. ‎Olariche appealed to the people of Akwa Ibom for maximum support and cooperation with the command by sharing information about criminals and criminal activities to ensure a safer society. ‎He said, “Security is a collective responsibility. Our doors are ever open for constructive collaboration, intelligence sharing, and mutual respect.” The post NSCDC Gets New Commandant In Akwa Ibom appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Finance Minister: This Is the Wrong Time to Impose New Taxes
body: Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, has declared that this is the wrong time for governments to impose new taxes or increase the tax burden on vulnerable people and productive sectors of the economy. Oyedele spoke on the sidelines of the 2026 annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank in Bangkok, Thailand, where he presented the communiqué of the Intergovernmental Group of Twenty-Four (G24). According to him, governments should balance revenue mobilisation with the need to protect vulnerable populations from additional financial pressure. “This is the wrong time to impose new taxes or increase the tax burden, particularly on vulnerable populations and productive sectors of the economy,” Oyedele said. Responding to a question on how developing countries could reduce debt-servicing costs without cutting essential public spending, the minister said governments should look inward for savings and improve revenue mobilisation without imposing additional burdens on citizens and businesses. “The measures, as you asked, would first involve every country looking inward to identify areas for savings and revenue mobilisation, while bearing in mind that this is the wrong time to impose new taxes or increase the tax burden, particularly on vulnerable populations and productive sectors of the economy,” he said. Oyedele said borrowing remained necessary for economic growth but stressed that it should be used to support job creation and inclusive development. “Borrowing and debt financing are necessary conditions for growth, and every emerging and developing country must be able to use debt financing in a way that has an overall positive impact, particularly by stimulating job-rich and inclusive growth,” he said. He also said public financing, which is often constrained, should be directed towards essential services such as healthcare and education, while private capital could help meet other investment needs. On the balance between taxation and borrowing, Oyedele said neither option should be considered in isolation. “If you collect taxes, you raise the money now, and that itself has a lot of trade-offs. What taxes are you collecting? If you collect taxes from the most vulnerable, you deprive them of money to provide food, healthcare and education,” he said. According to Oyedele, “debt is future taxes, so it’s not one or the other. It’s about striking a balance, bearing in mind that, ultimately, the purpose of taxation and borrowing is to cater for the people.” Daily Trust reports that the meeting is holding from October 12 to October 18, 2026. It is being attended by delegations from over 190 countries. The Nigeria delegation include Chief Executive Officers of financial institutions, representatives of the private sector, Civil Society Organisations, Non-Governmental Organisations and other stakeholders. The meeting, aimed at promoting global macro-economic financial stability along IMF’s long-standing mission, provides policy advice, surveillance of member countries’ economies , and financial assistance to countries facing balance-of-payments issues.

title: Government spent millions on Trump ads. And, federal agents raid Ilhan Omar's home
body:
Good morning. You're reading the Up First newsletter. Subscribe here to get it delivered to your inbox, and listen to the Up First podcast for all the news you need to start your day.
The U.S. government continues to pay for ads promoting President Trump , even after he announced that his MAGA Inc. super PAC would take over funding. A federal judge ordered the ads to be taken down, yet they remained on air. An NPR analysis of data from AdImpact finds that nearly $22 million in taxpayer funds have been spent since the campaign began in late September. Almost $10 million of that was spent after Trump pledged on an Oct. 5 Truth Social post to fund the campaign privately. The White House has called the ads public service announcements, but a lawsuit by Common Cause and others argued they were funded without congressional approval, violating restrictions on taxpayer-funded publicity and propaganda.
President Trump leaves the stage after speaking during an election rally in Syracuse, New York on Oct. 9, 2026. Alex Wong/Getty Images hide caption
Trump has ramped up his campaign travel ahead of the midterm elections. He rallied supporters in Youngstown, Ohio, last night and is heading to Alaska today. More events are planned for later this week. He has been trying to encourage his supporters to vote by telling them to pretend he is on the ballot.
Federal agents searched Rep. Ilhan Omar's home in Washington, D.C. , yesterday morning. Omar, D-Minn., says the search was politically motivated by the Trump administration. The Department of Justice told NPR in a statement that Homeland Security Investigations agents "executed a judicially authorized search warrant," approved by the DOJ, as part of an ongoing federal investigation. Current and former federal officials with knowledge of the search who were not authorized to speak publicly confirmed the details, revealing that this multi-year probe includes whistleblower complaints and focuses on allegations of immigration fraud .
The safest way to protect yourself from measles when traveling is to be vaccinated. Malte Mueller/Getty Images hide caption
Living Better is a special series about what it takes to stay healthy in America.
The U.S. is experiencing its worst measles resurgence in decades. More than 3,600 confirmed cases and two deaths have been reported as of late September. Outbreaks in several states and exposures in public places like bars, sports stadiums and public transit have raised concerns about travel safety. Almost all U.S. measles cases involve unvaccinated individuals, and as the outbreaks grow in some states, the risk of exposure is getting higher. Here's what to know before traveling by plane or train .
When Lee Krasner was asked in a 1978 interview what she was doing while her husband Jackson Pollock was becoming so famous, she said, "I was working all the time." Krasner is shown above, at work, in 1981. Ernst Haas/Getty Images hide caption
The Metropolitan Museum of Art's new blockbuster exhibition showcases the works of two 20th-century artists. Jackson Pollock is well-known for his drip paintings. His wife, Lee Krasner, has often been overshadowed by her husband. This show finally gives Krasner the recognition she deserves. With more than 120 pieces on display — 74 from Krasner and 48 from Pollock — the show highlights Krasner as a titan of Abstract Expressionism, too. Check out some of the photos from the exhibit .
U.S. economists Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford are announced as the winners of the 2026 Nobel prize in economics at the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences in Stockholm on Monday. Jonathan Nackstrand/AFP via Getty Images hide caption

title: Anthropic says it cut Claude reasoning token theft by up to 99% in fight against industrial-scale distillation
body:
Anthropic is battling large-scale distillation attacks on its Claude models. In these attacks, companies systematically copy an AI model's capabilities to train their own, smaller models . Anthropic says its new defenses have cut the volume of extracted reasoning tokens, the model's internal chain-of-thought steps, by 90 to 99 percent. Attackers use networks of hundreds of thousands of fake accounts to pull it off.
Anthropic names Chinese companies Zhipu and Moonshot as participants. Zhipu allegedly siphoned cyber capabilities from leading US models for its GLM-5.3 model, while Moonshot secretly routed queries through Claude. The stolen capabilities could end up in foreign military and surveillance systems.
Anthropic now restricts access to Claude's internal reasoning steps, runs a classifier that detects extraction attempts, and automatically bans flagged accounts. Tens of thousands have already been banned. Anthropic is calling on other AI developers to adopt similar protections, although the company admits that legitimate users are getting caught up in the process too. Ad Ad

title: Money-driven elections fuelling corruption – Haruna Iddrisu
body: Education Minister Haruna Iddrisu has warned that the growing influence of money in Ghana’s elections is fuelling corruption, calling for efforts to prevent financial resources from becoming the deciding factor in who wins political office. The Tamale South MP questioned whether political parties were sufficiently democratic in their internal processes. “But ultimately, you want to reduce the money politics and money being the yardstick in determining who gets elected to Parliament and who does not, because that’s what is building up the corruption,” he said. “Our corruption is driven by need and opportunity.” Mr Iddrisu raised the issue while discussing the implications of a recent Supreme Court ruling concerning an expanded delegate system. He questioned what the ruling could mean for Ghana’s democracy, the possibility of state funding for political parties and efforts to curb the influence of money in political competition. “What does that hold for an opportunity for state financing of political parties, even if it is a certain minimum or a threshold?” he asked. His remarks presented state financing as an issue for consideration, rather than a specific funding proposal. Mr Iddrisu also questioned how political parties were responding to constitutional requirements for democratic internal processes. “Are the political parties responding to that? And how are they responding to that? That must be of interest to all of us,” he said. The former Minority Leader further stressed the importance of accommodating dissent and constructive criticism, arguing that both should contribute to better governance and improvements in citizens’ lives. “But I think that for the good of our democracy, it’s good to tolerate dissent, and it’s good to tolerate constructive criticism,” he said.

title: What is known about West providing Ukraine with no intel on Russian missile launches
body:
MOSCOW, October 13. /TASS/. Ukrainian air defense systems were unable to intercept Russian ballistic missiles in time due to a lack of necessary data from Kiev’s Western partners, Ukrainian air force spokesman Yury Ignat said.
Vladimir Zelensky later confirmed this information.
TASS has summarized the key facts about the situation.
- Ukrainian air defense systems were unable to respond to Russian ballistic missile launches in time due to a lack of necessary data from Kiev’s Western partners, Ukrainian air force spokesman Yury Ignat said.
- He blamed the shortfall on "technical issues," noting that this was not the first time such an incident had occurred.
- Earlier, the Ukrainian air force confirmed that the country’s air defenses had been unable to receive data on Russian ballistic missile launches in time, adding that the ballistic targets were only detected by radar systems as the attack on Kiev was underway.
- The Ukrainian air force also said that the cause of the incident was being determined.
- On the evening of October 12, Ukrainian media reported that explosions were heard in Kiev before an air raid alert was issued.
- Later, Vladimir Zelensky said that Ukraine had not received intelligence from its partners before the overnight explosions.
- He called intelligence one of the most critical issues.
- Ignat told the Rada television channel that specialists would investigate the incident and coordinate with Western partners to resolve the problem.
- Meanwhile, Ukraine’s Center for Countering Disinformation under the National Security and Defense Council said on its Telegram channel that it was looking into the reasons for the disruption in the transmission of intelligence on Russian ballistic missile launches as various theories circulated online.
- The center noted that one possibility was that the transfer of intelligence to Ukraine had been suspended, although official details were still being verified.
- The European edition of Politico reported that US President Donald Trump could cut off US intelligence to Ukraine or pressure entrepreneur Elon Musk to disconnect Starlink satellite internet, on which the Ukrainian military depends heavily.
- The Financial Times newspaper reported, citing unnamed European officials, that the US administration was threatening to suspend the weapons procurement program and the provision of intelligence to Ukraine.
- Meanwhile, the Ukrainian news outlet Strana noted that there had been no official information confirming that the United States might have halted intelligence sharing with Ukraine.
- Meanwhile, Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrey Sibiga also said that Kiev continues to receive intelligence from the United States.
- The European Commission has received no notifications from Washington regarding a suspension of intelligence sharing with Kiev, EC Spokesman Christian Wigand said at a briefing in Brussels.
- Republican Senator Roger Wicker, chairman of the US Senate Armed Forces Committee, also stated that the United States was sharing intelligence with Ukraine.
- Ukrainian lawmaker Galina Yanchenko previously said that if the transfer of US intelligence to Kiev were suspended, Ukrainian authorities would be unable to obtain timely information on Russian ballistic missile launches.
- US journalist Tucker Carlson described US intelligence sharing with Kiev as the only reason the Ukraine conflict has not yet ended.
- Ukrainian authorities risk being unable to reach a bunker in time during Russian missile strikes without US intelligence, Andrey Klintsevich, head of the Center for the Study of Military and Political Conflicts, told TASS.
- According to Politico, the recent Russia-US diesel agreements came "in a difficult month for Ukrainians, with a bitterly cold winter fast approaching."
- This made Vladimir Zelensky think about "how angry he could actually afford to be."
- Russian President Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump held a phone call on October 9 during which they discussed petroleum product supplies, among other things.
- The Russian leader said that Moscow had reiterated its readiness to supply oil and petroleum products to the United States and global markets.
- According to Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak, Russia is lifting its ban on diesel exports earlier than planned and is ready to supply 300,000 tons of diesel in October, raising the volume to 500,000 tons in November and one million tons in December. Monthly supplies could subsequently reach three million tons.
- The US administration, in turn, issued a general license authorizing Russian diesel supplies to the global market until April 7, 2027.
- Zelensky criticized Trump for agreeing to lift sanctions on Russian diesel fuel supplies, describing the move as "obvious weakness."

title: ‘Breaking Bad’ actor RJ Mitte dies at 34
body: US actor RJ Mitte, best known for playing Walter White Jr., the son of drug kingpin Walter White in the award-winning television drama Breaking Bad , has died at the age of 34. Mitte died in Brownsville, Texas, on Monday, according to reports. His publicist confirmed to Reuters that the actor died by suicide. “It is with profound sadness that we share the tragic passing of beloved actor, philanthropist, and passionate disability rights advocate RJ Mitte,” his representative told the BBC. The actor, who had cerebral palsy, drew on his personal experiences to portray Walter ‘Flynn’ White Jr. in the Emmy-winning series. Bryan Cranston, who played his father in the drama, paid tribute to Mitte on Instagram, expressing his grief over the news. “I met him when he was only 14 years old when he was cast as Walter White Jr., a part he played with such joy and enthusiasm,” said Cranston. “That kid was pretty raw when we started shooting the pilot in February of 2007, but little by little we watched him grow into a really fine actor.” Cranston played Walter White, a high school chemistry teacher who turned to crime to provide for his family after being diagnosed with cancer. Reflecting on Mitte’s development as an actor and his work advocating for performers with disabilities, Cranston praised his former co-star for refusing to let cerebral palsy limit his ambitions. He noted that Mitte never allowed his condition to “be an excuse for anything”. “All that promise and potential now is such a loss,” wrote the actor, adding that he “thoroughly enjoyed being with him throughout the years on the series, and after the spotlight on Breaking Bad dimmed”. Cranston also expressed shock over the circumstances surrounding Mitte’s death. He said “it is especially devastating to hear that he took his own life.” Cranston added: “I’ll miss you, son.” Mitte’s representative, Sean Reilly, also paid tribute to the actor, highlighting his contribution to disability awareness and inclusion. “Mitte brought authenticity to the role and built a platform on disability awareness and inclusion,” Reilly told the BBC. Beyond acting, Mitte served as an ambassador for United Cerebral Palsy and Shriners Children’s, organisations that support people with disabilities and children requiring specialised healthcare. He also established The Mitte Foundation to support philanthropic activities and community initiatives. Through his advocacy, the actor used his public profile “to challenge stereotypes and promote greater representation for people with disabilities”, Reilly said. title: NATO recon aircraft spotted again over Black Sea
body:
MOSCOW, October 13. /TASS/. A US-registered NATO reconnaissance aircraft has been spotted again over the neutral waters of the Black Sea, a source in air traffic control services told TASS, noting that this is the aircraft’s first flight in the area since the beginning of the week.
"The Bombardier ARTEMIS II reconnaissance aircraft has been spotted again over the neutral waters of the Black Sea, where it is flying from west to east and back in the southern part of the water area," the source said. He noted that the aircraft is flying at an altitude of about 10 km, without using the civil aviation flight routes and without entering the airspace of any country.
The source recalled that this aircraft is permanently based at the airfield in Constanta, Romania, from where it typically takes off on weekdays for operating in the areas over the Black Sea, the Baltic states, or near the Kaliningrad Region. He also emphasized that the aircraft had already flown over the Black Sea last week. On Wednesday, October 7, it was accompanied by a Swedish Air Force Gulfstream S102B Korpen radar intelligence aircraft, which was flying a similar route.
The source noted in this regard that in late July, the Bombardier ARTEMIS II set a sort of record by remaining over the Black Sea for nine hours.

title: Ukraine's digital networks top winter priority - Balashov
body:
The Ministry of Digital Transformation has made the resilience of digital infrastructure and mobile networks a priority in winter preparations, so that they keep working during power outages, Deputy Minister of Digital Transformation for Cybersecurity and Cloud Technologies Vitaliy Balashov told Interfax-Ukraine.
"The government, in the person of the prime minister, has put winter preparation and maximum resilience first. So we have also put the resilience of digital infrastructure and mobile networks first, so that mobile operators can keep their networks running during blackouts," the deputy minister said in the interview.
The ministry took a systemic approach aimed at reform and long-term protection of physical infrastructure, and work on it is under way, but it has also singled out urgent measures that can be implemented before winter, he said.
Balashov said this means stepping up cooperation with foreign partners, "because one of the ways to protect physical infrastructure is to go outside Ukraine."
Among other areas of work, Balashov named a drafted document, the Concept for the Development of Cloud Services in Ukraine 26-31, which sets out a principle similar to the American Cloud First, under which any system, when it is created, should immediately be considered for hosting in the cloud.
The deputy minister said the ministry softened and reworded this approach as Cloud Smart. In particular, it proposed an option under which the ministry reserves the right, even at the level of principle, either not to move to the cloud or, conversely, to require use of the cloud where appropriate.
Separately, Balashov said the ministry has drafted another concept document that includes the Cloud Smart principle and a focus on a hybrid multicloud architecture model, which involves using different cloud environments and providers.
"It is important for us to follow the multicloud principle, because it diversifies risks, raises resilience and gives freedom to choose a provider," the deputy minister said.
In this component, the Digital Ministry regulates only state organizations, while businesses that are critical infrastructure will face additional resilience requirements, including use of a hybrid and multicloud model, he said.
"We do not impose specific providers. Business should choose them from those available on the market, taking its own needs and risks into account," Balashov said.
The deputy minister also said the Digital Ministry is open to cooperation and already works with foreign cloud providers.
The ministry also said it does not seek to depend fully on infrastructure abroad. In particular, Ukraine should have an option to keep a copy of state resources, while their owners must have procedures for restoring systems quickly if problems arise either in Ukraine or abroad.
Balashov said this function was enshrined in an update to Cabinet of Ministers resolution No. 1009, which amends resolution No. 205.
"If a system cannot be restored automatically, its owner must guarantee to us, as the ministry, that it can be restored within a clearly defined number of hours if problems arise either in Ukraine or abroad," he said.
According to him, both foreign providers authorized in Ukraine and Ukrainian companies with infrastructure abroad can be used to back up state registers abroad.
All operators, regardless of origin, must go through the same procedure to obtain the right to provide services to the state and critical infrastructure, the deputy minister added.
Balashov also said the procedure is currently quite complex and consists of confirming security certificates, equipment location and ownership of the equipment.
He said one reason for the changes to the law on cloud services is the complexity of its procedures, which large international cloud providers sometimes cannot pass because of their internal requirements.
"So we met them halfway and are simplifying this procedure a little, but we are not easing the security challenges in this procedure," Balashov said.
For the Digital Ministry, it is important that cloud providers working with the state and critical infrastructure facilities meet national security requirements, so the Security Service of Ukraine is involved in the procedure, the deputy minister said.

title: Generators cover Kyiv sewage but can't replace grid - mayor
body:
Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said the Ukrainian capital's sewage system is fully provided with backup power sources, but generators cannot fully replace the power supply of Kyivvodokanal.

"I want to note that generators cannot fully replace the power supply system of such a large operation as Kyivvodokanal. They help in emergencies in the power system. But they cannot work continuously. And specialists need time to switch the system to backup power in an emergency," Klitschko said on Telegram after visiting one of Kyivvodokanal's water pumping stations on Tuesday.

Kyivvodokanal currently has 103 generators, with capacity from 15 kW to 1 MW, to power pumps during emergencies and power outages, which were installed over the years of the full-scale war, he said. title: Wikipedians Believed AI Would Come and Go. They Were Wrong
body:
Already in 2018 Google was training AI to write “Wikipedia-like articles,” and by October 2024, a Princeton University study found that about 5 percent of nearly 3,000 newly created articles on English Wikipedia in a single month (August 2024) contained a substantial amount of AI-generated content. There were signs. ChatGPT was fond of em dashes—parenthetical statements that look like this one—and curly quotation marks. Sometimes, residues from the prompts used to compose articles were left behind (“Here is your Wikipedia article,” they might say.)
At first, Wikipedians tried to shape and control AI, to make its output “acceptable and constructive,” or to fix or remove if it proved otherwise. Generic fluff like “praising a village for its fertile farmlands, livestock, and scenic countryside” and fake sources were weeded out. By March 2026, AI content was found to violate its core principles so often that writing with large language models was banned outright, and their role restricted to translation and minor proofreading.
A much-read essay titled “Death of Wikipedia” explained this defensive posture. It predicted a ripple effect: As contributors reduced their contributions in response to AI pervading the platform, there might be a temptation to replace their work with still more AI, creating a downward spiral. One viral X post lamented that artificial intelligence seemed to be changing things in the wrong direction: “I want AI to do my laundry and dishes so that I can do art and writing, not for AI to do my art and writing so that I can do my laundry and dishes.” The “Death of Wikipedia” warned against something similar: Rather than AI performing Wikipedia’s “housekeeping” roles, it might compose its articles instead, leaving humans relegated to formatting and cleanup. The result would trap editors in an endless curatorial project derived not from human priorities but from the frostbitten harvests of machines.
“The potential ‘whittling down’ each year of our pool of talented writers is the greatest threat to Wikipedia,” another Wikipedian wrote, “as we must increase the number of editors, especially expert editors, to be able to fix the sprawling hellscape of weak, inaccurate and incomplete articles that drag down the project.” A Wikipedia written and read by machines threatened to create a new, deracinated Wikipedia, stripped not only of its context, but of its animating passion. It would be artless, and soulless. When the Wikimedia Foundation says that the care and commitment of Wikipedians to “reliable encyclopedic knowledge is something AI cannot replace,” that is not the same as saying that it will not be replaced.
Once Google introduced AI Overviews in search, they quickly became as central to the experience as Wikipedia was until recently. (This also means Wikipedia still does play a crucial role as a source, only at one step removed.) Anyone who uses AI agents knows that they give plausible, almost intuitive answers, which can pass a superficial review of their sourcing. They are also often wrong. If Wikipedia itself becomes corrupted by artificial intelligence, by what means will we prove when they are wrong?
There is also no reason to believe an AI encyclopedia, or any other encyclopedia, should be unifying. Whatever its shortcomings and eccentricities, Wikipedia is the closest thing to an “encyclopedia of everything” we have ever had. Once smartphones became widespread after the iPhone’s launch in 2007, the old speculations, however far-reaching, were realized: Wikipedia was costless, portable, immediate, and electric. Enormous and omnipresent, it really became an approximation of the “sum of all human knowledge.” But so what? What did access to this oracle mean for human flourishing? What good has Wikipedia done?
A documentary maker, wanting to bring Wikipedia’s story to the screen, asked me a sharpened version of this question. Yes, Wikipedia was the little encyclopedia that could. It had overcome humble origins to become massive. But the dictates of streaming television needed something more. Were there, she asked, any real-life episodes where Wikipedia had “saved the village”? Has Wikipedia saved lives? The answer is “probably,” though not in dramatic or famous ways. Quick-fire encyclopedic knowledge has helped with accidental poisoning, and there are signs that Wikipedia is accessed with special frequency during natural disasters. But these anecdotes are difficult to corroborate, and often, when Wikipedia’s role is scrutinized, it turns out to be incidental. If someone calls for help in an emergency, it is not the phone which is the hero.
Does Wikipedia perform a public good? This seems self-evident but is much harder to measure and, in a way, is out of the project’s hands. In 2013, when an online poster posed the question “If someone from the 1950s suddenly appeared today, what would be the most difficult thing to explain to them about life today?” the top answer went viral as a mordant sign of the times: “I possess a device, in my pocket, that is capable of accessing the entirety of information known to man. I use it to look at pictures of cats and get in arguments with strangers.” Elsewhere, the “arguments with strangers” line was expressed in less lighthearted ways. “The greatest threat to democracy may no longer derive from human agency but from new forms of technology, which have the capacity to undermine democracy without anyone having intended it,” the academic David Runciman wrote two years later. “The forces from which democracy needs rescuing are no longer pressing on it from the outside. They come from within.”
Less obvious to us now is that World Brain was also an antidote. The most significant new European encyclopedias that preceded it, the Great Soviet Encyclopedia and the Enciclopedia Italiana, were direct expressions of nationalist and totalitarian intent, so much so that the entry on “Fascism” in the Enciclopedia Italiana was credited to Benito Mussolini himself. Wells understood that “internationalism” needed its own encyclopedia as a counterweight, but that did not make it a simple force for freedom. He assumed that the World Brain would assist a world government in projecting its power, and though democratically available, his Permanent World Encyclopaedia would make such a world government omnipotent. A world government that was all-seeing as well as all-knowing would inevitably be repressive; a sinister side to Wells’ ideas seemed to have partly inspired George Orwell’s Nineteen Eighty-Four.
Orwell also critiqued Wells more explicitly in his 1941 essay “Wells, Hitler, and the World State.” One of its more perceptive observations is that Wells was not, in fact, a futurist. He was a nostalgic, Orwell thought, a “nineteenth-century liberal” who had spent 40 years repeating the same idea: that history was a battle between “the man of science who is working towards a planned World State” and “the reactionary who is trying to restore a disorderly past.” With Orwell’s help, we can see that Wells’ World Brain was an old idea, not a new one. Versions of it had preexisted Wells by centuries, and this particular encyclopedic worldview sprang from his Edwardian conception of Progress with a capital P.
The encyclopedia handed down to us from the Enlightenment is much more than a collation of facts in a book or on a website. It is a whole mode of seeing and doing, a lens through which a clear, scientific vision of all things can come into view, unobstructed by superstition. Witness the world in this way, and the world changes. So far-reaching is this idea that the philosopher Alasdair MacIntyre classed “encyclopaedia” as one of the three major approaches of Western ethics, what he called “rival versions of moral enquiry.” The others were “tradition,” starting with Thomas Aquinas and Aristotle, and “genealogy,” which began with Nietzsche. Tradition was a marriage of faith and reason. Genealogy emphasized hidden power relations. Encyclopaedia relied on reason alone, trying to build an objective picture of the world that could determine how to act, thanks to a consensus version of the truth. The purest expression of this was to be found in the 19th century, in the ninth edition of Encyclopaedia Britannica, which promised “the available facts of human history, collected over the widest areas … carefully coordinated and grouped together, in the hope of ultimately evolving the laws of progress, moral and material, which underlie them.”
When Three Rival Versions of Moral Enquiry was published in 1990, MacIntyre’s notion was already criticized for being out of date. One reviewer complained that it saddled “the encyclopaedists with their 19th-century dogmatic statements in Britannica and plays down the fact that few if any of their heirs hold such views today.” Yet there were some places that rational-liberal outlook did survive in an unapologetic form. It remained at the very forefront of Encyclopaedia Britannica—the 1987 edition opened with the motto of its associate, the University of Chicago: “Let knowledge grow from more to more and thus be human life enriched.” Most pertinently, it undergirded the beliefs of Wikipedia’s cofounders. Not only did Wikipedia’s text-heavy format reflect a centuries-old Enlightenment tradition, it was also created by two men who still believed, earnestly, that discovering the facts and learning lessons from them was not only the purpose of an encyclopedia, but the central task of a life well lived.
As Wikipedia affirmed its status as a knowledge institution, it also lost its immunity from the crises afflicting knowledge institutions everywhere. The only surprise was that it had been exempt for so long. At the end of her tenure as head of the Wikimedia Foundation, Sue Gardner had likened the experience to living on a peaceful tropical island as “cruise missiles flew overhead.” Culture war had broken out all around, and now Wikipedia was an island no more. In the 2010s, “disinformation,” “misinformation,” and “fake news” were all selected as words of the year in short order, and the saturation of information was just as blameworthy as its corruption. Instead of adjudicating between facts like judges, audiences acted like lawyers assembling a brief and took only what they wanted. The results of “doing your own research,” an off-kilter version of the Enlightenment demand “dare to know,” were algorithmically personalized pseudo-informational systems. Mired in this uncertain environment, Wikipedia approached its 25th anniversary facing unprecedented political, cultural, and technological threats.
All of this added an elegiac note to its birthday celebrations in January 2026. The Pew Research company marked the occasion by quantifying the encyclopedia’s staggering reach—in the decade between 2015 and 2025, Wikipedia had been viewed 1.9 trillion times, an average of 508 million views per day. These immense numbers nevertheless contained an unmistakable arc of decline. In the days prior to the anniversary, a long-time Wikipedian, Christophe Henner, published a long and detailed “wake-up call” for the Wikipedia movement. Since 2022, the encyclopedia had lost almost a quarter of its readership, more than 1.1 billion visits per month, a missing audience who, presumably, were seeking out AI summaries instead. Even when answers offered by AI agents contain links, readers tend not to follow them: One figure showed that the click-through rate from AI chatbots was only 0.33 percent; for the Google search engine, it had been closer to 9 percent. For a model whose lifeblood was readers becoming editors, it was a disaster.
Artificial intelligence was an existential risk to Wikipedia, Henner warned, and the encyclopedia risked being remembered as a “historical artifact that AI once trained on … a footnote in the training data of models that have moved on without us.” An editing crisis meant that fewer and fewer editors were performing more and more labor, “a smaller club working harder to maintain something fewer people see,” as he put it. Past moments of opportunity—for example, when Wikipedia might have harnessed the growth of the internet outside Western countries—had mostly been squandered. The energy generated by places like India and Nigeria going digital had passed Wikipedia by, and in the wake of all this, the encyclopedia risked becoming a “temple,” maintained by the last in a priest class of superannuated Wikipedians. Once sacrilegious ideas, like paying editors for their work, had to be considered anew. Otherwise, the whole of Wikipedia might be reduced to an abandoned cathedral.
Media coverage marking the occasion was just as bittersweet. In Nature, Dariusz Jemielniak wrote that “academic indifference” and artificial intelligence threatened Wikipedia’s survival, accusing agentic AI of exploiting a “parasitic relationship” that “endangers the last bastion of freely accessible, human-curated knowledge and undermines the premise of collaboration on which many of Wikipedia’s knowledge-sharing practices rely.” “Wikipedia’s Existential Threats Feel Greater Than Ever” was the headline for a Stephen Harrison piece in WIRED, a catalog of threats beleaguering the project. More dangerous than hostile think tanks and lawmakers was an increasingly indifferent public, slowly drifting away from its founding ideals. “Economic precarity [has] trained many Gen Zers to see any unpaid labor as a scam,” Harrison wrote. In the cold light of the dawning era, becoming a Wikipedia super editor during a period of unemployment seemed a distant luxury, or outright perplexing, “thankless work that AI companies strip-mine for a profit.”
The tide turning on Wikipedia was more than the advent of artificial intelligence or a fragmentation of reading habits. Christophe Henner thought the “AI summaries” were only a “convenient explanation.” “I’m skeptical,” he wrote:

What we’re witnessing is something more profound: a generational shift in how people relate to knowledge itself. Younger users don’t search. They scroll. They don’t read articles. They consume fragments. The encyclopedia form factor, our twenty-year bet, may be losing relevance faster than any single technology can explain. AI is an accelerant, not the fire.

Even this undersold the quantum of change. Something far older was fast losing relevance as well: It was the beginning of the end of the encyclopedic age. Near the front of the French Encyclopédie there is a diagram called the “figurative system of human knowledge,” which is now sometimes called “The Tree of Diderot and d’Alembert.” The Tree is a system for not only ordering “the parts of knowledge,” but connecting them in a logical chain so long it can wreath the universe. It represents a bold idea: that an encyclopedia’s unifying force will show how everything in existence is linked. It suggests that knowing everything will lead to knowing One Big Thing about everything. This old-fashioned idea was resuscitated in the computer age, and gathered momentum with the concept of AGI, artificial general intelligence, the moment machines surpass every form of human understanding. If realized, it will represent not only the end of encyclopedias, but their culmination. Human-written encyclopedias will still exist after AGI, but only as secular scriptures in the mind of a digital god.
One of the many artworks inspired by Wikipedia speaks to this phenomenon. In the 2010s, the bio-artist Joe Davis declared that he would engineer a real, living Tree of Knowledge, the tree described in the Bible that holds forbidden fruit and results in the fall of humankind. To do so, Davis planned to take a 4,000-year-old strain of apple trees and copy the English-language edition of Wikipedia into the letters of its DNA. He called the project Malus ecclesia, which in Latin is a pun that means both “evil church” and “apple tree church.” In interviews, Davis refused to say whether he would eat the Tree’s fruit; because of laws around genetic modification, ingesting an apple or even planning to may have been a criminal act. Mired in red tape, this tantalizing idea never came to fruition, but its forbidding message remains: The sum of all knowledge is cursed.
The real existing Wikipedia feels less melodramatic than that, and the most lasting dividend of Wikipedia may not be its contents but its process, which holds a promise quite unlike the Tree of Knowledge or even the Tree of Diderot. For years, the annual Wikimania conference has sustained a fledgling tradition: At the opening ceremony, Wikipedians wear their national dress. When almost three-quarters of the nations on earth are in attendance, this produces a real spectacle, even against a backdrop of convention center carpet. All around the room are people wearing hanboks and kaftans and kimonos (the practice was initiated by a Japanese Wikipedian), and when they intermingle, the effect is like those old, quaintly hopeful pictures canvassing the “Peoples of the World.” Appreciating the depth and variety on display takes longer. Those golden headdresses, called serimpak, are worn by the seafaring tribes of Borneo, and that is why they are shaped like ships. The chapan robes that seem to swirl under their resplendent colors are from central Asia; those heavy ponchos, overkill against the air-conditioning, have come all the way from the Andes. Someone offers Jimmy Wales a conical nomad’s hat from Burkina Faso, but he cannot accept all the paraphernalia presented to him. There is too much.
Those might be lederhosen in the distance, although someone jokes that the real German national dress is sandals with socks. At least one tech type seems to be wearing Hawaiian shorts for a similar reason, as the official livery of Silicon Valley. Everywhere there is embroidery, silk and brocaded colors, headscarves and skullcaps, a pageant of signs and patterns from parts unknown. Once congregated, the people wearing this garb do not generate an atmosphere of hubris. In this room their shared mission seems humble. Their talk is the slow, uncertain work of mutual understanding, graced with the tentative socializing of the shy. They are bounded by human fallibility, the same thing that ennobles them. Together, they call to mind a Latin phrase very different from Malus ecclesia. E Pluribus Unum—out of many, one.

title: Governor Rimbasa implores Futuyo to renounce rebellion, embrace elections
body: Western Equatoria State Caretaker Governor Badagbu Daniel Rimbasa has appealed to former governor Gen. Alfred Futuyo and others to abandon rebellion, come home, and participate in elections, saying he has given them a blanket amnesty. He made the plea on Monday at the Yambio Freedom Square during a public rally, which was also addressed by Odrande Tako, a youth leader, Flora Gume, the acting women’s leader in the state, among others. “Those in the bush, Futuyo, you come [home]; you cannot rule in the bush. You are a former governor of Western Equatoria; please listen to my message wherever you are,” he said. “You come back and stand for elections. Do not destroy your homeland. We are here for peace.” Governor Rimbasa also announced an amnesty for those who took up arms. “Today, I am standing here as a caretaker governor, and I am announcing an amnesty for everyone who has taken up arms against the government. The way is open; come and surrender; we will welcome you,” he said. “I am also requesting the church and Islamic leaders to talk to these boys (rebels); they are our boys; we do not want more killing in Western Equatoria. We want them to come and elect their leaders, to come and participate as youth who can represent their people in elections. Some of them should come and stand for elections.” The governor said dialogue was essential to ensuring safe roads, protecting civilians and creating a peaceful environment for elections. Odrande Tako, a youth leader, urged young people who have taken up arms to consider their future and the welfare of their families. “When are you going to have a good life? When are you going to sleep in a good house? When are you going to send your children to school?” he asked. “I want to call upon the youth to work for peace during this time of elections. I also urge my brothers in the bush to return home to work together to make Western Equatoria a peaceful state where people travel safely without fear of attacks.” For her part, Flora Gume, the acting women’s leader in the state, expressed concern over attacks and reported abductions of women travelling along the Juba-Yambio Road. She said many women depend on the road for business and livelihoods, warning that insecurity makes it difficult for them to earn money and provide food for their families. “We women are hurting because we are abducted on the highway and exposed. These crude practices are not part of our culture,” she said. “We appeal to our youths, our boys, that we are your mothers and sisters and use that road to improve our families’ livelihoods and put food on the table because government does not pay salaries.” Meanwhile, a women’s representative who did not reveal her name for fear of reprisals urged young people not to allow themselves to be used by politicians in ways that could destroy their future. “Without peace, there is no development; without peace, our children will not go to school, and we will not have access to the roads we are talking about,” she said. “Today, I want to call upon the rebels to come back home. Together, let us develop Western Equatoria.” The speakers called on armed groups, the government and local communities to work together to restore security and ensure civilians can travel safely and participate in the planned elections without fear or intimidation. The post Governor Rimbasa implores Futuyo to renounce rebellion, embrace elections appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

title: Sybiha: We have moved from ‘no cards’ to ‘don't play your cards’ – that is an achievement
body:
In less than two years, Ukraine has moved from "no cards" to "don't play your cards," stated Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiha.

"In less than two years, we have moved from 'no cards' to 'don't play your cards.' That is an achievement," he said during a panel discussion at the Warsaw Security Forum.

The minister emphasized that "the frontline in Ukraine is the frontline of Europe's defense," and that the future of Europe and the global security architecture is currently being decided in Ukraine.

At the same time, he stressed that air defense systems remain a top priority for Ukraine, specifically interceptors and all types of ammunition, particularly for F-16s, which are effective at intercepting jet-powered Shahed drones.

title: Ukraine receives no intelligence warnings from partners last night, Zelensky confirms
body:
MOSCOW, October 13. /TASS/. Ukraine did not receive any intelligence from its partners before explosions rocked the country’s capital last night, Vladimir Zelensky said.
"Unfortunately, there was no warning from our partners," he wrote on Telegram. According to Zelensky, the intelligence issue is among the most critical ones.
Meanwhile, Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrey Sibiga has claimed that Kiev continues receiving intelligence from the United States. "Do we receive intelligence from the US? Yes, we continue this cooperation," the Ukrinform news agency quoted him as saying.
Ukrainian media outlets reported late on Monday that explosions in Kiev had occurred before air raid sirens were activated.
The Financial Times earlier cited European officials claiming that the US administration was threatening to halt weapons procurement for Ukraine and intelligence sharing with Kiev.

title: Sybiha: Ukraine continues to receive intelligence from U.S.
body:
This was stated by Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha during the Warsaw Security Forum, according to a Ukrinform correspondent.
“You are probably wondering whether we are receiving intelligence from the American side. Yes, we are continuing this cooperation,” said the foreign minister.
Sybiha noted that an air raid alert was issued late on Tuesday night, but he explained this was due to Russia’s use of a specific type of weaponry.
As previously reported, the Financial Times , citing sources, wrote that U.S. officials had threatened to halt the exchange of intelligence if Ukraine continued to attack oil refineries on Russian territory.
On October 9, U.S. President Donald Trump, following a phone call with Kremlin leader Vladimir Putin, announced an agreement on the supply of Russian diesel fuel to the U.S . and global markets and a temporary easing of relevant U.S. sanctions against Russia. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky criticized this decision, calling the easing of sanctions a sign of weakness.
The next day, Trump stated that “it is time for Ukraine to get a new president,” claiming that Zelensky allegedly had opportunities to end the war but failed to take advantage of them. He also accused Ukraine of contributing to the diesel fuel shortage through strikes on Russian oil refineries and called for an end to these a ttacks.

title: Konstantinos Argyros Puts His Aegean Album Before Grammy Voters
body: Konstantinos Argyros has launched an Argyros Grammy bid, putting his album “Kampanes – The Sound of the Aegean” forward for consideration for a 2027 Grammy Awards nomination. The Greek singer posted the album’s Grammy Consideration campaign on his Instagram account in mid-October. Artists and labels run these campaigns to promote their work to the voters who choose the nominees. The Argyros Grammy bid targets two categories: Best Global Music Album for “Kampanes” and Best Global Music Performance for its title track. However, a consideration campaign is not a nomination. Members of the Recording Academy decide which entries make the final list of nominees. Argyros Grammy bid and the album “Kampanes”, which means “bells”, pays tribute to the sound of the Aegean and to Greek island songs. In July, the record became the first Greek-language album to enter the Billboard Top World Albums and Top Album Sales charts. Greek City Times reported at the time that the album debuted at No. 12 on the world albums chart . Fans can find the album on streaming services, as well as on CD and double vinyl. It comes out on Pedagon Records, the label Argyros created with Panik Records in partnership with the American company 10K Projects. Since then, Argyros has also released a new single, “Revma” , on Panik Platinum and Pedagon Records. Key dates for the 2027 awards First-round voting for the 2027 awards runs from 12 to 22 October 2026, according to the Recording Academy’s official calendar . That round determines the nominees in every category. The Academy will then announce the nominations on Monday 16 November 2026. Until that date, the Argyros Grammy bid remains a submission rather than a nomination. Final-round voting follows from 10 December 2026 to 7 January 2027. The 69th Grammy Awards will take place at Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles on Sunday 7 February 2027. In the meantime, Argyros continues his international concert dates, with shows planned in Paris and London. Source: in stagram The post Konstantinos Argyros Puts His Aegean Album Before Grammy Voters appeared first on Greek City Times .

title: Anduril Announces Steelfin a Low-cost Alternative to Lockheed Martin s PAC-3 Missile
body:
Anduril on Monday unveiled ‘Steelfin,’ a family of mass-producible surface-to-air interceptor missiles that has been engineered to deliver cost, volume, and capability against cruise, ballistic, and hypersonic missile threats.
Steelfin missiles compatible with RTX’s M903A2 (Patriot launcher)
Steelfin variants are compatible with established land- and sea-based launch infrastructure, including the M903A2 (Patriot launcher), Mk 41 Vertical Launch System, Typhon, and other emerging containerized launch systems
Similarly, Steelfin is designed to integrate with any fielded fire control software system (AEGIS, IBCS, etc.), ensuring that it fits seamlessly into established battle management processes and procedures.
Steelfin is a two stage design, encompassing a first-stage booster and second-stage terminal interceptor, offering the flexibility required to align interceptor performance to each threat.
The first stage can accommodate different solid rocket motor boosters to meet specific range, performance, booster types, launch configurations, or packing density requirements.
The second stage uses a common terminal interceptor architecture, sharing the same baseline airframe, avionics, software, flight control system, and interfaces across all Steelfin variants.
Steelfin delivers a diversity of effects to meet a diversity of threats.
Steelfin offers a common interceptor architecture that produces a family of interceptor missiles, each of which can be configured for a specific mission.
Steelfin is designed to be configured for threats across the air-and-missile defense spectrum - from point defense, lower-tier integrated air and missile defense, to upper-tier ballistic missile defense - while targeting a fraction of the cost of today’s benchmark interceptors in each mission class.
The standard open architecture interfaces between each subsystem in the terminal stage enable Anduril to integrate commercial-off-the-shelf components (COTS) and compete open architecture designs among multiple vendors, expanding the supplier base and reducing the risk of supply chain disruptions that could inhibit large-scale production.
Anduril has been building and refining Steelfin for years, investing alongside multiple customers to deliver a capability that is urgently needed today. Anduril has already completed ballistic testing with representative air vehicles, and will begin flight testing Steelfin variants next year.

title: Excessive borrowing ‘cracked’ Ghana’s economy under Akufo-Addo – Haruna Iddrisu
body: Education Minister Haruna Iddrisu has blamed excessive borrowing under former President Nana Akufo-Addo’s administration for Ghana’s economic difficulties. He criticised the previous government’s management of public debt. “Currently, the economy, as I indicated, my measure is to look at the NPP’s own standing and lack of criticism of the state of the economy; for me, it is an admission that we are probably doing better than they were doing. And the revelation of their excessive appetite for borrowing is what cracked the Ghanaian economy. We became debt-sustainable, and a country in distress,” he said on JoyFM on Tuesday, October 13. Mr Iddrisu also defended the Mahama administration’s economic performance, arguing that improvements in currency stability had helped businesses plan and manage their operating costs. “We are doing our utmost best as a government to walk out of that economic crisis. Now we have achieved stability,” he noted. Meanwhile, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) has raised Ghana’s economic growth forecast for 2026 to 5.7% and projected year-end inflation at 4.8%, despite global economic pressures and uncertainty. The growth forecast represents an increase of 1.1 percentage points from the 4.6% projected in April. The projections are contained in the IMF’s latest economic outlook report, released on the sidelines of the Annual IMF/World Bank Meetings in Bangkok, Thailand.
