title: Patriot versus hypersonic missiles. The debut of a new missile
body:
During this year’s AUSA exhibition in Washington, Lockheed Martin presented the latest addition to the well-known anti-missile armament family: the PAC-3 Edge interceptor. The new design is being developed for the US Army’s Future Interceptor programme and is intended to provide a direct response to cutting-edge, difficult-to-detect hypersonic threats, as well as advanced cruise and ballistic missiles.
The American manufacturer positions the Edge as a highly effective solution for destroying targets at significantly higher altitudes and ranges than before, which will markedly expand the capabilities of integrated air and missile defence. In practice, this means that within the US Army, the new missile will fill the operational gap existing between the currently deployed PAC-3 MSE missiles and the long-range THAAD system, designed to intercept ballistic targets at the highest altitudes.
In terms of design, the PAC-3 Edge is based on the extensive experience gathered during the operation of earlier versions of the PAC-3 family. It utilises combat-proven technology from the PAC-3 MSE (Missile Segment Enhancement) missiles, which operate on the hit-to-kill principle. PAC-3 missiles are extensively used against Russian missiles in Ukraine and support defence in the Middle East. The PAC-3 Edge also draws on experience from the lower-cost PAC-3 ACE (Adapted Capability Effector) variant and an earlier production cost-reduction initiative known as PAC-3 CRI (Cost Reduction Initiative). However, engineers have added entirely new elements to the proven solutions, which are intended to give the missile higher speed, greater power, and unprecedented manoeuvrability.
A key element of the new missile is the active seeker head, designed and manufactured by the corporation’s Strigo Product Center division, as well as a multi-pulse solid rocket motor developed by Northrop Grumman, replacing the dual-pulse propulsion used in the MSE version. The entire control system has also been redesigned, resulting in a significant increase in range and maximum intercept altitude.
From its inception, the project has been designed for full integration with the US Army’s current and future defence architecture. The new missile will be able to seamlessly operate with the IBCS integrated battle command system, standard M903 launchers, containerised launchers, as well as HIMARS Flex launchers.
Despite the impressive presentation, the manufacturer is currently withholding technical details and has not disclosed hard data regarding the exact range, altitude, maximum speed, or estimated unit cost. However, the preliminary programme schedule is known, according to which the first field tests will take place as early as next year, and the achievement of so-called residual operational capability is planned for 2031. This involves delivering a small series of missiles to the military, ready for use in emergency situations, even before the official induction of the weapon into service and the launch of full-rate production.
The debut of the new missile is part of a broad expansion of the American defence sector’s production capacity. In January 2026, Lockheed Martin signed a seven-year agreement with the Department of Defence to scale up production of the currently used PAC-3 MSE missiles, which envisages an annual capacity increase from the current approximately 600 to as many as 2,000 units, while in the whole of 2025, the corporation delivered 620 missiles of this type to its customers.

title: Affi Agbenyo’s EC appointment is constitutionally appropriate, but politically, people have the right to remind us – Haruna Iddrisu
body: Tamale South Member of Parliament, Haruna Iddrisu, has stated that President John Mahama’s appointment of Emelia Affi Agbenyo as one of the two new Deputy Chairpersons of the Electoral Commission is “constitutionally appropriate”, although critics reserve the right to remind the NDC government of its actions in the past against similar appointments. Mr Iddrisu made this comment on the Joy Super Morning Show on Tuesday, October 13. The swearing-in of 43-year-old Emelia Affi Agbenyo has stoked controversy following her affiliation with the incumbent National Democratic Congress (NDC). The young international development cooperation professional is on record as having served as a spokesperson for the NDC on governance in the 2024 general elections. Since her appointment, social media has been awash with some posts she made in the past that were deemed political in support of the NDC. A video of her speaking on a media platform as a representative of the NDC has also gone viral. As a result, many have questioned her independence and neutrality in such a sensitive office. For many of the critics, the NDC has acted hypocritically, considering it criticised the then New Patriotic Party administration for similar appointments. But Mr Iddrisu says while the criticisms are legitimate, the appointment is equally legitimate. “I know Affi very well, and I’ve worked with Affi. Affi, as at yesterday, was working under my Ministry, under TVET Services as Deputy to the Chief Executive. Now, is it constitutionally appropriate? Those are the questions you should ask. Does the President have the power under Article 45 to appoint? Now, one of the things we have not been able to do well is to use legislation to define the parameters of who is eligible. Beyond Article 45, 46, providing that there shall be an Electoral Commission, which shall have two deputies, we must have legislation which then defines a threshold as to who can enter into the Electoral Commission.” Asked what kind of Electoral Commission he expects, Mr Iddrisu said, “I just want an Electoral Commission that does not endanger democratic ethos and values. Persons who are independent, persons who are courageous, and persons who uphold the values of transparency. “I share this crude idea with you: anytime people get worried about appointments to the Electoral Commission, you know I’ve supervised the Electoral Commission, even as its Chairman and Vice-Chairman, in terms of their budget for seven years. I’m sure I can say that probably maybe Kyei Mensa-Bonsu, I’ll come next in terms of depth and information on the Electoral Commission and its operation within the annals of Parliament. The MP and Minister of Education hinted that there would be major reforms to the constitution to address complex issues such as this. “Now, there’s a school of thought, and I’m sure it’s part of the constitutional review process that President Mahama has ignited, and be assured that there will be political and economic reforms led by President Mahama. There will be far-reaching changes; I’m sure when Parliament comes back, the Attorney General, on behalf of President Mahama, will introduce two important bills in Parliament. One, a bill seeking to amend the entrenched provisions of the Constitution, and two, a bill seeking to amend the non-entrenched provisions of the Constitution.” “So, I think that the appointment is constitutionally appropriate, but politically, people have the right to remind us that if you seek equity, do equity. Maybe that’s what it is reminding us of.” When he was reminded that Affi Agbenyo had publicly campaigned on platforms for the NDC in the past, Mr Iddrisu said it will only be a problem if she does that while in her current position. “If she does that whilst in office, that would be unacceptable as Deputy Electoral Commissioner.” The experienced politician also disputed the notion that EC officials have the power to manipulate results in anyone’s favour. “I was going to share my crude view with you, even though I’m hesitant. In Tamale South, the Electoral Commission, Deputy Electoral Commission- how do they impact my election? It is to provide me with a fair, open, transparent platform. But the onus of winning the election is mine. It’s not that of the Electoral Commission. And the onus of avoiding fraud, or being cheated, or somebody treating you unfairly, is largely also mine. You know, many times, MPs abandon their role. You can check throughout history. Every day, up to the election, I spend my maximum time at the Electoral Commission. I’ll monitor every ballot box, what goes into the box, against the population of that polling station and others, into the night deployment of election officers. “But I can understand the reservations that are being legitimately expressed by the Ghanaian people. If they are unhappy about it, the government has taken note of it,” he stated.

title: PEC sets Nov. 13 special election for Ngardmau governor amid impeachment standoff
body: Speaker Miozawa is acting governor By: Eoghan Olkeriil Ngirudelsang Ngardmau, Palau — The Palau Election Commission (PEC) has scheduled a special gubernatorial election for Ngardmau State on Nov. 13, moving forward with a second impeachment-driven contest after a court order nullified the first. Election date set after second impeachment resolution In a public notice and radio announcements issued last week, PEC said it will conduct a “Ngardmau State Gubernatorial Special Election” on Nov. 13. The commission tied the special election to K.N. Resolution No. 11-27-2026, the legislature’s second impeachment resolution against Gov. Jennifer Ngiraiwet, passed by seven members of Kelulul Ngardmau on the same night the Appellate Court voided the first impeachment resolution, K.N. Resolution No. 11-21-16, and cancelled the Sept. 18 special election. The first impeachment had triggered a special election which was called off two days before polling when the Appellate Court ruled the legislature failed to afford the governor constitutionally required notice and an opportunity to be heard. PEC: ‘By law we have to conduct a special election within 60 days’ In a recent phone interview, before the Nov. 13 date was announced, PEC Director Yamaguchi said that after receiving the second impeachment resolution, the commission’s attorney reviewed it and was tasked to prepare the rules and regulations relating to the special election, all of which will be subject to the election board’s approval. “Once approved, we will put out an announcement soon regarding the election date and nominating petition deadlines,” he said. Yamaguchi explained that, “the first and second impeachment are separate matters. We prepared for the first impeachment resolution and set an election date but that was cancelled by the court order. Now, we have received a second resolution and it will go through the same process because by law we have to conduct a special election within 60 days.” Yamaguchi stated that, “That is the process until there is another court order issued to cancel the election from being conducted.” Costs manageable; most expenses tied to worker overtime and logistics According to Yamaguchi, while elections are costly, a special election like the one scheduled for Ngardmau is still within budget and does not require much special funding. Yamaguchi revealed that the “bulk of expense regarding a special election such as this, is mainly the additional funds to pay election workers working at non-working hours including money spent for other election preparations such as for fuel and drinks for workers.” He said, “however, when an election gets cancelled as in the case of Ngardmau, those provisions will be saved awaiting the next election.” Small-state ballots to be printed locally; counting done manually In terms of ballots, he shared that “special machine-readable ballots are only ordered off island during national elections when large number of ballots are being processed so that vote counting may be done by the special votes counting machines of the election office.” He explained that “but in the case of a small state election like what will be done for Ngardmau, ballots can be printed by printing shops on island costing a few cents per page because the vote counting will be done manually by election workers.” Nominating petitions due Oct. 29; Ngiraiwet, Miozawa expected to run again PEC announced that the deadline for submitting gubernatorial nominating petitions is Oct. 29. In the previously cancelled special gubernatorial election following the first impeachment resolution, Gov. Ngiraiwet and Speaker Terrence Miozawa were the candidates. Many Ngardmau residents say that if the new special election goes through, both Miozawa and Ngiraiwet will run again. The second impeachment resolution repeats allegations of bribery and personal enrichment, while questions remain over whether Ngiraiwet was given the notice and opportunity to be heard required under the court’s earlier ruling. Supporters of both the governor and the legislature have continued to debate the issue publicly, but barring further court action, the Nov. 13 special election is set to proceed. The post PEC sets Nov. 13 special election for Ngardmau governor amid impeachment standoff appeared first on Island Times News .

title: France, Poland, Spain, do not see agriculture as blocking further EU progress for Ukraine
body:
LUXEMBOURG — Three of the EU's largest member states, France, Poland, and Spain, said on Oct. 13 they want Ukraine's EU accession process to continue and that Kyiv's strong farming sector should not be used to slow membership talks.
Ukraine is partway through unlocking the six to-do lists of reforms it must complete to join the EU, but one of the as-yet unopened lists covers agriculture.
The sheer size of Kyiv's agricultural sector raises concerns among EU farmers, who are less competitive and heavily dependent on subsidies, and who fear that Ukraine joining the EU will drive them out of business.
French far-right presidential candidate Marine Le Pen has already leaned on farmers' fears about Ukraine as the French elections near.
"There are member states that have a lot of doubts," said Poland's European Affairs Minister Ignacy Niemczycki, ahead of a meeting of European affairs ministers in Luxembourg, though he did not name specific countries.
But France, Poland, and Spain all said they support Ukraine being able to advance its EU membership bid.
Spain's European Affairs Minister Fernando Sampedro told the Kyiv Independent that "we really hope that in the case of Ukraine and Moldova we will be able to open all clusters as soon as possible."
"The earlier the better, so that we can accompany the strong efforts that both governments are doing," Sampedro said.
French European Affairs Minister Benjamin Haddad commended Ukraine for passing a bill on minorities the day before, which persuaded Hungary to lift its block on membership talks.
"We support the opening of all negotiation clusters with Ukraine and Moldova... I think now it is time to move forward," Haddad said.
Later on Oct. 13, Ukraine will unlock clusters two and three, which cover a wide range of economic reforms. It had already opened clusters addressing the rule of law and external relations earlier in the year.
When asked by the Kyiv Independent if Ukraine is ready to open the final two, Haddad replied, "I support that."
Niemczycki told journalists that "opening a cluster does not mean closing it," and explained that opening clusters is required for negotiations to take place.
"This is a very good moment, because we can tell our friends from Ukraine to enter the EU. To get closer, you have to do this, this, and this," Niemczycki said.
He also said that Polish business is "open to competition, but they want Ukraine to follow the same rules," which, for him, means Ukraine aligning with the EU.
Other countries likewise spoke in favor of progressing Ukraine's EU membership bid, such as Germany and Finland, which, like Poland, see Ukraine's joining as a geopolitical asset.
"We are absolutely not afraid of Ukrainian agriculture," Finnish European Affairs Minister Joakim Strand told the Kyiv Independent.
"We think that Ukraine is doing an excellent job when it comes to defending Europe today, and we hope and believe that the future of Ukraine is within the European Union," Strand said.

title: Impeachment court announces new Sara Duterte trial schedule
body: MANILA, Philippines — Amid its looming weeks-long break, the Senate impeachment court on Tuesday, October 13, issued the new schedule for the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte. The court is set to take a break until November 8 to give way to deliberations on the proposed 2027 national budget. Impeachment court presiding officer Francis “Chiz” Escudero announced the new calendar starting next month will be as follows: November 9: 10 am – 2:30 pm November 10: 10 am to 6pm November 11: 10am – 2:30pm November 12-13: 10 am to 6:30pm November 19-20: 10am-6:30pm November 23: 10am – 2pm November 30: Holiday Following the resumption of the trial, the defense counsel is expected to present its evidence on November 9, to counter the allegations of unexplained wealth against Duterte . – Rappler.com

title: Europe Pushes Back Against Trump’s Russian Diesel Deal, Vows to Keep Sanctions
body:
European governments have pushed back against US President Donald Trump’s diesel agreement with Russia, pledging to maintain sanctions as Germany opposed following Washington’s lead and EU ministers warned against rewarding Moscow while its attacks on Ukraine continue.
The clearest responses emerged on Oct. 12, three days after Trump announced the arrangement with Russian leader Vladimir Putin. The EU also approved its largest single expansion of sanctions listings against Russia’s military-industrial complex, underscoring the divergence between Brussels and Washington.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
Trump presented the diesel deal as a way to ease fuel prices. As Kyiv Post reported , the arrangement envisages Russian supplies to US and global markets, backed by a temporary US sanctions authorization through April 2027.
European officials instead emphasized the risk of giving Russia economic relief before it changes its conduct in Ukraine.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said Berlin would maintain sanctions and argued that Russia’s continued attacks justified stronger restrictions.
“For Germany and for Europe, such a decision is out of the question,” he said at a Berlin news conference, according to Anadolu .
Merz said pressure was necessary to bring Moscow to the table for serious negotiations. He pointed to Russian strikes on civilian energy infrastructure following Trump’s announcement of an energy ceasefire over the weekend.
The chancellor nevertheless said European governments remained in contact with Washington on a common approach to ending the war, acknowledging disagreements over strategy.
At the EU foreign ministers’ meeting in Luxembourg, Ireland’s Helen McEntee described the diesel agreement as concerning and urged renewed pressure on Russia, while stressing that cooperation with the US remained essential.
Swedish Foreign Minister Maria Malmer Stenergard was more direct.
“I very much regret this [deal]. I hope it will not go into force,” she said, as reported by Euronews .
She called on European countries to increase support for Ukraine, including through the use of frozen Russian assets.
Lithuania’s Kęstutis Budrys argued that the arrangement would help neither fuel prices nor transatlantic unity. Estonia’s Margus Tsahkna linked it to US domestic politics ahead of November’s midterm elections and questioned its practical impact.
On Oct. 12, the European Council adopted sanctions against 1,569 individuals and entities , comprising 826 Russian companies and 743 executives.
The measures target suppliers of components for weapons including missiles, drones and aircraft. More than half of the listings concern the ballistic-missile production chain, according to EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas.
The council attributed the measures to Russia’s escalating aggression and attacks on civilian infrastructure. The decision followed earlier council calls for increased pressure, rather than being presented as a package devised in response to Trump’s announcement.
European ministers supported a halt to attacks on energy infrastructure only if Russia also complied, according to the council’s account of the meeting .
“But a ceasefire cannot work if only one party honors it,” Kallas said.
She also warned that an arrangement focused solely on refineries would disproportionately benefit Russia, whose refining network is much larger than Ukraine’s.
Zelensky said Russian attacks on Ukraine’s electricity infrastructure continued after Trump’s Oct. 11 announcement, while Kyiv had temporarily refrained from strikes on Russian energy facilities.
Trump defended the agreement on Oct. 12, despite continued Russian attacks after his announcement that an energy ceasefire had taken effect.
“I made the right choice for the American People,” he wrote on Truth Social. He also accused the EU of buying $250 billion in Russian energy, without identifying the period covered or the source of that figure.
A day earlier, Trump had declared that both Ukraine and Russia had agreed to stop attacks on energy infrastructure immediately. His announcement caught Zelensky by surprise : The Ukrainian president said Kyiv was still awaiting details from Washington.
By Oct. 12, the Kremlin had still not confirmed an agreement. Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said contacts were continuing, while Zelensky said Ukraine had temporarily held off striking Russian energy facilities, but Moscow continued attacking Ukraine’s power grid.
The diesel concession also came before the first major deadline under the sanctions legislation Trump signed on Sept. 18.
As Kyiv Post’s analysis of the Graham sanctions law explains , Oct. 18 is the deadline for many initial measures under the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026. The law targets Russian financial institutions, foreign military suppliers and shipping networks, but gives the president substantial discretion through waivers and tariff decisions.
Signing the law does not itself establish how much additional pressure Moscow will face. With that deadline still five days away, Washington has already granted relief for Russian diesel, while the scale of its implementation of the new penalties remains to be seen.
The dispute comes after Ukrainian attacks forced major Russian refineries to reduce production, with effects visible in both plant operations and export figures.
Reuters reported on Sept. 15 that three of Russia’s six largest diesel-producing refineries had significantly reduced or halted output following drone strikes. Kirishi was shut, while Volgograd and NORSI were operating at roughly a quarter of their designed capacity, according to market sources. Together, the six plants normally account for about half of Russian diesel production.
September’s seaborne diesel and gasoil shipments subsequently fell 28% from August to 144,000 barrels a day, their lowest level in more than a decade of Vortexa records,
That decline, however, reflects both refinery damage and Moscow’s restrictions on exports to preserve domestic supplies. It does not represent an equivalent collapse in all Russian petroleum exports: higher fuel oil and naphtha shipments pushed total seaborne oil-product exports to a three-month high.
Nonetheless, Russia is now promising a recovery. Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said on Oct. 12 that diesel exports could return to 3 million to 3.5 million metric tons a month by year-end, as Reuters reported. That remains a forecast, with deliveries dependent on available fuel and the recovery of a refining network Ukraine has repeatedly struck.
Lesia Dubenko is a Ukrainian political scientist and analyst. A graduate of Lund University (MSc in European Affairs), she covers issues relating to international affairs, migration, and disinformation.

title: Europe remains major buyer of Russian oil despite rhetoric, Kremlin says
body:
MOSCOW, October 13. /TASS/. European countries themselves remain major buyers of Russian crude oil and petroleum products, Kremlin Spokesman Dmitry Peskov said on Tuesday.
"The topic of 'European cynicism' – as noted by [US Treasury Secretary Scott] Bessent – is being widely discussed in the global media. The fact is that European countries, just like all other nations, are heavy buyers of Russian oil and Russian petroleum products," Peskov told TASS.
He made the statement when asked if the Kremlin sees a risk of Europe disrupting the Moscow-Washington fuel deal through new sanctions or other trade barriers.
Earlier, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent pointed out that statements by European countries criticizing US agreements with Russia on diesel fuel supplies are utterly cynical. He noted that, since the start of the war, Europeans themselves have paid more money to the Russians than to the Ukrainians because they are unable to wean themselves off Russian energy resources.

title: Candidates Set for Upcoming Angaur and Ngatpang Gubernatorial Elections
body: By Eoghan Olkeriil Ngirudelsang KOROR, Palau — The field of candidates is set for two upcoming state general elections in Palau, with Angaur State featuring a rematch of former contenders and Ngatpang State seeing a single candidate run unopposed. In Angaur State, voters will choose between incumbent Gov. Kennosuke A. Suzuki and challenger Warren Fukuichi in the Nov. 3 general election. Both candidates previously competed for the same office. According to the Palau Election Commission, Angaur law requires a primary election if more than two candidates file for governor. Although a primary was tentatively scheduled for Sept. 8, none was necessary because only Suzuki and Fukuichi filed. Ten candidates are competing for five at-large seats in the Angaur State Legislature: Gene F. Larson, Marvin Ngirutang, Arkagius Yamada, Jake Ramon, Helena Gulibert, Audry Rafael, Arnold Asao, Ethel Arurang, Micheal Erik Vereen and Olkeriil Kazuo. The 5-member elected legislature serves alongside four traditional chiefs. In Ngatpang State, Miwa “Tant” Nabeyama is running unopposed for governor after emerging as the sole candidate to file nominating petitions by the deadline. With the filing window closed, any additional contenders would have to run as write-in candidates. Because Nabeyama is uncontested, no primary election will be held. Voters will cast their ballots in the Ngatpang general election on Dec. 10. Nominating petitions for seats in the Ngatpang Legislature remain open, with the election commission accepting filings until Nov. 10. title: Total of 260 terrorism suspects detained in North Caucasus this year — NAC
body:
MOSCOW, October 13. /TASS/. Since the beginning of the year, 33 terrorist crimes have been prevented in the North Caucasus, and 260 people have been detained for planning terrorist attacks, financing terrorism, and propagating or justifying terrorism, the information center of Russia’s National Anti-Terrorism Committee (NAC) reported following a meeting held by NAC Chairman, Director of the Russian Federal Security Service (FSB) Alexander Bortnikov.
The meeting was devoted to improving the effectiveness of preventive work with youth in the North Caucasian Federal District.
"Since the beginning of the year, 260 people have been detained in the North Caucasian Federal District for preparing terrorist attacks, financing, propagating, and justifying terrorism. This year, 33 terrorist-related crimes have been prevented in the region," the NAC’s information center reported. In addition, more than 4,000 websites disseminating terrorist content have been blocked since the beginning of the year.
"Alexander Bortnikov noted that active preventive work in the district has decreased the number of terrorist-related crimes. The security of the region's information space has been significantly strengthened," NAC reported. Since the beginning of the year, more than 4,000 online resources disseminating terrorist ideology and inciting inter-ethnic conflicts have been blocked. These included numerous platforms administered by Ukrainian special services that offered quick financial gain in exchange for committing terrorist acts. Attempts to recruit minors into plotting terrorist crimes were thwarted in a timely manner at several schools.
Nevertheless, it was noted at the meeting, "the situation in the sphere of countering terrorism in the North Caucasus remains complicated, as terrorist organizations and Ukrainian special services are not scaling back their propaganda and recruitment activities, having targeted adolescents and young people as their primary objective."
The meeting participants worked out additional measures to improve the system of preventive measures in the district, and set the task for the regional and municipal entities involved in prevention to better coordinate their efforts.

title: 8 injured in knife attack at supermarket in South Korea
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 13 (MNA) – At least eight people were injured Tuesday when a man attacked shoppers at a supermarket in Incheon, northwestern South Korea, according to local media.
The man, in his 60s, was arrested following the stabbing incident at the Homeplus hypermarket, The Korea Herald reported.
One of the injured was reported to be in cardiac arrest.
Police are investigating the motive and circumstances of the attack, the report added.

title: AWS Lambda Web Functions
body:
Today, we’re announcing AWS Lambda Web Functions , a new form factor that lets you run standard HTTP web applications on Lambda without rewriting your code into an event handler. You can take a standard port-listening server built with Express, Hono, Fastify, Next.js, or any Node.js framework, deploy it with a single command, and Lambda automatically handles scaling, multi-region distribution, and active CPU billing. No adapters, no infrastructure to manage, and no framework lock-in.
With this launch, AWS Lambda now offers three distinct form factors, each built on the same Firecracker isolation technology and designed for a different programming model.
Lambda Event Functions are what you already know as Lambda functions. They use the event-driven, single-concurrent handler model with wall-clock billing. We’re introducing the “Event Functions” name to highlight that programming model: your function receives an event, processes it, and returns a response. The event-driven programming model is ideal for event processing, queue consumers, and invocations triggered by other AWS services.
Lambda Web Functions use an HTTP-native programming model with multi-concurrent execution and active CPU billing. Your code listens on a port and handles standard HTTP requests. That programming model is ideal for web applications, API backends, and interactive HTTP workloads where multiple concurrent requests and I/O-heavy processing are the norm.
Lambda MicroVMs provide isolated, stateful sandbox environments with customer-managed lifecycles for running untrusted or user-generated code.
The three complement each other. An application might use Event Functions for asynchronous backend processing, Web Functions for the user-facing API and server-side rendering layer, and MicroVMs for interactive code execution features, all within the same AWS account and sharing the same operational model.
Why Web Functions Modern web applications need to serve global audiences with fast, consistent response times while giving developers the freedom to use standard frameworks and iterate quickly. Building this today typically requires assembling multiple infrastructure components, configuring multi-region deployments, setting up latency-based routing, and tuning billing models to avoid paying for I/O wait. Developers often find themselves adapting their application code to fit a specific compute model rather than deploying the HTTP server they already have.
Lambda Web Functions removes this complexity. Each execution environment handles multiple requests simultaneously (up to 128 concurrent requests per environment), which means a burst of incoming traffic can share warm environments instead of mapping each request to a new one. Web Functions meter the CPU time your code uses, so time spent waiting on a database query or an API call consumes little CPU. Memory is metered for as long as the execution environment exists. For I/O-heavy web workloads like server-side rendering, API backends, and AI inference endpoints streaming token responses, this can reduce compute costs.
Let’s try it out To get started, I wrote a simple Express.js server. This is the same code I run locally with node index.js , no Lambda-specific adapters or wrappers required.
The only difference from running locally is the AWS_LAMBDA_HTTP_ENDPOINT environment variable, which Lambda sets to the host and port your server must listen on. To run locally, set it yourself, for example AWS_LAMBDA_HTTP_ENDPOINT=127.0.0.1:3000 node index.js .
With my code ready, I deployed using the AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI) :
One command. No prior resource setup. The CLI bundled my source, created the Web Function, published its first revision, attached a Web Function endpoint, and returned a live HTTPS URL in under a minute.
A revision is an immutable snapshot of the code I deployed. The endpoint is the HTTPS URL that routes traffic to a revision, or splits traffic across revisions. Those are the resources I use to iterate and to control how traffic moves to new code.
Next, I wanted my application to serve users in Europe and Asia with lower latency. I redeployed with multiple regions:
Lambda Web Functions replicated my code to all three regions and configured latency-based routing automatically. Each request now routes to the Region with the lowest latency for the caller, on a best-effort basis, through one global URL ( <domain-id>.lambda-web.global.on.aws ).
When I updated my code and ran the same deploy command again, the CLI detected the existing function, uploaded the new revision, and pointed the endpoint at it. Total turnaround from code change to live: seconds.
For production workflows that require a more gradual rollout, I can shift traffic between revisions with a single API call:
This sends 90% of endpoint traffic to the current revision and 10% to the new one, giving me a canary deployment without additional tooling.
Better together with Amazon CloudFront For applications that combine static and dynamic content, Web Functions works well alongside Amazon CloudFront . You can select a Web Function endpoint as the origin for your CloudFront distribution. Static assets are served from the cache while dynamic requests route to your Web Function, giving you CDN performance for static content with serverless compute for the dynamic parts.
Web Functions improves the private-origin experience with CloudFront. With this launch, you attach CloudFront origin access control (OAC) to a Web Function endpoint instead. CloudFront signs requests to the origin, and the endpoint allows only your distribution to invoke it. You get the same private-origin pattern CloudFront already provides for Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) , without exposing the endpoint or adding custom authorization to your app.
Now available AWS Lambda Web Functions is available today in US East (N. Virginia), US East (Ohio), US West (Oregon), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), and Europe (Ireland). Web Functions run Node.js 24 (nodejs24.x) on Arm64 at launch and support Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) connectivity, allowing your function to access resources that exist within a VPC.
To get started, deploy your first Web Function in under a minute:
For pricing details, visit the AWS Lambda pricing page . To learn more, see the Lambda Web Functions documentation .
Micah Walter is a Sr. Solutions Architect supporting enterprise customers in the New York City region and beyond. He advises executives, engineers, and architects at every step along their journey to the cloud, with a deep focus on sustainability and practical design. In his free time, Micah enjoys the outdoors, photography, and chasing his kids around the house.

title: Palau Lawmakers Push to Cut Sales Tax and Lower Everyday Bills
body: Twin Senate bills aim to cut the PGST tax in half and remove extra taxes on groceries, power, and phone bills. By: L.N. Reklai KOROR, Palau (Oct. 12, 2026) — Lawmakers in Palau are working on two new bills to help families save money on daily living costs as prices for groceries and basic services keep going up. The bills were brought forward by five senators—TJ Imrur Remengesau, Stevenson J. Kuartei, Salvador “Sadoi” Tellames, Lentcer Basilius, and Kerai Mariur—who want to change how the Palau Goods and Services Tax (PGST) works. PGST is the extra tax added to items when you buy them at a store or pay a bill. The first proposal, Senate Bill No. 12-83 , wants to cut the main PGST tax rate in half, dropping it from 10% down to 5%. It would also stop the government from charging sales and income taxes to public service companies like the Palau Public Utilities Corporation (PPUC), Palau National Communications Corporation (PNCC), and Belau Submarine Cable Corporation (BSCC). Senators explained that electricity and phone services are essential for everyday life. They pointed out that “since the implementation of the PGST Act, individuals and families have felt the financial impact of the new tax regime in their daily lives,” making it harder for people to pay their monthly bills. The second proposal, Senate Bill No. 12-82 , focuses directly on food. It would remove the PGST tax from all grocery items—whether raw ingredients, cooked food, or snacks. Lawmakers said this is necessary because “the cost of food has increased substantially, placing a disproportionate burden on low-income households, large families, senior citizens, and other residents with limited financial resources.” While many local families would love to pay less at the cash register, top government leaders urge caution. President Surangel Whipps Jr. warns that cutting taxes too much could leave the government without enough money to run public services, fix roads, or run essential community programs. During discussions about tax policy, President Whipps cautioned that “the proposal to reduce the Palau Goods and Services Tax (PGST) while increasing subsidies risks government revenue and stability.” When discussing broad tax cuts and money-back programs, President Whipps added that “the rebate was an untargeted subsidy that would have diverted public funds away from targeted assistance programs… and provided government money to individuals who do not require assistance.” This debate leaves Palau at an important crossroads: while senators want to give families instant relief on their grocery and power bills, executive leaders argue that a strong tax system is necessary to keep the country running smoothly. Lawmakers will continue reviewing both bills to decide what comes next. The post Palau Lawmakers Push to Cut Sales Tax and Lower Everyday Bills appeared first on Island Times News .

title: Accra Mall brings Soulful Weekend Vibes to October with Live R&B and Jazz
body: Saturday afternoons in Accra have a mood of their own. After a long week, many people want to get out of the house, meet friends, or enjoy a good meal without the rush of a crowded party or a packed schedule. Sometimes, all it takes is good company, good food, and good music. This is the idea behind Soulful Serenade, happening at Accra Mall on October 17. The event will bring live R&B, jazz, and lounge-style music into the mall’s weekend atmosphere, offering visitors a relaxed setting to shop, dine, and spend time with family and friends. The music selection is deliberate. With their smooth rhythms and easy listening, R&B and jazz lend themselves naturally to relaxed social settings. Whether visitors are catching up over a meal, browsing their favourite stores, or meeting friends, the performances will add another dimension to the experience. For the Mall, the initiative is part of a broader effort to create experiences that complement the everyday reasons people visit. “We want people to see the Mall as a place where they can meet people, enjoy good food, spend time with family and friends, and experience entertainment,” said Anthony Asamoah, Marketing Manager at Accra Mall. “Soulful Serenade is about creating that kind of atmosphere, where good music becomes part of the reason you want to spend a little more time here.” With Soulful Serenade, a regular Saturday will become an opportunity to slow down, reconnect, and enjoy live music. Come with your vibe and get your groove on!

title: New Society Aims to Unite Palau’s Gaming Community
body: By: Summer Kennard KOROR, Palau (October 12, 2026) Good Gamers Society, a nonprofit organization established to bring Palau’s gaming communities together, is working to promote responsible gaming, address cyberbullying and create more opportunities for young people interested in esports. Formally incorporated in October 2025, the organization grew out of a group of friends who organized an esports tournament in 2024 at WCTC on Lebuu Street. The event featured Tekken 7 and PlayerUnknown’s Battlegrounds (PUBG) competitions. According to Good Gamers Society President Tabesul Ngirailemsang, the response to the tournament demonstrated the community’s interest in organized gaming events. “For a whole year, young gamers kept asking us, ‘When’s the next one?’ That told us the demand was real,” Ngirailemsang said. The continued interest encouraged the group to establish an organization that could unite gamers, organize competitions and provide opportunities for the community to grow. Good Gamers Society focuses on organizing tournaments and workshops, promoting healthy gaming habits and mental well-being, and encouraging respectful behavior online. In August, the organization held a Youth Gamer’s Workshop at Palau High School with more than 20 young participants. The workshop addressed healthy gaming, mental well-being and online safety, with support from the Noncommunicable Disease Fund through the Ministry of Health and Human Services. Ngirailemsang said the response from young people and the wider community has been encouraging, and the organization is preparing for a community gaming tournament. He described Palau’s gaming community as larger and more diverse than many people realize, with players participating in games such as Mobile Legends, PUBG, Call of Duty Mobile, Apex Legends and sports titles including NBA 2K and MLB The Show. The community includes high school students, working adults, parents and people from different occupations and backgrounds. Despite this interest, Ngirailemsang said Palau lacks the structure and resources needed to support the gaming community’s development. “There are very few places where gamers can come together in person, and not many organized competitions to give them something to work toward,” he said. For local gamer Imrur Remengesau, the cost and availability of equipment and unreliable internet connectivity are among the challenges of gaming in Palau. Remengesau, who has been playing video games for nearly 11 years, currently plays NBA 2K26, EA Sports FC 26, UFC 6 and Call of Duty. He said gaming allows him to relax, relieve stress and connect with friends. “After a long day, gaming gives me a chance to relax and focus on something that I enjoy and find rewarding,” Remengesau said. He said gaming consoles and controllers can be expensive to purchase locally, while ordering equipment online can take a long time. A stable internet connection is also important for online play, particularly in competitive games. Ngirailemsang similarly identified internet reliability and access to equipment as challenges for Palau’s gaming community. He said gaming has yet to receive the same level of recognition and support from schools, businesses and the wider community as traditional sports and the arts. Remengesau said he would like to see more gaming events, workshops and tournaments covering different types of games. He also proposed establishing a dedicated gaming center where players could meet, practice and compete. “I would also love to see Palau develop an esports team that could represent the country in regional and international competitions,” Remengesau said. Ngirailemsang said stronger partnerships and more organized opportunities could help Palau develop its gaming community and potentially send players to compete in regional tournaments. Beyond competition, Good Gamers Society wants to challenge the perception that gaming is simply a waste of time. Ngirailemsang said gaming can provide opportunities for people to unwind, connect with others and develop skills such as teamwork, communication and problem-solving. He also pointed to potential career paths associated with esports and the broader gaming industry, including streaming, event management, design and technology. However, he emphasized that gaming must remain balanced with other responsibilities. “The key is that gaming should fit into your life, not take it over,” he said. The organization encourages players to take breaks, stay physically active, drink water, protect their sleep and prioritize school, work and family responsibilities. Ngirailemsang also acknowledged concerns among parents about excessive gaming, saying the organization shares those concerns, particularly because some of its members are parents themselves. Rather than discouraging gaming altogether, he encouraged parents to take an active role by learning about the games their children play, asking who they interact with online and establishing reasonable limits together. He said parents should also watch for warning signs, including disrupted sleep, declining school performance and withdrawal from family activities. Good Gamers Society also emphasizes the importance of using credible research when discussing gaming’s potential benefits and risks. Ngirailemsang said the organization looks to peer-reviewed studies, universities and health organizations when sharing information. While some research points to potential benefits, he said the organization also recognizes the risks associated with unhealthy gaming habits, including gaming disorder, which the World Health Organization recognizes as a health condition. “We think being upfront about the risks is what makes our message about healthy gaming believable,” he said. Through its workshops, tournaments and community outreach, Good Gamers Society aims to create an environment where gamers can participate safely, develop their skills and connect with others while maintaining healthy habits. The post New Society Aims to Unite Palau’s Gaming Community appeared first on Island Times News .

title: Angry Military Veterans lay siege to Pension board over alleged Underpayment
body: ‎Military veterans have protested over alleged underpayment of their pensions, demanding an urgent recalculation of their entitlements in line with approved adjustments to the salaries of serving military personnel. ‎ ‎The protesters, led by Lt. Col. Innocent Azubuike, coordinator of the Veterans Association of Nigeria, stormed the Military Pensions Board in Abuja, on Tuesday morning. They accused the board of using a pension computation formula that allegedly reduced the percentage increases approved for retired personnel. ‎ ‎Speaking during the protest on Tuesday, Azubuike said the approved adjustments provided for an 80 per cent increase for personnel from the rank of private to staff sergeant, 50 per cent for warrant officers to colonels, and 30 per cent for brigadier generals and higher ranks. ‎ ‎He alleged that the board failed to apply the approved percentages directly to the pensions veterans were already receiving, instead using a calculation method that reduced their entitlements. ‎ ‎“We have gotten presidential approval for the consequential allowance on the percentages allotted to various rank categories,” he said. ‎ ‎“Now, in paying us this consequential adjustment, Pension Board did not pay this very approved percentage.” ‎ ‎Azubuike said the veterans had earlier approached the Ministry of Defence in August to demand the inclusion of retired personnel in the salary-related adjustments after discovering that they had initially been excluded. ‎ ‎According to him, the ministry acknowledged the omission and subsequently included them in the approved adjustments. ‎ ‎However, he accused the Military Pensions Board of introducing a calculation method that allegedly undermined the approved increases, despite the fact that the pension rates of retirees had already been determined by their ranks and years of service at retirement. ‎ ‎He argued that the approved percentage should apply to the pension each retiree was receiving before the adjustment, rather than being subjected to another calculation based on the conditions under which the individual retired. ‎ ‎“Even though it’s short-changing the criteria, it’s short-changing military veterans, but that criteria wasn’t still followed,” he said. ‎“We are about 100,000 military veterans,” he said, adding that he had records to support the allegations of discrepancies in pension payments. ‎ ‎Another protester, Master Warrant Officer Duru Augustine, said the alleged underpayment had left retired personnel feeling betrayed after years of service to the country. ‎ ‎“Honestly, honestly, it’s bad. Having in your own constituency, being treated like a slave,” Augustine said. ‎ ‎He maintained that the dispute concerned the implementation of approved pension adjustments, which he said veterans had fought to secure after discovering that retired personnel were initially excluded. ‎ ‎Augustine recalled that the veterans protested on August 19, after which, according to him, the Minister of Defence, Christopher Musa, acknowledged their concerns and supported their inclusion in the adjustment. ‎ ‎He said the National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission had also provided a chart explaining the calculations, arguing that the board should implement the approved percentages rather than introduce a different method. ‎ ‎“It’s an insult to the president of the Federal Republic of Nigeria. It’s an insult to the capacity of the commander-in-chief of the armed forces, for him to go back and do whatever he feels like doing,” he said, referring to the alleged departure from the approved adjustment framework.

title: Opinion: Why South Africa’s defence industry deserves national pride status
body:
South Africa’s defence industry is having a moment. Exports reached R10.1 billion in 2025, nearly tripling the previous year’s total, with 582 permits approved for 42 countries. Europe now accounts for 42 percent of those sales. Defence Minister Angie Motshekga has referred to the South African Defence Industry (SADI) as being “world class” and something we should be proud of. Industry leaders believe annual exports could reach R30 billion within five years, while Trade and Industry Minister Parks Tau has said that the SADI is far from a niche sector standing apart from our industrialisation programme but rather is one of its most advanced expressions.
All this praise and yet both Ministers of Defence and Trade have not called for our SADI to be formally designated as a National Pride Industry. This omission is not neutral. It leaves the industry’s identity ambiguous, caught between its undeniable technical achievements and the ethical questions that shadow any arms trade. Formal recognition would not resolve those tensions but would certainly force the state to confront them honestly.
The case for pride rests first on capability. South Africa’s engineers have produced systems that compete globally and are often combat tested: the A-Darter air-to-air missile, the Seeker family of unmanned aerial vehicles, and now the Milkor 380, the largest drone developed on the African continent, with a range exceeding 4 000 kilometres and an endurance of up to 35 hours. These are not assembled from imported kits. They are conceived, designed, and built in South Africa, by South African innovators. The Milkor 380 alone represents a leap in sovereign capability, and its successor, the 780, is already in development.
But capability alone cannot constitute pride. Turkey’s defence industry also inspires national fervour, yet it does so through a techno-nationalism that celebrates military strength as an end in itself. South Africa’s claim to pride must be different. It must rest on something more than the ability to build effective weapons.
That something is the ethical framework the industry operates within, and the uncomfortable truth and sad reality is that this framework remains incomplete. South Africa’s National Conventional Arms Control Act is among the strictest in the world. The problem lies not in the law but in its enforcement. The National Conventional Arms Control Committee (NCACC) has repeatedly approved questionable exports, and the Pretoria High Court ruled in 2024 that permits must be suspended to countries facing credible war crimes allegations. More than a year later, there is little indication this has been done.
This is precisely why “National Pride Industry” status matters so much. The designation would not be a reward for past virtue. It would be a commitment to future accountability. Calling the industry a source of national pride means insisting that its conduct meets the standard that pride implies. It means refusing to hide behind the fiction that arms sales are neutral commercial transactions.
South Africa has already demonstrated that an ethical approach is possible. The industry exports to Germany, France, Australia, and India, all established democracies with no comparable ethical concerns. It has built a reputation for reliable, cost-effective systems that fill niches larger producers ignore. The private sector, which drives most of this innovation, exports 80 to 90 percent of its output. These are achievements that deserve recognition, not apology.
What they do not deserve is silence about the cases where the system fails. The gap between South Africa’s legal commitments and its enforcement record is not an argument against the industry. It is an argument for formalising what the industry should mean. A National Pride designation would make the ethical standard explicit and therefore enforceable in public discourse. It would give critics a benchmark against which to measure performance. It would make it harder for the state to look away.
South Korea, Sweden, China, and France all treat their defence industries as critical national capabilities, not as embarrassing relics. They do so not because they are warmongers, but because they understand that the technological spillovers from defence research in materials science, electronics, aerospace, and communications drive broader economic innovation and create high-value jobs.
South Africa’s defence industry already exists in a difficult position. It must serve a defence force whose budget has fallen below 0.7 percent of GDP. It must compete globally while navigating some of the world’s most stringent export controls and survive without reliable domestic procurement.
Through all this, it has continued to innovate. That is worthy of pride. But pride should not be a mere slogan – it should be a standard. South Africa should designate its defence industry a National Pride Industry not because the weapons are impressive, but because the country is willing to hold itself to the principles it claims to uphold.
We speak often of national pride. We feel it when the Springboks take the field, or when a South African innovation captures global attention. Yet we have allowed a sector that should be a cornerstone of that pride, a high-science, high-skill industry that competes with the best in the world, to slide toward the precipice of irrelevance. It is time to reverse course.
Shaun Kinnes is a researcher with special interests in areas of defence, human security, and climate-induced conflict.

title: Beware of ‘instant loan’ offers, ROP cautions
body:
MUSCAT, OCT 13 ‘NEED a loan?’ If you see this advertisement on social media, beware. It could be a massive scam. Authorities in Oman have sounded a fresh alert against a new wave of loan shark scams specifically targeting expatriates in Oman, luring victims with advertisements in their language offering instant loans. The fraud, which is being widely circulated among various community groups, promises soft personal loans of up to RO 40,000 within hours, with minimal documents and no bank verification. “To avoid falling victim to such scams, please be vigilant, verify the details, and ensure everything is legitimate before transferring any money,” the advisory says. According to the Royal Oman Police (ROP) and the Central Bank of Oman (CBO), fraudsters are now impersonating official financial institutions on social media applications such as WhatsApp, Snapchat and Instagram, and directing victims to fake links to collect personal and banking information. “Citizens and residents have been advised to ignore such messages and not to open electronic links unless they are sure of their reliability,” the ROP said, adding that the CBO is not concerned with providing personal and housing loans or any other banking services to individuals. Bank Muscat said it would never ask for OTP, CVV, bank card or civil ID copies through SMS or WhatsApp, and that anyone who receives such a message should not act upon it and should alert the bank immediately. The modus operandi is similar to cases flagged earlier by security agencies. Fraudsters circulate ads in vernacular languages stating “Loan Approved - One Lakh to Three Lakhs based on CIBIL” and ask victims to download APK files disguised as loan apps. Once installed, these apps gain access to contacts, SMS, call records, camera and location. Victims are then asked to upload their ID proofs such as Aadhaar, PAN, bank account details and photographs. “They may even transfer a small amount initially to gain confidence. Later they demand payments under various pretexts - processing fee, GST, insurance, verification charges - without disbursing the promised loan,” the warning notes say. In Oman, loan sharking is a criminal offence. An official source earlier stated that anyone involved in usury or lending money without a licence at unreasonably high interest rates faces a jail term of at least three months and a fine of at least RO 200. If the lender takes advantage of the borrower’s need, the punishment can go up to three years plus doubling of the fine, and up to five years with deportation for repeated offences. STAY SAFE Do not trust loan ads on social media Never share OTP, CVV, bank card or civil ID copies Do not install APK files sent via WhatsApp links Avail loans only from licensed banks in Oman regulated by the CBO Report such numbers immediately to the ROP on 9999 or at the nearest police station
