title: Taiwan Embassy Celebrates 115th National Day Aboard Coast Guard Vessel Chiayi, Highlighting Strong Taiwan–Palau Friendship
body: The Embassy of the Republic of China (Taiwan) in the Republic of Palau hosted a reception on the evening of October 8 to celebrate the 115th National Day of the Republic of China (Taiwan). In conjunction with the Taiwan Coast Guard Administration’s (CGA) 2026 Training Mission, the National Day reception was held aboard the CGA patrol vessel Chiayi for the first time. His Excellency President Surangel S. Whipps, Jr. and First Lady Valerie Whipps attended the celebration, together with members of Palau’s Cabinet, the Olbiil Era Kelulau (Palau National Congress), distinguished guests from various sectors, representatives of the Taiwan Chamber of Commerce in Palau, and members of the Taiwanese community. The gathering celebrated Taiwan’s National Day and reaffirmed the enduring friendship between Taiwan and Palau. This year’s National Day theme, “A Democratic Taiwan, Moving Forward with the World,” carries special significance as Taiwan marks the 30th anniversary of its first direct presidential election in 1996. This milestone reflects the unwavering commitment of the Taiwanese people to safeguarding democracy, freedom, and human rights over the past three decades. Democracy is not only a fundamental value shared by Taiwan and Palau, but also an essential foundation for global peace and economic prosperity. In his remarks, H.E. Ambassador Andy Kang I Chen highlighted that three decades of democratic development have established Taiwan as a trusted partner in the international community. He reaffirmed Taiwan’s commitment to advancing values-based diplomacy and integrated diplomacy, while deepening cooperation with diplomatic allies and like-minded partners. Ambassador Chen also reviewed major achievements in Taiwan–Palau relations over the past year, including the visit of Vice President Bi-khim Hsiao to Palau, the participation of Minister of Foreign Affairs Lin Chia-lung in the 55th Pacific Islands Forum (PIF) Leaders Meeting at the invitation of Palau, and Taiwan’s participation in the Pacific Prosperity Exhibit organized by the Palauan government, which showcased the “Taiwan Model” of pursuing shared prosperity with Pacific partners. Ambassador Chen further noted that visits to Palau by the Republic of China (Taiwan) Navy’s Fleet of Friendship, Youth Ambassadors, and delegations from the medical, educational, and business sectors have demonstrated the breadth and depth of bilateral exchanges. Looking ahead, Taiwan will continue to leverage its strengths to expand cooperation with Palau across various fields. He also expressed sincere appreciation to President Whipps, the Palauan government, the Olbiil Era Kelulau, and the people of Palau for their longstanding and steadfast support for Taiwan–Palau relations and Taiwan’s meaningful international participation. In his remarks, CGA Deputy Director-General Hsu Jing-Zhih emphasized the special significance of hosting Taiwan’s National Day reception aboard a Coast Guard vessel for the first time. He noted that the occasion symbolized the further expansion of Taiwan–Palau friendship into maritime law enforcement cooperation and exchanges between frontline personnel. Since the signing of the bilateral Coast Guard Cooperation Agreement in 2019, Taiwan and Palau have continued to strengthen their partnership through joint patrols, maritime search and rescue exercises, and personnel exchanges. The visit of the CGA vessels Chiayi and Penghu, together with renewed joint maritime patrol operations, demonstrated how mutual trust has been translated into concrete action. She reaffirmed Taiwan’s commitment to working closely with Palau to address maritime security challenges, including search and rescue operations, illegal fishing, and transnational crime, while jointly safeguarding peace, security, and order in the Pacific. In his address, President Surangel S. Whipps, Jr. extended his warm congratulations on the 115th National Day of the Republic of China (Taiwan) and reaffirmed the longstanding and close friendship between Palau and Taiwan. President Whipps emphasized that the two nations share not only a common Austronesian heritage but also universal values of democracy and freedom. He highlighted the frequent high-level exchanges between the two countries, including multiple visits to Palau by President Lai Ching-te and the visit of Vice President Bi-khim Hsiao in June 2026, as clear demonstrations of the strong and enduring bilateral partnership. President Whipps further recognized Taiwan as a trusted partner in the international community, highlighting its pivotal role in the global technology and semiconductor industries and its significant contributions through sharing expertise and achievements in technology, healthcare, and agriculture. He called upon the international community to support Taiwan’s meaningful participation in international organizations and mechanisms, including the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA), the World Health Organization (WHO), and the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO). He stressed that excluding Taiwan represents a loss to the international community and reiterated Palau’s unwavering support for Taiwan’s international participation. President Whipps concluded by once again extending his National Day congratulations and expressing his hope that Taiwan and Palau would continue to prosper together while upholding their shared values of democracy and freedom. The National Day reception also featured a special musical performance by students from the Mandarin language class at Mindszenty High School, who performed the song “Hand in Hand” (手牽手). The performance also highlighted the growing cultural and educational exchanges between the two countries, bringing a memorable touch to the festive occasion. On October 9, the Embassy of the Republic of China (Taiwan) in Palau also organized a Taiwan–Palau Joint Flag-Raising Ceremony and Coast Guard Vessel Tour, attended by Palau’s Minister of State, Hon. Gustav Aitaro. The event further highlighted the close partnership and cooperation between the two countries. Following the ceremony, participants bid farewell to the CGA patrol vessel Penghu as it departed to carry out a joint maritime patrol mission with Palau. The operation underscored the two countries’ continued commitment to strengthening maritime law enforcement cooperation, enhancing maritime security, and deepening the longstanding friendship between Taiwan and Palau. This year’s National Day celebrations also featured a Taiwan–Palau Pickleball Friendship Match, attended by Ambassador Chen, President Whipps, First Lady Valerie Whipps, Minister Ngiraibelas Tmetuchl, Minister Charles I. Obichang, Minister Jennifer Olegeriil, Delegate Stephanie Ngirchoimei, and CGA Deputy Director-General Hsu. In addition, students from Taiwan’s Central Police University accompanying the Coast Guard fleet during its visit to Palau participated in a friendly swimming competition with students from Palau High School. Both sporting events were marked by enthusiastic participation and lively interactions, further fostering people-to-people exchanges, mutual understanding, and friendship between Taiwan and Palau. The post Taiwan Embassy Celebrates 115th National Day Aboard Coast Guard Vessel Chiayi, Highlighting Strong Taiwan–Palau Friendship appeared first on Island Times News .

title: Russian attacks kill at least 10, injure 80 across Ukraine over past day as Moscow hits homes, railway infrastructure
body:
At least 10 people were killed and 80 others injured across Ukraine over the past day, as Russia continued to target residential buildings in cities including Kyiv, regional authorities said on Oct. 13.
In Kharkiv Oblast over the past day, Russia attacked the city of Kharkiv and settlements in the surrounding region, killing four people and injuring 36, including four children, regional governor Oleh Syniehubov said. President Volodymyr Zelensky later raised the number of injured in a missile strike on Kharkiv, meaning that 42 people were injured in the Oblast in total.
All four deaths occurred in residential buildings.
In Kyiv , at least two people were killed and 14 others injured in drone attacks throughout the day, including a strike on a 25-story residential building in the Darnytskyi District.
Kyiv also came under ballistic missile attack shortly after 10 p.m. local time on Oct. 12, with powerful explosions reported before an air raid alert was issued in the Ukrainian capital. Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said a warehouse and railway infrastructure had been damaged.
In Vinnytsia Oblast , Russia struck a production complex belonging to Ukrainian confectionery company Roshen , the company said.
"Thanks to the timely activation of the warning system and the prompt evacuation, the lives of employees were saved," Roshen said in a statement .
Overnight on Oct. 13, Russian forces launched five ballistic missiles, 108 Shahed-type attack drones, including 74 jet-powered versions, as well as Gerbera and Parodiya decoy drones, and nine Banderol missiles, Ukraine's Air Force said .
Ukrainian air defenses shot down or suppressed 88 drones, while strikes were recorded at 17 locations. Debris from downed drones fell at seven locations, the Air Force said.
Air defenses were active in the far-western Lviv Oblast overnight as Russian drones "struck villages and private homes," Lviv Mayor Andrii Sadovyi said , though he reported no casualties.
In eastern Donetsk Oblast , four people were killed and 11 others were injured in Russian attacks across the region over the past day, regional governor Vadym Filashkin said.
In northeastern Sumy Oblast , two people were injured in Russian strikes, regional authorities said .
In southern Kherson Oblast , Russian attacks injured six people, regional governor Oleksandr Prokudin said.
In southeastern Zaporizhzhia Oblast , over the past day, Russia carried out 910 attacks against 58 settlements in the region — five people were injured in the attacks, regional authorities said .
Dnipropetrovsk and Chernihiv oblasts also came under Russian attacks, but no injuries were reported.

title: Sahara Champions Global Shipping Collaboration for $20m Mercy Ships Healthcare Impact
body: Sahara Energy Geneva has highlighted the power of business collaboration to deliver lasting impact, with Mercy Ships Cargo Day celebrating more than $20 million raised over the past decade to support healthcare interventions in Africa. A statement by the Head, Corporate Communications, Sahara Group Ltd, Bethel Obioma, revealed that more than 500 guests from over 150 shipping and trading companies gathered in Geneva recently for the 10th anniversary Gala of Mercy Ships Cargo Day, celebrating a decade of industry support for the international charity. Head of Chartering at Sahara Energy Geneva and Chairman of the Cargo Day Geneva Committee, David Walker, joined industry leaders at the event, where he thanked the global shipping community, sponsors, media partners and Cargo Day committees in Geneva, London, Houston, Dubai and Singapore for supporting the initiative. Cargo Day brings together charterers, shipowners, shipbrokers, and other shipping professionals who contribute through pledges, cargo commissions, and address commissions to support the work of Mercy Ships. Director, Sahara Geneva, Kola Motajo, said Sahara’s involvement reflects the company’s belief in the ability of enterprise and partnerships to deliver impact beyond business. “At Sahara, our focus is always on impact and lives transformed. Cargo Day demonstrates what is possible when businesses and individuals unite around a shared purpose. The $20 million milestone reflects the collective commitment of the global shipping community to improving healthcare in Africa. As Sahara looks Beyond XXX, we remain committed to building connections that create lasting value and possibilities for generations to come,” Motajo said. Reflecting on Cargo Day’s growth, Walker said: “Ten years ago, we raised $300,000 and there were 70 people at the Gala. Today, we have more than 500 people coming from around the world to support such a great cause.” Cargo Day 2025 raised more than $2.5 million, with 93 companies participating, including charterers, brokers, shipowners, and other partners. Mercy Ships operates two hospital ships supporting patients in Africa with free life-changing surgeries, while also providing training and mentoring for local healthcare professionals. Cargo Day funding contributes to expenses associated with operating the hospital ships. The 2026 Cargo Day campaign begins November 4 and will run through November and December, with companies participating through Mercy Cargoes, address commissions and pledges.

title: Spox Ihnat: Russia deploys about 200 jet-powered drones per day
body:
According to Ukrinform, Yurii Ihnat, a spokesperson for the Ukrainian Air Force, made this statement during a television broadcast.
“Right now, it’s about 100 during the day and 100 at night—and that’s just counting jet-powered UAVs . They also combine them with other drones,” Ihnat said.
According to him, the Ukrainian military is gradually improving its effectiveness in intercepting jet-powered drones thanks to the experience gained, but Ukraine needs additional missiles and ammunition for ground-based air defense systems and aviation.
He noted that even a small number of drones that reach their targets can cause significant damage to Ukrainian facilities.
As previously reported, Yurii Ihnat, a spokesperson for the Ukrainian Air Force, stated that Russia is stepping up its use of jet-powered drones to attack Ukraine: while it used about 350 such UAVs in June, it used about 3,500 in Sep tember.

title: Cobra Warrior ends with more than nine hundred sorties
body: Exercise Cobra Warrior 26-2 has concluded after three and a half weeks, generating 942 sorties and more than 2,500 flying hours across fourteen complex missions, according to the Royal Air Force . Around 1,800 personnel from the United Kingdom, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands and the United States took part. The exercise began on 14 September and was delivered by the Air and Space Warfare Centre, sponsored by No 11 Group. Combat air, intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance, air mobility, support helicopters, force protection, cyber and command and control capabilities were brought together to test the rapid integration, resilience and combat effectiveness needed to deter threats, defend the homeland and fight as part of a NATO force. For prospective tactical leaders it marked the end of the Typhoon Qualified Weapons Instructor Course, putting candidates into a multinational environment and requiring decisions under operational pressure. Squadron Leader Mike, officer commanding the course with 29 Squadron, said: “Exercise Cobra Warrior 26-2 has once again provided the culmination of the Typhoon Qualified Weapons Instructor Course, allowing candidates to test themselves alongside allied air forces in a demanding multinational environment. “The exercise challenges prospective Weapons Instructors to demonstrate the judgement, adaptability and leadership required of the next generation of Typhoon tactical leaders.” The Air Command and Control Force coordinated British and international participants through the planning and execution of the missions. Group Captain Chris Misiak, Commander Air C2 Force, said: “The Air C2 Force has been central to the success of Cobra Warrior, integrating UK and international participants into a single coordinated air operation. Exercises such as this ensure Allied air forces can plan, operate and respond together in an increasingly complex security environment.” Germany deployed eleven Eurofighter Typhoons and around 200 personnel from Tactical Air Wing 31 Boelcke. Oberstleutnant Mike Schill, the German detachment commander, said: “The exercise gives us the opportunity to hone operational tactics and strengthen readiness alongside our NATO partners. Training together deepens cooperation and improves our ability to operate collectively in defence of the Alliance.” Maggiore Valerio C, the Italian detachment commander, said: “Cobra Warrior has confirmed itself as a first-class training exercise, offering an opportunity to test the capabilities of Air Forces, the integration between assets, and the level of standardization required to operate effectively with allied nations in modern scenarios.” Personnel from RAF Global Enablement, the Tactical Medical Wing, the RAF Regiment and allied support units sustained the flying effort, supporting deployed operations and protecting personnel through the exercise. The post Cobra Warrior ends with more than nine hundred sorties first appeared on UK Defence Journal .

title: Death toll as a result of evening attack on residential building in Kharkiv grows to four
body:
In Kharkiv, the fourth body was recovered from the rubble of a 4-story apartment building, which was hit by the Russian Banderol the day before, the total number of dead has increased to four, the mayor of the city, Ihor Terekhov, said.

"The fourth body was pulled out from under the rubble of a house in Kholodnohirsky district," Terekhov wrote in his Telegram channel.

As reported, on Monday evening, the Armed Forces of the Russian Federation launched a massive attack on Kharkiv using Banderol missiles. One of them ended up in a 4-story residential building in Kholodnohirsky district of the city. As a result of this collision, three people were killed and another 10 were injured.

title: Javelin output nearly doubles as global demand rises
body: The Javelin Joint Venture has nearly doubled its annual All-Up-Round production capacity over the past two years, and has delivered the first of a new lightweight launcher to the United States Army, according to Lockheed Martin . Lockheed Martin is increasing output on its existing manufacturing line and through the missile’s supply chain partners, and is putting money into accelerating the long-lead parts and equipment that higher production rates require. Rich Liccion, vice president of the joint venture and programme director for Javelin at Lockheed Martin, said: “By scaling our Javelin production line to meet increasing global demand, we’re extending Javelin’s legacy of performance excellence for years to come. Our increased output ensures that warfighters worldwide continue to rely on an anti-tank missile system that has delivered unmatched precision for over 30 years.” The venture was awarded the largest single-year Javelin production contract to date in May 2025, a follow-on under an indefinite-delivery, indefinite-quantity production contract first awarded in May 2023. All test stations critical to the ramp are due to be built by the end of this year, verifying that the missile and its subcomponents meet environmental, performance and functional requirements. Sixteen further test stations that duplicate essential capabilities will then be upgraded, modernising legacy equipment and sustaining production capability over the longer term. The Lightweight Command Launch Unit is the next-generation launcher for the system, built to work with all current, past and future Javelin variants. Raytheon has invested $22 million in modernising the factory that builds it, at Tucson in Arizona, to increase speed and expand capacity, and annual production there is being increased in collaboration with the US Army. Jenna Hunt Frazier, president of the joint venture and Javelin programme director at Raytheon, said: “Delivering the LWCLU into soldiers’ hands underscores our commitment to accelerating meaningful capability upgrades. Our investment in modernisation and production capacity ensures the Army can field this advanced launcher more quickly, giving soldiers better awareness and greater lethality on today’s battlefield.” The new unit offers twice the target detection and recognition range of the launcher it replaces while cutting size by thirty per cent and weight by twenty-five per cent, with improved optics and a day and night surveillance capability. Javelin is built by the joint venture between Raytheon at Tucson and Lockheed Martin at Orlando in Florida, which has produced more than 55,000 missiles and more than 12,000 reusable command launch units to date. The post Javelin output nearly doubles as global demand rises first appeared on UK Defence Journal .

title: Who’s Emelia Affi Agbenyo, the 43-year-old newly sworn-in Deputy EC Chair?
body: The swearing-in of 43-year-old Emelia Affi Agbenyo as one of the two new Deputy Chairpersons of the Electoral Commission has stoked controversy following her affiliation with the incumbent National Democratic Congress (NDC). The young international development cooperation professional is on record as having served as a spokesperson for the NDC on governance in the 2024 general elections. Since her appointment, social media has been awash with some posts she made in the past that were deemed political in support of the NDC. A video of her speaking on a media platform as a representative of the NDC has also gone viral. As a result, many have questioned her independence and neutrality in such a sensitive office. For many of the critics, they’re particularly unhappy that the NDC, which criticised previous EC officials and tagged them as politically aligned to the New Patriotic Party (NPP) have gone ahead to do the same. But who is Emelia Affi Agbenyo and what else is she known for? Before her appointment to the EC role, she was Deputy Director General in charge of operations at the Ghana TVET Service. As an international development cooperation professional, Emelia Affi Agbenyo has worked in strategic leadership, corporate governance, public sector management, and international development administration. Career path Her experience spans diverse sectors, including inclusive governance, skills development, private sector and enterprise development, donor negotiations, institutional capacity strengthening, public sector reform, and stakeholder engagement. As Deputy Director General in charge of Operations at the Ghana TVET Service, she provided executive oversight of nationwide operations, driving organisational performance, institutional transformation, and policy implementation. She is passionate about inclusive governance, gender equality, and social inclusion, and has led numerous initiatives advancing gender transformation, particularly within the informal sector. Her work reflects a strong commitment to strengthening governance systems that promote equity, participation, and opportunities for marginalised groups. Emelia Affi Agbenyo Her leadership experience spans policy design, organisational development, resource mobilisation, and managing complex multi-stakeholder partnerships. She has successfully led large-scale national and donor-funded programmes in inclusive policy implementation, skills and enterprise development, and gender transformation. She has managed strategic partnerships with organisations including UNDP, USAID, KOICA, GIZ Ghana, and the former Council for Technical and Vocational Education and Training. Beyond her executive role, she serves as a Commissioner of the National Development Planning Commission of Ghana and a Board Member of the African Trade Chamber and Education and Aspirations. Education Emelia Affi Agbenyo holds a Master of Arts (Hons) in Education Management & Leadership from the University of Ghana, Legon; a Bachelor of Arts in Psychology and Linguistics also from the University of Ghana; and a Master’s in Education, Leadership and Management from GIMPA. She is currently pursuing a Master’s in International Relations at GIMPA. She pursued General Arts at Chemu Secondary School in Tema, where she completed her studies in 2002.

title: Nigerian, Ugandan Youths Deploy Solar Technology to Tackle Environmental Challenges
body: Funmi Ogundare A Nigerian and a Ugandan youth innovators are deploying solar technology and Artificial Intelligence (AI) to address environmental and economic challenges, including energy poverty, food waste and agricultural losses, while improving livelihoods in their communities. Stanley Anigbogu, the 2025 Commonwealth young person of the year, has converted 600 kilogrammes of discarded plastic bottles into a community energy hub serving internally displaced persons in Abuja, while Shifra Ainomugisha, the 2026 award recipient, is using solar-powered cold storage, irrigation and AI to help small holder farmers in Uganda reduce post-harvest losses. Their initiatives demonstrate how youth-led innovations can support environmental sustainability, strengthen food security and create economic opportunities, with the Commonwealth providing platforms to connect young innovators with partners, investors and policymakers. Anigbogu, who founded LightEd in 2020, developed the Lighthouse for Peace project to address energy challenges at the Durumi camp for internally displaced persons in Abuja, drawing on his childhood experience of unreliable electricity. The project transformed about 30,000 discarded plastic bottles into useful infrastructure, including a community energy hub, 30 solar streetlights and 20 floodlights. The facility also provides charging services for more than 250 devices weekly, enabling children to study after sunset, improving safety within the community and providing young volunteers with opportunities to acquire green skills. “I want to ensure that darkness never limits another child’s ambition,” Anigbogu said. His initiative combines plastic waste recycling with renewable energy to address environmental concerns and the everyday challenges faced by displaced families. Similarly, Ainomugisha’s agricultural intervention emerged from her experience growing up on her family’s tomato farm in western Uganda, where significant quantities of produce were lost before reaching the market. Concerned about the impact of post-harvest losses on her family’s income and ability to support her education, she co-founded Solafam Uganda Limited, a woman-led social enterprise that provides technology-driven solutions to smallholder farmers. The enterprise deploys solar-powered cold storage facilities to preserve fresh produce, while solar irrigation systems help farmers maintain production during dry periods without relying on expensive diesel-powered equipment. It also developed LYN AI, a WhatsApp-based agricultural adviser that provides farmers with guidance on planting, pest management, irrigation, harvesting and market decisions. Through the combination of renewable energy and AI, the initiative seeks to reduce food waste, improve agricultural productivity and strengthen farmers’ incomes. Ainomugisha plans to expand Solafam’s operations into West and Southern Africa, adapting its technology to the needs of different farming communities. The Commonwealth youth awards, an initiative of the Commonwealth youth programme, provides a platform for young innovators to develop and scale their projects through seed funding, visibility and access to an international network of policymakers, investors, partners and youth organisations. The recognition has also enabled Ainomugisha to bring attention to the challenges faced by smallholder farmers and the potential of youth-led innovation to address them. Meanwhile, Anigbogu continues to pursue other technology-driven initiatives alongside his work with LightEd. He founded Artechubs Nigeria to address educational challenges through technology and Re-build Inc., a hardware research, development and engineering studio focused on helping to bridge Africa’s infrastructure gap. He is also a member of the 23-person international taskforce shaping the 2026 Commonwealth youth forum, scheduled to hold from November 2 to 4 in Antigua and Barbuda alongside the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting. Themed, ‘Investing in Youth Agency: Co-Creating Pathways Towards Shared Prosperity’, the forum is expected to bring together more than 300 youth delegates from five Commonwealth regions. Anigbogu and Ainomugisha will share their experiences of translating personal and community challenges into practical solutions using solar technology and AI. Their recommendations will be presented to Commonwealth leaders, with the aim of ensuring that young people’s perspectives inform discussions on resilience-building and shared prosperity. While Anigbogu is demonstrating how discarded plastic can be converted into renewable-energy infrastructure for vulnerable communities, Ainomugisha is showing how technology can help farmers preserve their harvests and improve their livelihoods.

title: Sybiha calls for tougher sanctions against Russia following strike on ships near Bulgaria
body:
Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiha has called on international partners to step up sanctions against Russia and take decisive measures to protect freedom of navigation following Russian strike on commercial vessels near Bulgaria's territorial waters, which resulted in injuries to citizens of Ukraine and Azerbaijan.
“Russia's latest attack on commercial vessels near Bulgaria's territorial waters, which injured Ukrainian and Azerbaijani citizens, once again demonstrates Moscow's deliberate disregard for civilian lives and maritime security in the Black Sea,” he said on X Tuesday.
He called on partners to step up pressure on the Russian Federation, expand sanctions, and take decisive measures to hold Russia accountable and protect freedom of navigation.
“The Black Sea is a lifeline for global food security. Russia is attacking it to weaponize hunger and hold the world hostage. This must be met with strength,” the foreign minister emphasized.
For his part, Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev reported that the Chelsea 3—a Malta-flagged vessel registered in Odesa and owned by a Ukrainian—was struck by three drones 18 nautical miles east of Byala. A distress signal from the vessel was received at 01:30.
“All 15 crew members—seven Ukrainian and eight Azerbaijani nationals—were safely transported to the port of Varna. Five are receiving medical assistance,” Radev said on X.
According to him, Bulgaria is seeking support in investigating the attacks to determine the origin of the drones, as well as assistance in strengthening air and maritime surveillance and enhancing response capabilities. The country's permanent representatives to NATO and the European Union have been informed of the incident. "We do not have clear and conclusive evidence to attribute responsibility to either side. However, as I have already noted, logic suggests that the outcome benefits the Russian Federation. Therefore, I will summon the Russian ambassador for a meeting today," the Bulgarian Prime Minister stated.
Furthermore, during an extraordinary meeting of the Security Council under the Council of Ministers, information was received regarding another vessel that had been struck 17 nautical miles east of Krapets. According to Radev, the vessel sank, and one crew member was rescued.

title: Pacific Nations Gather in Palau for Landmark High Performance Workshop on the Road to Brisbane 2032
body: Ten North Pacific National Olympic Committees, together with regional and international sporting bodies, convene in Palau this week to plan the region’s high-performance pathway toward the Pacific Games Tahiti 2027, LA 2028 and Brisbane 2032. PALAU, 12 October 2026: Ten National Olympic Committees (NOCs) from across the North Pacific have gathered in Palau today for the second North Pacific High Performance Workshop, a five-day programme running from 12 to 16 October 2026 under the PacificAus Sports Brisbane 2032 Games Pathways Program. The workshop builds on the inaugural Strategic Review and High Performance Enhancement Workshop held in Palau in March 2026. Having developed the Framework earlier this year, the focus now turns to implementation, including the formal endorsement and public launch of the Framework, with each delegation leaving with a costed, resourced national action plan. Over the five days, delegates will review Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games performance and benchmark athlete readiness against Commonwealth and Olympic standards. They will also prepare for the Pacific Games Tahiti 2027, the Naoero 2028 Micronesian Games and look forward to LA 2028 Olympic Games qualification pathways and Brisbane 2032 Olympic and Paralympic Games, with cultural identity embedded throughout the programme. NOCs attending: Federated States of Micronesia, Guam, Kiribati, Palau, the Marshall Islands, Naoero, the Northern Mariana Islands, Papua New Guinea, Solomon Islands and Vanuatu. The workshop programme also features contributions from the Australian Olympic Committee. The International Olympic Committee, Oceania Sport, Oceania Athletics, Oceania Weightlifting Federation, Oceania Zonal Volleyball Association, the Pacific Games Council, and the Oceania Paralympic Committee are also represented, reflecting the breadth of stakeholders invested in the region’s high-performance future “High performance planning is not a one-off exercise. It is a discipline that Pacific nations must build together, region by region and sport by sport,” said Baklai Temengil , Secretary General of the Palau National Olympic Committee and President of the Oceania National Olympic Committees (ONOC). “This workshop matters because it ensures the investment being made in key programs is matched by strong national plans and shared accountability across every stakeholder, from our National Olympic Committees to government and international partners.” The delegates from across the Northern Pacific were welcomed to the workshop by Brett Pelttari , Chargé d’Affaires, Australian Embassy in Palau “Australia is a proud supporter of Pacific sport, and this workshop builds directly on the Australian Government’s recent $15.6 million investment in Pacific athletes on the road to Brisbane 2032,” he said. “As Prime Minister Albanese said when announcing that investment, Australia looks forward to welcoming the best of the best sporting talent from the Pacific and supporting them to go for gold. Brisbane 2032 is shaping as a true home Games for the whole of Oceania, and Australia is committed to walking that path together with our Pacific neighbours.” “The Australian Olympic Committee is proud to stand alongside our Pacific neighbours as they build the plans, people and systems that will carry their athletes to the world stage,” said Ian Chesterman, President of the Australian Olympic Committee. “Brisbane 2032 is an opportunity for the whole Oceania Olympic family. By investing alongside the Australian Government in planning, people and partnerships now, we can ensure Pacific athletes arrive at those Games prepared, supported and ready to compete with the best in the world.” The post Pacific Nations Gather in Palau for Landmark High Performance Workshop on the Road to Brisbane 2032 appeared first on Island Times News .

title: IN BRIEF: FSB foils drone attack on military airfield in Voronezh Region
body:
MOSCOW, October 13. /TASS/. Russia’s Federal Security Service (FSB) detained a Russian woman suspected of preparing a drone attack on a military airfield on orders from the Security Service of Ukraine, the FSB said in a statement.
TASS has compiled the key details available so far.
- The Federal Security Service in the Voronezh Region foiled a large-scale act of sabotage and terrorism orchestrated by the Security Service of Ukraine, which planned to attack the Russian Defense Ministry’s Baltimor military airfield with short-range drones, the agency said.
- Law enforcement operations made it possible to expose and disrupt the illegal activities of a Russian woman who had been recruited by a Ukrainian intelligence officer during a trip to Ukraine in 2022.
- Acting on instructions from her handler, she traveled to Voronezh and rented a garage, where she planned to assemble and launch drones meant to be used to destroy infrastructure and aircraft, as well as kill military airfield staff," the FSB said.
- The drones were supposed to be operated remotely by personnel based in Ukraine.
- According to the FSB, the woman retrieved nine drones equipped with explosive devices, along with drone control equipment, from previously established caches and took them to the garage. Each drone carried 500 grams of foreign-made explosives.
- FSB officers responded immediately after receiving intel, promptly detaining the accomplice of Ukrainian intelligence agencies and preventing the act of sabotage before it was carried out, thus containing the potential consequences of the Kiev regime’s actions against the military facility, the FSB said.
- The woman confessed to cooperating with the Ukrainian intelligence service, according to a video released by the FSB.
- She said she had been living in Ukraine when Russia launched its special military operation.
- According to the suspect, a Ukrainian intelligence officer recruited her and suggested that she travel to Russia to carry out his orders in exchange for a cash reward.
- On his instructions, she traveled to Voronezh and rented a garage near the military airfield, the woman said.
- She added that she had retrieved drones and explosives from caches, brought them to the garage and assembled them as instructed by her handler.
- The woman also said that she had planned to return to Ukraine after completing her mission.
- The suspect has been taken into custody.
- Efforts are ongoing to establish all circumstances of the crime and identify all those involved," the FSB said.

title: Qatar's government revenue fell 42% in first half due to Iran war, Emir says
body: Qatar's revenue fell 42 per cent in the first half of this year, as exports of liquefied natural gas (LNG) dropped due to the impact of the Iran war, Emir Sheikh Tamim said during a Shura Council meeting. LNG exports from Qatar, the world’s second-largest supplier before the conflict, has fallen sharply due to the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz as well attacks on its Ras Laffan complex . “The crisis naturally had an adverse impact on public finances, with total revenues falling by 42 per cent during the first half of the year, while public expenditures decreased by 14 per cent – all without compromising essential services or development priorities,” Sheikh Tamim said. “We decided against curtailing essential services and chose not to alter development priorities, aiming to sustain the economic momentum Qatar is experiencing.” Measures taken before the crisis, such as strengthening reserves, reducing public debt, adopting conservative oil-price assumptions in the budget and developing non-oil revenue, helped Qatar absorb the economic fallout, he said. About 17 per cent of Qatar’s LNG capacity is offline after Iranian strikes damaged two of its 14 export trains, removing 12.8 million tonnes a year from the market. QatarEnergy has said repairs will take three to five years, meaning even a safe reopening of Hormuz would restore access to only part of Qatar’s prewar supply. Gas prices have soared globally due to the disruption. Disruption to Qatar's energy sector affects markets and consumers worldwide, the Emir said on Tuesday. “The closure of the Strait of Hormuz, along with direct damage to some energy facilities in Ras Laffan Industrial City, has disrupted a significant portion of the country's exports,” he said. However, the economic fallout is concentrated mainly in the energy sector, while non-hydrocarbon industries continue to grow, accounting for about 80 per cent of real gross domestic product, he added. “This reflects the national economy's ability to withstand and continue growing under exceptional and complex circumstances,” Sheikh Tamim said. Economies across the Gulf are projected to contract by an average of 4.3 per cent for 2026, down 5.7 percentage points from April, driven by lower export volumes due to the Strait of Hormuz's closure, leading to significant losses in output and government revenue, the World Bank said last week. Qatar's economy is estimated to be hit the hardest among all countries in the region, facing a 20.9 per cent contraction this year, compared to 1.8 per cent growth in 2025, the World Bank said. The estimate would represent the country's weakest economic performance in five decades, after its average monthly gas production fell by about 67 per cent between March and July due to damage sustained at its sites. Meanwhile, the International Monetary Fund in its update this week said it expects Qatar's economy to contract by 15.6 per cent this year, before rebounding to growth of 18.8 per cent in 2027. Investments of $60.7 billion However, Qatar will emerge from the regional crisis more resilient and better adapted to global changes, Sheikh Tamim said. “We have a portfolio of projects and investment opportunities valued at approximately 221 billion riyals [$60.7 billion] over the next five years,” he said. Planned investments will cover infrastructure, public-private partnerships and private-sector projects in real estate and hospitality, he added. Sheikh Tamim said Qatar had faced three simultaneous responsibilities during the crisis: protecting its sovereignty, fulfilling its role in global energy and economic security, and keeping diplomatic channels open. “Our strategy for shouldering these responsibilities consisted of four main elements: first, firmly defending the homeland without being drawn into war; second, maintaining services, supply chains and economic activity; third, contributing to efforts to secure a ceasefire and open waterways; and fourth, encouraging negotiations and seeking opportunities to return to talks to reach peaceful solutions to the conflict,” he said. Sheikh Tamim said the goal is “not merely to return to the pre-crisis status quo, but to use recovery as a springboard to accelerate economic diversification and strengthen national capabilities”. “God willing, Qatar will emerge from this crisis more resilient and better adapted to global changes,” he added.

title: Anthropic warns AI models could soon copy themselves across home devices
body:
Anthropic said Monday that small AI models are "months away" from developing the capabilities needed to replicate themselves across internet-connected devices in the home, marking the latest warning from the frontier lab about the technology's potential safety risks.
Anthropic described how AI models could potentially infiltrate internet-connected devices, such as smart ovens or Android TV boxes, and use their computing power to run themselves and spread to other devices, without relying on expensive data centers.
The AI model would be "challenging to shut down," Anthropic said in a blog post, "since there's no centralized point to shut off."
The company acknowledged that there is not yet a "fully rogue replicator."
Agents are, however, "becoming increasingly capable of completing the individual steps in the replication chain (and passing on their adaptations to future copies of themselves)," Anthropic said.
Anthropic's latest research adds to growing safety concerns around AI, such as the ability for models to carry out cyberattacks and the technology going rogue. In September, improvements in frontier models sparked industry-wide warnings of existential risks to humanity.
Executives and researchers at Anthropic and rival OpenAI repeatedly warned about the potential risks of increasingly powerful AI, with some calling for tighter guardrails and measures to control the pace of the technology's development .
Anthropic said it carried out various tests to see if AI could self-replicate. One of those tests involved running a small Google model, Gemma4-26B-A4B, across a network of 15 cheap off-brand Android TV boxes.
The company noted that these types of devices often have weak security, which could allow a model to infiltrate them. A model that is too large to fit on one device could "split into pieces, or shards" and run across multiple devices, Anthropic said.
"In practice, an AI worm wouldn't necessarily consist of just one model or strategy. A swarm of different models deployed on different types of hardware using a variety of replication schemes might represent a more realistic 'worst case scenario' attack," Anthropic said.
It's still "uncertain exactly what form autonomous AI replication will take," the AI lab said, warning that it could be a "slow, distributed" system sitting on insecure devices or a "powerful cyber model that breaches datacenters at a high pace, or a model that scams people for compute credits."
"As a prediction that goes beyond our experiments, we expect a future awash with agents running on all types of hardware, including some that aren't under human control," Anthropic said.
"The rise of slow replicators would also be a bellwether for more aggressive, faster ones that can breach more hardened machines or be effective API key thieves," the company added.

title: Dangote Targets 1.4m Barrels Daily Refining Capacity by 2029
body: * Promises to accommodate small bidders Blessing Ibunge Blessing in Port Harcourt President of Dangote Industries Limited, Aliko Dangote, has unveiled plans to expand the capacity of the Dangote Petroleum Refinery to 1.4 million barrels per day by early 2029, while assuring small investors that they would be accommodated in the company’s ongoing Initial Public Offering (IPO). Dangote, who disclosed this on Monday during the final IPO roadshow, themed ‘Back to Where It All Began,’ held in Port Harcourt, said the planned expansion would position the refinery among the world’s largest refining complexes and strengthen Nigeria’s industrial capacity. Speaking virtually at the event organised by Financial Derivatives Company for Dangote Petroleum Refinery, he said the refinery’s current capacity stood at 500,000 barrels per day, with further expansion expected to raise output substantially. “But what we have today, we are at 500,000 barrels per day. And by the beginning of 2029, we will be at 1.4 million barrels per day,” he said. Dangote added that the expansion would be accompanied by significant growth in petrochemical production, including a projected 2.5 million tonnes of polyolefins and a 400,000-metric-tonne linear alkylbenzene plant, which he described as the largest of its kind in Africa. He also highlighted plans for a 1,900-kilometre pipeline intended to extend the refinery’s reach into eastern and southern Africa, underscoring his ambition to build an industrial platform serving markets beyond Nigeria. “We’re not even started,” he said, signalling further expansion opportunities. Addressing concerns about the reported oversubscription of the IPO and the limited number of shares available to the public, Dangote assured retail investors that smaller bidders would not be shut out. “Yes, definitely. Most of the smaller people who are bidding for 50,000 shares and below will definitely be sure that we accommodate all of them,” he said, drawing applause from participants. He also defended the offer price of N525 per share, describing it as attractive in view of the refinery’s financial performance and growth prospects. “I think it’s an extremely very, very good price,” Dangote said, adding that the company expected its full-year performance to exceed earlier projections. He expressed confidence that investors would benefit from the refinery’s expansion, declaring: “This is the right shares to buy. This is the shares of the future.” Speaking at the event, Chief Executive Officer of Financial Derivatives Company, Bismarck Rewane, described the IPO as an opportunity for Nigerians to move beyond being consumers of the country’s industrial output to becoming investors who could benefit financially from its growth. He said the listing could significantly expand the Nigerian capital market, attract more investment and deepen public participation in strategic industrial assets. Rewane also highlighted the refinery’s broader economic significance, including its potential to stimulate industrial development, improve productivity and create investment opportunities across the energy value chain. Similarly, economist and Chief Executive Officer of the Centre for the Promotion of Private Enterprise, Dr. Muda Yusuf, said the refinery could strengthen Nigeria’s macroeconomic fundamentals by reducing dependence on imported petroleum products, easing pressure on foreign exchange and supporting industrialisation. He noted that its impact extended beyond fuel production to petrochemicals, plastics, packaging, logistics and other related industries. Yusuf also said the IPO had generated unprecedented public interest in the capital market, creating opportunities for broader investment participation and wealth creation. In his remarks, Chief Paul Usoro (SAN) urged Nigerians, particularly residents of the oil-producing South-south region, to participate in the share offer, arguing that communities supplying the country’s crude oil should also have a stake in its refining and downstream value chain. He recalled the long queues that once characterised fuel distribution in Nigeria, saying investment in domestic refining could help sustain improvements in petroleum supply, while giving shareholders an opportunity to participate in the industry’s growth. Usoro disclosed that he had invested in the company, urging prospective investors to consider the refinery’s potential economic and commercial benefits.

title: ‘Not Right’: Finland Seeks EU Ban on Russian Tourist Visas
body:
Finland has called for a complete EU ban on issuing tourist visas to Russian citizens while Moscow continues its war against Ukraine.
Finnish Foreign Minister Elina Valtonen said on Monday, Oct. 12, that the European Commission should tighten its guidance on Russian visa applications and propose the legislative changes needed for an EU-wide ban.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
“As long as Russia continues its invasion, Russian citizens should not be issued tourist visas,” Valtonen said.
“It is not right that Russians can travel to Europe to enjoy the way of life and freedoms here while their country bombs the homes of Ukrainians,” she added.
Finland stopped issuing visas to Russians for tourism and other non-essential travel under a government decision adopted in 2022. Valtonen said the same restriction should finally be introduced across the EU.
According to Finland’s Foreign Ministry, Schengen countries granted Russian citizens close to 500,000 tourist visas in 2025.
Finland argues that restrictions imposed by individual member states are insufficient because a Schengen visa issued by one country generally allows its holder to travel throughout most of the passport-free zone.
Valtonen has invited other EU governments to join a letter asking the European Commission to develop a common approach.
Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo has also said he intends to raise the proposal at the next European Council meeting.
“One concrete measure that I will present at next week’s European Council meeting is for Europe to stop issuing tourist visas to Russians,” Orpo told Finnish broadcaster Yle .
He linked the proposal to security concerns over alleged Russian sabotage operations inside Europe.
“Why on earth are we letting them into European territory as tourists, where they can move freely?” Orpo said.
The proposal concerns tourist and other non-essential travel. It would not automatically prohibit entry on humanitarian grounds, for family reasons, or for Russians seeking protection from political persecution.
Finland’s proposal goes beyond ordinary tourist visas.
Helsinki is also seeking a ban on Schengen visas for members of Russian President Vladimir Putin’s inner circle and people or organizations under EU sanctions.
The letter proposes restrictions on Russian athletes and members of sports teams with close ties to the Kremlin. Finland also wants the EU to effectively enforce an agreed entry ban covering current and former Russian combatants who participated in the war against Ukraine.
The European Commission previously proposed barring people who have served in the Russian Armed Forces since the invasion , arguing that Europe should remain inaccessible to those who joined Moscow’s war.
EU officials and several member states have described Russian veterans as a potential security threat, particularly amid allegations that Moscow is recruiting individuals to conduct sabotage, arson, and surveillance operations across Europe.
Estonian Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna earlier warned that the EU needed a coordinated system for identifying and blacklisting former combatants, declaring that there could be “no path from Bucha to Brussels .”
An EU-wide tourist visa ban has not yet been adopted and would require agreement among member states as well as changes to the bloc’s common visa rules.

title: The Illusion of the AI Renaissance Man
body:
Back in the day, I used to make YouTube videos talking about anime (yes, cringe as hard as you want).
I had to source the clips, cut them, edit the videos, write the script, record my voiceover, render the video, realize I left something out, fix it, re-render the video, and so on.
To be honest, I kind of loathed video editing. Writing the script and thinking about what I wanted to say was the fun part for me. For some of my friends at the time it was the opposite; they loved focusing on the visuals, but sitting down to write a script seemed bothersome.
Today, we live in a world with AI models. I could hand off the video editing to them, or at minimum the arduous task of selecting relevant clips, cutting them to ~5-8 seconds in length (to avoid copyright problems), and stitching them together.
In a way then, some would argue that AI can turn you into some kind of renaissance man. You can do the work of a video editor, script writer, researcher, and also be your own social media manager/marketer at the same time. Right?
But I was doing all of this myself anyway before LLMs even existed in their current form. I already was the renaissance man, bro.
I’m not arguing about the capabilities of AI. I’ve already gone through the five stages of grief and have accepted the fact that these tools are, at minimum, useful for productivity.
In fact, they’re so good at a wide range of tasks that they can quite easily do all of the busywork that you don’t want to do. AI doing the work for you doesn’t really make you a renaissance man, it makes you more of a manager or director. In the long term I think this could breed specialists.
In my YouTube experience, what AI would’ve allowed me to do in reality is become more of a specialist. I’d be entirely focused on writing the script and spending more time honing it, as opposed to learning video editing or sound engineering.
But learning that broad range of skills is what allowed me to find work in the first place. I’m not sure how that changes today with AI.
This push towards speciality is happening in my real work, too. When I write documentation, I no longer carve out hours to learn how to tweak outputs in the web framework I’m using. AI does that, so I get to focus on the documentation itself.
For blog posts, I’m spending much less time scouring Google for sources and charts and statistics. I use AI to write up a research report, check the sources are reliable, and then include them in my own writing.
All of this is to say that I get to focus on my craft (writing words). I can do more, and I’m certainly more productive because of AI. But that’s because it’s doing all of the stuff which would make me a true generalist.
I’ve been operating under the assumption that people, you, me, will still want to keep a craft. I don’t want to outsource writing too, but it would be very easy to do, even though AI writing still needs human guidance (for now).
The question that’s been on my mind for a while now is:
What do you choose to do when AI can already do it?
People in the AI scene love to talk about P(doom): the probability that AI will wipe out all of humanity. I personally think that the biggest threat (right now, at least) is deciding to outsource everything to AI.
I would consider myself one of the fortunate ones. I grew up reading books and learned how to program before LLMs came into existence. The experience for newcomers now must be something kind of unimaginable.
There’s a tool out there that can do everything you can do, but better. This puts them in a very precarious position: they are pushed to go full LLM and focus on speed, so they don’t fall behind their peers.
I’m not sure how much you can learn doing things this way; I can’t really speak for it. While it’s true that the former might be better for your brain, it’s going to be worse for productivity.
All I can say is that I think it’s a bad idea to outsource everything .
As people use AI to pick up the slack elsewhere, I think it’s preferable to make sure you don’t make it pick up the slack everywhere. You should use the time and effort saved meaningfully.
AI is described as having “spiky” intelligence right now because it’s especially good at math and code. My bet is that we will need to fit ourselves in around the “spiky” intelligence that LLMs seem to have today.
It’s weird. I think on one hand, AI will push us to the pinnacle of specialism which can be a good thing, because we can hone our focus on a single thing more than ever.
Yet, outside the scope of labour, humans are naturally generalists. We cross-pollinate across topics, and have different interests. These can be extremely important for scientific breakthroughs or unique pieces of art. By rejecting this, maybe we’ll lose something in the long run.
I think there is probably a counterargument here focused on getting AI to teach you things, instead of doing the work for you. If AI becomes good enough at this, then I think you can become a sort of renaissance man.
Honestly, I’m not sure. I think my thesis is still changing. AI has made me think a lot about where I want to spend my time. I still want to be as good at writing and marketing as I can be. Outside of work, it’s a bit more tricky.

title: Ukraine's future in Putin's hands, Russian victory all but assured — British politician
body:
BEIJING, October 13. /TASS/. The future of Ukraine will be decided by Russian President Vladimir Putin and the Russian government as Moscow's victory in its special military operation is a foregone conclusion, George Galloway, leader of the Workers Party of Britain, told TASS.
"It will be decided by president Putin and the Russian government, in particular. Because the war (Russia’s special military operation - TASS) is won [by Russia]," he said following a lecture hosted by the Russian Cultural Center in Beijing. "And the question is, now, what terms they will impose on the Ukrainian regime, both in terms of its own dissolution, for the solution there must be cannot possibly have [Vladimir] Zelensky continue in office," he added.
The key to bringing the situation in Ukraine to normal is not holding a presidential election there, the British politician argued. "It's not a new president with cleaner hands <…>. The change that's required is in the nature of any remaining rump Ukrainian state," Galloway explained. "Is that rump state going to be used in the future, in the new generation, perhaps as a knife in the back of Russia, or is it going to be a friendly government towards Russia and absolutely neutral," he wondered.
According to the politician, this neutrality means that the former Soviet republic cannot be part of NATO, nor should the North Atlantic Alliance be in Ukraine, Galloway continued. "I wouldn't trust the current political class in Ukraine at all. Nor Zelensky, nor any of the pretenders to his throne," he emphasized. "I would like to see Ukraine have the same relationship to Russia as Belarus does. Why can't they all be members of a union state?" he asked rhetorically.
Such a status for Ukraine would guarantee to the Russian side "no recurrence of the circumstances which led to the special military operation," according to Galloway. "Whether that's what happens or not, we cannot have, after all, this blood, all this treasure, all this wreckage of international relationships. People being confiscated, sanctioned, killed even," he added.
The Ukraine problem "has to be resolved once and for all," the leader of the Workers Party of Britain insisted. "The Russian speaking territories, all of them will have to be returned to Russia. Down to the Odessa, includes Transnistria, and whatever is left," he maintained.
As regards a recent statement from US President Donald Trump who announced an energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine, it will hopefully lead to a "permanent resolution of this conflict," Galloway said. "Too much dislocation and disruption to the international system has already occurred, <…> [and this problem] has to be resolved now, once and for all," he concluded.

title: The Journey Continues: The 20th Palau Pledge Dive Camp
body: Koror, Palau — October 5 to October 10, 2026 — The Palau Pledge Dive Camp returned this intersession with a powerful reminder that it is about more than scuba certification. It is about shaping our young Palauans to understand their connection to the ocean and their responsibility to protect it. Across the six days, campers took part in a program that blended science, culture, and hands-on ocean experience, continuing to bring the Palau Pledge to life through action and learning. The week began with our campers joining the Ngedebuul Youth Camp and partnering with the Palau Sailing Association for a cultural immersion in traditional navigation. Mr. Edwin Mario introduced the students to the basics of traditional Palauan outrigger canoe knowledge, connecting ancestral practices with modern sailing. In the afternoon, students had the opportunity to apply what they learned by heading out on the water and experiencing sailing firsthand. The students also visited the Alingano Maisu with the Micronesian Voyaging Society , where the crew shared the story of how the canoe was created and emphasized the importance of preserving traditional navigation as a vital part of Micronesian cultural heritage. The experience reminded students of our shared responsibility to ensure that this invaluable knowledge and tradition continue to be passed down to future generations rather than being lost. On Day 2 , Educational Trip – Building on the connection between culture and environmental stewardship, the camp next explored food security, aquaculture, and conservation . At the Palau Community College Cooperative Research and Extension (PCC-CRE) Research and Development Station and Hatchery in Ngermlengui , students learned about plant tissue culture, agricultural research, and the role of aquaculture in strengthening Palau’s food security. These activities highlighted the importance of local research and sustainable food production in supporting resilient communities. The group then traveled to Todai in Ngerchelong , where Ranger Snyder Skang shared the historical and cultural connections between Todai and Kayangel. Students learned about the significance of these connections and modern-day efforts to protect northern Palau’s ocean resources. For the remainder of the week, participants trained with Sams Tours , completing their Open Water scuba certification. Beyond certification, students gained confidence in the water and a deeper appreciation for the marine environment they are now more prepared to explore and protect. The Palau Pledge Dive Camp reflects a continued commitment to youth empowerment through education, culture, and conservation. By connecting science, tradition, and lived experience, the program supports the next generation of ocean stewards grounded in Palau’s values and identity. As the camp concluded, participants left not only as certified divers, but as Palau Pledge Ambassadors carrying forward the spirit of the Palau Pledge—protecting what they love, and sharing that responsibility with others. About the Palau Pledge Dive Camp The Palau Pledge Dive Camp is a youth program that combines environmental education, cultural learning, and dive training to inspire stewardship of Palau’s marine environment. Rooted in the Palau Pledge, the program encourages responsibility, respect, and care for Palau’s land and sea. Supported by the NCD Grant Funding Mechanism to promote physical activity and healthy lifestyles, and the Canada Fund for Local Initiatives (CFLI) , a Government of Canada program supporting local community projects, the camp encourages youth to care for Palau’s land, sea, and cultural heritage. The program also promotes healthy choices through an alcohol- and drug-free environment. The post The Journey Continues: The 20th Palau Pledge Dive Camp appeared first on Island Times News .

title: “We don’t need to hit the entire plant”—Ukraine’s drones go for refinery parts sanctions make hard to repair
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); Ukrainian drones have helped push Russia into its worst fuel crisis since the Soviet Union fell, The Washington Post (WaPo) reported on 11 October. Diesel is where this war reaches American drivers. US President Donald Trump blames rising diesel prices mostly on Russia’s war in Ukraine, while experts blame mainly the US war with Iran. Some of his allies now accuse Kyiv of trying to sway the US midterms. Drones go for the first stage of refining The Washington Post looked at dozens of strikes between 1 April and 31 August. Three refinery experts then examined satellite images of 54 strikes with visible damage. In over half, the damage seems to be to the desalting and distillation units, known by the Russian acronym ELOU-AVT. These units clean the crude of water and salt, then split it into separate compounds, the first steps toward gasoline and diesel. More than a third appear to have hit secondary units, which turn those compounds into jet fuel, gasoline, and liquefied petroleum gas. From April through August, drones struck two-thirds or more of the 36 big Russian refineries that S&P Global Energy tracks, a strike every third day. Some took as many as five hits. On 16 June, drones set the Moscow refinery’s distillation towers on fire. That strike and a second one days later kept the plant offline into September, WaPo reported, citing data firm Kpler. Ukraine targeted the refinery again on 20 September. Explore further Trump’s Russian diesel deal, which drew fury in Ukraine, is unlikely to lower prices, experts say “We don’t need to hit the entire plant,” a Ukrainian drone battalion commander with the call sign Tango told The Washington Post. Ukraine knows where to strike so that a refinery stops and stays down, he said. His unit, Ukraine’s 1st Separate Center of Unmanned Systems, runs long-range strikes deep inside Russia. Sanctions slow the repairs The EU banned exports of oil-refining equipment to Russia the day after the 2022 invasion, and the US followed days later. WaPo reported that the bans cover the distillation and secondary processing units Ukraine keeps hitting. The bans make spare parts hard to get, Alexander Kolyandr of Eurasia Group told the paper, and the strikes come faster than repairs. Since last year, Ukraine has doubled the size of each wave, decoys included, a person involved in the strike campaign told WaPo. The decoys are unarmed and draw Russian fire, wasting air-defense ammunition, WaPo explained. Without them, the person said, Ukraine would simply lose expensive systems. András Rácz of the German Council on Foreign Relations told WaPo that even if only 2–3% of drones get through, the damage is significant. title: Ukrainian minehunter quintet trains with Royal Navy destroyer
body:
Five Ukrainian minehunters have completed seven days of training in the eastern Solent alongside Royal Navy destroyer HMS Dauntless, preparing for mine countermeasures operations in Ukrainian waters.
The five Ukrainian minehunters are based in Portsmouth as part of the UK’s support to Ukraine. The vesselas are: Henichesk, Mariupol, Melitopol, Chernihiv and Cherkasy.
They completed seven days of training, including gunnery exercises, destroying practice mines, and sailing in close formation with HMS Dauntless.
Spread along the Dorset, Hampshire and Isle of Wight coastlines, the training was the final chapter of a larger exercise intended to refine the military response of Joint Expeditionary Force nations to protect Europe’s northern flank, Exercise Lion Protector.
The UK Commando Force trained in the Faroe Islands as part of the exercise, marking the first Royal Marines deployment to the islands since World War II. The training focused on protecting the Greenland-Iceland-United Kingdom (GIUK) Gap.
Under the supervision of UK military personnel, the Ukrainian vessels conducted gunnery exercises off Portland.
The training then focused on mine countermeasures, with Ukrainian crews practicing how to locate, identify and, when necessary, neutralize underwater explosive devices using the Seafox remotely operated vehicle. The system has been used by the Royal Navy for minehunting for approximately two decades.
Crews aboard two Ukrainian vessels, Chernihiv and Cherkasy, conducted live firings of their Seafox systems, followed by controlled detonations to neutralize simulated mine threats.
The final phase of Lion Protector focused on the ability of Joint Expeditionary Force (JEF) navies to protect maritime infrastructure and maintain the security of sea lanes.
The exercise concluded with the Ukrainian vessels maneuvering as a task group alongside HMS Dauntless. The Royal Navy destroyer is preparing to escort the UK flagship HMS Prince of Wales during the next phase of its Firecrest 2026 deployment to the High North.
Lion Protector followed Sea Breeze, the Ukrainian Navy’s annual exercise held off the UK’s south coast over the summer, in terms of scope and complexity, according to the Royal Navy.
