title: Will The German Navy’s F127 Frigate Displace Other Procurements Over High Cost?
body: Expenditures in the double-digit billion-euro range associated with the procurement of eight F127 air defence frigates now trigger concerns among the other German service branches that their own projects could be sacrificed. By Waldemar Geiger / hartpunkt – translation by Naval News Media reports repeatedly circulated claims that a single ship of this new class could cost around five billion euros. However, according to the lead construction shipyard, TKMS , the claimed figure is too high. The debate over other projects being crowded out by the F127 demonstrates that, despite the exemption of defence spending from the constitutional “debt brake” budget threshold, spending on all procurement projects planned under the Bundeswehr’s growth plan is not supported by unlimited funding. Planners, armament officials, and budget authorities must reportedly now set priorities and determine towards which projects, and at what scale, the available funds should be directed. In the case of the F127—which is intended for Ballistic Missile Defence and is therefore slated to receive state-of-the-art US technology such as the SPY-6 radar and the Aegis combat management system—the risk of this program displacing funding on other projects appears to be less severe than initially suggested. Sources familiar with the matter told hartpunkt that an acquisition of all eight ships in their original configuration is reportedly off the table. Reportedly the effort already faces a significant amount of pressure to produce savings in order to reduce overall cost. Whether other procurement projects could nevertheless be adversely affected remains not entirely clear at this point. Within the F127 procurement program, observers currently identify two basic choices for proceeding with the effort: The first option would be to not compromise on the specification itself, but rather purchase fewer frigates. An alternative would be to stick to an acquisition of eight frigates, but reduce capabilities of the design. This could imply a different radar-suite, reduced magazine depth for missile ordnance, or reduced endurance and availability. If this seconbd path is indeed taken, it will be interesting to see whether the project will be realized within the existing industrial team or whether alternative industrial arrangements are chosen. This article by Waldemar Geiger was originally published in German language at hartpunkt.de . It has been translated and republished with authorization. The post Will The German Navy’s F127 Frigate Displace Other Procurements Over High Cost? appeared first on Naval News .

title: Vietnam’s Vice President Visits Georgia
body: Vietnamese Vice President Võ Thị Ánh Xuân arrived in Georgia on October 12 for an official visit, with the delegation holding meetings with Georgian Dream government officials and signing bilateral cooperation documents. Xuân was welcomed at Tbilisi International Airport by Georgian Dream Foreign Minister Maka Botchorishvili. During the visit, she met with Georgian Dream Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze, GD-elected President Mikheil Kavelashvili, and the disputed Parliament Speaker Shalva Papuashvili. On October 12, Xuân met with Irakli Kobakhidze at the Government Administration, where an expanded-format meeting was also held with members of both governments’ cabinets. The meeting touched upon the relations between Georgia and Vietnam and opportunities for cooperation in “various fields,” highlighting that the “opening of the Embassy of Georgia in Vietnam will be an important step in this process,” according to the government’s press service. The sides also expressed readiness to strengthen political and economic ties, underscoring “growing dynamics of trade turnover between Georgia and Vietnam in recent years and the positive indicators in tourism.” According to the press service, they also highlighted Georgia’s “strategic location” and “the role of the Middle Corridor as a route connecting Europe and Asia, which creates new opportunities to strengthen ties between Georgia and Vietnam.” Kobakhidze thanked the Vietnamese official for “supporting Georgia’s sovereignty and territorial integrity.” He later hosted an official dinner for Vice President Xuan, with both sides reaffirming “their readiness to further deepen bilateral relations.” Separately, Georgian Deputy Foreign Minister George Zurabashvili met with his Vietnamese counterpart, Đặng Hoàng Giang, on the same day. According to the Georgian Foreign Ministry, the officials discussed “prospects for developing bilateral and multilateral cooperation,” focusing on Georgia’s “transit potential and opportunities for deepening trade and economic relations.” The meeting concluded with the signing of “a Memorandum of Understanding on Cooperation” between the Georgian and Vietnamese foreign ministries. On October 13, GD-elected President Mikheil Kavelashvili hosted Vice President Xuân at the Presidential Palace. “The sides discussed developing bilateral relations, deepening high-level political dialogue, and expanding cooperation in trade and economy, transport, investment, tourism, education, culture, and technology,” Kavelashvili’s administration said, adding that he congratulated the Vietnamese Vice President on her re-election. During the meeting, “innovation, information-communication technologies, artificial intelligence, science, and research” were highlighted as key areas of cooperation, as well as “developing direct links between universities and academic cooperation.” Disputed Parliament Speaker Shalva Papuashvili, along with the ruling party MPs, met Vice President Xuân on the same day. Papuashvili thanked the Vietnamese side for their support of Georgia’s territorial integrity and “underscored the importance of international law principles in today’s turbulent world.” According to the Parliament’s press release, “Xuân emphasized the rapid pace of Georgia’s economic development and the efforts of the Georgian authorities aimed at protecting national interests, identity, and culture.” The parties discussed “the importance of deepening parliamentary cooperation, including between friendship groups and sectoral committees.” “Xuân stated that Vietnam is ready to become a bridge between Georgia and the countries of Southeast Asia and to help deepen Georgia’s relations with that region,” the press release said, adding that the meeting also covered potential cooperation in trade, economy, business, innovation, tourism, education, culture, and sports. “The parties welcomed the plan to open a Georgian embassy in Vietnam next year, which will help bring relations between the two countries to a new level,” the press release noted. title: Yemeni military intercepts, shoots down Saudi UAV in Saada
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 13 (MNA) – Yemeni Army has said that its air defense units have intercepted and shot down a Saudi Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) in the airspace over the country’s northwestern Saada province.
Spokesman for the Yemeni Armed Forces Brigadier General Yahya Saree said in a statement on Tuesday morning that the Yemeni Armed Forces detected and targeted an armed Wing Loong II reconnaissance drone belonging to the Royal Saudi Air Force (RSAF), using an appropriate weapon.
The development came shortly after the Yemeni army successfully targeted King Khalid International Airport in the Saudi capital, Riyadh, in a new ballistic missile strike.
Saree said in a separate statement that the operation achieved a direct and accurate strike on the airport.
He renewed a stern warning to international airlines, aviation experts, personnel, workers and travelers worldwide, advising them not to fly to Saudi airports, which he described as unsafe, according to Press TV.
The warning specifically excludes the airports and airspace associated with the holy cities of Mecca and Medina.

title: BAE Systems unveils MDACS 155mm cannon for air defence and ground strikes
body: The exhibition runs from 12 to 14 October at the Walter E. Washington Convention Center. The prototype shown there differs substantially from earlier MDACS technology demonstrators. Mounted on an Oshkosh FMTV-family chassis, the system has a split cab with a central opening that accommodates the barrel during transport. A hydraulically raised support holds the barrel in place, while two side stabilisers and a rear stabiliser steady the three-axle vehicle during firing. The gun sits in a large unmanned turret at the rear and uses a fully mechanised loading system. BAE Systems describes MDACS as air-transportable and able to fire different precision-guided munitions according to the mission. For air defence, MDACS uses the Hypervelocity Projectile (HVP), a guided round. For strikes against fixed and moving ground targets in contested environments, it fires Scorpio-XR, an HVP-derived munition that BAE Systems says doubles the range of existing 155mm cannon-launched projectiles. The U.S. Army reportedly aims to have a complete battery available for testing by the end of September 2027. The planned configuration comprises eight guns in four two-gun platoons, each with an MFPR radar, alongside two MDBM command posts and ammunition vehicles. The battery is intended to protect fixed and semi-fixed U.S. military installations against a broad range of air threats at moderate cost. Its development builds on earlier U.S. Army and Air Force work exploring the use of 155mm artillery for air defence. HVP has been under development since 2013 and has been tested from the 155mm M777 towed howitzer and the 127mm Mk 45 naval gun. Reported ranges from those trials were approximately 31.5km and more than 74km respectively, although these are not MDACS range figures. Technical problems during HVP’s development have driven up costs. Simulations nevertheless suggest that the guided artillery round could remain cheaper than guided air-defence missiles. “The threat environment is evolving faster than traditional procurement cycles can keep up with,” said Jason Casciotti, vice president of BAE Systems’ Weapon Systems product line. BAE Systems said it was drawing on proven technology and an established supply chain to accelerate delivery.

title: ‘Serious blow’: Guterres condemns new US sanctions on International Criminal Court
body: NEW YORK, 12 OCTOBER 2026 (UN NEWS CENTRE) —The United States has imposed sanctions on the International Criminal Court (ICC) as an institution, with Secretary of State Marco Rubio vowing on Friday to “dismantle the ICC, brick by brick” unless it ends what Washington regards as a “threat” to its citizens. The court hit back forcefully, calling the step unprecedented, following sanction measures by the US already in place against 13 judges and prosecutors. The ICC described the measure as “an assault on the rule of law and on the very foundations of the international legal order”. The designation, the court said, is aimed at disrupting its operations and “intimidating those who work for or cooperate with the court”. But, it will not be deterred. “The court will continue to fully discharge its mandate, with independence and impartiality, acting only on the basis of the law and the evidence for the sake of the countless victims of grave crimes,” said ICC President Tomoko Akane. Yet, the court acknowledged that it cannot stand alone. “Its fate now rests also in the hands of the States that created it,” the statement said, adding that the Rome Statute’s promise “is only as strong as the resolve of those who made it”. “No one should be punished for serving the cause of justice. History will judge this moment,” it concluded. Rubio: ‘We will end the ICC’ Announcing the sanctions, Rubio said the U.S would “ban transactions with this rogue court, cutting off their resources and crippling its ability to operate”. “America never joined the court. We don’t need it. And we don’t want it,” he added. Rubio said the door to diplomacy remained open, but he issued a stark warning. “Either the ICC will end its threats, or we will end the ICC,” he said, adding that Washington expected allies to “rein in the court”. Guterres condemns move UN Secretary-General António Guterres strongly criticised the U.S decision, according to his spokesperson, Stéphane Dujarric. The UN chief condemned the new sanctions against the court “as an institution”. Guterres was “deeply alarmed” by the expected impact on the court’s “continued ability to perform its important mandates” and called the sanctions “a serious blow to our collective pursuit of international criminal justice, of which the ICC is a key pillar”. He reiterated his “unwavering support for the independence of the court and its officials” and called on all States to uphold their commitments under international law. The UN remains committed to cooperating with the ICC under the relationship agreement approved by the General Assembly on 13 September 2004, the statement added. Independent UN human rights experts warned separately that the U.S sanctions were a “brash attempt” to dismantle a collective international legal system to hold perpetrators of the gravest crimes to account. They called on States committed to the rule of law to stand together in defence of the court and its independence. “Sanctioning the institution entrusted with delivering justice for the gravest international crimes is an assault on the foundations of international accountability and rule of law,” the experts said. “No State should place itself beyond the reach of the law by intimidating the court established to enforce it and attempting to dismantle it.” The UN Human Rights Council-appointed experts – who are not employed by the UN and receive no salary for their work – added that the attack “directly injures the victims of atrocities and their advocates, who rely on the ICC for justice, accountability and reparation”……PACNEWS The post ‘Serious blow’: Guterres condemns new US sanctions on International Criminal Court appeared first on Island Times News .

title: Iran accused of waging 'systematic campaign' against UK
body: Iran is conducting a “ systematic campaign ” against UK interests that should be met with offensive action by security services, a politician and former British Army officer has said. Mike Martin, who served on several tours with the Intelligence Corps in Afghanistan , urged Britain's Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood to take much tougher action against the regime, which has been blamed for several attacks and plots, including the recent incident at RAF Fairford, a base that had been used by US aircraft . Seven men have been arrested and released on bail while inquiries into a potential bomb plot continue, with the US withdrawing its B-1 bomber aircraft in the meantime. Two Iranians have been arrested for allegedly planning a lethal attack on Manchester’s Jewish community. Ms Mahmood announced on Monday that the government has created a specialist counter-terrorism section to tackle state threats from countries such as Iran. However, after Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he suspected the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps was behind the Fairford incident, Mr Martin told parliament during an urgent debate on UK national security: “I think it’s safe to say that there’s a systematic Iranian campaign on British soil.” The Liberal Democrat MP, who sits on the defence committee, said the government’s measures against Iran, which included imposing sanctions on the head of counter-espionage operations in the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) and summoning the Iranian ambassador in London, were “largely defensive in nature”. “Sometimes offence is the best form of defence, and I wonder whether the Home Secretary has considered that perhaps we need to increase the costs on the Iranians for their actions and considered signalling that fact to the Iranians to deter them from future activity?” Mr Martin said. Former deputy prime minister Oliver Dowden told parliament on Monday that Iran considered the UK its enemy and “ smells weakness ”. He said Iran had attempted attacks at bases in Diego Garcia in the Indian Ocean, Akrotiri in Cyprus and Fairford in Gloucestershire. The UK introduced sanctions on the IRGC in July, after the first two incidents and a series of attacks against dissidents in previous years. Ms Mahmood said the threats from Iran have been discussed with Britain’s allies. “We will always make sure we take both collective action to deal with the threats we all face, but also make sure we are always protecting the British national interests,” she said. She said she would not provide “a running commentary on wider discussions”, but added the government “will always take every appropriate step to keep our people safe”. In her statement, Ms Mahmood outlined how the new National Security Act gives the government “powerful new tools to tackle state threats”. She announced her department was “building a specialist mission in counterterror policing to disrupt state threats and tightening security around military bases”. Britain will also establish a National Centre for Information Defence to tackle disinformation from states and will give “intelligence agencies and police stronger powers to bear down on cybercriminals”. In addressing the threat posed by states such as Iran, she said: “Make no mistake: our police and security services are on permanent watch.” Foreign ministries from almost 30 countries including the US, Canada, France ​and Germany, issued a statement on Monday condemning “Iran’s use of violent attacks, including the acts ‌of lethal plotting, arson, sabotage, cyber attacks, and other ⁠hybrid activities against us and our partners”. “The UK has also ​concluded this event demonstrates the IRGC’s continued willingness to project hostile activity beyond its borders through covert networks ​and proxy actors,” ‌the statement added. Mr Burnham said: “We will not tolerate these threats on our soil. We will crack down on Iran’s use of criminal networks using our full range of powers to target them and their funding streams. And we will bring further sanctions to restrict the capacity if Iran and the IRGC do us harm.”

title: Document Review with Unsiloed and TypeSafe Jev
body:
Separate uncertain readings from implausible values with source evidence, typed Jev questions, and a prescription walkthrough.
An extraction pipeline can read a value correctly and still pass bad data downstream. A clearly printed extra zero survives excellent optical character recognition (OCR).
Using Unsiloed and TypeSafeâs Jev together helps us check for OCR failures and general mistakes in a document. Unsiloed extracts structured fields and locates them on the page. Jev judges the extracted information against focused questions. We can combine these results to decide which fields need review.
A Jev request separates the information it considers ( state ) from the decisions it makes ( questions ). In our workflow, state contains the records Unsiloed extracted and the context needed to interpret them. Each question tells Jev what to check and which answer type to return; it can also define criteria for the possible answers.
The type determines what our code receives. A Noul returns the probability that a statement is true. A Choice selects from named options; a Score evaluates a rubric of ordered levels. Choice and Score also return a probability distribution and a confidence value summarizing its concentration. Noul has no separate confidence field.
The three types can share state in a single request, as the diagram shows. Later, we'll use only Noul in our example.
A Noul value of 0.04 means a 4% probability of yes to our question, a strong no . It does not mean âJev is 4% confident.â Values near either end indicate a clear direction; values near the middle deserve caution.
Unsiloed preserves what is printed and provides confidence scores that help identify ambiguous readings. For our example, we use a medication list with six rows. A coffee stain obscures one dose, while another row contains a clearly printed but implausible quantity. We'll follow both through extraction and Jev's checks.
Our extraction schema defines the fields Unsiloed should return for each medication. It requests the complete dose cell, including quantity and unit, without correcting surprising quantities or guessing obscured text from usual prescribing practice. Enable source citations with enable_citations=true and wait for the extraction job to complete before constructing Jevâs state.
Each field has two Unsiloed confidence scores : extraction_score measures confidence in the extracted value, while grounding_score measures confidence that the value was located in the document. Both range from zero to one. The citation identifies its page and bounding box, the rectangle around the source text.
Here is the stained cetirizine dose from the saved response, with pixel coordinates on the original 1,200 Ã 1,500 image:
Assign each medication row an ID, such as row-5 , and keep it with the extracted fields and their citations. This lets our code match Jevâs answer to the same row later. Keep the citations so reviewers can locate each extracted field on the original page.
Send Jev the extracted values and context. It judges the instruction as extracted, without seeing the image or Unsiloed scores. We ask one Noul question per row: is this dose and frequency plausible for this medicine? All six rows share one request, with each question evaluated independently .
In the server-side module that connects the two APIs, construct this request (one row and its question shown):
The context and criteria are shortened here; the recorded request contains the exact text and all six rows. We use row-5 as the question ID so our code can match the answer to that row. We also include it as row_id inside the instructions so Jev knows which record to judge: question IDs are not sent to the model .
Post the request as JSON to https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone . Authenticate with your TypeSafe API key in the Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY> header , keeping the key on the server. The recorded answer at answers["row-5"] is { "type": "noul", "noul": 0.94 } . Match that answer to the saved row-5 extraction using the shared ID.
Our code now decides whether the row needs review. For the reading check, we take the lowest Unsiloed score across the rowâs fields, so a low score on any field flags the whole row. For the plausibility check, we use Jevâs noul value.
In the same module, pass those two values as reading and plausible to this function. It returns the reasons to send the row for review, or an empty array when neither check flags it. These demo rules also flag missing or invalid scores:
Here, a reading score below 0.90 or a plausibility answer below 0.50 triggers review. These are example cutoffs: test them against manually reviewed documents before using them in production. Jev answers near 0.50 may also need review because neither yes nor no is clearly favored.
Keep both reasons when both checks fail. A plausible instruction can still contain misread text, so a high Jev answer must not cancel a low Unsiloed score. Save the original extraction and Jev request and response alongside the reviewerâs decision so you can later check why a row was flagged and how it was resolved.
Step through the saved API results to see what Unsiloed reads, what Jev checks, and why the two flagged rows need different kinds of review.
For the stained cetirizine dose, Unsiloed extracts â1 tabletâ with an extraction score of 0.74 and a grounding score of 0.76. Jev returns 0.94 for plausibility, but it never sees the stain. That judgment depends on the extracted text being right. The reading check still flags the row because someone must confirm the obscured mark.
The ibuprofen row reverses the pattern. Unsiloed reads â10 tablets, three times dailyâ with both scores at 0.99; Jev returns 0.04 for the same plausibility question. The reviewer needs to investigate the clearly printed instruction. Neither model substitutes an assumed intended dose.
Each check flags a review need the other misses. The other four rows clear both demo thresholds, as the recorded responses show. The explanations and routing labels come from our application; Jev returns the typed answers, not those explanations.
One medication list in this demo produces a Jev request with six questions and 1,812 input tokens . At Jev 1.13.0âs published price of $42 per billion input tokens , with output free (checked September 30, 2026), that adds $0.000076 per document . Processing 100,000 similar documents would add about $7.61 in Jev charges.
This is a Jev-only estimate; Unsiloed extraction and human review cost separately. Your actual charge depends on the text and questions sent. For a closer estimate, take the input_tokens from a representative Jev response and apply the published rate.
Upload a sample PDF and get structured output in minutes. No integration required.

title: 1 dead, several injured in roller coaster incident at Six Flags park: Police
body:
Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem, 42, died at Six Flags Over Georgia, police said.
A beloved Atlanta school worker was killed when he fell from a massive roller coaster at a Six Flags amusement park in Georgia, authorities said.
Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem, 42, of Atlanta, was found dead beneath the ride at Six Flags Over Georgia on Monday, according to the Cobb County Police Department.
"Preliminary information gathered through witness and employee interviews indicates Kariem was ejected from the ride and struck other patrons before falling beneath the attraction," the Cobb County Police Department said in a statement on Tuesday.
Kariem was at the Six Flags park with several family members to celebrate his niece's birthday and was sitting beside his niece when he was ejected from the Goliath roller coaster, a relative told ABC News.
The relative, who did not want to be publicly identified, said he "was a good, good man" and a dedicated family man who treated his wife and stepdaughter well.
Kariem worked for the Atlanta Public Schools, a spokesperson for the school district confirmed Tuesday, calling him a "cherished member of the Wesley International Academy."
His "presence and impact will be deeply missed by our students, staff, and all those whose lives he touched," the spokesperson said in a statement. "Our thoughts are with everyone mourning his loss during this difficult time."
Kariem was the IT manager, a technology teacher and robotics coach at Wesley International Academy, where he had worked for over 12 years, according to the school.
"His love for Wesley, dedication to our students, and commitment to our school community were evident in everything he did," Wesley International Academy said in a statement. "Mr. Kariem was deeply loved and respected, and his absence will be felt throughout our school community."
A bio on the school's website stated that the favorite part of Kariem's job was "the opportunity to make a meaningful impact on both students and staff through technology," and that in his spare time, he enjoyed "creating custom products with his laser engraver and 3D printers, grilling and trying new recipes, watching anime, and spending time with family and friends."
The Cobb County Police Department said Tuesday that its investigators "continue to examine the circumstances surrounding the incident."
The state's Office of the Commissioner of Insurance and Safety Fire, which is responsible for the safety of amusement park rides in Georgia, also said it is "actively investigating" the incident.
"Our investigative team is conducting an in‑depth and comprehensive review to determine the circumstances surrounding the incident and to ensure full compliance with all applicable policies and procedures," Garrison Bennett, the agency's press secretary, said in a statement on Tuesday.
Several people were also injured in the incident, which occurred shortly before 4 p.m. Monday at the Atlanta-area amusement park, according to police.
Distraught witnesses described the horrific incident to ABC News, saying they saw the man coming out of his seat on the amusement park's Goliath roller coaster, then hit the ride several times before falling to the ground. Witnesses told a local station that the fall was captured on their souvenir pictures.
Riders on the Goliath were seen being evacuated off the roller coaster on Monday, after it stopped near the top of the ride.
A Six Flags spokesperson said that the "park team and local authorities responded immediately, and we are cooperating fully with local authorities as they complete their investigation."
"We are deeply saddened by the guest incident at our park today," the spokesperson said in a statement on Monday. "Our thoughts and heartfelt condolences are with the guest's family, friends, and loved ones. We are also providing support to the guests and team members affected."
The Goliath roller coaster reaches an elevation of 200 feet and speeds up to 70 mph, according to the amusement park's website. The ride first opened in 2006 at the amusement park, located west of Atlanta in Austell.
The manufacturer of the Goliath coaster, Switzerland-based Bolliger & Mabillard, said the company is "deeply saddened by this tragic accident."
"Our thoughts are with the family and those affected," Olivier Bolliger of Bolliger & Mabillard said in a statement Tuesday. "We are actively investigating the incident and will not comment further until we have a better understanding of what happened."
The Six Flags spokesperson said that "out of an abundance of caution," the theme park company has "temporarily closed similar attractions across our parks."
In addition to the Goliath roller coaster at Six Flags Over Georgia, nine similar hypercoasters in six theme parks across North America are temporarily closed .
Six Flags is not releasing additional information on the incident at Six Flags Over Georgia at this time "out of respect for the family's privacy," the spokesperson said.
ABC News' Faith Abubey, Matt Foster and Jason Volack contributed to this report.

title: Bulgaria to Summon Russian Ambassador After Attacks on Black Sea Ships
body:
Bulgaria will summon Russia’s ambassador after overnight attacks on commercial ships off its Black Sea coast, including a drone attack on a Ukrainian-owned cargo vessel and a separate incident in which another ship reportedly sank, Bloomberg reported Tuesday, Oct. 13.
Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev said authorities did not have sufficient evidence to formally identify who was responsible. Ukraine blamed Russia and called for additional sanctions.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
The Malta-flagged Chelsea 3, owned by a Ukrainian company, was attacked at about 1:30 a.m. on Tuesday, roughly 18 nautical miles (20 miles) off the coast near the Bulgarian town of Byala, Radev said, according to Bloomberg.
Crew members reported an attack by three drones, but all survived and were rescued.
Radev also described a second incident about 17 nautical miles (19 miles) off the village of Krapets, where preliminary information indicated that another vessel had been struck and sunk.
Despite the decision to summon Russia’s ambassador, Radev said Bulgaria lacked the evidence needed to accuse a specific party.
“We lack solid, clear evidence to level accusations against any specific party,” he said.
He nevertheless suggested Russia could benefit from the incidents.
Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha blamed Russia for the attacks near Bulgarian territorial waters, saying Ukrainian and Azerbaijani citizens had been injured.
Sybiha said the attacks demonstrated Moscow’s disregard for civilian lives and the safety of shipping in the Black Sea. He urged international partners to increase pressure on Russia, impose additional sanctions, and take action to protect freedom of navigation.
“The Black Sea is a vital artery of global food security,” Sybiha said.
“Russia is attacking it to weaponize hunger and hold the world hostage.”
Sybiha called for a decisive international response to hold Russia accountable and safeguard commercial shipping.

title: 'Absolutely unacceptable' — 11 crew members lost at sea after commercial ships hit by drones near Bulgaria's Black Sea coast
body:
Two cargo ships were struck by drones near Bulgaria's Black Sea coast overnight on Oct. 13, Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev said.
According to Radev , the Maltese-flagged Chelsea 3, registered in Odesa and owned by a Ukrainian company, was hit by three aerial drones about 18 nautical miles east of the coastal town of Byala in Bulgaria .
All 15 crew members, seven Ukrainians and eight Azerbaijani nationals, were evacuated to the port of Varna, and five received medical assistance, Radev said.
He added that another vessel was struck 17 nautical miles east of Krapets, a Bulgarian village, as he was told at an extraordinary meeting of the Security Council under the Council of Ministers.
The vessel sank, and five crew members were rescued, while 11 crew members were still missing at sea, according to Bulgarian officials, reported Reuters . Reuters further said that Bulgarian media had identified the ship as the ⁠cargo ship Azov Concord.
Radev called the attacks " absolutely unacceptable " and said Bulgaria had informed its permanent representatives to NATO and the European Union. Sofia is seeking assistance to strengthen surveillance of the air and maritime domains and improve its response capabilities.
Bulgarian authorities have not established who was responsible for the attacks. Radev said there was no clear and conclusive evidence to attribute responsibility to either the Ukrainian or Russian side, but argued that "the logic suggests that the outcome benefits the Russian Federation." Radev said he would summon Russia's ambassador for a meeting on Oct. 13.
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen condemned the attacks, saying the Black Sea had become "another front of escalation of the Russian war in Ukraine."
"Putting the lives of the crew in grave danger and threatening security in the Black Sea. We stand with Bulgaria and thank its rescuers for their swift response."
Ukraine's Infrastructure Ministry said Russia has repeatedly targeted Ukrainian ports, port infrastructure, and civilian commercial vessels in the Black Sea, posing a threat to international shipping and logistics routes.
Attacks by Ukraine and Russia in the Black Sea intensified over the summer.
In July, Ukraine launched Operation Molochka, a campaign targeting Russia's shadow fleet in the Black Sea and the Sea of Azov in an effort to tighten the noose around Russian-occupied Crimea .
Turkey called on Moscow and Kyiv in August to impose a moratorium on attacks against vessels, following a series of strikes in the region that involved Turkish-flagged ships.
While Kyiv has said it is ready to accept a moratorium on attacks in the Black Sea, Moscow has shown no interest in de-escalating the situation.
On Aug. 6, drones reportedly struck several merchant vessels in the Black Sea, including two ships in Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone. A Russian strike on a separate civilian vessel that day killed at least one crew member and injured several others.
Ukraine established its own Black Sea maritime corridor in August 2023, after Russia withdrew from a U.N.- and Turkey-brokered grain deal. Since then, Russia has regularly targeted ports and civilian shipping.

title: French Navy Boards Russia-Linked Tanker in Indian Ocean
body:
The French navy intercepted and boarded an oil tanker linked to Russia’s so-called shadow fleet in the Indian Ocean, President Emmanuel Macron announced Monday.
The French joint staff said naval inspectors boarded the vessel to verify its nationality after doubts arose over its claimed Benin registration. The operation took place around 450 nautical miles south of Réunion Island, an overseas territory of France.
Macron said the ship — the DF Peak — was suspected of sailing under a false flag and being involved in illicit fuel transportation. The vessel is under U.S., EU, U.K. and Ukrainian sanctions.
The tanker was being escorted to Réunion for further checks, said armed forces minister Catherine Vautrin.
The DF Peak is at least the sixth shadow-fleet tanker French authorities have detained over the past year, according to the exiled outlet The Insider.
La France est déterminée à lutter contre la flotte fantôme, partout dans le monde. Ce matin, à plus de 450 nautiques au sud de La Réunion, notre Marine nationale a arraisonné le pétrolier DF Peak, suspecté de naviguer sous un faux pavillon et impliqué dans des activités illicites de transport de carburants. Cette action, conduite conformément au droit international de la mer, témoigne de notre détermination à faire respecter le droit et à lutter contre tous les trafics illicites, où qu’ils se produisent.
President Vladimir Putin has previously condemned European seizures of Russia-linked tankers as “piracy and robbery” and threatened retaliation.
Built in South Korea in 2006, DF Peak previously operated as the NS Captain and later as the Kaliningrad under Russia’s state shipping giant Sovcomflot.
Maritime database records cited by The Insider and Mediazona claim the DF Peak dropped its Russian flag in June 2025 to register under Benin and is currently registered to Hong Kong Ding Feng Shipping.
Russia's embassy in France said on Tuesday that France's seizure of the DF Peak was a blatant violation of international law, the state RIA news agency reported.
RIA cited the Russian embassy as referring to the seizure as "piracy" and as saying it was trying to determine if any Russian citizens had been among the ship's crew.
It was also quoted as saying that France had not notified Russia about the tanker's seizure.

title: Z.ai GLM-Legal Beats Claude Fable 5 and Kimi K3 on Harvey LAB
body: Z.ai just released GLM-Legal . GLM-Legal is a legal AI model from Z.ai, built on GLM-5.3-Flash and trained for agentic legal work. It targets contract review, evidence analysis and compliance research. The key result is a 19.2% all-pass rate on Harvey’s Legal Agent Benchmark (LAB) . That is nearly 3x its base model’s 6.7%. For developers, the catch is access: the API is application-only for now. TL;DR Size: Built on GLM-5.3-Flash, a 320B-total, 18B-active MoE with a 1M-token context and 128K max output. Z.ai lists no separate GLM-Legal parameter count. Runs on: Z.ai’s hosted API only, by application. No public weights. The base model self-hosts on multi-GPU servers via vLLM or SGLang, with FP8 weights. Performance: Top-10 on Harvey LAB at a fraction of frontier cost. Within 2.3 points of the LegalBench leader. Best: 19.17% Harvey LAB task pass rate, #7 of 79 on Vals AI, at $0.15 per test. Worst: 41.83% on Vals AI’s Legal Research Bench, below its own base model (45.19%). Bottom line: Best: frontier-class legal agent scores at about 1/128 the cost of Claude Fable 5. Worst: gated beta with no price, no weights and slow runs (1h12m per task). What is GLM-Legal? GLM-Legal is a domain-specialized version of GLM-5.3-Flash for law firms, in-house counsel and compliance teams. The base is Z.ai’s first natively multimodal GLM-5 model . It has 320B total parameters with 18B active. It mixes sparse and linear attention to cut long-context serving cost. It reads text, images, video and files, and outputs text. How was GLM-Legal trained? Training ran in 2 stages: Mid-training on expanded legal corpora, to strengthen reasoning from facts to rules to conclusions. Post-training with reinforcement learning across tens of thousands of legal task environments . The Z.ai team also describes the agent harness co-evolving with the model during post-training. Edge cases in training exposed harness bottlenecks. Harness fixes then exposed the model to more realistic constraints. How does GLM-Legal score on Harvey’s Legal Agent Benchmark? Harvey LAB is an open-source benchmark of 1,250 tasks across 24 practice areas . Over 75,000 expert-written rubric criteria grade the work. A task passes only if every criterion passes. Harvey calls this all-pass grading. Vals AI runs the held-out set with 2 LLM judges and internet disabled . Agents get file tools plus docx , pptx and xlsx skills. On that leaderboard, GLM-Legal scores 19.17% and ranks #7 of 79. Its base, GLM-5.3-Flash, scores 6.67%. The 12.5-point lift is the core claim, and an independent evaluator reproduced it. Z.ai’s launch chart shows GLM-Legal ahead of Kimi K3 (12.92%), Claude Fable 5 (11.25%) and GPT-6 Astra (5.42%). Those figures match Vals AI. The chart omits 6 models ranked higher, led by Muse Spark 1.2 at 25.42%. GLM-Legal also passes 92.5% of individual criteria. Top models sit near 90% to 95% on that measure. Does GLM-Legal match frontier models on LegalBench? Roughly. Z.ai claims parity on LegalBench and the Chinese-focused PLawBench without publishing numbers. Vals AI scores GLM-Legal at 86.23% on LegalBench . Claude Fable 5 leads at 88.56% . Kimi K3 scores 86.21% . title: Drones attack two cargo ships off Bulgaria’s coast, one Ukrainian-owned. Sofia plans to summon Russian ambassador.
body: Two cargo ships came under attack overnight on October 13 in the Black Sea off Bulgaria’s coast, the country’s prime minister, Rumen Radev, said. Three drones struck the Ukrainian-owned vessel Chelsea 3 , sailing under a Maltese flag, about 18 nautical miles (roughly 33 kilometers) east of the city of Byala. All 15 crew members — seven Ukrainian citizens and eight Azerbaijani citizens — were evacuated. According to preliminary reports, five sailors sustained minor injuries. Another ship sank about 17 nautical miles east of the village of Krapets. One crew member from that ship was rescued. “This is absolutely unacceptable: yet another attack in close proximity to Bulgaria’s territorial waters,” Radev said in a televised address. He added that he has a call scheduled with NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte. According to Radev, there is not yet “solid and unambiguous evidence to bring accusations,” but “logic suggests the outcome benefits the Russian Federation.” Bulgaria intends to summon Russian Ambassador Eleonora Mitrofanova over the incident. Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said that “Russia’s latest attack on commercial vessels near Bulgaria’s territorial waters, which injured Ukrainian and Azerbaijani citizens, once again demonstrates Moscow’s deliberate disregard for civilian lives and maritime security in the Black Sea.” He called on partners to increase pressure on Russia. A week earlier, drones attacked two other cargo ships off Bulgaria’s coast, about 110 kilometers (68 miles) from shore. The crew of one ship was evacuated, while the other sank. Reuters reported that this was the first known drone attack on civilian ships in Bulgarian waters since the start of the war in Ukraine. title: IMF: Poverty Remains High in Nigeria Despite Economic Growth
body: . Raises country’s 2026 growth forecast to 4.2%, retains 4.3% for 2027 Nume Ekeghe in Bangkok, Thailand The International Monetary Fund (IMF) on Tuesday said despite Nigeria’s economic growth holding up, poverty remains high and the population continues to suffer, urging the government to provide targeted, temporary support to vulnerable households. The Fund said the disproportionate increase in food and energy prices had intensified the cost-of-living crisis, highlighting the need for policymakers to balance the immediate needs of households with medium-term fiscal stability. The IMF also upgraded Nigeria’s economic growth projection for 2026 by 0.1 percentage point to 4.2 per cent, while retaining its 2027 forecast at 4.3 per cent. The projections were presented in the IMF’s 2026 World Economic Outlook, titled “Resilience Under Strain, Urgent Choices,” released at the ongoing Annual Meetings in Bangkok, Thailand. Speaking on fiscal policy responses to rising living costs in Africa, Research Department Division Chief, Deniz Igan, said policymakers needed to address immediate household needs, particularly food and energy security, while maintaining medium-term economic stability. “The thing to emphasise here is that what we are advocating for is for policymakers to balance the near-term needs of the population, and that involves food security. That involves energy security. Given that the prices of food and energy are increasing disproportionately, while also keeping in mind medium-term stability, how to do that is, of course, a great question,” she said. More details shortly…

title: WHO warns of outbreaks in Western Pacific due to gaps in vaccine programmes
body: MANILA, 12 OCTOBER 2026 (PACIFIC ISLAND TIMES) —Nearly 1.7 million babies or about one in every 11 born in the Western Pacific missed the first routine vaccine dose in 2025, the World Health Organisation said, warning of the risks of otherwise eliminated diseases resurging in the region. WHO noted that coverage with three doses of vaccine against diphtheria, tetanus and pertussis declined from 94 percent in 2019 to 89 percent in 2025. “Behind every outbreak is a gap: a missed child, delayed action, weakened trust, or communities not reached through regular vaccination programmnes,” said Dr Saia Ma’u Piukala, WHO regional director for the Western Pacific. Health leaders noted that measles is one of the most contagious diseases that expose weaknesses in immunisation systems. “In an interconnected region, an immunity gap in one place can become a risk elsewhere,” WHO said. WHO reported last year that the measles cases in the Western Pacific rose by 743 percent from 2022 to 2024. Imported measles cases linked to international travel in the region have been reported by Australia, Hong Kong, Japan, New Zealand, South Korea and Singapore. WHO said nine countries in the region are working toward measles elimination by 2030. “But elimination cannot be sustained through catch-up campaigns alone,” the organisation said. “It depends on health workers reaching communities, reliable vaccine supplies, strong surveillance and laboratories, good data and community trust.” For the Western Pacific, WHO said the next chapter of immunization is about protecting what countries have already achieved, reaching those still being missed, and ensuring the benefits of vaccination reach every generation. Health representatives from the Western Pacific will meet in Manila for the 77th session of the WHO Regional Committee for the Western Pacific from 19 – 22 October to discuss accelerating advancement of immunisation in the region. The summit will tackle a proposed regional plan through 2030, focusing on three connected priorities: reducing zero-dose and under-immunised populations; achieving and sustaining measles elimination; and advancing immunisation across the life course. The plan also emphasises sustainable national financing and ownership, investment in the systems needed to deliver vaccines reliably and greater cooperation between countries……PACNEWS The post WHO warns of outbreaks in Western Pacific due to gaps in vaccine programmes appeared first on Island Times News .

title: North Korea tests technically upgraded ballistic missile component — news agency
body:
PYONGYANG, October 13. /TASS/. North Korea’s Missile Administration conducted a test launch of a tactical ballistic missile to verify a technically upgraded key component, the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) reported.
"The technical upgrade of the key component, confirmed today, is a major success," the DPRK Missile Administration stated.
According to KCNA, the modernization is expected to lead to significant improvements in the power and accuracy of North Korea’s offensive weapons systems. The agency did not specify which component of the missile was upgraded.
The test took place on October 12 as part of regular work by the DPRK Missile Administration and its subordinate research institutes aimed at improving weapons systems.

title: Delta aircraft isolated at Ben Gurion Airport over bomb threat: reports
body: October 13, 2026, 11:09 (UTC +3) Delta confirms incident at Ben Gurion In a statement, Delta told AeroTime: “Nothing is more important than the safety of our customers and crews. Out of an abundance of caution, Delta Flight 234 JFK-TLV was deplaned upon landing and inspected by local authorities to evaluate a potential security issue. No credible threat was found, and customers and crew were transported safely to the terminal. The airline added: “We are grateful for the Delta team’s professionalism, and we apologize to our customers for any inconvenience.” A Delta Air Lines aircraft was isolated at Tel Aviv’s Ben Gurion Airport (TLV) due to a bomb threat, according to Israeli media. On October 13, 2026, The Jerusalem Post reported that a Delta flight from New York was taken to a remote runway following an anonymous report of a “suspicious” device on board. The Delta Airbus A330neo, registered N423DX, was inspected by airport officials who concluded there were no “unusual findings”. “The aircraft was thoroughly inspected by Ben Gurion Airport security personnel,” an Israel Airports Authority spokesperson told The Times of Israel . “Operations have returned to normal.” Dmitriy Feldman svarshik / Shutterstock.com The flight left New York John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK) on October 12, 2026, at 15:55, and arrived in Tel Aviv shortly after 08:25. This latest incident comes just under two weeks after a flydubai pilot attacked his captain on a flight to Israel and is suspected of attempting to crash the aircraft . The Boeing 737 MAX 8 operating from Dubai to Tel Aviv diverted to Saudi Arabia on September 30, 2026, after transmitting emergency transponder codes, including one used to indicate unlawful interference with an aircraft. The first officer attacked the captain with an axe located in the cockpit for emergency use. Despite being stabbed, the captain managed to open the cockpit door which allowed passengers to gain entry to the flight deck and restrain the attacker. AeroTime has contacted Delta Air Lines for more information on the suspicious device incident. title: Tinubu’s Achievements: Delta Deputy Gov, Diaspora Nigerians Disagree in Atlanta
body: Michael Olugbode in Abuja Delta State Deputy Governor, Sir Monday Onyeme, has clashed with Nigerian community leaders in Atlanta, United States, over President Bola Tinubu’s performance, with the deputy governor defending the administration’s economic reforms and infrastructure projects while his audience challenged their impact on ordinary Nigerians. The disagreement, which occurred during Onyeme’s recent working visit to Georgia, exposed a sharp divide over whether the federal government’s policies are delivering the promised transformation or worsening the economic hardship confronting millions of citizens. While Onyeme described Tinubu as a once-in-a-generation leader whose decisions were repositioning Nigeria for sustainable growth, some members of the audience cited the high cost of living, persistent insecurity, deteriorating highways and alleged irregularities in public procurement as evidence that the administration had fallen short of expectations. The exchanges became particularly pointed when community leaders Raymond Ekuerhare and Chief Emeka Chimekwene rejected the deputy governor’s glowing assessment, insisting that Nigerians abroad were not relying on social media alone to evaluate developments at home. Onyeme had accused Nigerians of using social media to spread misinformation, disinformation and half-truths about the achievements of Tinubu’s administration and the government of Delta State Governor, Sheriff Oborevwori. He argued that such narratives were damaging Nigeria’s international image and preventing citizens abroad from appreciating what he described as the transformative impact of the President’s eight-point Renewed Hope Agenda. “I have been around for a while, both as a private citizen and now in government. There is no Nigerian leader that even comes close to President Tinubu in terms of achievement, in making tough choices that will set the country apart, now and in the near future,” he said. The deputy governor, who identified himself as a professional accountant, maintained that the administration’s policies were laying the foundation for long-term economic stability, improved governance and accelerated development. But Ekuerhare, a business and community leader, who said he travelled to Nigeria almost every other month, disputed that assessment, pointing to the gap between government claims and the realities confronting citizens. He specifically cited the condition of the Benin-Asaba, Ore-Benin, Benin-Warri and Warri-Ughelli-Bomadi roads, arguing that the state of the highways undermined claims of impressive infrastructure development. “The eight-point Renewed Hope Agenda is only good on paper but not affecting people’s lives for good,” he said. Ekuerhare also questioned the administration’s record on security, arguing that insecurity and kidnappings continued to undermine the freedom of movement and economic activities of Nigerians. Chimekwene, another Delta State community leader in Atlanta, raised concerns over public procurement, particularly contracts he alleged had been awarded without competitive bidding to the Chagoury Group. He argued that allegations of non-competitive contract awards raised questions about transparency and accountability, insisting that a government seeking to transform the country must demonstrate that public resources are being managed responsibly. “We don’t depend on social media for serious matters of the state. We have family members at home; their lives and living conditions have not improved under President Tinubu,” he said. Chimekwene also challenged Onyeme’s economic assessment, arguing that the hardship experienced by households made it difficult to describe the administration’s record as transformational. He, however, expressed greater confidence in Onyeme’s account of the impact of Governor Oborevwori’s MORE Agenda in Delta State, saying members of the Diaspora could more readily verify some of the state government’s projects during visits home. Responding to the criticisms, Onyeme insisted that the federal government’s policies had created the conditions enabling state and local governments to pursue development programmes more effectively. He placed particular emphasis on local government autonomy, describing the Supreme Court’s July 2024 judgment on the financial independence of local councils as a landmark step towards strengthening grassroots governance and advancing true federalism. The judgment followed the Federal Government’s legal action seeking to protect local governments’ constitutional rights, including their access to funds without unlawful interference by state governments. Onyeme said successive administrations had failed to fully realise local government autonomy despite reforms introduced in 1976 under the military administration of General Murtala Muhammed and continued under General Olusegun Obasanjo. He argued that the Tinubu administration had placed the issue at the centre of governance, enabling the country’s 774 local government areas to take greater responsibility for services directly affecting citizens. According to him, local councils are now better positioned to undertake projects in road construction, primary healthcare, community education, sanitation, waste management and local security. He also defended the removal of the petrol subsidy, foreign exchange reforms, tax changes and electricity sector reforms, arguing that the measures were designed to eliminate structural weaknesses, improve government revenue and create a more sustainable economic environment. The deputy governor maintained that the reforms were beginning to produce results, pointing to economic growth in 2025 and 2026, increased emphasis on non-oil activities and improved investor confidence. However, he acknowledged that the policies had imposed difficulties on households, insisting that the sacrifices would eventually yield long-term benefits. Infrastructure development became another major point of contention, with Onyeme citing the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, the Sokoto-Badagry Superhighway, the Abuja-Kaduna-Zaria-Kano dual carriageway and the proposed Akwanga-Bauchi-Gombe-Biu-Maiduguri Superhighway as evidence of the administration’s development ambitions. The projects are intended to improve connectivity, facilitate trade and strengthen economic links between different parts of the country. But Chimekwene challenged the presentation of the projects as major achievements, arguing that many remained at relatively early stages of completion. Onyeme acknowledged concerns over the pace of construction, attributing delays in some cases to the technology being deployed for road development. He nevertheless maintained that the projects represented an important investment in Nigeria’s long-term transport infrastructure. The disagreement in Atlanta comes against the backdrop of far-reaching economic changes introduced by Tinubu since assuming office in May 2023. The removal of the petrol subsidy and the unification of the foreign exchange market were among the administration’s earliest major policy decisions, intended to reduce fiscal pressures, improve market efficiency and attract investment. However, the reforms also contributed to immediate cost pressures, particularly through higher transport and production expenses, while the depreciation of the naira and increases in food prices intensified concerns about household purchasing power. The administration has subsequently pursued tax reforms, investment initiatives and infrastructure projects as part of its broader economic agenda. Yet the extent to which the resulting growth and government revenue gains translate into better living conditions remains central to the debate over its performance. Insecurity, including kidnapping and attacks in parts of the country, has also continued to feature prominently in public criticism of government performance. Against this background, the Atlanta encounter illustrated the difficulty of reconciling the government’s emphasis on macroeconomic reforms and long-term infrastructure investment with citizens’ demands for immediate relief, safer communities and functioning public infrastructure. Onyeme urged Nigerians in the Diaspora to help correct what he considered misleading narratives about the country and to project Nigeria positively through their words and actions. The meeting was hosted by Chief Collins Odinjor and his wife, Alero, with support from Mr Kingsley Dike and his wife, Tilda, and Mr Frederick Ogodo and his wife, Henrietta. Others present included former Super Eagles coach Samson Siasia and his wife, Eunice; Professor Nuru Akinyemi of Kennesaw State University; Dr Dave Ogwu; Mr Felix Ochei; Pastor Orlando Scott; Attorney Ani Alumona Oluku; Mr Henry Nketeh; Ekuerhare; Chimekwene; Mr Ken Eze; and Mrs Ndidi Ogwu, who moderated the question-and-answer session.

title: Houthis threaten 'swift, painful' response if US assists Saudi strikes in Yemen
body: A Saudi-led coalition spokesperson said on Tuesday that a warning would be issued shortly for civilians to evacuate a site in Yemen's Sanaa ahead of a special operation.On Monday, the Iran-backed Houthis threatened to launch a "swift and painful response" against the US and its regional interests if Washington joined Saudi Arabia's military campaign in Yemen, Houthi political bureau member Mohammed al-Bukhaiti told AFP. "If the US becomes involved in the aggression against Yemen, we will not deliberate over the decision to respond; rather, there will be a swift and painful response targeting the US and all its interests in the region," Bukhaiti said.His warning came following US President Donald Trump's comments weighing American involvement following the recent deadly attacks on Saudi infrastructure, including a strike on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh on Saturday that killed 13 people and wounded hundreds more. The attack was the deadliest on Saudi soil in more than a decade.Trump said the airport attack was "not acceptable" and indicated that Washington was considering joining Saudi strikes against the Houthis, after reportedly rejecting earlier requests for military assistance from Riyadh."The Houthis are misbehaving very badly. They're misbehaving very badly. No good," Trump said on Monday.Bukhaiti warned, "all employees and workers at Saudi oil facilities and airports to stay away from these sites, as they have become legitimate targets."He said the Houthi campaign was intended to demonstrate to the crown prince "that he can no longer wage aggression against Yemen from a safe position".Saudi capital's airport to remain shut this week as airlines cancel servicesAuthorities also extended the closure of Riyadh's international airport until Saturday and suspended operations at King Khalid International Airport to "allow for the completion of procedures to ensure the safety and operational readiness of the airport's facilities," the Saudi civil aviation authority said in a statement.Late on Monday, the Houthis said they had attacked the airport with a ballistic missile, shortly after Saudi Arabia said it had intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile fired by the group towards Riyadh.The Houthis also said in a statement that they targeted an airbase in Khamis Mushait in the kingdom's southwest with a drone. There was no immediate Saudi confirmation.A Notice to Airmen issued on Monday showed King Khalid International Airport will stay closed until October 17.The attacks have also raised worries over civil aviation becoming a target in armed conflict."This level of sustained intense attack on civil aviation is unprecedented," said Mark Zee, founder of OPSGROUP, a membership-based organization that provides aviation safety advice."I think this requires us to rethink how we view the current risk picture, and tread very carefully," he said.Air traffic radar showed flights avoiding Riyadh despite still flying over Saudi airspaceAir traffic tracker Flightradar24 showed planes avoiding the city on Monday, though jets crossed Saudi airspace and landed at the country's top hub, Jeddah, on the west coast.Cancellations across all Saudi airports reached 46.4%, Cirium, an aviation analytics firm, said.

title: DOE: Visayas may face more red alerts in 2027 without sufficient backup systems
body: CEBU, Philippines – Energy Secretary Sharon Garin said on Monday, October 12, that the Visayas could face more red alerts in 2027 if the government is unable to secure ancillary services procurement agreements (ASPAs) for 250 megawatts of power reserves. For months, major coal-fired power plants in Visayas have been on forced and unplanned outages due to operational damage, system failures, and the region’s growing energy demand. “We overwork our coal power plants. Imbes na magmaintenance siya or dapat hindi siya 100%, talagang sinasagad natin kasi kulang ang supply (Instead of doing maintenance or it not operating at 100%, we’re really overworking it because the supply is lacking),” Garin said in an interview during a summit convening energy experts and officials in Cebu. Data from the Department of Energy (DOE) as of April 30 showed that Visayas’ coal plants contribute at least 1,233 megawatts of dependable energy capacity of the existing 3,449 megawatts of dependable capacity in the region — a third of the region’s dependable power mix is coal-based. In 2025, system peak demand in the Visayas had grown to 2,691 megawatts from 2,201 megawatts in 2020, according to DOE data. This presents a huge problem to power plants as they are forced to work overtime to meet the demand, exposing plants to high-stress and early deterioration. To address this, Garin said that the Visayas should have its own set of ancillary services, particularly battery energy storage systems (BESS), to offset the lack of supply and keep plants operating at a stable capacity. “The batteries will work more like a stabilizer para kung kailan kulang ang supply, tapos malaki ang demand, siya ang mag-susupply (so when there is a lack of supply, and the demand is great, this will be the one to supply),” Garin added. Batteries and barges As early as May 22, the DOE directed the National Grid Corporation of the Philippines (NGCP) to execute ASPAs for at least 250 megawatts of Visayas reserves. On October 5, the DOE called out the NGCP for failing to file the required ASPAs. “The Visayas needed these reserves on the grid months ago. What was missing was timely execution. Delays in contracting left consumers with less protection when generating units unexpectedly went offline,” Garin said in the DOE’s October 5 press release. As a system operator, it is the NGCP’s responsibility to balance the supply and demand of power to maintain the quality of electricity that flows through the grid. Without the ASPAs, the DOE reported that red alerts could occur for at least 22 of the 52 weeks in 2027, around February to November. With the ASPAs, the number of weeks with red alerts could drop to only four weeks. At present, the Visayas grid has 134 megawatts of dependable capacity from its BESS. Garin shared, in a presentation on the Visayas energy road map during the Cebu summit, that they are expecting to put up at least 250 megawatts of BESS and deploy power barges — power plants installed on a barge — between 2026 and 2027. But the reserves are only for the short term. In the long term, the DOE is hoping to increase the region’s energy supply with new base load plants that provide steady power. This, Garin said, would come in the form of coal, nuclear, diesel, and geothermal energy sources. By 2028, the DOE expects 150 megawatts in baseload capacity from an expansion project of Therma Visayas Inc.’s coal-fired power plant in Toledo City. This project is not covered under the country’s moratorium on new coal-power projects. Apart from the additional 150 megawatts, a 220-megawatt gas-based power plant in Cebu, and 470 megawatts from a renewable energy plant in Cebu and Bohol are set to be finished before the end of 2028. Panay Island is also expected to get a 220-megawatt gas-based power plant and a 135-megawatt baseload plant in the same year. “We have a very fragile system but the good thing is we are already working on it to make it less fragile,” Garin said. – Rappler.com

title: CSG takes 9.5% stake in MDA Space, becoming its largest shareholder in space sector push
body: The companies could explore joint investment in manufacturing or assembly facilities in Europe and cooperation on strategic acquisitions. title: IMF projects average oil price at $95.74 per barrel in 2026 and $87.39 in 2027
body:
BANGKOK, October 13. /TASS/. The International Monetary Fund (IMF) forecasts that the average price of a barrel of oil will be $95.74 this year and $87.39 in 2027. This forecast is included in the organization's latest World Economic Outlook report, released in Bangkok, where the governing bodies of the IMF and the World Bank are holding their off-site meetings.
"The average price of oil in US dollars a barrel was $67.74 in 2025; the assumed price, based on futures markets, is $95.74 in 2026 and $87.39 in 2027," the report says.
According to the authors, oil prices are projected to rise by 41.6% this year and fall by 8.7% next year. These figures represent upward revisions of 9.5 and 3.1 percentage points, respectively, compared to the Fund's previous World Economic Outlook report released in July.
Fund experts emphasize that the forecast factors in an expected recovery of shipping in the Strait of Hormuz to pre-war levels between March and October 2027. However, they note that if the war between the US and Iran is not resolved by June 2027, shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and the Bab el-Mandeb Strait would be effectively paralyzed and damage to oil infrastructure would escalate. Consequently, a resumption of oil supplies should not be expected before the end of 2027. In such a scenario, the experts forecast that oil prices could climb to $130 per barrel between the fourth quarter of this year and the first quarter of 2027, returning to baseline scenario levels only by the fourth quarter of next year.
Natural gas prices are estimated by Fund experts to rise by 48% this year compared to 2025 levels. Fertilizer prices are projected to increase by an average of 10% in 2026 compared to the previous year.

title: Stop Dividing South-east for Selfish Political Interests, Ebonyi Group Tackles Umahi
body: Adedayo Akinwale in Abuja The Association of Ebonyi Indigenes Socio-Cultural in the Diaspora (AEISCID) has warned the Minister of Works, David Umahi, to stop dividing the South-east for selfish political interests. The group was reacting to a viral video in which Umahi said Ebonyi leaders were being attacked for refusing to support the presidential candidate of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi in the 2027 presidential election. Umahi had in the video said: “You are calling out people like us because we said we will not vote for him and we tell our people not to vote for him, and you are insulting us,” while challenging Obi to mention any Ebonyi indigene he appointed when he was governor of Anambra State. The minister also waded into Ebonyi State’s 2027 governorship zoning debate, saying: “Just like it’s not the turn of the South East and Peter Obi to be president of Nigeria, it’s not the turn of Ebonyi South to be governor of Ebonyi State.” He added he would meet with the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) candidate, Ifeanyi Odii, to ask him to step down. However, the President AEISCID, Paschal Oluchukwu, in a statement issued yesterday described Umahi’s comments as “shameful, uncivil, uncouth and unbecoming” of a former governor and serving minister. The group said Umahi had appointed himself an “unofficial spokesperson” of Ndi Igbo and accused him of attempting to pitch Ebonyi people against Anambra and the rest of the Igbo nation. Oluchukwu noted: “We wish to vehemently condemn these statements as they are shameful, uncivil, uncouth and terribly unbecoming of a leader at the level of Umahi.” The group noted that it was troubled by what it called Umahi’s “senseless and relentless attacks” on Obi and other Igbo politicians for exercising their constitutional right to contest elections. The Diaspora body also accused Umahi of hypocrisy on the zoning principle, recalling that he refused to step down in 2015 when his predecessor, Martin Elechi, anointed Prof. Onyebuchi Chukwu from the same Ebonyi South zone. According to the group, Umahi’s current zoning advocacy is a ploy to perpetuate his political influence in Ebonyi through Governor Francis Nwifuru, whom it described as his puppet. It alleged that Umahi single-handedly nominated his son, Osborn Umahi, as Chairman of Ohaozara LGA and is positioning him for higher offices, including the governorship in 2039. The group urged the PDP governorship candidate, Odii to ignore Umahi’s call to step down and continue to offer alternative ideas to Ebonyians, insisting that “Ebonyi voters, not Umahi, will decide the 2027 election.” It claimed that the Nwifuru administration has recorded no significant development project in nearly four years due to godfatherism. To this end, the group gave Umahi 72 hours to recant his divisive statements and apologise to Obi, Odii, Ebonyi people and Ndigbo at large, or face legal action. The group also urged President Bola Tinubu to call the minister to order, saying his role as a member of the Federal Executive Council should be to preach peace and unity, not incite hate. Elections Campaign ‘ll Be Issue-based, Says APC’s PCC Women Directorate Jonathan Eze The Director of Women Mobilisation of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council (PCC), Dr Betta Edu, yesterday declared that the 2027 presidential campaign would be issue-based, expressing confidence that the achievements of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s administration will provide compelling evidence for his re-election. Edu, who stated that in Abuja, said Nigerian women were increasingly recognising the direction of the Tinubu administration and had intensified grassroots mobilisation across communities, households, and voting constituencies to secure another mandate for the president and sustain the implementation of his policies and development programmes. She maintained that the APC would approach the forthcoming election with a clear message anchored on its record in government, ongoing infrastructure projects, economic reforms, educational opportunities, and initiatives designed to improve the livelihoods of Nigerians. According to her, the party has substantial achievements to present to the electorate and would campaign on policies, programmes, and measurable results rather than empty promises or personality-driven rhetoric. Edu expressed profound gratitude to President Tinubu for his leadership and commitment to the Renewed Hope Agenda, as well as the First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, for her consistent advocacy for women, families, and national development. She also appreciated Vice President Kashim Shettima and his wife, Nana Shettima; the Senate President and his wife; the Speaker of the House of Representatives and his wife; the Director-General of the Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdulaziz Yari; the Secretary of the APC Presidential Campaign Council; and Chairman of the Progressives Governors Forum, Governor Hope Uzodinma; APC governors and other party leaders, governors, stakeholders, and members of the APC leadership for their contributions to strengthen the women’s grassroots mobilisation and advance the administration’s agenda. The APC PCC women mobilisation director also expressed appreciation to the various women’s groups, associations, support organisations, and political structures within the party for their unwavering commitment, solidarity, and continued support for the administration and the party’s mobilisation efforts. She acknowledged the contributions of wives of governors, women leaders, and grassroots organisers whose activities across states, local government areas, and communities have continued to strengthen the APC’s engagement with women and expand its political reach. Edu said their commitment, organisational capacity, and willingness to work collectively would remain indispensable to the party’s preparations for the 2027 general election. According to her, women remain a formidable force in Nigeria’s electoral process, not only because of their numerical strength but also because of their influence within families, community associations, markets, professional bodies and local political structures. She stressed that the APC’s mobilisation strategy would go beyond rallies and public declarations to sustained engagement, political education, and direct communication with voters, as well as election-day voters’ sensitisation and mobilisation. Edu said the objective was to ensure that Nigerians understood the administration’s policies, assessed their impact on their lives, and made informed decisions about the country’s future. The director identified the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND) as one of the significant initiatives through which the Tinubu administration was expanding access to higher education and creating opportunities for young Nigerians to pursue their academic ambitions. She noted that the student loan programme was helping to address financial barriers that could prevent eligible students from accessing or completing tertiary education while offering families additional support in meeting the cost of education. According to her, “NELFUND reflects the administration’s recognition that investment in education is essential to human capital development, economic productivity, and the long-term prosperity of the country.” She said the programme, alongside ongoing infrastructure development, economic reforms, and other sectoral interventions, formed part of the administration’s record that the APC would present to Nigerians during the election campaign. Edu further maintained that the party would communicate these achievements in clear and practical terms, enabling citizens to understand the policies, opportunities, and reforms available to them. She added that the 2027 election would provide an opportunity for Nigerians to evaluate the administration, of which we can proudly say that the president has performed well. “The reforms were demanding, but now is time for prosperity,” she said. For the Women Mobilisation Directorate, she said the immediate priority was to consolidate existing structures, strengthen coordination among women’s groups, and ensure that the party’s message reached voters in both rural and urban communities. She urged APC women to remain united, organised and committed to the party’s objectives, stressing that their collective contributions would be vital to presenting the administration’s achievements to Nigerians and consolidating support ahead of the 2027 general election. The group noted that Umahi failed to deliver his own polling unit and ward for the APC in the 2023 presidential election and lost his senatorial bid even in his Uburu village.

body:

title: Trump may cut off Ukraine’s access to intelligence, Starlink
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 13 (MNA) – US President Donald Trump could cut off Ukraine’s access to US intelligence and Starlink, a media outlet has reported.
US President Donald Trump could cut off Ukraine’s access to US intelligence or pressure Elon Musk to disable SpaceX’s Starlink internet service for Kiev, Politico Europe reported.
According to the report, the recent Russia-US diesel agreements came "in a wretched month for Ukrainians, ahead of a fast-approaching frigid winter." This made Vladimir Zelensky think about "how angry he can actually afford to be."
