title: Control needed over military AI use, SA MP tells international parliamentary body
body:
South African Member of Parliament (MP) Doris Mpapane used her podium turn during a peace and international security discussion, part of the 153rd Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU) assembly, to call for a legally binding international instrument to regulate military use of artificial intelligence (AI).
Mpapane, who chairs the oversight committee on The Presidency, among others, was one of a South African Parliamentary delegation at the 5 to 9 October IPU Assembly in Arusha, Tanzania. The delegation, led by National Assembly (NA) Speaker Thoko Didiza, also included the National Council of Provinces (NCOP) public representative who chairs the Select Committee on Security and Justice (SCSJ) Jane Mananiso.
Speaking on behalf of the South African delegation, Mpapane is reported as calling for clear safeguards to ensure AI-enabled systems do not operate beyond meaningful human control, according to Parliamentary Communication Services (PCS). She told the IPU Standing Committee on Peace and International Security rapidly advancing AI technologies operating without proper human oversight constitute significant risks to civilians, adding ongoing conflicts showed the need for governance and accountability to keep pace with technological developments.
“Parliamentarians must strengthen their understanding of the legal, ethical and policy implications of artificial intelligence. We must actively contribute to shaping the norms, safeguards and governance frameworks that will guide its military use,” she is on record as saying with the rider that parliaments should assist with transparency, accountability and meet international law requirements by scrutinising procurement, development and deployment of AI-enabled military systems.
Mpapane had it further a multilateral, inclusive approach to developing international rules for the military application of AI is needed. “All countries, regardless of their technological capacities, have a stake in shaping the rules that will govern the military application of artificial intelligence and its implications for international peace and security.”
On another aspect of military operations – maritime security – Mpapane told the IPU committee tasked with peace and security that oversight of secure shipping lanes, undersea cables, ports and energy infrastructure are vital to economic stability.
Referring to recent developments in the Strait of Hormuz, which showed how increased use of military force, rather than dialogue, to resolve disputes could heighten instability, she said the consequences extend beyond the immediate conflict.
“South Africa is not distant from these consequences. Our position on the Cape [sea] route makes us part of the global maritime system. We face our own infrastructure threats. These include cyberattacks, sabotage by organised criminal networks, undersea cable vulnerabilities, illegal fishing, illicit exploitation of natural resources and extreme weather linked to climate change. These threats already affect our national security and economic stability,” she is reported as saying.
Mpapane identified three areas where parliaments can strengthen maritime and critical infrastructure security. They are keeping legal and regulatory frameworks responsive to evolving threats; using budgetary oversight to ensure sustained investment in surveillance, cybersecurity and emergency response capabilities; and strengthening parliamentary diplomacy to promote dialogue and de-escalation.
In closing she noted: “War has never provided a lasting resolution to disputes. It disrupts trade, raises costs, undermines economic stability and places the greatest burden on ordinary people”.

title: FACTBOX: Damaged school in Kaluga Region, 604 UAVs, aftermath of attacks on Russia
body:
MOSCOW, October 13. /TASS/. Air defense systems intercepted and destroyed 604 Ukrainian drones over Russian regions overnight, Russia’s Defense Ministry reported.
A Ukrainian drone attack damaged a school, two private houses and a car in the Mosalsky District of Russia’s central Kaluga Region.
Damage from falling drone debris was recorded in the city of Nevinnomyssk in Russia’s North Caucasus Stavropol Region.
TASS has compiled key details about the aftermath.
- On-duty air defense systems intercepted and destroyed 604 Ukrainian fixed-wing unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) over Russian regions between 8:00 p.m. Moscow time (5:00 p.m. GMT) on October 12 and 8:00 a.m. Moscow time (5:00 a.m. GMT) on October 13, the Defense Ministry reported.
- According to the ministry, drones were downed over the Bryansk, Belgorod, Oryol, Kaluga, Tula, Kursk, Voronezh, Tver, Lipetsk, Ryazan, Rostov, Smolensk, Moscow, Stavropol and Krasnodar Regions and the waters of the Sea of Azov.
- Last night’s drone attack on Moscow was one of the largest since the beginning of the year, according to TASS calculations based on data posted by Mayor Sergey Sobyanin on his Max channel.
- According to the mayor, a total of 417 UAVs were heading toward Moscow between 8:30 p.m. Moscow time (5:30 p.m. GMT) on October 12 and 7:00 a.m. Moscow time (4:00 a.m. GMT) on October 13.
- Air defenses intercepted most of the drones on the distant approaches, while 65 UAVs were brought down while approaching Moscow, Sobyanin said.
- Air defense forces shot down 73 Ukrainian UAVs over the Kaluga Region, Governor Vladislav Shapsha reported on his Max channel.
- According to the governor, drones were intercepted over the Babyninsky, Baryatinsky, Borovsky, Dzerzhinsky, Zhizdrinsky, Zhukovsky, Iznoskovsky, Kozelsky, Maloyaroslavetsky, Medynsky, Mosalsky, Peremyshlsky, Sukhinichsky, Khvastovichsky, Ferzikovsky and Yukhnovsky municipal districts and the outskirts of the cities of Kaluga and Obninsk.
- As many as 14 Ukrainian drones were destroyed over the Tula Region overnight, Governor Dmitry Milyayev said on his Max channel.
- Air defense forces shot down 13 Ukrainian UAVs over the Voronezh Region overnight, Governor Alexander Gusev wrote on his Max channel.
- Air defenses repelled a large-scale aerial attack on the Stavropol Region, Governor Vladimir Vladimirov reported on Max.
- There have been no casualties reported so far.
- Damage from falling UAV debris was recorded in the industrial zone of the city of Nevinnomyssk.
- Inspection of the crash sites and assessment of the damage are underway.
- Emergency services began cleanup operations.
- A school, two private houses and a car were damaged in a drone attack on the Mosalsky District of the Kaluga Region, Governor Vladislav Shapsha said on his Max channel.
- Emergency services are working on site.

title: Ukrainian firms, PDW to test Kurbas cameras on drones
body:
Ukrainian companies The Fourth Law and Odd Systems have announced signing a memorandum of understanding with U.S. defense technology company Performance Drone Works (PDW), under which the integration of Kurbas cameras into PDW drones will be assessed, with the possibility of localizing production in the U.S. later, the companies said.
"Ukraine is showing how fast technology can evolve when engineers and operators work closely together. We aim to combine proven technology with the U.S. engineering and production capacity needed to deploy it at scale," PDW CEO James Slider said, according to the release.
The Fourth Law and Odd Systems said in a joint release that the document was signed at the annual AUSA exhibition in Washington.
Under the agreement, the companies plan to assess the integration of cameras developed by Odd Systems, as well as technical specifications and requirements for further production in the U.S. In particular, PDW will become a manufacturing and industrialization partner for The Fourth Law and Odd Systems in the U.S.
Among other things, the companies also intend to set up production of thermal sensors in the U.S. under the newly created Project Foundation initiative, headed by Ihor Nakonechny.
"Kurbas cameras were created and tested at the front. Together with PDW we can bring this technology to American platforms and, through Project Foundation, build a thermal sensor supply chain directly in the United States," The Fourth Law CEO and Odd Systems co-founder Yaroslav Azhniuk said in the release.
The release also said PDW is building capacity to integrate selected partner technologies and produce components for its platforms, and over time for the entire industry of unmanned systems in the U.S. and allied countries.
Performance Drone Works is a U.S. defense technology company specializing in the development of multipurpose aerial robotic systems, as well as software, communications, training systems and production capacity. It is headquartered in Huntsville, Alabama.
The Fourth Law and Odd Systems were founded in Kyiv in 2023 by entrepreneur Yaroslav Azhniuk. They operate in Ukraine, elsewhere in Europe and in the U.S.
The Fourth Law specializes in developing scalable autonomy for robotic systems, with a primary focus on defense.
Odd Systems develops and makes thermal and daytime cameras for drones and other robotic systems.
Last week The Fourth Law and Odd Systems announced the launch of a joint project, Project Foundation, to produce uncooled thermal sensors in Europe and the U.S.

title: Trump stands by Russia diesel plan despite backlash: 'I made the right choice'
body:
A group of senators, including some Republicans, pushed back on the agreement.
President Donald Trump doubled down Monday on his decision to allow Russian diesel imports amid growing backlash, calling it the "right choice" and arguing that Europe has previously purchased energy products from Russia as well.
Trump said in a Monday morning social media post that the "European Union paid Russia 250 Billion Dollars for Energy" and added, "I made the right choice for the American People — ALWAYS, AMERICA FIRST!"
Trump did not specify the period covered by $250 billion figure. Estimates from the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air tracking how much the EU has spent importing fossil fuels from Russia since the start of war with Ukraine roughly align with the figure Trump mentioned.
Trump's comments come after a small group of bipartisan senators came out against the Trump administration's plan to lift Russian oil sanctions and import a new supply amid spiking prices in the U.S. The senators, in a statement on Sunday, urged the administration to reverse its decision due to the ongoing war with Ukraine and ban on Russian energy imports.
"The United States should not provide Putin with a financial lifeline while Russia continues to kill Ukrainian civilians. The Administration must immediately reverse course," the senators wrote in the statement.
Trump announced on Friday that he made a deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin to immediately import 300,000 tons of its diesel fuel, with a promise that millions more are coming.
The statement was signed by Republican Sens. Susan Collins, Thom Tillis, John Curtis and Lisa Murkowski as well as Democratic Sens. Jeanne Shaheen, Richard Blumenthal and Ron Wyden.
The senators also argued the move violates a 2022 law banning Russian energy imports and opens the door to allowing Russia to potentially benefit financially on its war against Ukraine.
"President Trump's decision to allow Russian diesel imports to the U.S. runs directly counter to that law. The Administration has also failed to consult with Congress or submit any explanation to justify its decision as required by statute," the senators wrote in the statement.
In April 2022, Congress passed the Ending Importation of Russian Oil Act, banning imports of Russian energy products. While the law does allow the president to lift the ban under certain conditions, it requires a justification to Congress before doing so, which the senators argue did not happen.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy sharply criticized the decision, too, saying in an interview with ABC News over the weekend that the deal amounts to an "obvious weakness."
"It plays into Russia’s hands -- allowing it to kill more, wage war for longer, have even less respect for America, and inflict even greater losses and damage on the world," he said. "We count on America's fair support for our defense of life, for our defense of people in Ukraine -- and on the United States having a correspondingly strong conversation with Russia. A strong one, not a weak one."
Trump's decision comes weeks after he signed the bipartisan Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act , which authorizes tariffs on countries that continue to purchase Russian oil. Now, some senators, such as Tillis, say Trump's recent action runs counter to the efforts in the legislation.
"I completely reject it," Tillis said on NBC’s "Meet The Press" on Sunday. "If President Trump wants to end the strain of energy supplies, number one, get things right in Iran, and number two, recognize that it was Vladimir Putin, not Zelenskyy, that started this war. And it's Vladimir Putin who owns the responsibility for energy prices to the extent that they come from that part of the world."
Tillis said the agreement to purchase Russian diesel is "essentially, I think, tarnishing Lindsey Graham's efforts to try and get those sanctions bill through."
However, other Republicans are continuing to stand by Trump, including House Majority Whip Tom Emmer, who is a vocal supporter of Ukraine and previously voted to establish sanctions on Russia.
Emmer told ABC News' "This Week" co-anchor Jon Karl on Sunday that the deal was "another example of our president thinking out of the box" to address the American public's concerns about high oil and gas prices by importing fuel to the U.S. ahead of the midterm elections.
"He's listening to the American people, Jon. The American people are hurting because of this world market when it comes to diesel and fuel in general,” Emmer said.
Emmer also hailed the deal as another tactic in Trump's attempt to broker a peace deal between Russia and Ukraine.
"I think this is just another step of trying to get that resolved," he said.

title: Araghchi says aggressors must be held accountable
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 13 (MNA) – Iran's foreign minister said holding enemies of the country accountable for military aggression and environmental damage is an undeniable necessity, adding that Iran neither forgives nor forgets.
Iranian Foreign Minister Seyyed Abbas Araghchi said in a social media post that protecting the environment against military aggression and holding the enemies of this land accountable is an undeniable necessity, adding: "We neither forgive nor forget."
He recalled remarks he made on Sunday at the first International ECOCIDE Conference at the Department of Environment, where he said environmental destruction during war is a silent crime with consequences that extend beyond the battlefield.
Araghchi said military attacks by the United States and the Zionist regime against Iran and the targeting of the country's oil and energy facilities have created serious environmental hazards. He warned these could threaten human health, natural resources, and the right of future generations to a healthy environment.

title: Liquidity crunch freezes UAH 18 bln VAT refunds - minister
body:
The government has run into a state budget liquidity crisis in October, so only defense spending, pensions, wages and social benefits are being financed, while other spending has been prioritized or suspended until the single treasury account is restored, Finance Minister Serhiy Marchenko said in parliament on Monday.
"... about UAH 39 billion has been pushed back to the end of the year. In addition, as of today, UAH 46 billion is sitting unprocessed in the treasury on the single account, including road repairs, maintenance and development of administrative centers, repairs of penal institutions, purchases of school buses, current and capital repairs of housing and preparations for the heating season, and purchases of backup power," the head of the Finance Ministry said.
He said budget refunds of value-added tax to taxpayers, totaling UAH 18 billion, have also been suspended.
Marchenko said the government is actively looking for domestic resources and has stepped up the work of a working group on de-shadowing the economy. "Its work will produce proposals on avoiding the artificial splitting of businesses, countering illegal production and sale of tobacco products, de-shadowing the labor market, misuse of humanitarian aid and other issues," the minister said.
He said the Finance Ministry has also significantly stepped up borrowing on the domestic market.
"We have practically fulfilled the annual borrowing plan, but we are increasing borrowing so as to have enough liquidity, first of all to make social payments and payments for the security and defense sector," Marchenko said.
At the same time, according to the ministry's website, the offering of domestic government bonds at primary auctions on October 13 has again been cut, to UAH 2 billion from UAH 5 billion last Tuesday, when the ministry managed to sell UAH 2.2 billion of bonds.

title: Yei registers 748 epilepsy cases, 448 mental health cases
body: Health authorities in Yei River County in Central Equatoria State have recorded 748 epilepsy cases and 448 mental health cases since the beginning of 2026, with hundreds of patients still receiving treatment. The county announced the figures on Monday, October 12, during its commemoration of World Mental Health Day, held under the theme “Lived Experiences Heard: Real Voices, Real Change.” According to county health authorities, 25 epilepsy patients have recovered, while 723 remain under treatment. Of the 448 mental health cases recorded, 40 patients have recovered, while 408 continue to receive care. Speaking during the event, County Health Director Simon Sebit attributed the rising mental health burden to depression and called for appropriate interventions, including counselling and medical treatment. He further appealed to health partners to ensure a continued supply of medicines for epilepsy and mental health patients. “There are many people who ran mad or mentally ill here in Yei, and that is what we call depression because the mind is not thinking straight,” he said. “However, with treatment, the person can come back and think straight. Tramadol and smoking marijuana can bring such disorder in the brain. If you see anyone in such a situation, bring them to the hospital for treatment.” Gaga Frank, a youth leader, called for sustained public awareness to combat stigma and encourage people experiencing mental health challenges to speak openly about their experiences. “We must end stigma in our communities and families at different levels, encourage open conversations and create safe spaces where young people can express their feelings without fear or discrimination or judgment,” he said. “I call upon schools, churches, government institutions, health workers and development partners to work together to promote mental health awareness and ensure that those who need support can access it.” For her part, Christine Siama, a mental health survivor, commended health workers in Yei for supporting her recovery. “I was treated in Juba, but there was no doctor who could heal me, but I finally got healed here. They say our place, Yei, is small and insecure, but thankfully I received my treatment here in Yei,” she said. “I have suffered a lot there in Juba, running up and down in between cars and motorcycles, but thank God that I am now okay.” Another survivor, Agness Kaku, described her recovery journey as challenging and highlighted difficulties in accessing essential medicines. “I am one of the people who recovered from mental illness, but it is not easy considering what I went through,” she stated. “To those who are supplying the drugs, we have difficulties in accessing drugs consistently, and a mentally unwell person will think negatively about their illness and have no hope.” Meanwhile, Agnes Nyoka, representing the South Sudan Health Association (SSUHA), urged communities and health partners to take collective responsibility in addressing mental health challenges, including tackling gang-related activities. “Let us come together and make sure we kick out mental health issues. Let us take patients to the hospital, and the health department will determine whether they need drugs or psycho-social counselling,” she said. “Narcotic drugs are the problem, and our children have joined gangs and even raped girls. We say the children are spoilt and give up and fail to talk to them. Let us work to heal them so that they become productive.” The World Health Organization (WHO) estimates that one in five people in South Sudan is likely to experience a mental health condition due to ongoing conflict and dire humanitarian situations. The commemoration was organised in collaboration with the World Health Organization, the Ministry of Health and local partners to promote awareness, challenge stigma and amplify the voices of people living with mental health conditions. The post Yei registers 748 epilepsy cases, 448 mental health cases appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

title: Russia Reportedly Strikes Dnipro With Guided Bombs, Wounding 64-Year-Old Man
body:
Russian forces reportedly attacked Dnipro with guided aerial bombs (KABs) on the morning of Tuesday, Oct. 13, damaging apartment buildings, vehicles, and transport infrastructure and injuring a 64-year-old man.
Mykola Lukashuk, head of the Dnipropetrovsk Regional Council, said the city had been targeted with guided aerial bombs in a Telegram post published at 7:30 a.m.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
“A loud morning. The enemy attacked Dnipro with guided aerial bombs. A man was injured. Apartment buildings, transport infrastructure, and vehicles were damaged,” Lukashuk wrote.
Oleksandr Hanzha, head of the Dnipropetrovsk Regional Military Administration (OVA), said the injured man was 64. Medics provided him with the necessary care, but he declined hospitalization.
The type of weapon used in the attack has not been independently confirmed. If the use of guided aerial bombs is verified, the strike could mark a new escalation in Russian attacks on Dnipro.
Reports of a Russian guided aerial bomb attack on Dnipro also emerged in early October last year. However, the weapon was later identified as a Hrom-1 missile, which had reached the city for the first time.
The Hrom-1 is a missile-bomb system that can be used as either a missile or a glide bomb. The two versions differ in their warheads and range: the missile carries a 315-kilogram warhead and has a range of up to 120 kilometers, while the bomb variant carries a 480-kilogram warhead and can travel up to 65 kilometers.
“The difference is due to the fact that the missile has a jet engine, while the bomb does not,” Ukrainian outlet NV reported.
In the morning on Oct. 12, Russian forces also attacked the city of Dnipro and the surrounding Dniprovskyi district. One person was killed in the city , while a fire broke out at a shopping center in the region’s suburbs.
In the early hours of Oct. 11, 2026, Russians attacked Dnipro with drones, damaging a high-rise building and setting warehouses ablaze. Several people were also injured.
On Oct. 10, Russia attacked the city three times throughout the day. The third strike sparked fires at food warehouses.

title: Trump may cut off Ukraine’s access to intelligence, Starlink — media
body:
BRUSSELS, October 13. /TASS/. US President Donald Trump could cut off Ukraine’s access to US intelligence or pressure Elon Musk to disable SpaceX’s Starlink internet service for Kiev, Politico Europe reported.
According to the report, the recent Russia-US diesel agreements came "in a wretched month for Ukrainians, ahead of a fast-approaching frigid winter." This made Vladimir Zelensky think about "how angry he can actually afford to be." Politico noted that Zelensky "risks provoking Trump into cutting off vital US intelligence support or pressuring Elon Musk to disable SpaceX’s Starlink internet service, on which Ukraine’s military heavily relies."
Russian President Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump held a phone call on October 9, particularly discussing petroleum product supplies. The Russian leader said that Moscow had reiterated its readiness to supply oil and petroleum products to the United States and global markets. According to Novak, Russia is lifting its ban on diesel exports ahead of schedule and is ready to supply 300,000 tons of diesel in October, increasing the volume to 500,000 tons in November and 1 million tons in December. Monthly supplies could subsequently reach 3 million tons. The US administration, in turn, issued a general license authorizing Russian diesel supplies to the global market until April 7, 2027.

title: Elazar Yair Wilensky, 14, identified as victim of Hezbollah ordnance explosion in northern Israel
body: Elazar Yair Wilensky, 14, was identified as the student killed on Monday when an unexploded munition detonated during a school trip in the Ramim Ridge area of northern Israel, near the Lebanese border.Wilensky, the youngest of five siblings, was described by his family as “a boy who loved life. Smart and intelligent, full of joy, a good and beloved friend, whose entire future was still ahead of him.”He is survived by his parents, three sisters, and a brother.The Ma'alot-Tarshiha Municipality said in a statement that Mayor Moti Ben-David and the rest of the city “share in the profound grief of the Wilensky family and extend their condolences at this difficult and painful time.“The Ma'alot-Tarshiha Municipality continues to closely support the families of those affected. At the same time, welfare teams and educational psychological services continue to provide emotional support and assistance to students, families, and educational staff.” The incident occurred when a group of students and teachers from ORT Ma'alot High School's yeshiva program was struck by an explosion involving unexploded ordnance during a hiking trip.Some 24 teachers, children injured in explosion meters from Lebanese borderAccording to the initial reports, 24 teachers and students were wounded in the incident. One person was critically injured and pronounced dead shortly afterward. Two others were seriously injured, 10 sustained moderate wounds, and another 12 were lightly injured. The victims suffered wounds of varying severity, including some that were serious.A medical evacuation helicopter was dispatched to the scene. The IDF declared the incident a mass-casualty event and sent helicopters to the area.The incident occurred near Mitzpor Pa'ar (the Pa'ar lookout), approximately 50 to 100 meters from the Lebanese border.A nearby military outpost had been manned by Combat Engineering Corps soldiers throughout the war, leading Hezbollah to direct heavy fire at the area during the fighting.The assessment is that the explosion was caused by a Hezbollah missile or artillery shell that had landed in the area but failed to detonate at the time.The area is densely vegetated, which is believed to explain why the unexploded munition had not been discovered previously.A preliminary investigation showed evidence that one of the students put the Hezbollah cluster munition into his bag, and it later detonated.

title: Russian strikes hit Ukrainian defense plants, logistics centers, railway infrastructure
body:
MOSCOW, October 13. /TASS/. Russian forces hit military-industrial facilities and logistics centers as well as railway and port infrastructure as a result of last night’s strikes, Russia’s Defense Ministry reported on Tuesday morning.
TASS has compiled the key details about the strikes.
- Last night, the Russian Armed Forces delivered group strikes with precision-guided land-, air-and sea-launched weapons on Ukraine’s military-industrial plants, logistics centers, railway facilities and port infrastructure as well as sea vessels used for transporting military supplies to Ukraine, Russia’s Defense Ministry said.
- According to Russia’s top brass, a Pulp Mill Print workshop housing a production site for missiles and long-range unmanned aerial vehicles was struck in Kiev.
- Also in Kiev, Russian forces struck the Darnitsa locomotive depot for repairs and maintenance of trains used for transporting military and dual-use supplies to Ukrainian battlegroups.
- In addition, the strikes hit a Nova Post logistics center in the settlement of Ternovka in the Nikolayev Region used to store dual-use cargo designated for supplies to the Ukrainian army.
- Russian forces struck a drone depot in Meshkovo-Pogorelovo in the Nikolayev Region during the past night.
- In addition, a bulk carrier type of vessel carrying military and dual-use supplies to the port of Nikolayev was struck in the Bugsky Liman (the Bug Estuary).

title: Dnipro attack wounds man, hits transport, homes - Hanzha
body:
Russian forces attacked Dnipro on Tuesday morning, wounding a local resident and damaging a transport facility and residential buildings, Dnipropetrovsk Regional Military Administration head Oleksandr Hanzha said.

"A 64-year-old man was wounded in the Russian attack on Dnipro. Medics gave him all the necessary help. He declined hospitalization," he said on Telegram.

Enemy strikes on the city damaged a transport infrastructure facility, high-rise residential buildings and cars, he said. Emergency services are working at the impact sites, and the scale of the destruction is being clarified.

title: ‘Yandex Pay’ partially resumes operations after Ukrainian drone strikes on data centers
body: Dmitry Pirogov, the head of Yandex Pay’s fintech division, announced that the company has restored access to transfers and payments for some users. “Many of you can already see your money and manage it. We’re restoring access gradually so the service can handle the load. If some functionality isn’t available to you yet, please wait a little longer,” he wrote in the payment service’s Telegram channel. Pirogov stressed that the service “is still operating unstably”: some functions remain unavailable, and errors are possible during certain operations. Yandex Pay also announced special terms for users from October 11–17, covering savings accounts as well as loan payments. From the start, we built our infrastructure so that data on transactions would be replicated simultaneously across multiple data centers, because we work with literally the most valuable data our users have: data about their money. After the recent drone attacks on our data centers, our engineers had to completely rebuild the infrastructure in order to preserve this key principle and restore access to familiar functions. That’s why our service was hit especially hard, and recovery is taking longer. In recent days, Ukraine has struck three of the six data centers belonging to Yandex: facilities in the Ryazan region, Kaluga, and Vladimir. title: Northrop Grumman Barrett Team Up to Produce 25mm Precision Grenade Launcher
body:
Northrop Grumman and Barrett Firearms have signed a teaming agreement for Barrett to manufacture the weapon component of Northrop Grumman’s Precision Grenadier System (PGS), a shoulder-fired, semi-automatic 25mm grenade launcher.
Production will take place at Barrett’s Nashville, Tennessee, facility, where the company will also integrate an inductive setter that allows operators to program compatible Northrop Grumman ammunition.
Weighing just under 12 pounds (5.4 kg), the PGS features a five-round magazine and is designed to help infantry squads engage targets in defilade (protected from direct observation or fire), close-quarters combat and small unmanned aircraft systems (sUAS).
Northrop Grumman has developed four 25mm rounds, leveraging existing ammunition components and automated production lines to improve manufacturing efficiency and reduce programme risk:
The ammunition suite is intended to provide infantry with versatile engagement options against concealed targets, close-range threats and small aerial systems.
The agreement combines Northrop Grumman’s medium-calibre ammunition development and manufacturing expertise with Barrett’s commercial and military weapons production capabilities.

title: Wealth Over Water: How Galamsey Is Threatening Ghana’s Water Security
body: Ghana is Africa’s top gold producer. But as the country digs deeper for gold, it is confronting a different and potentially more consequential scarcity: clean water. A new visual analysis by researcher and data visualisation analyst Fatah Maltaba Abass , titled Wealth Over Water: A Visual Analysis of Water Security and Environmental Governance Impacts of Illegal Gold Mining in Ghana , brings together data from the Water Resources Commission (WRC), Ghana Water Limited, COCOBOD, the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), Pure Earth, the World Gold Council and peer-reviewed studies. The analysis maps a growing tension at the heart of Ghana’s resource economy: the country is generating wealth from gold while putting some of the natural resources that support its population, agriculture and industry under increasing pressure. One of the clearest examples is water. Scientists at the CSIR-Water Research Institute reported in August 2026 that about 60% of Ghana’s water bodies are polluted, with illegal mining identified as a major contributor alongside agriculture, industrial activity, household waste and other human activities. The researchers warned that some affected water bodies could be difficult to restore even if the pollution stopped immediately. That distinction matters. Galamsey is not the only source of Ghana’s water pollution — but in several mining-affected basins, its impact is particularly severe. A country moving closer to water stress The pressure is not coming from pollution alone. Ghana’s renewable water availability per person has fallen from about 3,000 cubic metres annually in the 1960s to 1,650 cubic metres today, according to the Ministry of Works, Housing and Water Resources. The figure is below the 1,700 cubic metres per person threshold commonly used to indicate water stress. At the same time, Ghana’s population has grown from roughly seven million people in 1960 to more than 30 million today. The implication is straightforward: there is less renewable water available per person, while demand continues to rise. The Wealth Over Water analysis warns that continued deterioration could eventually push Ghana towards a future where it has to consider importing water. That should be treated as a warning scenario rather than a formal government forecast. When rivers become too dirty to treat The deterioration is visible in Ghana’s river systems. Turbidity — a measure of the amount of suspended material in water — has reached extraordinary levels in some mining-affected rivers. The analysis records readings of 94,800 NTU on the Ayensu, 64,000 NTU on the Birim and up to 32,000 NTU on the Pra. Other affected rivers include the Offin and Ankobra. The figures are not simply an environmental concern. They directly affect the cost and efficiency of producing drinking water. Ghana Water Limited has previously reported that extreme turbidity can force it to lose up to 50% of water during treatment, compared with a normal loss rate of about 5%. More polluted raw water requires more treatment chemicals and can increase operational and maintenance costs. In some cases, the problem becomes severe enough to threaten the continued operation of treatment plants. There have, however, been measurable improvements at some locations following enforcement operations. The analysis records turbidity reductions of 70% to 90% at selected monitoring points, including Densu/Nsawam. The broader picture remains troubling: large sections of the country’s water resources continue to face contamination pressure. The heavy metals behind the concern The problem is not only mud. Research cited in the analysis identifies heavy metals including arsenic, lead and mercury in mining-affected environments. Some studies have reported arsenic concentrations as high as 330 times national standards in specific contaminated locations, while lead and mercury have been recorded at levels many times above applicable safety limits. These figures need to be interpreted carefully. They are site-specific measurements from contaminated locations, not evidence that Ghana’s entire water system contains those concentrations. But they illustrate the severity of contamination that can occur around poorly regulated mining and processing sites. Mercury is particularly important because it can enter aquatic food chains and eventually reach people through fish consumption. Cocoa is paying a price too The damage does not stop at the riverbank. Galamsey has increasingly encroached on cocoa-growing areas, particularly in some of Ghana’s major producing regions. COCOBOD has reported that illegal mining has affected 81% of cocoa farmland in the Eastern Region, 74% in Western and 68% in Ashanti in areas assessed. The impacts include destroyed cocoa trees, early pod dropping, wilting and yellowing leaves and reduced yields. But Ghana’s cocoa production decline should not be attributed entirely to illegal mining. Weather conditions, swollen shoot disease, ageing farms and other structural challenges have also contributed significantly to the industry’s recent difficulties. The distinction is important because the data show galamsey as one component of a wider cocoa production crisis, rather than a single explanation for it. The risk to farmland, however, is immediate: once a productive cocoa farm has been excavated, restoring it is far more difficult than preventing its destruction. From shovels to excavators The scale of the environmental damage has also changed as mining has become increasingly mechanized. In 2024, Ghana imported GH¢6.2 billion worth of excavators, according to the Lands Minister, making the machines one of the country’s largest import categories. The government subsequently introduced measures to track excavators and prevent their diversion into illegal mining. The significance is simple. An excavator can disturb an area of land in hours that would take individuals with basic tools considerably longer to work. That changes galamsey from a collection of small pits into a potentially large-scale landscape transformation By March 2026, the National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) said its operations had resulted in the seizure of 94 excavators, the destruction of nearly 3,000 illegal mining sites and 237 arrests. The figures demonstrate the scale of enforcement activity. They also raise another question: How much does Ghana spend fighting galamsey, and how much of that expenditure translates into lasting environmental recovery? When the pollution reaches the food chain The environmental damage can eventually become a food-safety issue. The analysis highlights studies reporting elevated concentrations of lead and mercury in food samples from mining-affected areas, including cassava, leafy vegetables, tomatoes and river fish. Among the reported results, lead in some tomato samples reached 48 times the applicable safety limit. Again, these should not be interpreted as evidence that Ghanaian food generally contains dangerous levels of heavy metals. They are findings from specific samples and locations. But they demonstrate a potential pathway particularly concerning for communities that depend directly on rivers for fishing, irrigation and household use. Contaminated mining area → polluted water or soil → crops and aquatic life → human consumption. The forest-water connection The destruction also extends upstream. Forest reserves are important to Ghana’s water security because forest ecosystems help protect watersheds, regulate water flows and reduce erosion. That made the controversy surrounding L.I. 2462 particularly significant. The 2022 legislative instrument created a framework under which mining could take place in protected forest reserves under certain conditions. It subsequently became the focus of sustained public opposition before being revoked by government in 2025. Why the cycle is difficult to break The Wealth Over Water analysis estimates that more than one million people are directly involved in artisanal and small-scale mining, with millions more dependent on the sector. For some miners, daily earnings can significantly exceed what is available from alternative livelihoods. This is another reason galamsey has proved difficult to eliminate: the economics work for some of the people involved That creates a difficult enforcement equation. A mining site can be destroyed. An excavator can be seized. A miner can be arrested. But if the economic incentive remains, another operation can emerge elsewhere. This is why the long-term response cannot rely solely on raids and equipment seizures. It also requires action against illegal financing and gold-trading networks, effective regulation of legitimate small-scale mining, alternative livelihoods and sustained environmental monitoring. The bill Ghana does not see Ghana’s gold industry generates foreign exchange, employment and government revenue. But illegal and environmentally destructive mining creates another bill — one that does not appear neatly in the national budget. It is reflected in higher water-treatment costs, damaged cocoa farms, degraded river systems, lost agricultural land, threatened fisheries and environmental restoration. Potentially in the rising cost of securing clean water for a growing population. That is the central tension captured by Wealth Over Water . Ghana is rich in gold, but the natural systems that support the wider economy are not limitless. The country’s renewable water availability has already fallen to 1,650 cubic metres per person, below the commonly used water-stress threshold. At the same time, scientists estimate that about 60% of Ghana’s water bodies are polluted, with galamsey among the major contributors. The question, therefore, is no longer simply how much gold Ghana can extract. It is how much of the country’s water, farmland, forests and ecological wealth can be consumed in the process — and who ultimately pays for the damage.

title: Finland is buying Swedish anti-aircraft systems
body:
Finland has signed an agreement with the Swedish Saab group for the delivery of RBS 70 NG anti-aircraft systems. The country has been using earlier versions of this solution in several configurations for nearly 20 years.
Information about the conclusion of the contract was announced on 28 August . The value of the contract concluded by the Finnish Defence Forces Logistics Command was specified at SEK 1.2 billion (approx. USD 120 million). It is not known how many RBS 70 NG sets the Finns are acquiring in total. The agreement includes an option allowing for further purchases in the future, as well as training packages, maintenance equipment, and spare parts.
Puolustusvoimat on tehnyt noin 108 miljoonan euron tilauksen Saab RBS 70 NG -ilmatorjuntaohjusjärjestelmästä. Sen aiempi versio on jo käytössä Suomessa tunnuksella ITO05. @ReservilainenFi-artikkeli kertoo millaisesta ohjuksesta ja järjestelmästä on kyse. https://t.co/6fMPstbcfg
“We are proud to continue supporting the Finnish Defence Forces and contribute to ensuring the security of the country’s airspace. With the RBS 70 NG, Finland will gain modern short-range air defence capabilities, allowing for effective countering of evolving aerial threats,” says Görgen Johansson, head of Saab’s Dynamics business area.
It is worth noting that the Finns have been using earlier versions of the RBS 70 in at least two configurations since 2008 (nearly 20 years). These are part of the ASRAD-R (local name ItO 2005) very short-range air defence system. One vehicle within this system features 4 RBS 70 BOLIDE launchers, which are mounted as a module on a Unimog 5000 light-duty truck chassis or a Sisu Nasu all-terrain vehicle.
The RBS 70 NG is a modernised variant of the RBS 70 very short-range air defence (VSHORAD) system, developed by the Swedish company Saab Bofors Dynamics in 2011. It is used to combat aerial targets such as unmanned aerial vehicles, helicopters, and aircraft, using laser-guided missiles both day and night. The maximum distance at which the RBS 70 NG can eliminate aerial threats is 8,000–9,000 metres, with an altitude ceiling of up to 5,000 metres.
The NG version is characterised by, among other things, an improved sighting system, the integration of missiles with a thermal imaging camera, the implementation of an automatic target tracking function, and simplified operation during operator training. Currently, the RBS 70 NG is used by the armies of countries such as Argentina, Brazil, the Czech Republic, Sweden, Norway, and Ukraine.

title: UAE weather: Rain expected across parts of country in coming days
body: Rain is expected to fall across parts of the UAE in the coming days, according to the latest forecast by the National Centre of Meteorology. The NCM is forecasting wet weather in Al Ain from Tuesday until Thursday this week, while rain is expected to fall in Fujairah on Tuesday and Wednesday. The highest temperature this week is expected in Sweihan, where it is tipped to reach 42°C each day until Friday. The highest temperature in Abu Dhabi is forecast to be 39°C on Tuesday, Wednesday and Friday, while in Dubai the thermometer will peak at 38°C on the same days. The NCM also predicted there was a probability of foggy weather on both Wednesday and Thursday mornings. The rain, particularly in the eastern parts of the country such as Al Ain, is being caused by a low-pressure system from the south-east bringing moisture-laden air from the Arabian Sea. These systems then meet the mountains on the UAE’s east coast, wherer the air rises and meets a relatively cooler layer abovem, and this can lead to the formation of convective clouds and rain.

title: France seizes Russian ‘shadow fleet’ oil tanker in Indian Ocean
body: France’s navy detained an oil tanker called the DF Peak that belongs to the “shadow fleet” on October 12, French President Emmanuel Macron said. La France est déterminée à lutter contre la flotte fantôme, partout dans le monde. Ce matin, à plus de 450 nautiques au sud de La Réunion, notre Marine nationale a arraisonné le pétrolier DF Peak, suspecté de naviguer sous un faux pavillon et impliqué dans des activités… pic.twitter.com/GS91egdvzN — Emmanuel Macron (@EmmanuelMacron) October 12, 2026 The tanker was detained more than 450 nautical miles south of Réunion Island in the Indian Ocean. Authorities suspect it was flying a false flag and illegally transporting fuel. According to data from Marinetraffic, the tanker was sailing under Benin’s flag and was headed to the port of Cruz Grande in Chile. It wasn’t clear where the vessel had sailed from. The magazine Maritime Executive writes that the tanker was built in 2006 and originally belonged to the company Sovcomflot, sailing under the name NS Captain . It was renamed Kaliningrad in 2024 and took its current name in 2025. Its operator is now a company based in Hong Kong. Maritime Executive also says that Benin’s national registry, whose flag the tanker flies, was once “considered a haven for Russia-linked shadow fleet vessels.” The U.S. sanctioned the tanker in February 2024. The European Union, Switzerland, Canada, the U.K., and Ukraine followed with sanctions of their own. France has detained tankers belonging to the “shadow fleet,” including some reportedly linked to Russia, several times since the start of 2026. In January, French authorities detained the tanker Grinch . In March, they detained the tanker Deyna , which was allowed to leave the port of Marseille a month later. In June, French authorities detained the tankers Tagor and Deliver . Also in mid-June, the U.K. detained a Russian “shadow fleet” tanker for the first time after it tried to pass through the English Channel. title: Raytheon to advance target-detection capabilities for naval radars
body:
Raytheon, an RTX business, has been awarded a contract from the Office of Naval Research (ONR) to develop advanced target‑detection capabilities for naval radar systems.
Under the contract, Raytheon's Advanced Technology team will develop and evaluate advanced signal and data-processing algorithms and integrate targeted software upgrades to extend detection range, increase sensitivity and improve radar-system efficiency.
These enhancements will undergo rigorous laboratory and field testing to validate performance and operational use, preparing them for transition into Raytheon's SPY‑6 family of radars and other future naval radars.
Work under this contract will be conducted at Raytheon facilities in Portsmouth, R.I., and Andover, Massachusetts, through 2031.
Raytheon recently scored a contract valued up to $6.3 billion for the production and sustainment of Standard Missile-3 Block IB (SM‑3 IB) interceptors.
"Modernizing fielded radar systems with software-first upgrades is one of the fastest and most cost-effective ways to deliver mission-ready capability," said Colin Whelan , president of Advanced Technology at Raytheon.
"These enhancements will enable naval operators to detect smaller objects at greater distances and classify targets more quickly, providing the fleet with faster, more informed decision‑making."
The program continues Raytheon's extensive work in software-defined apertures and leverages knowledge gained from prior ONR initiatives, including ASPIRE and STORM, which established foundational hardware and software advancements for next-generation radar capability.

title: Russian attacks on Kharkiv region leave four killed, more than 50 injured over past day
body:
According to Ukrinform, Oleh Syniehubov, head of the Kharkiv Regional Military Administration, reported this on Facebook .
Three people were killed in Kharkiv, and 37 were injured. Among those affected were a 10-year-old boy and a 16-year-old girl who suffered acute stress reactions.
In Lozova, a 71-year-old woman was killed. Seven women and a 9-year-old girl suffered acute stress reactions.
In the village of Chervona Poliana, within the Barvinkove community, women aged 54 and 60 and a 14-year-old boy suffered acute stress reactions.
In the settlement of Vysokyi, a 49-year-old man was injured, while a 71-year-old woman suffered an acute stress reaction.
In the village of Peremoha, within the Lozova community, a 38-year-old woman suffered an acute stress reaction.
Russian forces attacked Kharkiv’s Kyivskyi, Kholodnohirskyi, and Shevchenkivskyi districts using drones and missiles.
In addition, Russian forces used nine missiles, one guided aerial bomb, seven Geran-2 drones, five Molniya drones, three FPV drones, and 24 drones whose type has yet to be identified in attacks on the Kharkiv region.
In Kharkiv, the attacks damaged 10 apartment buildings, 13 private houses, a sports complex, 11 cars, an enterprise, railway infrastructure, and a bank building.
In Kupiansk district, an administrative building and power lines were damaged in Shevchenkove, along with a house in the village of Shypuvate.
In Izium district, three houses were damaged, as were power lines in the village of Malynivka, a house in Chervona Poliana, and a shop in Izium.
In Kharkiv district, a house and two outbuildings were damaged in Derhachi. Railway infrastructure and an administrative building were damaged in Liubotyn, while two private houses were damaged in Vysokyi and the village of Cherkaska Lozova.
In Lozova district, two houses were damaged in Lozova and a shop in the village of Peremoha.
In Chuhuiv district, a civilian enterprise in the village of Bazaliivka was damaged, along with two tractors, a combine harvester, and power lines in the village of Martove.
The transit evacuation center in Lozova received 171 people over the past day. Since it began operating, a total of 64,497 people have registered at the center.
As Ukrinform previously reported, the bodies of three people were found beneath the rubble of a residential building in Kharkiv’s Kholodnohirskyi district following a Russian missile strike .

title: Saudi fighter jets launch airstrikes on Yemen’s Saada
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 13 (MNA) – In its fresh attacks, Saudi fighter jets on Tuesday targeted the communications network of Saada province in Yemen.
Saudi fighter jets targeted areas in Yemen’s Saada province on Tuesday. The fighter jets bombed Marran District, located in southwest of Saada province in northern Yemen.
It has also been reported that Saudi fighter jets targeted the communication network in Al-Ghamr border area, west of Saada province.
The Yemeni Ministry of Health announced yesterday that 385 people have so far been killed and wounded in Saudi attacks since September 3.
The ministry also added that five people were killed and fifteen others wounded following a Saudi attack on a girls' school and a medical center in Al-Quhaf area in ​​Jabal Habashi District, Taiz Governorate, in southwestern Yemen.

title: Drones hit more merchant ships off Bulgaria - media
body:
The merchant ship Chelsea 3, sailing under the Maltese flag and registered at the port of Odesa, was attacked by three aerial drones about 15 nautical miles from the city of Byala, Prime Minister Rumen Radev said, Bulgarian National Radio reported.
"The alert about the incident came in at 1:30 am. All 15 crew members (seven citizens of Ukraine and eight of Azerbaijan) were evacuated to Varna. The five injured seamen were given medical aid," it said.
Chelsea 3 left the Turkish Black Sea port of Giresun for the port of Giurgiulesti, and the declared cargo was meant for Moldova. The 136-meter ship, which is listing, is now drifting without a crew off Cape St. Athanasius, Bulgarian National Radio correspondent in Varna Daniela Stoyneva said.
On October 6, two merchant ships were hit by aerial and naval drones in the same area, in Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone in the Black Sea about 70 nautical miles east of Byala. The Togo-flagged Alfa Watan sank, and its crew of 12 Syrian citizens went missing. The second ship, the Palau-flagged Able, was damaged and caught fire.
"Another attack on merchant ships in the immediate vicinity of Bulgaria's territorial waters is absolutely unacceptable," Prime Minister Radev said.
During an emergency meeting of the Security Council under the Council of Ministers, word came in of yet another attacked ship. It sank about 17 nautical miles east of the village of Kropets. According to preliminary data, one crew member was rescued.
Bulgaria's permanent representatives to NATO and the European Union have been informed. "I will talk to NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte," Radev said. He also said he would summon Russian Ambassador to Sofia Eleonora Mitrofanova.

title: Helicopter Maker Sikorsky Unveils Fist Portable Drone System for Rapid Deployment in Remote Locations
body:
Helicopter maker Sikorsky has introduced the Nomad 100 fast pack , a containerised vertical take-off and landing (VTOL) uncrewed aerial system (UAS) designed for rapid deployment in contested and infrastructure-limited environments.
The 20-foot International Organization for Standardization (ISO) container houses four Nomad 100 aircraft, mission-command software, communications, power and sustainment equipment. According to Sikorsky, two aircraft can be mission-ready in under 15 minutes, with the remaining two available within four to six hours. The container can subsequently be repacked, transported and redeployed, reducing reliance on established airfields, external support and large deployment teams.
Designed for operations from naval vessels, tactical vehicle staging areas and improvised landing zones, the system targets military requirements for rapidly deployable autonomous aircraft with minimal logistical support.
Depending on configuration, the Nomad 100 fast pack can support intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance (ISR), tactical reconnaissance (ISR-T), light attack and contested logistics. The wider Nomad family also has potential applications in maritime patrol, search and rescue (SAR) and persistent communications, as well as defence, Homeland Security, forestry and civilian operations.
The twin-proprotor Nomad combines helicopter-like vertical lift and hovering with fixed-wing flight characteristics intended to provide extended range and endurance. Its articulated-rotor design supports runway-independent operations in confined environments on land and at sea; a hybrid-electric powertrain may be used in certain configurations.
The aircraft uses Sikorsky’s MATRIX autonomy system, designed to enable operator-commanded aircraft to plan, execute and adapt missions in dynamic environments. Its open architecture supports integration with existing command-and-control systems, including the US Army’s Universal Unmanned Aircraft System Controller and the US Marine Corps’ MAGTF Agile Network Gateway Link (MANGL).
The United States Marine Corps awarded a $15.5 million contract to Sikorsky for the Medium Aerial Resupply Vehicle – Expeditionary Logistics (MARV-EL) Increment 2 program

title: LA 2028: Black Queens pumped up for second leg of Mauritius tie
body: Ghana will look to wrap up qualification in the second round of the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games when they host Mauritius in the second leg at the Essipong Stadium on Tuesday. The Black Queens go into the fixture with a commanding advantage, having beaten their opponents 3-0 in the first meeting last week, Thursday, at the Côte d’Or National Sports Complex in Mauritius. Kim Lars Bjorkegren’s side are chasing Olympic Games football for the first time, having failed to reach the heights since the introduction of women’s football at the summer games in 1996. The winner of the tie over two legs will advance into the next stage of the competition, where they will face one of Uganda or Zambia in the third round of the qualifiers. Mauritius, on the other hand, will be playing for pride and will hope to cause an upset away from home after a difficult first leg. Björkegren’s team held their final training session at the Essipong Stadium on Monday evening, with the Swedish trainer going on to address the media. title: Ukraine ready for various ceasefire formats, but EU must exert crushing pressure on Moscow – Sybiha
body:
Ukraine is ready to consider various truce options; however, compelling Moscow to agree to peace requires uncompromising pressure from Europe, Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiha stated on X on Monday while attending the EU Foreign Affairs Council meeting in Luxembourg.
“When it comes to peace efforts, Ukraine is ready for different types of ceasefire. Energy. Food security. A full ceasefire. The question is how to force Moscow to agree. For this, we need decisive pressure. Ukraine knows where to press, but we need the EU to be ready to do it,” the foreign minister stressed.
Sybiha urged partners to apply not half-measures against the Russian Federation, but "devastating pressure," including the full utilization of the aggressor state's frozen assets, trade and transit embargoes, maritime restrictions, maximum visa restrictions for Russian citizens, and entry bans for Russian combatants and their relatives.
The Foreign Minister welcomed the EU Council's adoption of a major sanction package against Russia, additional financial contributions from member states to support Ukraine's defense, and the agreement to open the next two negotiating clusters regarding Ukraine's accession to the European Union.
Sybiha noted that he had arrived in Luxembourg directly from Dnipro and Pryluky (in Chernihiv region), where he had visited sites of brutal Russian strikes and met with Ukrainian troops the day before. He stated that he had briefed his European counterparts on the current frontline situation and enemy plans, and presented a specific list of the defense forces' needs for countering Russian aerial terror.
Furthermore, the Ukrainian minister called for increased isolation of Russia in international sports and culture, outlined Kyiv's position on EU enlargement reforms, and discussed with diplomats ways to address the funding gap for defense needs.

title: Freeze the Controller, Defrost the Food: Uncovering Vulnerabilities in Danfoss Refrigeration Controllers
body:
Danfoss AK-SM 800A controllers are widely deployed to manage refrigeration infrastructure in supermarkets, cold-storage facilities, warehouses, and other commercial environments. Because these systems provide centralized management of refrigeration equipment, compromising the management interface can have significant operational consequences.
Team82 researched the attack surface of the Danfoss AK-SM 800A platform and identified multiple vulnerabilities affecting the embedded web management interface. Team82 disclosed the vulnerabilities to Danfoss, which addressed them in a new firmware version .
Our research uncovered a hidden "code-of-the-day" authentication mechanism that could be abused to bypass normal authentication, a command-injection vulnerability leading to remote code execution, and an issue allowing authenticated users to inject arbitrary Nginx configuration directives, which could be leveraged to manipulate web traffic and trigger a denial-of-service condition.
Our analysis began by examining the internet exposure of these devices, where we identified thousands of publicly accessible management interfaces. We then reverse engineered the firmware to reconstruct the architecture of the embedded web service, ultimately tracing each vulnerability from the HTTP request handlers down to the underlying implementation.
These findings demonstrate how undocumented functionality, insecure command construction, and dynamically modifiable web server configurations can combine to create powerful attack chains against internet-accessible cyber-physical systems.
How we researched the Danfoss AK-SM 800A platform
Some details on the Code-of-the-Day vulnerability we uncovered
How we used CVE-2025-41451 to achieve remote code execution
The successful coordinated disclosure with Danfoss.
Danfoss is one of the largest manufacturers of refrigeration and HVAC equipment worldwide. Its solutions are deployed throughout supermarkets, cold-storage facilities, warehouses, and commercial buildings.
Among its management platforms is the AK-SM 800A , a centralized system manager responsible for coordinating refrigeration controllers throughout an installation.
The platform aggregates information from numerous field devices while providing operators with a web-based management interface for monitoring and configuring the entire refrigeration environment.
From a single console, administrators can:
The system effectively becomes the operational control center for Danfoss refrigeration infrastructure.
Because technicians frequently administer these systems remotely, the AK-SM 800A includes an embedded web server that exposes a browser-based management interface. This convenience significantly reduces maintenance costs, allowing engineers to troubleshoot problems without traveling to every installation.
Before diving into the firmware, we wanted to answer a simple but important question: could an attacker actually reach these systems in the first place?
Industrial control systems are often assumed to be safely tucked away on isolated networks. Unfortunately, that assumption doesn't always hold true.
To understand the real-world exposure of the Danfoss AK-SM 800A, we searched publicly available internet-wide scanning platforms, including Shodan and Censys, for signatures associated with its management interface. It didn't take long to find what we were looking for. Numerous controllers were directly accessible from the public Internet.
Many of these exposed systems displayed the distinctive HTTP/S title of the Danfoss StoreView management interface, suggesting that administrators had exposed the web console for remote management.
For an attacker, this significantly lowers the barrier to entry. Instead of first compromising a corporate network or gaining physical access to a supermarket, they can simply scan for exposed controllers, identify devices running vulnerable firmware, and begin interacting directly with the embedded web application.
That discovery also influenced the direction of our research. While the controller supports multiple industrial communication protocols, the Internet-facing web interface represents the most realistic entry point for a remote attacker. As a result, we shifted our attention there first.
Once we started reverse engineering the firmware, it became clear that the web interface was much more than a simple management portal. Behind it was a surprisingly complex architecture, with multiple interacting components that ultimately became the focus of our security analysis.
Instead of a single HTTP server processing requests, the platform implemented multiple layers of reverse proxies, CGI handlers, and application logic spread across several independent processes.
Understanding this architecture became the key to discovering every vulnerability that followed.
After extracting the firmware and examining the filesystem, we began identifying the binaries and configuration files responsible for servicing HTTP requests.
The first component we encountered was an externally exposed Nginx instance responsible for listening on the management ports used by the web interface. Rather than directly implementing application logic, this Nginx server acts primarily as a reverse proxy responsible for dispatching requests to other components within the system.
The main nginx.conf configuration file defines that requests with the suffixes .cgi will be routed into a CGI instance running on the system sm_fcgi_app. The CGI executable sm_fcgi_app handling the routed request is responsible for initial handling of the web request according to system configuration sm_fcgi_app.conf .
Inspecting the handling of the request inside the sm_fcgi_app executable, we understood that it implements initial processing of the request and then forwards it to the internal Nginx using the method forward_xml_request .
The internal Nginx instance is configured to listen on the local interface.
Further down in the configuration, we found that requests targeting URLs with the .cgi suffix are forwarded to a separate CGI service running as part of a task created by the sm_app executable . This task, named Task_Web , implements the core logic of the device's web application. Once requests reach this component, they are fully parsed, processed, and dispatched to the appropriate application handlers.
Authentication code is often one of the most security-sensitive components of an embedded management platform. At this point, we focused on the request-processing logic responsible for user authentication. Specifically, we analyzed requests sent to the xml.cgi endpoint with the action=" getauth " parameter.
Analyzing the handling of this request led us to the xml_get_data function, which dispatches incoming requests to their corresponding action handlers based on the requested operation. In our case, the request was routed to the handler for the getauth action.
While analyzing this routine, we discovered a potential authentication bypass that allows an attacker to avoid the standard password verification performed against the user credentials stored on the system.
This behavior became apparent after we identified two request attributes (redacted) whose purpose was not immediately clear. When either of these attributes is included in a request, the authentication flow is redirected to a function that contains a code path leading to another function named check_code_of_day .
A closer examination of these functions revealed what appears to be a hidden authentication mechanism, likely intended for vendor support or maintenance. Instead of validating the configured administrator password, the application accepts a specially crafted authentication request containing a generated "code of the day."
Based on our analysis, this alternate authentication path is activated by setting specific request parameters to 1 and supplying a precomputed password. Rather than comparing this value against the configured user credentials, the application validates it against a password generated internally from the device's current date and time.
By reverse engineering the check_code_of_day routine, we were able to fully reconstruct the algorithm responsible for generating this daily authentication code. This demonstrated that anyone capable of reproducing the algorithm could generate valid authentication credentials without knowing the administrator's password. If discovered by a malicious actor, this hidden authentication mechanism could be abused to completely bypass the normal login process and gain administrative access to the device's web management interface.
This routine generates a daily authentication password based solely on the device's current date. By reproducing the same algorithm, an attacker can generate a valid authentication code for any given day and use it to bypass the standard login process. Successful authentication through this hidden mechanism results in a fully authenticated administrative session, granting privileged access to the device's web management interface.
Successfully bypassing authentication dramatically expanded the attack surface available for analysis. Instead of being limited to the small number of unauthenticated endpoints, we gained access to the device's full administrative interface and every management function it exposed. Like many embedded management platforms, the AK-SM 800A includes a wide range of configuration pages for network settings, alarm management, user administration, email notifications, logging, and system maintenance.
When reverse engineering embedded web applications, one of the first places we look is functionality that interacts with the underlying operating system. Configuration pages that invoke external utilities are particularly attractive because they often involve constructing shell commands from user-controlled input.
The SMTP Email configuration page quickly stood out. By tracing the request responsible for updating the email settings, we eventually reached the code responsible for constructing the command executed by the operating system.
The value fetched from item number 0x1be1 is formatted into the OS shell command. This is our email authentication password. The field value being formatted into the shell command is not sanitized according to our analysis and could potentially include OS shell directives that yield subsequent commands controlled by a potential attacker.
During our analysis, we noticed that the externally exposed Nginx instance includes the configuration file headers.conf as part of its server configuration.
Further investigation revealed that the web application exposes functionality for replacing this file and reloading the external Nginx instance at runtime, effectively allowing new configuration directives to be applied without restarting the device. This capability is exposed through the action=" load_nginx_headers " endpoint, which accepts the contents of a new headers.conf file via an authenticated file upload.
While testing this functionality, we discovered that an attacker could abuse it to implant arbitrary routing directives into the Internet-facing Nginx configuration. This allows an attacker to modify how requests are handled by the web server and potentially manipulate clients interacting with the device.
During further testing, we also identified an unexpected edge case. Requests directed to a maliciously implanted route triggered an unhandled exception inside the sm_app process responsible for servicing web requests. The resulting crash terminated the web service, allowing an authenticated attacker to repeatedly trigger a denial-of-service condition against the management interface.
Claroty Team82 privately reported these vulnerabilities to Danfoss through a coordinated vulnerability disclosure process. Danfoss investigated our findings and released firmware version R4.3.1 , which addresses the vulnerabilities described in this research.
Customers using affected AK-SM 800A controllers should upgrade to firmware version R4.3.1 or later as soon as possible. Organizations should also avoid exposing management interfaces directly to the Internet and ensure that access to administrative services is restricted to trusted management networks or secured through VPNs and other appropriate network segmentation controls.
We appreciate the collaboration of the Danfoss Product Security Incident Response Team throughout the disclosure and remediation process.
Amir Zaltzman is a vulnerability researcher on Team82.
CWE-77 IMPROPER NEUTRALIZATION OF SPECIAL ELEMENTS USED IN A COMMAND ('Command Injection'):
Improper neutralization of alarm-to-mail configuration fields used in an OS shell command injection in Danfoss AK-SM8xxA Series, prior to version 4.3.1, may lead to post-authenticated remote code execution on an attacked system.
Danfoss created release R4.3.1 to address CVE-2025-41451.
CWE 287: Improper Authentication An Improper Authentication vulnerability exists in Danfoss AK-SM8xxA Series, resulting in an authentication bypass. Install the latest patch with number 4.2 to remediate this vulnerability. This flaw could enable an attacker to generate a web report that discloses sensitive information such as internal IP addresses, usernames, store names, and other sensitive information.e
CWE-15 EXTERNAL CONTROL OF SYSTEM OR CONFIGURATION SETTING:
A post-authenticated external control of system web interface configuration setting vulnerability exists in the Danfoss AK-SM8xxA Series prior to version 4.3.1, which could allow for a denial-of-service attack induced by improper handling of exceptional conditions.
Danfoss created release R4.3.1 to address CVE-2025-41452.

title: Kyiv should strike targets in Russia as it deems necessary – former Trump envoy Kellogg
body:
Ukraine should have full freedom of action to strike military and energy facilities within Russian territory in response to Moscow's aggression, said retired Lieutenant General Keith Kellogg, former special envoy for Ukraine to U.S. President Donald Trump, in an interview with Bloomberg Television.
“One shouldn’t allow any sanctuaries for the opponent in a conflict. Moscow has been hitting Ukrainian energy infrastructure before, and Kyiv should strike targets in Russia as it deems necessary. Let Ukrainians do what they’ve been very good at,” emphasized Kellogg on the sidelines of the Warsaw Security Forum. He added that Russia is not winning the war but merely prolonging it, acting from a position of weakness due to significant losses.
His remarks stand in stark contrast with the US president’s call on Kyiv over the weekend to halt air strikes on refineries in Russia, as well as the controversial agreement to bring more than 2.25 million barrels of Russian diesel fuel to the global market.
Commenting on this energy agreement, the former special envoy noted that it would not have a tangible impact on the market and that Vladimir Putin was merely trying to turn the approaching U.S. midterm elections to his advantage. The general described Trump’s harsh remarks directed at President Volodymyr Zelenskyy as political "noise," noting that public rhetoric would ultimately align with the actual situation on the battlefield.

title: Airbus Kratos Complete First European Flight of Valkyrie Combat Drone Target 2029 Deployment
body:
Airbus and Kratos Defense & Security Solutions have completed the first flight of the U740-Valkyrie, advancing their plan to deliver a combat-ready uncrewed Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA) by 2029.
Conducted at a test facility in Northern Europe, the flight reportedly met all objectives, including rocket-assisted take-off designed for runway-independent operations, manoeuvres at various altitudes and speeds up to Mach 0.8, and in-flight mission adjustments. The milestone paves the way for advanced testing of Airbus’ Multi-platform Autonomous Reconfigurable and Secure (MARS) mission system.
MARS is designed to provide European control over the aircraft’s software, mission applications, data and hardware, preserving German or broader European sovereignty over its operational use. Its AI-enhanced software enables autonomous missions and coordination of multiple aircraft, while human oversight is intended to ensure critical decisions comply with established rules of engagement and applicable ethical and legal standards.
The Valkyrie is designed to operate autonomously or under the command of crewed fighters such as the Eurofighter, extending their range, firepower and survivability while undertaking high-risk missions. Its design supports both rail launch and conventional runway-based take-off and landing.
The U740 Valkyrie is a Europeanized variant of the U.S.-developed XQ-58A Valkyrie, adapted by Airbus Defence and Space for European Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA) requirements. While the U.S. version uses American military autonomy systems, the U740 integrates Airbus’ MARS mission system to ensure European control over mission software and operational data. With a maximum take-off weight of approximately 3,000 kg, a range exceeding 5,000 km and a service ceiling of 45,000 feet, it is designed for runway-independent launch and high-risk reconnaissance, electronic warfare and strike missions alongside crewed fighters such as the Eurofighter Typhoon.
The U740-Valkyrie measures 9.1 metres long, with an 8.2-metre wingspan, and has an approximate maximum take-off weight of three tonnes. Its stated range exceeds 5,000 kilometres, and its service ceiling is 45,000 feet. It features an internal weapons bay and external underwing payload stations.
The aircraft is intended to support crewed fighters in high-risk missions, with autonomous capabilities and alternative launch options potentially reducing dependence on conventional airfields.
The first flight advances the programme towards its 2029 combat-readiness target, but further testing must validate the integrated aircraft and MARS system, including autonomous mission execution, multi-aircraft coordination and operational compliance. The companies have not disclosed a final procurement quantity, programme cost or confirmed operational deployment schedule in the information provided; 2029 remains a target, not confirmation of entry into service.

title: Russian strike on Ukraine’s Kharkiv kills three
body: Rescuers clearing rubble at a residential building damaged in a Russian strike found the bodies of three people who had been killed, said Oleh Syniehubov , head of the regional administration. A rescuer responding to the strike was injured and hospitalized, Ukraine’s State Emergency Service said. In total, Syniehubov said, Russian strikes on Kharkiv on October 12 injured 37 people in the city. Search and rescue operations continue in Kholodnohirskyi District, where a Russian strike destroyed an entire section of a four-story residential building, he said.
