title: Interior Minister urges public to share drug intelligence
body: The Minister for the Interior, Mohammed Mubarak Muntaka, has appealed to the public to share intelligence on suspected drug trafficking and other criminal activities without making excessive financial demands on security agencies. He said some informants demanded large sums of money before providing information, placing additional pressure on agencies already operating with limited resources to combat drug-related offences. Speaking on Joy FM’s Super Morning Show in an interview monitored by the Ghana News Agency, Mr Muntaka cited a case at the Narcotics Control Commission (NACOC) in which an individual allegedly demanded US$20 million from the Director-General before providing information on suspected drug activities. “We are pleading with our citizens that we need to keep all of us safe. We don’t have unlimited resources. Sometimes we do this from our own pockets. Please help us without necessarily making untoward demands,” he said. The Minister said similar demands were made by people who approached the Interior Ministry with information about suspected criminal activities, with some requesting as much as GH¢5,000. “I sit at the ministry, people run and come, there is this thing happening and you have to give me something; they demand 5000,” he revealed. Mr Muntaka said about 99 per cent of the information received was credible and deserved consideration for compensation, but acknowledged that the Ministry had limited resources to meet all the demands. He assured informants that the Government would provide assistance where necessary, including transport costs and security protection for people whose cooperation exposed them to potential danger. “Where we genuinely need to assist you to cover your transport and other things, we will. Where we have to protect you with security due to the information you gave us, we will do so. But the demands sometimes break our necks and makes our people pissed off,” he said. The Minister stressed that public cooperation was essential to the fight against drug trafficking, particularly as international criminal networks, including South American cartels, use West Africa as a transit route. “We need international collaboration with our neighbours and all citizens. If you see something, say something,” he appealed. Providing an update on anti-narcotics operations, Mr Muntaka said the Government had recorded 28 drug seizures over the preceding 20 months, including 11 involving cocaine. He also reported five drug-related operations conducted internationally, with two in Belgium and one each in Australia, France and the Netherlands. According to the Minister, measures to strengthen anti-narcotics operations include training more security personnel in image analysis, retooling security agencies and providing incentives to officers. He added that rigorous checks at the airport would commence soon and urged the public to cooperate with security personnel, despite any minor inconveniences the exercises might cause. Data from NACOC, the National Intelligence Bureau, the Ghana Police Service and foreign authorities indicated that the 28 seizures recorded since March 2025 involved consignments intercepted in Ghana and shipments seized abroad after leaving or passing through the country. Other substances seized included cannabis, methamphetamine, heroin and pharmaceutical opioids, although the specific drugs involved in some consignments were not publicly disclosed.

title: Tehran slams UK over baseless Fairford claims
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 13 (MNA) – Iran's Foreign Ministry strongly condemned British claims linking Tehran to an alleged security incident at RAF Fairford, calling them a false-flag plot to advance anti-Iran campaigns.
Iran's Foreign Ministry strongly condemned British allegations linking Tehran to an alleged security incident at RAF Fairford air base, describing them as a despicable plot designed to advance an anti-Iran campaign and to evade accountability for Britain's role in the US-Israeli military aggression against the Iranian nation.
In a formal statement, the ministry said the British government cannot escape its political and legal responsibility, or the potential consequences of its claims, by relying on vague language without presenting any solid evidence or proof.
The statement specifically criticized the use of terms such as "highly likely" and "almost certainly," calling them a blatant attempt to lend false credibility to the attribution while sidestepping accountability for baseless accusations.
The ministry highlighted Britain's well-known track record of fabricating security-related allegations against other nations, noting that such practices have, in some instances, contributed to tensions and destructive conflicts in West Asia. It said the British government must be held accountable for persisting in this dangerous approach that undermines international peace and security.
Categorically rejecting the accusations, the Foreign Ministry held the British government, as well as the planners and perpetrators of false-flag operation, fully responsible for all consequences arising from the fabrication.

title: Greek Australian Journalist Gillian Lantouris Wins Mersina Halvagis Award
body: Nine News Melbourne journalist Gillian Lantouris has received the 2026 Mersina Halvagis Award from Crime Stoppers Victoria, recognising her work promoting crime prevention and community safety. Lantouris, who is Greek Australian, announced the honour on Instagram, paying tribute to Mersina Halvagis, a young Greek Australian woman whose life was tragically cut short at the age of 25. Mersina’s family, including her father George, has spent years advocating for victims’ rights, raising awareness about crime prevention and continuing to seek answers and justice. Lantouris praised the family’s determination, describing them as campaigners who have never abandoned their fight. She also highlighted the work of Crime Stoppers Victoria, crediting the organisation with providing an important avenue for the public to share information that can assist investigations. “It has been a pleasure to work alongside Stella Smith and the team to promote important campaigns that are instrumental in helping Victoria Police keep our community safe,” Lantouris wrote. She also encouraged the public to remember that Crime Stoppers accepts anonymous reports. Honouring Mersina Halvagis The award honours the memory of Mersina Halvagis and recognises efforts to support crime prevention and victims’ rights. View this post on Instagram For the Greek Australian community, Mersina’s story remains closely connected to her family’s long campaign for answers and justice. Their advocacy continues to raise awareness of the impact of crime on victims, families and the wider community. Lantouris’s recognition also highlights the contribution of journalists and community organisations working to promote public safety and encourage people to come forward with information. Source: Gillian Lantouris, Instagram The post Greek Australian Journalist Gillian Lantouris Wins Mersina Halvagis Award appeared first on Greek City Times .

title: Afadzato South DCE commissions water projects, teachers’ bungalow
body: Manfred Tawiah, District Chief Executive (DCE) for Afadzato South, has commissioned and handed over the second phase of 20 development projects across the district to improve access to essential infrastructure and social amenities. The exercise started at Goviefe Todzi, where a mechanised borehole water project was inaugurated and handed over to the community. The chiefs and elders expressed gratitude to the Afadzato South District Assembly, Mr Frank Afriyie, Member of Parliament (MP) for the area, and the Government for the facility. They described the borehole as a major relief, noting that the community had endured water shortages for many years. At Have Atsiame, another mechanised borehole project was commissioned and handed over to residents. The team later inaugurated and handed over a third mechanised borehole at Nyagbo Odumase to improve access to potable water and support socio-economic activities. The main ceremony was held at Tafi Mador, where a newly completed six-unit teachers’ bungalow with ancillary facilities was commissioned and handed over. Togbui Adza Kofi V, Chief of Tafi Mador, in a welcome address, said inadequate accommodation for teachers had remained one of the community’s major challenges over the years. He said the situation had made it difficult to attract and retain trained teachers in the area and expressed optimism that the new bungalow would help address the challenge. Addressing the gathering, Mr Tawiah reaffirmed the Government’s and the District Assembly’s commitment to improving infrastructure and living conditions in communities across the district through the execution of development projects. Mr David Kofi Anku, Assembly Member for the Tafi Mador Electoral Area, commended the MP, the DCE, the District Assembly and the people of Tafi Mador for their support towards the successful completion of the project. At Liati Dzogbega, another mechanised borehole project was inaugurated and handed over to residents, who welcomed the intervention and expressed appreciation for the facility. The residents, however, appealed to the DCE and the Assembly to establish a kindergarten school in the community to facilitate access to early childhood education. They said the absence of a kindergarten school compelled children to travel to neighbouring communities to access education, creating difficulties for parents and guardians. The second-phase commissioning exercise forms part of the Assembly’s efforts to expand access to basic social services, address critical community needs, and improve the wellbeing of residents.

title: War is not imminent or inevitable, says NATO commander
body: NATO’s Supreme Allied Commander Europe has told an audience in Warsaw that he does not assess conflict to be either imminent or inevitable, while arguing that the alliance must still prepare for what is possible, according to remarks at the Warsaw Security Forum. General Alexus Grynkewich made the point before setting out the approach he calls a Theory of Victory. “Before I describe this theory in more detail, let me make one point very clear. I do not assess that conflict is imminent or inevitable. It isn’t,” he said. “We help avoid conflict by clearly articulating our defensive intentions, and by maintaining open lines of communication to resolve misunderstandings and encourage transparency.” “But deterring conflict also requires warfighting readiness, and readiness requires to plan against what is possible, not just what is probable,” he said. “As America’s first president, George Washington, stated, the most effective way to preserve peace is to prepare for war. Or, as America’s current president puts it, this is peace through strength. In the case of NATO, that’s the strength of 32 nations, together.” He described the alliance as unlikely to be taken unawares, drawing on “a sophisticated layering of intelligence provided by multi-source collection assets that deliver tremendous amounts of data” and advanced algorithms used to make sense of it. “This means the Alliance is unlikely to be caught by surprise. We will see if an attack is coming, giving us time to assess intent and rapidly position our forces,” he said. “In doing so we aim to deter, but these movements also prepare us to deny any potential attack, including those aimed at seizing and holding NATO territory as a fait accompli.” Speaking of Poland’s accession to NATO in 1999, he said: “It reminds us NATO is a defensive Alliance, constructed to preserve peace. And as such, we have no plans, no intentions, and no ambitions beyond the protection of our people and the defence of our territory. “Still, no one should mistake our defensive nature for weakness or lack of resolve. Through our collective strength we aim to deter and keep the peace. But if someone is foolish enough to attack us, we will fight.” His Theory of Victory, which he stressed is a common vision and his commander’s intent and not a military plan, sets out three stages, blocking an initial attack, blunting it if it persists, and breaking the enemy forces and the warfighting system supporting them if required. General Grynkewich said implementing it would require him to issue orders he hopes never to give, and that demonstrating the readiness to do so is what prevents the need arising. “If attacked, we are ready to fight tonight, but we are not complacent,” he said, adding that any adversary weighing an attack should conclude “today is not the day.” The post War is not imminent or inevitable, says NATO commander first appeared on UK Defence Journal .

title: From Earth to Orbit, France’s Ecosystem Delivers Agentic Computing at Scale With NVIDIA
body: Companies in France are deploying agentic computing across industries spanning space, financial services, the public sector and scientific research, demonstrating how the country’s ecosystem has moved from ambition to application. France’s progress sits on deliberate groundwork. The AI Action Summit in February 2025 and Choose France Summits in 2025 and 2026 anchored major compute commitments on French soil. What the ecosystem has built since then spans the full stack. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements Sovereign AI Infrastructure France-based companies are expanding agentic infrastructure on NVIDIA technology. Bull is extending its European AI server production to NVIDIA Vera Rubin Ultra NVL72 systems, planned for 2028, with trays produced in Europe and rack integration at its Angers factory — inaugurated Friday, Oct. 2. Altair-1, the first satellite in a $1 billion, 50-satellite constellation with on-board autonomous capabilities, launched this month and has successfully reached orbit. Integrated by Loft Orbital and built in Abu Dhabi by Orbitworks , a joint venture between Loft Orbital and Marlan Space , the satellite is flying NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin edge modules, running Mistral’s models, for real-time Earth observation and autonomous operations in orbit. Open Models NVIDIA Nemotron open models are in production across French organizations that require sovereign, trustworthy data. LINAGORA and Docaposte have secured the CANUT framework agreement , making Twake.ai, built on NVIDIA Nemotron, the sole referenced sovereign digital workplace for more than 2,500 French public organizations. In financial services, SBS is launching a sovereign platform enabling banks to deploy governed generative and agentic services within their own environments, in collaboration with NVIDIA. Last week, Mistral introduced under private preview Mistral Large 4 open model, with state-of-the-art, open weight performance in cyber defense, manufacturing, finance and multimodal tasks, and a solid foundation for customizing models across key industries. Fondation Inria , with NVIDIA’s support, is launching a working group on open source advanced modeling and tool adoption, with findings to come in the spring of next year. Agents at Work Across Industries Across retail, public services, telecommunications and science, the pattern is consistent: open models and NVIDIA infrastructure are driving results in France. L’Oréal is integrating NVIDIA ALCHEMI into its research workflows so scientists can explore formulation possibilities in silico and better help guide laboratory research. Combining computational predictions with hands-on experimentation can make the discovery process up to 100x faster than traditional methods and maximize the potential of the group’s proprietary active ingredients. Mirakl has onboarded more than 70 million products with fine-tuned and open models running on NVIDIA GPUs and inference software, cutting seller catalog onboarding to under two hours. Photoroom and Vestiaire Collective a re demonstrating the measurable business impact of advanced visual modeling on marketplace performance. Omi helps brands bring accurate products into AI-generated marketing visuals at scale, combining its approved 3D digital twins with open models optimized on NVIDIA for 4x faster inference. In Côte-d’Or, ThinkDeep and Akila built a digital-twin agent — powered by NVIDIA Cosmos open world models, Nemotron and Omniverse libraries — managing nearly 5,800 kilometers of roads and buildings, cutting total operating costs by 10% and targeting 30% as deployment progresses. Port Sud de France runs goods processing and port security on ThinkDeep’s DeepBrain platform powered by Nemotron and Cosmos. Enchanted Tools, a robotics company headquartered in Paris, is deploying social robots to support patients in healthcare settings including pediatric cancer care. In telecom, Bouygues Telecom and Prisme.ai have launched AI Studio V2, powered by NVIDIA full-stack infrastructure, to offer all of its employees the ability to build their own agents, securely and in a controlled environment In quantum, Alice & Bob has integrated the NVIDIA NVQLink platform for its superconducting cat qubits, showing how GPUs can make quantum error correction more efficient, including for faster qubit modalities. Quandela has also been using NVQLink to build an integration between a DGX Spark system and its photonic qubits — advancing QPU-GPU supercomputing and exploring hybrid quantum-classical applications. title: Crete’s Disputed Footprints Draw Scientists Back to Trachilos
body: Researchers from Australia’s Curtin University have rescanned the Trachilos footprints in western Crete in 3D, as scientists stay split over whether an early human ancestor made them. A Curtin team returned to the coastal site near Kissamos in May 2025 to take fresh scans and create a photo mosaic, according to a Curtin University project brief . The university plans to share the data online through Sketchfab and augmented reality. That matters because the site normally stays covered for protection, the brief said. As a result, visitors cannot see the prints. Curtin has not published any new conclusion on the age of the Trachilos footprints or on what made them. Trachilos footprints age dispute Polish palaeontologist Gerard Gierliński first noticed the tracks in 2002. In 2017, his team described them as possible hominin tracks about 5.7 million years old. That age would put a human-like walker outside Africa far earlier than expected. In October 2021, a University of Tübingen team led by Uwe Kirscher and Madelaine Böhme dated the Trachilos footprints to about 6.05 million years ago in a study in Scientific Reports . Greek City Times reported that the Cretan tracks had been dated to more than six million years ago. At the time, Kirscher said: “The tracks are almost 2.5 million years older than the tracks attributed to Australopithecus afarensis (Lucy) from Laetoli in Tanzania.” A younger date proposed Utrecht University geologists Willem Jan Zachariasse and Lucas Lourens challenged that age. In their November 2022 paper , they argued the rock layers formed in the Late Pliocene, about three million years ago. By then, Crete was an island about 100 kilometres from the European mainland, they said. As a result, it lay out of reach of any hominins of that age. Some scientists doubt the marks are footprints at all, the Utrecht paper noted. Others accept them as tracks but question whether a human-like maker could have made them. So the Trachilos footprints remain unconfirmed as hominin tracks. The site has also suffered damage. Shortly after the 2017 publication, thieves chiselled eight prints out of the rock, the Curtin brief said. Greek City Times first covered the find in September 2017 . Source: Curtin University The post Crete’s Disputed Footprints Draw Scientists Back to Trachilos appeared first on Greek City Times .

title: Council of State urges sustained dialogue, negotiations as teachers resume work
body: The Council of State has urged stakeholders to sustain dialogue and negotiations as teachers return to the classroom, following their nationwide strike. Teaching and learning resumed on Monday, October 12, after the National Association of Graduate Teachers (NAGRAT), and the Pre-Tertiary Teachers’ Association of Ghana (PRETAG) declared strike over their conditions of service, including promotions and upgrade onto appropriate salary scales. The Council of State held discussions with the leadership of the teacher unions on Friday, October, 9, 2026 as part of efforts to resolve the industrial dispute. In a release shared with Ghana News Agency, the Council commended the suspension of the strike, calling on parties to honour their commitments within agreed timelines to resolve outstanding matters. The Council acknowledged the consequences of prolonged industrial action and affirmed its commitment to providing a forum for constructive engagement on matters of national importance. “…While the suspension of the strike is a welcome development, the Council recognises that sustained progress will depend on the implementation of commitments made and the resolution of outstanding issues. “The return to the classroom must therefore be accompanied by continued engagement and demonstrable progress towards meeting agreed obligations,” it said. The Council reiterated the importance of dialogue, good faith and accountability in resolving disputes that affected essential public services, and thanked government institutions for their efforts to resolving the concerns of the teachers. The suspension of the strike followed a series of engagements involving the Council of State, the Fair Wages and Salaries Commission (FWSC), and other relevant stakeholders. During the strike and negotiations, the Controller and Accountant-General’s Department (CAGD) affirmed its commitment to ensuring that payroll issues related to the validation, promotions and upgrade of teachers were addressed in accordance with due process.

title: Over 400 drones head toward Moscow Region overnight — mayor
body:
MOSCOW, October 13. /TASS/. More than 400 drones headed toward the Moscow Region between 8:30 p.m. Moscow time on October 12 and 7 a.m. on October 13 (5:30 p.m. - 4 a.m. GMT), with air defenses neutralizing most of them on the distant approaches, Moscow Mayor Sergey Sobyanin said.
"Between 8:30 p.m. on October 12 and 7 a.m. on October 13, 417 UAVs headed toward the Moscow Region. Air defenses neutralized most of them on the distant approaches," he wrote on his Max channel.
Sobyanin added that air defenses destroyed 65 drones approaching Moscow during that period.

title: Six new pups arrive on Pentulive
body:
Six puppies were born on Yle’s popular Pentulive (Puppy Live) over the weekend, with thousands of viewers following the birth.
Early on Saturday morning, mother Hilkka, the hitherto star of Pentulive (Puppy Live), gave birth to six puppies — two females and four males.

title: We are committed to leaving a legacy in Mandari – Bole-Bamboi MP
body: Yusif Sulemana, Member of Parliament (MP) for Bole-Bamboi Constituency, has reaffirmed his commitment to facilitating development interventions in the Mandari community to help improve the living conditions of the residents. He assured the chiefs and people of the community that the President John Dramani Mahama-led government would leave a lasting legacy in that community. Mr Sulemana gave the assurance at Mandari at the weekend when he addressed the chiefs and people of the community during its maiden homecoming ceremony held on the theme: “United for Progress: Building the Mandari We Want.” The event brought together scores of community members and government officials, including Mr Yussif Jajah Issaka, MP for Ayawaso North Constituency and representatives of the Ghana Library Authority. It provided a platform for the people to discuss the development priorities of the community as well as showcase their culture, including the performance of the Sato, Giwaah and Gbere dances. “I have said it, and I will continue to say it, that His Excellency the President John Mahama and my good self owe the people of Mandari, and we are not running away from it. We are committed to making sure that we leave a legacy in this community, and I have no doubt in my mind that at the end of the day we will leave that legacy”, Mr Sulemana indicated. He recalled supporting several projects in the community even before becoming an MP, including the construction of a dam, a borehole and a community library, among others. The MP said he had initiated steps to facilitate the expansion and upgrading of the health facility in Mandari into a health centre to help enhance the quality of services delivered. Other interventions he pledged to facilitate included the construction of a community centre and provision of three mechanised boreholes in Mandari, and provision of furniture to schools across the constituency, including Mandari. Mr Sulemana also expressed commitment to youth development, and said he had assisted some youth in Mandari to secure recruitment into the security services, while 17 others had been recruited as water guards. The MP commended the chiefs and people of the community for facilitating the homecoming event to strengthen unity and mobilise support for the community’s development. Mr Abdulai Mahamud, the Bole District Chief Executive (DCE), observed that sustainable development required strong partnerships between government, communities and other stakeholders. He encouraged people from Mandari living outside the community to contribute their knowledge, skills, networks and experience to the community’s development. Mr Mahamud said the Assembly had developed a concept note to guide efforts to address farmer-herder conflicts and would engage traditional authorities to work towards a lasting solution. Mr Sampson Mabkuu, Upper West Regional Liberian, who represented the Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Library Authority at the event, indicated that about GHS200,000.00 had been earmarked to expand the Mandari community Library. He said that was because Mr. Ziblim Alhassan, CEO of the GLA, recognised the important role libraries play in promoting education, literacy, knowledge and the development of young people. Mr John Tesinia Seidu, the Youth President of Mandari, called on young people in the community to play an active role in addressing the community’s development challenges. He said the youth were ready to contribute their energy, innovation and skills to community development but needed to be heard, involved and treated fairly in the distribution of resources.

title: Homemade Phyllo Dough: How to Make Paper-Thin Greek Pastry at Home
body: Homemade phyllo dough takes about 2.5 hours with Chef John’s Allrecipes method, which home cooks rate 4.7 out of 5. Homemade phyllo dough sheets ready for pies. Photo: Allrecipes Homemade phyllo dough starts with flour, oil and water Phyllo, also written as filo, is the paper-thin pastry behind baklava, spanakopita and other Greek pies. Most home cooks buy it frozen. Still, Chef John Mitzewich shows that homemade phyllo dough is within reach when the mix rests and you roll layers. Allrecipes says the approach beats opening a supermarket packet, and the sheets freeze well for later. Greek City Times has previously profiled the last traditional phyllo master , whose craft treats hand-rolled pastry as a skill rather than a shortcut. The same pastry turns up across Greek City Times recipes, from a Lemonopita lemon pie to a rose-shaped dessert . As a result, a batch of homemade phyllo dough can feed several of those dishes without another ftrip to the freezer For a short primer on the pastry itself, see Wikipedia’s entry on filo . Baklava also remains one of the best-known uses. TasteAtlas summarises classic baklava for context before you bake. Ingredients for Chef John pastry The Allrecipes yield is about 20 sheets, or eight serves. For servings, homemade phyllo dough needs pantry staples plus a cornstarch mix that keeps layers from sticking. 2 cups plain flour, plus more for kneading, with 5 teaspoons olive oil and ½ teaspoon fine salt ¾ cup warm water (110°F / 43°C) and 2 teaspoons white wine vinegar ½ cup cornstarch mixed with 2 tablespoons plain flour, for dusting while rolling Chef John notes that finished sheets can wrap baklava. Rolled homemade phyllo dough also keeps in the freezer for up to three months when sealed well. Thaw it overnight in the fridge. Each serving comes to about 178 calories, according to the Allrecipes nutrition panel. How to knead, rest and roll the sheets Preparation takes about 30 minutes. The ball then rests for 1 to 2 hours, so Chef John’s full timeline is about 150 minutes. Measure the cornstarch mix before you divide, since rolling moves in batches. Place the flour in a bowl and make a well. Drizzle in the olive oil and add the salt. Pour in the warm water and vinegar. Mix for 10 to 12 minutes, until the mass pulls away from the bowl. Knead on a lightly floured surface until smooth, then until elastic, as Chef John directs. Wrap the ball and rest it at room temperature for one to two hours, as Chef John does. Divide into twenty 20-gram portions. Roll each into a ball and cover so they do not dry out. Work in batches of five. Dust the bench and first ball with cornstarch mix. Flatten to about 5 inches (13 cm), dust again, and stack four more circles. Roll the stack larger, separate, re-dust, and restack until paper-thin, about 10 to 12 inches (25 to 30 cm). Homemade phyllo dough is ready. Use at once, or layer between parchment, roll up gently, wrap, and refrigerate. Repeat with the remaining balls in batches of five. When you want the sheets later, Chef John says the wrapped rolls freeze for up to three months. Then thaw them overnight in the refrigerator to keep them pliable. Tips from home cooks More than 40 home cooks have rated this homemade phyllo dough on Allrecipes. Member CCC wrote: “My first time making phyllo dough and this recipe produced perfect phyllo!” Elizabeth Aires added: “Never imagined I could make phyllo. Mine was so thin it was translucent.” Several reviewers also needed extra cornstarch mix, so keep a spare bowl ready. Chrissy noted that about twice the dusting kept her baklava layers free. Others stretched the sheets with a pasta roller after the hand work, then used them in spanakopita. In particular, rest the ball fully before you roll homemade phyllo dough. Dust generously between layers. Separate the stack before the final roll so the sheets do not weld together. The original full recipe page is on Allrecipes, along with Chef John’s video. Finally, a quiet afternoon and a clean bench are all you need to skip the frozen box and roll your own sheets. Source: Allrecipes The post Homemade Phyllo Dough: How to Make Paper-Thin Greek Pastry at Home appeared first on Greek City Times .

title: Russian emergencies minister thanks North Korea for help in liberating Kursk Region
body:
PYONGYANG, October 13. /TASS/. Russian Emergencies Minister Alexander Kurenkov thanked North Korea for helping liberate the Kursk Region from Ukrainian armed formations during a meeting with North Korean Premier Pak Thae Song.
"I would like to take this opportunity to thank you for the assistance that Korean soldiers and officers provided to Russia in liberating part of the Kursk Region," he said.
Kurenkov laid flowers at the Liberation Monument and the Memorial Museum of Combat Feats at the Overseas Military Operations in Pyongyang. He also toured the museum’s exhibition honoring the courage of North Korean servicemen who participated in liberating the Kursk Region and clearing it of mines.
The minister left a message in the museum’s distinguished visitors’ book. "On behalf of the Russian Emergencies Ministry and myself, we bow in respect to the heroes of the Korean People’s Army and will forever honor their memory! Thank you for your courage and brotherly assistance. May friendship between Russia and North Korea grow stronger, and may peace and security ensure the well-being of our peoples," he wrote.

title: Greater Accra teachers resume work after strike suspension
body: Public pre-tertiary school teachers in the Greater Accra Region have resumed teaching following the suspension of a two-week nationwide strike over outstanding allowances and promotion arrears. A Ghana News Agency (GNA) visit to selected schools in the region on Monday showed teachers supervising pupils, conducting assemblies and teaching in classrooms. Some teachers who spoke to the GNA expressed satisfaction with the resumption of classes and hoped the Government would expedite payment of their outstanding entitlements. ‎At the Mantse Tackie Tawiah Cluster of Schools at Adabraka in the Korle Klottey Municipality, teachers reported for duty and supervised pupils cleaning the school compound before assembly. ‎Teachers also participated in a morning meeting to plan activities for the week. ‎Mr Wellington Akwetey Amanor, Headmaster of Liberty Avenue One and Four Basic School, said the school would organise early morning and late afternoon “extra classes” to recover instructional time lost during the strike. He said he would engage the teachers to develop schedules for the additional classes. At McCarthy Hill Basic School at Awoshie in the Ablekuma North Municipality, pupils returned to school, with low absenteeism reported. ‎Teachers were also seen teaching at Adenta Community School, while those at the Teshie Laboma Cluster of Schools said they would work to make up for the lost instructional time. ‎‎The strike was declared on September 25, 2026, by the Ghana National Association of Teachers (GNAT), the National Association of Graduate Teachers (NAGRAT) and the Coalition of Concerned Teachers. ‎The unions suspended the action on Friday, October 9, following engagements with the Ministry of Labour, Jobs and Employment, the Council of State and the Fair Wages and Salaries Commission (FWSC). ‎‎The union leadership directed members to resume work on Monday, October 12, while engagements on their outstanding grievances continued. ‎‎The unions embarked on the strike over delays in placing promoted staff on their appropriate salary scales and the non-payment of promotion allowances and arrears.

title: Drone attack damages houses and cars in Lviv region
body:
Maksym Kozytskyi, head of the Lviv Regional Military Administration, reported this on Telegram , according to Ukrinform.
"According to preliminary information, during an air raid alert, a downed enemy drone fell onto a residential building in the village of Murovane, in Lviv district," he wrote.
According to the official, two houses are on fire, and three cars have been damaged.

title: Russia Launches Missile and Drone Attacks, Killing 2 in Kyiv and 4 in Kharkiv Despite Trump’s Ceasefire Claim
body:
Russian forces launched a massive wave of missile and drone attacks across Ukraine overnight on Oct. 12-13, killing two women in Kyiv and four people in Kharkiv, where a missile strike destroyed part of a four-story apartment building.
The attacks continued despite US President Donald Trump’s claim that Kyiv and Moscow had agreed to an energy ceasefire, an arrangement neither side had publicly confirmed.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
In Kyiv, Russia struck with six ballistic missiles late Monday, hitting transport and warehouse facilities hours after a drone slammed a residential complex, killing two women and wounding nine people.
In Kharkiv, Russian missiles devastated residential neighborhoods, destroying an entire entrance section of a four-story apartment building. Three people were rescued from the rubble.
Ukraine’s Air Force said the ballistic missiles targeted several districts at around 10:10 p.m. local time.
Ukrainian radar detected the incoming missiles, but the military said it had received no advance information about launches from Russian territory.
The Air Force said it was investigating the circumstances, while the missile types had not yet been established.
The attacks continued late into the night, with renewed warnings of incoming Russian drones.
Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko confirmed missile impacts in two districts on the capital’s left bank.
In the Dniprovskyi district, a missile struck a transport infrastructure facility, while another hit a four-story warehouse in the Desnianskyi district.
Emergency services were dispatched to both locations, Klitschko reported on Telegram .
Earlier Monday, a Russian drone struck the courtyard of a residential complex in Kyiv’s Darnytskyi district, causing fires inside the building and igniting parked vehicles.
Ukraine’s National Police confirmed that two women, aged 39 and 59, were killed and nine people wounded, including a minor.
Investigators, explosives specialists and emergency crews worked at the scene, documenting damage and collecting evidence, according to the official police statement .
Earlier in the day, Russian drone strikes and falling debris damaged homes and other civilian buildings across several Kyiv districts.
Police reported damage in six districts, including three private homes in Darnytskyi and two preschools in Solomianskyi and Shevchenkivskyi districts.
Children and staff at both educational institutions had taken shelter, preventing casualties there.
At 11:17 p.m., authorities warned of another drone threat, urging Kyiv residents to remain in shelters.
In northeastern Ukraine, Russian missile strikes on Kharkiv late Monday left four people dead and 41 injured, according to Ukraine’s State Emergency Service (DSNS).
At first, in a report issued at 7:40 a.m., rescuers said the bodies of three people had been recovered from the rubble.
The attack struck the Kholodnohirskyi and Shevchenkivskyi districts, destroying an entire entrance section of a four-story residential building.
Four additional fires in the Kholodnohirskyi and Shevchenkivskyi districts have been extinguished.
Kharkiv Regional Military Administration head Oleh Syniehubov said Russia had used approximately 10 Banderol-type missiles, according to preliminary information.
Among the wounded was a 19-year-old man admitted to intensive care with severe burns. Another seriously injured man required surgery.
At least 10 private homes were damaged in Kholodnohirskyi district.
In Shevchenkivskyi district, a separate strike hit a five-story apartment building, triggering fires in a ground-floor bank premises and nearby vehicles.
Overall, the massive Russian missile attack has killed three people and injured at least 15 others, including one rescuer. Four people have been rescued.
In a report issued at 12:22 p.m., the State Emergency Service said the death toll from a Russian missile strike on a residential building in the city’s Kholodnohirskyi district had risen to four. Another 41 people were injured.
“Search and rescue operations are ongoing. Information is being updated,” the report added.
Elsewhere in Kharkiv region, Russian drones struck the city of Lozova on Monday, killing a 71-year-old woman and leaving seven people suffering from acute stress, including a nine-year-old girl.
Two fires broke out in residential areas after the strikes, according to emergency officials.
Prosecutors said preliminary evidence indicated that Russia had used two Geran-3 drones.
In southern Ukraine, a Russian Shahed-type drone struck a cargo terminal in Mykolaiv, damaging a logistics facility and sparking a fire.
Emergency crews extinguished a blaze covering approximately 500 square meters. No casualties were reported, according to regional authorities.
In Sloviansk, Donetsk region, Russian forces carried out another strike while emergency crews were extinguishing a fire caused by an earlier attack.
A woman was injured and 44 residential buildings were damaged, according to the State Emergency Service.
The attacks reached western Ukraine early Tuesday, when a downed Russian drone fell onto a residential building in the village of Murovane, near Lviv.
According to Lviv Regional Military Administration head Maksym Kozytskyi, the incident occurred during an air raid alert.
Two houses caught fire, and three vehicles were damaged.
No casualties had been reported at the time of the initial update, while emergency services worked at the site.
The strike brought the overnight destruction to western Ukraine, far from the front lines, as Russian drones continued threatening residential communities across the country.
Russian forces also attacked Rivne and surrounding areas on Monday evening, damaging residential buildings and civilian facilities.
Regional Military Administration head Oleksandr Koval said a nonresidential building was damaged in Rivne, with no casualties initially reported.
In Sarny district, several strikes hit a nonoperational industrial facility. Residential buildings and dormitories were also damaged.
Koval urged residents near the impact sites to move at least 100 meters away while authorities assessed the damage.
The latest strikes followed an attack on Rivne region on Sunday, Oct. 11, which wounded three people.
The nationwide attacks followed US President Donald Trump’s announcement on Sunday, Oct. 11, that Ukraine and Russia had agreed to an energy ceasefire – a claim neither government had publicly confirmed.
During his evening address Monday, President Volodymyr Zelensky condemned Russia’s continuing strikes and urged Washington to act decisively.
“It is Russia that continues these brutal strikes. It is Russia that is prolonging the war. Even now, in response to the American proposal, it is sending Shahed drones,” Zelensky said.
“We hope the United States will recognize these signals from Russia and act decisively. Strength is needed to force Russia to end this war,” he added.
Zelensky said Ukraine was prepared to suspend long-range attacks on Russian oil refineries and export facilities if Moscow stopped targeting Ukrainian energy infrastructure.
But Russia’s continued strikes raised questions about whether the Kremlin intended to observe any reciprocal ceasefire.
The attacks also came amid controversy over Washington’s decision to temporarily ease restrictions on Russian diesel exports, despite Ukraine’s calls for stronger economic pressure on Moscow.
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: Kazakhstan Can Build on Its Strengths, Advance Digital Entrepreneurs, Says NVIDIA’s VP
body: The Astana Times provides news and information from Kazakhstan and around the world. ASTANA – Kazakhstan can turn its strengths in energy, mining, transport and industrial operations into an AI competitive advantage by investing in infrastructure, encouraging local talent and supporting entrepreneurs. In an interview with The AT, NVIDIA Vice President of Physical AI Simulation Rev Lebaredian said access to intelligence will influence where companies are built, where research happens and how productive an economy can become. President Tokayev holds meeting with NVIDIA VP Lebaredian in Astana on October 1. Photo credit: Akorda. During his visit to Kazakhstan this October, Lebaredian held talks with President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev about the company’s plans for Kazakhstan’s AI infrastructure development, as the nation has already launched two supercomputer clusters based on NVIDIA technologies. The country has emerged as the second market for US-based AI infrastructure company Firebird and NVIDIA, which are developing a computing facility in Ekibastuz. The project envisages developing computing infrastructure with a capacity of approximately 300 megawatt, with the potential to expand to 1 gigawatt. Rev Lebaredian. In a Q&A interview below, Lebaredian discussed the infrastructure needed to support the transition, the opportunities AI agents and physical AI offer local businesses and why access to computing, practical education and opportunities for young entrepreneurs to solve real-world problems will be critical to building a sustainable AI ecosystem. Kazakhstan is developing its AI ecosystem, from public-sector digitalization to private-sector innovation. From NVIDIA’s perspective, what are the country’s key strengths today, and what capabilities could be strengthened further as Kazakhstan develops its AI ecosystem? Kazakhstan is thinking about AI at the level of national development. President Tokayev’s vision recognizes that this technology will shape the economy and the opportunities available to the next generation. The country has energy resources, substantial industries and people who understand difficult physical problems. Mining, energy, manufacturing and logistics are all places where AI can create tremendous value. The next step is to connect those strengths. Computing infrastructure should be accessible to entrepreneurs, researchers and students. Industrial companies should become customers and development partners for local teams. Universities should give people opportunities to build with technology. I would put particular emphasis on entrepreneurship. A country captures more of the opportunity when its people create the products and companies that others use. Kazakhstan has an opportunity to develop that capability and serve markets far beyond its borders. AI infrastructure is becoming a critical factor in a country’s ability to develop and deploy AI. What infrastructure does Kazakhstan need to build or strengthen — including computing capacity, data centers and networking — to support the next stage of its AI development? AI is becoming essential infrastructure. Access to intelligence will influence where companies are built, where research happens and how productive an economy can become. You have to think about the whole system: energy, chips, infrastructure, models and applications. Power and cooling enable the computers to operate. Networking connects them into an AI factory. Software and models turn that capacity into something people can use. An AI factory produces intelligence. That intelligence can power agents doing useful work across an economy—helping design products, develop software, serve customers and operate industrial systems. Infrastructure investment creates the foundation for that productive activity. Kazakhstan also needs people who can design, operate and continually improve these systems. And it needs access models that put the capacity within reach of small teams. The value of the infrastructure grows with what people build on top of it. Beyond infrastructure, what opportunities do you see for Kazakhstan’s local technology companies, startups and researchers to develop AI solutions of their own? Are there particular sectors where Kazakhstan could build distinctive capabilities? Start with problems Kazakhstan understands deeply. The country’s experience in energy, mining, transport and industrial operations is a source of valuable knowledge. A team that understands how a mine works could develop intelligence for autonomous equipment. Researchers working on materials or energy systems could build AI tools that help engineers explore designs much faster. A logistics company could turn its operational knowledge into software used across many markets. AI agents expand who can participate. People with deep knowledge of an industry will increasingly be able to direct agents to build software, construct simulations and test ideas. Their expertise becomes much more powerful when they can translate it into a working system. That opens the door to a new generation of entrepreneurs. The ambition should be to solve important problems in Kazakhstan and build companies that serve the world. Your work at NVIDIA focuses heavily on Omniverse and simulation technologies. How could digital twins, simulation and physical AI be applied in Kazakhstan — for example, across industry, energy, mining, logistics, urban planning or other areas of the economy? Simulators are time machines. They let us explore possible futures before committing to one in the physical world. You can test how a factory will operate before building it. You can explore changes to a mine without interrupting production. You can train an autonomous machine through situations it might take years to encounter in reality. Physical AI depends on that capability. Robots and autonomous systems need a place to learn, practice and be tested. We need to understand how they will behave before putting them around people and valuable equipment. Until now, building these simulated worlds has required specialized skills and a great deal of manual work. AI agents are beginning to remove that barrier. With simulation libraries and the right tools, agents can help write the software, construct environments and run experiments. The direction is clear: everyone should be able to build and use a simulation. Someone who understands a physical problem should be able to describe what they want to investigate and work with an agent to test it. The results still need to be validated against reality. But the ability to ask and explore those questions can reach far more people. That is a profound opportunity for a country with Kazakhstan’s industrial base. As Kazakhstan looks to strengthen its role in the regional AI ecosystem, what capabilities would help it become a place where developers and companies build AI products and services, rather than simply consume AI technologies? Build a culture of creation, and give people the means to act on it. Computing access, strong education, open models, software tools and capital all matter. So do customers willing to work with a young company and institutions willing to let people experiment. Education should give people the confidence and ability to create. Put powerful tools in students’ hands. Have them build things, test ideas and solve real problems. Connect them with engineers and companies so they can see where their knowledge can take them. At NVIDIA, we build platforms that others can build on. AI agents are extending that opportunity to far more people. Someone with deep knowledge of an industry will increasingly be able to turn an idea into software or a simulation without having to master every underlying technology. Kazakhstan can develop a generation of entrepreneurs around that capability. The ambition should be that a young person in Kazakhstan can imagine something important, build it from home and bring it to the world. The post Kazakhstan Can Build on Its Strengths, Advance Digital Entrepreneurs, Says NVIDIA’s VP appeared first on The Astana Times .

title: Armenia, Azerbaijan, and Georgia, top stories this morning
body:
News in Georgia , Armenia , and Azerbaijan . Key headlines and top stories covered by local media, from 12-16 October, 2026
● The opening ceremony of the Leaders’ Summit, held as part of the 17th Conference of the Parties to the Convention on Biological Diversity (COP17), took place in Yerevan. UN Secretary-General António Guterres arrived to attend the event. The summit begins its work today.
COP17 will run from 19 to 30 October under the slogan “Acting for Nature”. The official negotiating venue for delegations, intergovernmental bodies and experts will be the so-called Blue Zone at the Meridian Expo Centre. The Green Zone, located at the Karen Demirchyan Sports and Concert Complex, will host open discussions for anyone interested, including residents of Armenia and the thousands of visitors, scientists and media representatives expected to arrive in the country. Around 15,000 participants and guests from across the world are expected to attend, including representatives of the 196 parties to the Convention.
● At a meeting with Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan, UN Secretary-General António Guterres thanked Armenia for the excellent organisation of COP17.
“I would like to congratulate Armenia on this. My colleagues tell me that it is always difficult to reach a common statement or agreement during negotiations. Armenia has demonstrated exceptional diplomatic skills, working wonders in bringing together different opinions and points of view,” he said.
Guterres also stressed the importance of establishing peace between Armenia and Azerbaijan, highlighting Pashinyan’s personal contribution to the process.
● “The war against nature is not over, and we continue to witness the very serious consequences of three global crises: climate change, biodiversity loss and pollution. They are all interconnected,” the UN Secretary-General said at a press conference ahead of COP17.
● Louise Mushikiwabo, Secretary-General of the International Organisation of La Francophonie, has also arrived in Yerevan. At a meeting with Prime Minister Pashinyan, she welcomed Armenia’s hosting of COP17 and expressed confidence that the conference would raise the country’s international profile. Mushikiwabo and Pashinyan also discussed preparations for the 10th International Francophonie Games, which Armenia will host in 2027.
● Deputy Prime Minister Mher Grigoryan met a delegation led by Haoliang Xu, UN Assistant Secretary-General and Associate Administrator of the UN Development Programme (UNDP). Grigoryan praised Armenia’s strategic cooperation with UNDP in the fields of human rights and democratic institutions, energy efficiency, water resource management and disaster risk reduction.
● Ignazio Cassis, the current Chairperson-in-Office of the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE) and head of Switzerland’s Federal Department of Foreign Affairs, has arrived in Yerevan. During meetings with Armenia’s foreign minister and prime minister, he welcomed the establishment of peace with Azerbaijan and expressed hope that a peace agreement would be signed as soon as possible.
● Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian also arrived in Armenia this morning to attend COP17.
● During a working visit to Washington, Armenian Deputy Defence Minister Karen Brutyan met Mary Beth Morgan, director of the US Defense Security Cooperation Agency (DSCA). The two discussed Armenian-US defence cooperation.
● “I consider the signing and ratification of a peace agreement between Armenia and Azerbaijan the most important task ahead of us. This does not mean that we are abandoning any other agenda, but this is the goal I have set for myself. The specific timeframe is to complete the process by 2031. I see that this is possible,” Nikol Pashinyan said at his weekly briefing.
● Foreign Minister Ararat Mirzoyan has assured journalists that Armenia’s new special representative for the normalisation of relations with Turkey will be announced once a candidate has been selected.
“Frankly speaking, the need to appoint a new special representative remains an open question, as it may turn out that the border with Turkey opens before an agreement is reached on appointing new representatives,” he said.
Before Armenia’s parliamentary elections in June 2026, Ruben Rubinyan served as Armenia’s special representative. He has since become speaker of parliament, and a new appointment is therefore expected.
● Russia has received no requests from Armenia or Azerbaijan to participate in the Trump Route (TRIPP) transit project, but both countries are aware of Moscow’s willingness to take part, Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov has said.
“We have welcomed the process of normalising relations between Armenia and Azerbaijan. We welcomed the agreement reached in Washington. We are ready to participate in infrastructure projects, as we have said repeatedly. Russian Railways holds a concession and operates through the South Caucasus Railway. We are familiar with all this infrastructure, and it is maintained and operated using our technology,” Lavrov said.
Context. Armenia’s railway network is managed under a concession by South Caucasus Railway, which is a wholly owned subsidiary of Russian Railways. The concession agreement runs for 30 years. Since the Russian company took over management, however, freight traffic has halved, some routes have ceased operating, and the investment commitments have remained unfulfilled.
Armenian experts therefore see no justification for extending the Russian concession. The Armenian authorities, who previously shared this view, have recently sought to avoid further escalation of tensions with Russia and have softened their rhetoric. More details here.
● The Armenian government has extended subsidies under a programme supporting exporters. The programme was launched after Russia imposed restrictions on Armenian producers. The government is using it to help local exporters gain access to new markets.
● “The government has recognised 100% of the shares in Electric Networks of Armenia (ENA) as being of overriding public interest. In the coming months, a record describing the property to be expropriated will be drawn up, the shares will be valued at market rates, and the current owners will receive compensation equal to the assessed value. As a result, 100% of ENA’s shares will be registered as the property of the Republic of Armenia. Long live the Republic of Armenia!” Romanos Petrosyan, the company’s interim manager, wrote on his Facebook page.
ENA’s former owner was Russian businessman Samvel Karapetyan, who is under house arrest in Yerevan on charges of calling for a seizure of power, money laundering and large-scale tax evasion.
● “Our Plan A is to make ENA a state-owned company and transfer its management to one or more leading international companies. We have no intention of privatising it. If, for objective reasons, we are unable to implement Plan A, we will move on to discussing other plans,” Nikol Pashinyan said.
● President Ilham Aliyev made strong statements at the seventh summit of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence Building Measures in Asia (CICA), held in Baku. Among other things, he said:
Azerbaijan pursues an independent foreign policy based on respect for the territorial integrity of other states.
Aliyev accused international organisations and Western institutions of applying double standards to the conflict between Azerbaijan and Armenia. He said they had ignored the fact that around 20% of Azerbaijan’s internationally recognised territory had been under Armenian occupation for 30 years, while more than one million Azerbaijanis had been expelled from their lands.
Four UN Security Council resolutions demanding the immediate, complete and unconditional withdrawal of Armenian forces from the occupied territories had never been implemented.
The activities of the OSCE Minsk Group, established in 1992 to resolve the conflict, were merely a pretence at mediation.
International inaction had contributed to the continuation of the conflict.
All three former presidents of Armenia and their supporters were war criminals and child-killers who had still not received the punishment they deserved.
In 2019, Armenia’s current prime minister said in what was then occupied Karabakh: “Karabakh is Armenia, period.” Armenia’s defence minister had threatened Azerbaijan with a new war to seize additional territories. The international community had not reacted.
No one had ever condemned Armenia for the occupation, war crimes, ethnic cleansing and mass killings, or for the desecration of the Azerbaijani people’s religious shrines.
The European Parliament and the Council of Europe had encouraged the aggressor — Armenia.
During the 44-day war in 2020 and the military operation in September 2023, Azerbaijan restored its territorial integrity, and the former separatist leaders were brought before an Azerbaijani court.
Until mechanisms are developed to ensure that the decisions of the United Nations and other international organisations are implemented, wars and conflicts will continue and new ones will emerge.
“If sanctions had been imposed on Armenia in good time for occupation, genocide and ethnic cleansing, Azerbaijan would not have had to break the back of Armenian fascism on the battlefield. The impunity enjoyed by the aggressor only made it more audacious.”
Baku offered Armenia peace, and the two countries have been living in peace for just over a year. This peace remains fragile and must be protected and strengthened.
● Leaders of participating countries who addressed the summit made the following statements, among others:
The President of Kazakhstan said that Kazakhstan and Azerbaijan had jointly begun implementing a project to lay a trans-Caspian fibre-optic communications cable along the seabed of the Caspian Sea. Work was also under way to develop the Caspian Green Energy Corridor. Plans had been drawn up to increase Kazakh oil supplies through the Baku–Tbilisi–Ceyhan pipeline. The president proposed that Central Asian countries and Azerbaijan jointly promote the establishment of an International Water Organisation under the United Nations.
The President of Israel said Azerbaijan had made CICA more active during its chairmanship. He described Azerbaijan as a country that develops regional partnerships, promotes tolerance, strengthens trust between states and strives to build a better future.
The President of Laos proposed developing a railway corridor based on the Laos–China railway, extending it through Central Asia into the wider Eurasian region, including Azerbaijan.
● Russia has received no requests from Armenia or Azerbaijan regarding its participation in the regional transit project known as the Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity (TRIPP), but both countries are aware of Russia’s readiness to take part, Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov told journalists in Baku. He stressed that the state-owned company Russian Railways holds the concession to manage Armenia’s railway system, adding that “Russia is therefore very familiar with the region’s infrastructure”.
● Azerbaijan’s Foreign Ministry has summarised the results of the seventh CICA summit held in Baku. The outcomes included the adoption of the Baku Declaration and a statement on cooperation in healthcare and occupational safety; Laos joining CICA as its 29th full member; The extension of Azerbaijan’s chairmanship for 2026–2028; The appointment of Ambassador Sultan Hajiyev as the organisation’s secretary-general for 2026–2030; Cambodia’s ratification of the Convention on the Privileges and Immunities, completing the process required for the document to enter into force.
● The presidents of Azerbaijan and Kazakhstan officially inaugurated the Trans-Caspian fibre-optic cable line online on the sidelines of the seventh summit. “This is a global project that will be used by all countries of Central Asia and the South Caucasus, as well as by a wider geographical area,” Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev said at the ceremony. “This is not a transport corridor, but something new that fits into the modern era of digitalisation. It is an entirely new form of cooperation,” Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev said.
● President Ilham Aliyev met with the Turkish foreign minister and the Emir of Qatar, who were attending the seventh CICA summit.
● A total of 13.2 billion manats (approximately $8 billion) is planned to be allocated from Azerbaijan’s state budget in 2027–2030 for the restoration and reconstruction of the Karabakh and East Zangezur economic regions — territories Azerbaijan regained from Armenian occupation as a result of the 2020 Second Karabakh War. According to the Ministry of Finance, these expenditures will account for 24.1% of total capital spending.
● Russian rapper Navai, who is of ethnic Azerbaijani origin, has been arrested in Kazakhstan. A narcotic substance was found in his car during an inspection at a border checkpoint as he entered Kazakhstan from Kyrgyzstan. His lawyer said the rapper had been placed in detention for two months. The Russian Consulate General has sent a diplomatic note to Kazakhstan’s Foreign Ministry.
● The Prosecutor’s Office has charged crime figures Vato Kipiani, Avtandil Bilanishvili and Shota Kipiani with group violence. Bilanishvili, known by the nickname “Katsro”, has become the subject of social media speculation over his possible links to the ruling party. According to the investigation, they physically assaulted a man at a restaurant in Tbilisi on 14 October. The Ministry of Internal Affairs confirmed the detention of Vato Kipiani and Avtandil Bilanishvili. The charge carries a prison sentence of up to two years. The alleged links between all three suspects and elite circles have long been widely discussed in Georgian media and on social media, and their arrests have caused a major stir.
● Parliament Speaker Shalva Papuashvili met with the speakers of the Italian and Cypriot parliaments in Rome during a conference of speakers of parliaments from Council of Europe member states. According to the parliamentary press service, the discussions focused on Georgia’s relations with the European Union and interparliamentary cooperation. Representatives of Italy and Cyprus reaffirmed their support for Georgia’s European future. Papuashvili spoke about the importance of resuming dialogue with the EU.
● Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze attended the official opening ceremony of the 17th Conference of the Parties to the UN Convention on Biological Diversity in Armenia. According to the Government Administration, following the event, the leaders of participating countries were hosted at an official reception by Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan and President Vahagn Khachaturyan.
● Economy Minister Mariam Kvrivishvili said, following meetings held in the United Arab Emirates, that the parties had discussed opportunities to expand trade and exports of Georgian products. According to her, investors are interested in Georgia’s energy, construction, tourism and logistics sectors. The meetings also addressed Georgia’s role in the Middle Corridor transit route. Kvrivishvili said the government plans to develop transport infrastructure and significantly increase cargo turnover. The minister did not specify the units of measurement for the projected increase or the timeframe for achieving the targets.
● It has only now emerged that a prisoner died in a Kutaisi prison on 9 October. According to the Special Penitentiary Service, he fell face down from the upper level of a bunk bed in a six-person cell. His cellmates called for help. The service said a doctor arrived at the scene immediately, but the prisoner could not be saved. An investigation into the incident has been launched. The exact cause of death remains unknown.
● Parliament Speaker Shalva Papuashvili said that a possible ban on opposition parties would strengthen democracy in Georgia. According to him, “there is no place in a democratic party landscape for parties that are hostile to the constitution”. Papuashvili cited Ukraine, Moldova and Germany as examples of countries where, in his view, mechanisms exist to ban anti-constitutional parties. He said that if the Constitutional Court agreed with the ruling party’s arguments and banned the opposition parties, society would only benefit. The court has not yet issued a ruling.
● Shalva Papuashvili accused the European Union of worsening its relations with Georgia. He said the failure to invite representatives of the Georgian government to the EU enlargement forum showed that Brussels was obstructing dialogue. Papuashvili accused EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas of being “superficial” and described the EU’s foreign policy as immature. He also accused former Georgian Public Defender Nino Lomjaria of facilitating foreign interference in the 2024 parliamentary elections, but provided no evidence to support the allegation. According to the list published by the European Commission, representatives of the Georgian government are not among the participants in the enlargement forum.
● Viktor Japaridze, a member of the pro-government parliamentary political group People’s Power, has reportedly sold the television channel PostTV, known for its reputation as a pro-government propaganda outlet, for a symbolic sum of 1,000 lari (around $400). Lawyer Abesadze wrote on social media that the sale was probably linked to the ongoing conflict within the ruling Georgian Dream party, adding that further details would be announced later. At this stage, the available information contains no official confirmation of the transaction or the identity of the new owner.
● David Okitashvili, president of the Georgian Chamber of Culture and an outspoken supporter of the ruling party, has called on the Prosecutor’s Office to investigate the costs of the funeral of Catholicos-Patriarch Ilia II. In an interview with PalitraNews, he said the public had a right to know how the money had been spent. Okitashvili accused the former culture minister of putting pressure on representatives of the cultural sector and alleged that the former minister had enjoyed the patronage of former Deputy Prime Minister Mamuka Mdinaradze. According to Okitashvili, the Prosecutor’s Office has not contacted him so far. His claims have not been independently verified. Read more here.
● A court has allowed former Deputy Head of the State Security Service Levan Akhobadze, who is accused of receiving a particularly large bribe, to pay bail of 500,000 lari (approximately $200,000), secured by property. The court had previously replaced his detention with bail and given him 30 days to pay the amount. According to the investigation, Akhobadze initially demanded 500,000 lari in exchange for helping a businessman recover money, but later agreed to accept half that amount. If convicted, he faces between 11 and 15 years in prison.
● Brothers Davit and Guram Kakulia, who are accused of organising a contract killing on the orders of crime boss Niko Kvaratskhelia, deny the charges and are seeking to have the case dismissed. Davit Kakulia called on the Kvaratskhelia family to file a complaint, while Guram Kakulia said he would refuse to attend future court hearings. The brothers have declined a jury trial. The court has referred the case for a substantive hearing, which is due to begin on 29 October. The arrest warrant issued in absentia for another defendant in the case, Besarion Zhvania, remains in force. He is wanted internationally. The Prosecutor’s Office has also ordered psychiatric and psychological assessments of the Kakulia brothers; the results are not yet known.
● Zurab “Girchi” Japaridze, one of the leaders of the Coalition for Change, was forcibly returned to Georgia from Turkey. He had been travelling to Brussels to attend a Renew Europe leaders’ summit, but was denied entry to Turkey and detained at an airport on 15 October. Japaridze said he had only learned then that he had been banned from entering Turkey since November 2025. According to him, Turkish officials explained that they had received information about him from official Georgian authorities. This claim has not been independently confirmed. News of his detention was first reported by the European political alliance Alliance of Liberals and Democrats for Europe (ALDE).
● A man in Zestafoni has been arrested on suspicion of robbing 12 graves. According to the Ministry of Internal Affairs, he stole metal components from grave fences and sold them to a scrap metal collection point. Police seized the stolen items as evidence. The investigation is being conducted under an article concerning disrespect for the deceased and the illegal possession of items taken from graves. The offence carries a prison sentence of up to two years.
● Georgian director Levan Koguashvili will receive a Golden Globe award in the Pioneer category. The award ceremony will take place in Tashkent on 23–24 October as part of the event “Golden Globe: The Silk Road”. Koguashvili will be honoured for his contribution to the development of regional cinema. The director is known for his films Street Days , Blind Dates and Brighton 4th . His new film, Guria , was presented at the 2026 Venice Film Festival and is Georgia’s candidate for the Academy Awards.
The poster features a photo of Mzia Amaglobeli, a prominent journalist convicted for slapping a police officer who had insulted her. Her words, “Fight before it’s too late,” are printed on the poster.
● UN Secretary-General António Guterres has arrived in Armenia to attend COP17, an international environmental summit held under the auspices of the United Nations.
● Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Trade Robert Abisoghomonyan commented on whether the issue of the return to Armenia of ethnic Armenians held in prisons in Azerbaijan would be raised during COP17. “The Foreign Ministry has repeatedly stated that it raises this issue on various platforms, and it may also be discussed during bilateral meetings with senior delegations arriving for COP17. However, this issue falls within the humanitarian agenda and is addressed through the relevant organisations. The COP17 summit is primarily devoted to environmental matters,” Abisoghomonyan said.
● Armenia and Russia will establish a working group to address issues concerning the operation of the Armenian railway, which is managed by Russia under a concession agreement. This was announced in a statement following a meeting in Yerevan between Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan, members of the government and Oleg Belozyorov, CEO of Russian Railways. Yerevan has been saying for several months that the concession agreement is causing Armenia to lose its competitive advantages, as Western partners are reluctant to use railways under Russian management. Armenia has proposed transferring the management to a third country acceptable to both Armenia and Russia. However, Belozyorov told journalists that the possibility of transferring the concession to another country had not been discussed. The main focus was on fulfilling the obligations under the concession agreement. “Views were exchanged on railway reconstruction projects on the Gyumri–Akhurik–Turkey border section and the Yeraskh–Nakhchivan section, which runs towards the border with Azerbaijan,” the press release said. “We are open to dialogue with the Armenian government and to a joint assessment of the effectiveness of the concession agreement. For our part, we intend to firmly uphold all the commitments we have undertaken,” Belozyorov said. According to the Russian company’s press release, investment in Armenia’s railways during the concession period has amounted to around $400 million. No dividends have ever been paid to the shareholder, and all profits have been reinvested in railway development.
● Nikol Pashinyan has posted a video on his social media page outlining what peace should look like after the peace agreement between Armenia and Azerbaijan has been signed and ratified. “Armenia should have a territory of 29,743 square kilometres, and border delimitation and demarcation should proceed on this basis, in accordance with the logic of the Alma-Ata Declaration,” adopted during the dissolution of the Soviet Union, the prime minister said.
● Nikol Pashinyan has also commented on Armenian and Azerbaijani enclaves and exclaves located on each other’s territories. In his view, there should be none. “The two countries, Armenia and Azerbaijan, should exchange territories of precisely defined sizes. All roads and communication routes should be open, and the countries should make no demands of each other and leave each other alone on all issues. No demands, including those concerning Karabakh or Western Azerbaijan. The most important question now is whether it is actually possible to achieve such a vision of peace. Following my meeting with the president of Azerbaijan in Turkmenistan, I formed a preliminary impression that we have an opportunity to shape peace in this way, and in the near future we will be working to turn this opportunity into reality,” Pashinyan said.
● “Perhaps tomorrow morning we will wake up and see a headline in the news: ‘Armenia-Turkey border is open’. I think the process has already matured considerably,” Foreign Minister and Minister of International Trade Ararat Mirzoyan said while speaking at the Warsaw Security Forum.
● Deputy Environment Minister Ara Mkrtchyan responded to opposition allegations that there had been elements of corruption in the organisation of COP17. He said that, of the 12 companies that had applied to supply goods, a list of the 10 companies that met the established criteria had been submitted to UN experts. The UN experts then conducted the selection process and chose two companies without any involvement by Armenian government agencies. Mkrtchyan also stressed that the prices of goods purchased for the summit could not be compared with ordinary retail prices. “There has been speculation about the prices of chairs, equipment and badges. But the amounts reflect more than the cost of the items themselves. The principle applied is ‘the cost of the product plus a comprehensive service’. The price includes extensive logistics, installation and round-the-clock servicing over 15 days. The quantities were enormous, and the deadlines were three to four times tighter than for ordinary events. In addition, all goods must strictly comply with UN environmental standards — for example, the use of plastic is not permitted,” the minister said. He also emphasised that COP17 would bring not only international prestige but also significant economic benefits. Around 20,000 visitors are expected, and their spending will go directly to the private sector, while a substantial portion of the money paid will return to the state budget in the form of taxes.
● Ruling-party MP Lusine Badalyan was denied entry to Russia, where she was due to attend a meeting of the CIS Interparliamentary Assembly’s Commission on Social Policy and Human Rights. “I was informed that I am banned from entering Russia. The reason is unknown. This is a strange and concerning situation, since I am a member of the national parliamentary delegation and was supposed to carry out my official duties,” Badalyan said.
● A meeting on reforming the migration management system was held under the chairmanship of the prime minister. Interior Minister Arpine Sargsyan recalled that earlier this year, a meeting with the same participants had discussed the citizenship component, with the aim of rethinking the institution of citizenship and linking it to the concept of “Real Armenia”. A draft law proposing amendments to the Law on Citizenship has been developed as part of this concept. The minister noted that Armenia has become a country of destination for migrants in recent years, with a significant influx of people, making migration management a key area of state policy.
● No chairperson was elected to the Constitutional Court, and a new election will be held after neither of the two nominated candidates secured the required number of votes in two rounds of voting.
● Armenia’s Prosecutor General’s Office is seeking the confiscation of real estate and funds belonging to MP Aghvan Vardanyan whose origins cannot be explained by his lawful income.
● From 1 July 2027, citizens of Armenia and other countries with which Kazakhstan has a visa-free regime will need an electronic travel authorisation to enter Kazakhstan. The document will be free of charge and valid for 180 days.
● A six-year-old child riding a scooter collided with a car in Yerevan. The child was taken to hospital, but doctors were unable to save their life.
Video: Camera traps in the Khosrov Forest State Reserve have captured images of bezoar goats.
