title: Ukraine war latest: Russian drones strike Kyiv morning and evening, kills 2, injures 14
body:
Russian drone attacks hit Kyiv twice on Oct. 12, killing one person and injuring at least 14 others, city authorities said.
During an evening attack, a Russian drone struck a 25-story residential building in Kyiv's Darnytskyi District, according to the Kyiv City Military Administration.
A woman was killed in the strike, while 11 people were injured, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said. Earlier in the day, Russia launched a drone attack on Kyiv, injuring three people, including an elderly woman.
Klitschko first said at 11:32 a.m. local time that air defenses were operating in the city.
Drone debris fell in an open area near residential buildings in the Solomyanskyi District of Kyiv and on a house in Darnytskyi District , while in the Pecherskyi District , a fire caused by wreckage of a drone that had crashed near a building was brought under control, Klitschko said.
Yuliia Sheremet, 38, the owner of the house that was damaged in Darnytskyi District, told the Kyiv Independent that her elderly, disabled father was at home when the attack occurred.
Sheremet was working not far away at the time, so she "immediately ran" to her house when she heard explosions and saw the smoke rise.
"And I saw there was no home anymore..."
Her father was injured but survived. Neighbors helped her to get him out. "It's nothing short of a miracle that Dad didn't die today," Sheremet said.
"I'm in shock... It's impossible to live like that, and I don't know how to carry on. We're all exhausted. We need help so that we can defend Ukraine."
Kyiv resident Yana Mohal, 25, woke up to a "horrible and loud" sound in Darnytskyi District, she told the Kyiv Independent. She went outside to see whether she could help Sheremet's father, an "elderly man with a dog," who was trapped in a damaged house.
Mohal added that it was the first time that the Russian attack had struck so close to her.
Russia is regularly attacking Kyiv and other cities across Ukraine. At least 16 people were killed and more than 100 others injured in Kyiv and the surrounding region between Sept. 25 and Oct. 2, according to a Kyiv Independent count based on official reports.
Russia struck a production complex belonging to Ukrainian confectionery company Roshen in Vinnytsia on Oct. 12, the company said.
"Thanks to the timely activation of the warning system and the prompt evacuation, the lives of employees were saved," Roshen said in a statement .
Vinnytsia Oblast authorities earlier reported that a Russian attack had hit a civilian infrastructure facility in the city and caused a fire. More than 50 rescuers and 13 pieces of emergency equipment were deployed to the site, while explosive ordnance specialists inspected the surrounding area. No injuries were reported.
Roshen later confirmed that its Vinnytsia production complex had been hit.
The company rejected claims circulating in Russian media that its facilities were being used to manufacture drones.
"The corporation's enterprises produce confectionery products and do not manufacture drones or other products for military purposes. The production complex in Vinnytsia is a civilian facility," the company said.
The company did not immediately disclose the extent of the damage to the plant.
"Strikes on food industry facilities endanger the lives of civilian workers, destroy production capacity and jobs, and disrupt the supply of goods," Roshen added.
A new model of interceptor drone developed by former Ukrainian Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov has been tested successfully, Fedorov himself claimed on social media, posting video footage of the drone successfully intercepting two Russian Geran-5 drones.
"Our new interceptor is already taking down jet-powered Shaheds over Kyiv. Two Geran-5s down in its first week," Fedorov said .
The development time from conception to the first successful tests was just one month, Fedorov claimed, while the new interceptor was deployed by "Lasar's Group," a special forces unit within the 27th Separate Brigade of Ukraine's National Guard.
The successful test comes as Ukrainian cities are under repeated assault from Russia's new generation of jet-powered drones, especially the Geran-5, which blurs the line between a drone and a cruise missile, according to experts.
"The Geran-5 much more resembles a low-cost cruise missile than a long-range drone like the original Shahed derivatives," Fabian Hoffmann, a senior research fellow at the Norwegian Institute for Defence Studies, told the Kyiv Independent .
The Geran-5 is particularly difficult to engage, flying significantly higher and faster than any of Russia's older drone models, with a maximum speed of 600 km/h (370 mph).
Ukraine's Security Service (SBU) has foiled an alleged Russian plot to bomb a bus carrying Ukrainian soldiers in the northwestern city of Rivne, detaining a 19-year-old student suspected of preparing the attack, the SBU and Rivne Regional Prosecutor's Office said on Oct. 12.
According to the SBU , the suspect planted an improvised explosive device under a bus transporting "an entire unit" of Ukrainian soldiers and installed a remotely accessible camera disguised in a juice box opposite the parking area to monitor the vehicle.
Russian intelligence operatives planned to detonate the bomb once the soldiers boarded the bus and were moving to their permanent deployment location, the SBU said.
The suspect acted in exchange for money after being recruited by Russian intelligence services through Telegram channels offering quick earnings, according to the SBU.
After arriving in Rivne , he allegedly collected the explosives from a hiding place designated by his Russian handler and planted the device under the military vehicle. The explosive device was reinforced with two glass bottles containing flammable liquid, the SBU said.
SBU officers discovered the plot, neutralized the explosives, and detained the suspect at the city's bus station when he attempted to leave for Kyiv . Investigators also seized his phone, which the SBU said he had used to report the planted device to his Russian handler.
The Rivne Regional Prosecutor's Office said the suspect had been formally notified of suspicion of an attempted terrorist attack. A court ordered his detention without bail. If convicted, he faces up to eight years in prison and possible confiscation of property.
Ukrainian defense company Fire Point trolled Russian tech giant Yandex on Oct. 12, after the company reported damage to another of its data centers, disrupting access to its financial services.
"Today, another Yandex data center was damaged," Dima Pirogov, head of Yandex's fintech division, wrote on X on Oct. 11.
Pirogov said the disruption had left many users unable to check their balances, pay for purchases, or transfer money.
"Dima, have you tried turning it off and on again?" Fire Point replied.
The incident follows a series of reported drone strikes on Russian data centers that have disrupted Yandex services.
Yandex's data center in Russia's Vladimir Oblast was completely shut down on Oct. 11 following a reported drone attack, Russian state news agency TASS said, citing the company.
Russia and four other members of the Russian-led Collective Security Treaty Organization (CSTO) have begun joint military exercises in Belarus on Oct. 12, the organization said.
The drills will run from Oct. 12 until Oct. 16 at two training grounds on Belarusian territory, involving more than 1,500 military personnel, over 300 pieces of military equipment, and around 80 drones, according to the CSTO .
Military contingents from Belarus , Russia , Kazakhstan , Kyrgyzstan , and Tajikistan are participating in the exercises.
The drills focus on training CSTO "peacekeeping forces" and involve exercises to respond to biological threats, the organization said.
CSTO Deputy Secretary-General Mirlan Turgunbekov said in an Oct. 11 statement that the exercise is "particularly relevant given the escalating military and political situation."
The CSTO, which was established in 2002, includes Russia, Armenia, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan, and Kyrgyzstan. Russia is by far the most powerful member of the alliance. Armenia is not particpating in the drills.
Belarus has supported Russia's full-scale war against Ukraine by allowing Moscow to use its territory as a staging ground for the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

title: Delta postpones Saudi Arabia launch after deadly airport attacks
body: Delta Air Lines has postponed the launch of its Atlanta–Riyadh flights until March 2027 following deadly attacks on the Saudi capital’s main airport. The airline announced the delay on October 12, 2026, less than two weeks before service was due to begin on October 23. The route would be Delta’s first direct passenger service to Saudi Arabia. Delta said it remained in contact with government and aviation partners, including Saudia and Riyadh Air, as it monitored developments. The decision came a day after the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) urged US airlines and other American aircraft operators to exercise caution when flying to or over Saudi Arabia. The warning, issued on October 11, 2026, cites ongoing military activity and interference with satellite navigation signals. It covers the Jeddah flight information region and remains in effect until December 10, 2026. The FAA said aircraft could face risks at any altitude, including while passing through the airspace or arriving at and departing from airports in Saudi Arabia. The notice advises caution but does not prohibit flights. The warning applies to US airlines and commercial operators, as well as certain FAA-licensed pilots and operators of US-registered civilian aircraft. The notice includes exceptions for operations involving foreign airlines. The action follows repeated Houthi attacks on King Khalid International Airport (RUH) in Riyadh. An October 10 strike killed 13 people and injured more than 300 . Another attack the following day killed one person and injured nearly a dozen. Saudi authorities have extended the airport’s closure until 21:00 GMT on October 17. Airlines including Lufthansa, Air France-KLM and Etihad have canceled services. The European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) also widened its Saudi airspace warning on October 9, 2026. It recommends that operators avoid two designated areas in the southeast and northwest of the Jeddah flight information region and exercise caution elsewhere. EASA said the Houthis’ increasing focus on aviation infrastructure had raised the danger to aircraft on the ground and during takeoff and landing. Missile and drone attacks, along with air-defense activity, also pose risks from falling debris and the possible misidentification of civilian aircraft. EASA advised airlines to keep their risk assessments current and prepare for changes to flight operations at short notice. Its bulletin is valid until November 16, 2026. The post Delta postpones Saudi Arabia launch after deadly airport attacks appeared first on AeroTime .

title: Military homes pilot tests new technology at Pirbright
body: Six refurbished homes at Pirbright are being used to test technologies intended to make service family accommodation warmer and cheaper to run, in a trial the Ministry of Defence describes as the first of its kind for military housing, according to the department . Each of the six carries a different combination of equipment, including solar panels, battery storage, electric heated skirting boards, hot water systems and zero-emission boilers, so the department can work out which combinations deliver the most benefit. All six have also been given modern kitchens, bathrooms, fencing and doors. Feedback from the families living in them will shape investment decisions across the estate. The trial follows a research and development day held earlier this year at which businesses showed technology that might be used in military housing. Sebastian O’Hara, operations director for accommodation at the Defence Infrastructure Organisation, said: “Service families deserve homes that are warm, safe and fit for modern living. “This pilot is the first of its kind for military housing giving us the opportunity to test new technologies in real homes and understand directly from families what makes the biggest difference to their day-to-day lives. The feedback we get from our families will be used to inform investment decisions, shape the future of military housing and ensure we focus on solutions delivering better outcomes for families. “This is about learning what works, listening to our customers and building a better housing service for the future. Through the new Defence Housing Service, we’re driving change across military housing, delivering better homes, raising service standards and putting the needs of Service personnel and their families at the heart of everything we do.” The work forms part of the Defence Housing Strategy, backed by £9.2 billion and intended to see 40,000 military homes modernised, refurbished or rebuilt over the next decade, delivered through the new Defence Housing Service. Separately, 3D scanning is being used to create digital versions of military homes, with around 2,000 properties due to be scanned and digitised over a two-year trial. The intention is to plan repairs and upgrades more efficiently, keep better records across a property’s lifetime and carry out some inspections remotely. A pilot will give families a greater role in signing off repairs and maintenance before jobs are closed, and a code of conduct will set expectations for how staff and contractors treat families. The post Military homes pilot tests new technology at Pirbright first appeared on UK Defence Journal .

title: Sikorsky packs 4 Nomad drones into a single shipping container
body: Sikorsky on Monday introduced a containerized kit that packs four of its Nomad 100 drones and the gear needed to fly them into a single shipping container. The announcement came as the Association of the U.S. Army’s annual meeting opened in Washington. The Nomad 100 fast pack fits four aircraft, mission-command software, power, communications and sustainment equipment inside one standard 20-foot shipping container, the company said in a release. In its planned configuration, two of the aircraft can be mission ready in under 15 minutes, and the other two available within four to six hours, according to Sikorsky. The system is designed to launch without a runway from sites such as naval vessels, tactical vehicle staging areas and improvised landing zones. After a mission, crews can repack the container, load it onto a compatible vehicle and move it to a new site. Depending on how a customer configures it, the kit could support intelligence, surveillance, reconnaissance and targeting missions, as well as light attack and contested logistics, the company said. Sikorsky said the U.S. military needs to rapidly expand its inventory of autonomous aircraft with compact systems that can be deployed, sustained and moved quickly in contested environments. “By packaging aircraft, mission command, communications, power and sustainment into a single containerized system, we are making it easier to move, employ and reposition VTOL UAS capability with urgency and flexibility,” Rich Benton, Sikorsky’s vice president and general manager, said in the release. The Nomad 100 has an 18-foot wingspan and is a Group 3 drone under the Defense Department’s classification system. It uses Sikorsky’s rotor blown wing design, which pairs a helicopter’s vertical lift and hover with the speed, range and endurance of a fixed-wing aircraft, and it flies with the company’s MATRIX autonomy software . The company has not released the Nomad 100’s payload, range or endurance. Sikorsky developed the aircraft with funding from the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency, or DARPA, under its Early VTOL Aircraft Demonstration program, known as EVADE. In July, Sikorsky said it had finished initial ground and flight testing of the Nomad 100 and would next put the drone through an intensive flight test campaign at a government facility. The company said DARPA chose MATRIX as the autonomy system for all five aircraft in the EVADE program. Sikorsky introduced the Nomad family in October 2025, after an extended flight test of a smaller prototype, the Nomad 50, with a 10.3-foot wingspan. Monday’s release did not say whether a fast pack has been built, or whether any military service has ordered or is evaluating one.

title: Sakana AI's self-improving model gets better at solving and judging, but can't catch its own blind spots
body:
Sakana AI's MASS method lets one language model improve itself by solving tasks, judging results, and refining workflows without a stronger teacher model. The study finds gains across all three roles, but shared blind spots can let errors pass as progress and feed into the next training cycle.
Researchers from Sakana AI and UC Berkeley have introduced "Multi-Agent Self-Supervision" (MASS), a method for recursive self-improvement (RSI). A single language model handles the task, optimizes how the work gets done, and evaluates the results.
At the research frontier, even experts often struggle to judge results because verification can require costly supporting evidence or lengthy experiments, the authors argue. A single plasma study can take more than 120 million CPU hours, according to the paper . Ad
The model itself may therefore be the best available judge, even though it can miss its own mistakes when reviewing its work. Using the same model to solve, check, and revise can reinforce those errors rather than correct them. Ad
Inspired by "Society of Mind," a book by AI pioneer Marvin Minsky, the researchers focus on how the model divides up the work. In MASS, a workflow is text appended to the prompt that defines each sub-agent's role and instructions. A "contract" specifies what information each sub-agent must return and which checks it must perform, while a "hop" sets the order of calls.
An orchestrator distributes the work among the sub-agents. When testing a trading strategy against historical prices, for example, the data specialist's contract must ensure the strategy uses only information available at each point in time. Ad
During the inner loop, the model's weights stay frozen as the team runs a candidate workflow and the evaluator compares the result against the current "champion." The optimizer uses that feedback to propose the next workflow, mainly by changing contracts and hops. In the outer loop, the champion runs 18 times per task, with the model ranking the results itself and selecting up to 15 runs for training.
The researchers remove the workflow text from the orchestrator's initial prompt in the training examples so the model learns to organize work based on the task alone. Specific assignments to sub-agents remain in the recorded traces, and the model takes on all three roles again after LoRA fine-tuning. Ad
The base model is Qwen3.6-27B , with Qwen Code as the harness . The researchers use twelve research tasks generated by GPT-5.5 across finance, robotics, and pharmaceuticals, reserving three for testing and nine for training. Only eight yield training data because the search finds no workflow that beats the reference on one training task. Ad
On the test tasks, the win rate against the base model rises from 53.9 percent after one round to 69.9 percent after two. On MLR-Bench, DSBench, ScienceAgentBench, and AstaBench, the model reaches 1.2 to 1.6 times the base model's score per output token. Gains in raw scores are sometimes small, with DSBench improving only from 0.473 to 0.482, while scores drop slightly on Terminal-Bench 2.0 and SWE-bench Verified.
The paper's appendix shows that completed MLR-Bench submissions rise from 31 to 50 out of 60, while their average grade falls from 3.07 to 2.88. The delegation tool goes unused in all 180 runs, leaving it unclear whether teamwork explains the gains.
Those gains are no longer statistically significant when results are compared task by task. The authors describe mixed results across research tasks, with AstaBench showing the same pattern.
Although the model trains only on solution traces, its performance in the other two roles improves as well. The self-evaluator's agreement with external judges rises from 73 to 93 percent. Workflows found after one round beat the base model's workflows 64 percent of the time, even when the base model runs both.
Without workflow instructions, the base model delegates to sub-agents in just one of 110 runs, compared with 87 after two rounds. It could already delegate when explicitly instructed, but now does so without being asked.
During optimization, task knowledge shifts into contracts and hops, while roles and instructions become more generic. That finding rests on a small sample of just eight to nine tasks.
Training on team traces produces a model with a 68.3 percent win rate, compared with 64 percent for a single-agent student, using 31 percent fewer training tokens. External judges prefer team results 85.1 percent of the time, though teams produce about 2.4 times as many tokens. When outputs are similar in length, judges prefer team results 80 percent of the time, based on just ten pairs.
The evaluated team runs perform better, but the comparison doesn't establish that delegation alone explains the advantage. Team and single-agent runs also differ in workflow instructions, review instructions, and which successfully completed episodes were selected.
Replacing only the evaluator with GPT-5.5 barely helped; the search progressed much faster only when the optimizer was stronger too. The authors conclude that good feedback helps only when the optimizer can act on it. With Qwen handling all three roles, the search still finds winning workflows for 11 of 12 tasks, but takes longer.
The extent of a workflow rewrite says little about its effect on results, and even byte-identical workflows can produce opposite outcomes. One run won all six external judgments, while another lost all six after the agent got stuck in a loop. The researchers suspect that limiting how much the optimizer changes at each step could help stabilize the search.
After failed simulations in a robotics task, the model had the simulator modified to move objects directly to the target, then reported success. External judges still rated the run positively five out of six times. In another trace used for training, a check passed even though it had returned only invalid values.
The authors see shared blind spots as the potential "Achilles' heel" of recursive self-improvement. If the model misses the same error in all three roles, that error could be accepted as an improvement and baked into the next model. The weakness would then affect both the system and its correction mechanism, prompting the authors to call for independent checks, limits on autonomy, and clear conditions for intervention. The code is publicly available.
Japanese research lab Sakana AI launched a dedicated research lab for recursive self-improvement in June, building on earlier work including the Darwin-Godel Machine and the AI Scientist . Google researchers are pursuing a related approach, automatically optimizing the scaffolding of prompts, workflows, and tools around a fixed model without letting agents overfit to their test tasks.
Vals AI recently found that agent teams cost 1.8 to 5.1 times as much as single agents but performed measurably better in only one of four comparisons. Anthropic showed that models engaging in reward hacking to game their reward systems also learn to deceive and sabotage safety checks.

title: European U740 Variant Of The XQ-58A Valkyrie Has Flown
body: Airbus and Kratos Defense & Security Solutions have completed the first flight of the U740 Valkyrie uncrewed combat aircraft, a Europeanized version of the XQ-58A Valkyrie , advancing their bid to deliver a combat-ready system to Germany by 2029. The flight comes as the German Air Force, or Luftwaffe, moves toward acquiring a new class of jet-powered combat drones, in what could become a major shift in the country’s traditionally limited armed-uncrewed-aircraft capabilities. The ride of the Valkyrie With the successful first flight of the Airbus U740 Valkyrie in Europe, we are one step closer to introducing an operational uncrewed Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA) to the German and other European Armed Forces. The flight achieved all… pic.twitter.com/S2sFrtdmGA — Airbus Defence (@AirbusDefence) October 12, 2026 The flight took place at an unnamed test facility in northern Europe, Airbus announced on October 12. The aircraft conducted a rocket-assisted takeoff, maneuvers at different altitudes, and flight at speeds of up to Mach 0.8. The test also included in-flight mission adjustments, with Airbus reporting that all objectives were met. The U740 Valkyrie uncrewed combat aircraft is prepared for launch. Airbus The next phase will introduce Airbus’ Multi-platform Autonomous Reconfigurable and Secure (MARS) mission system, which is intended to provide the aircraft’s European-controlled software and mission-management architecture. Airbus says MARS will support autonomous operations and coordination between multiple uncrewed aircraft while retaining human oversight of critical decisions. The U740 is based on Kratos’ American-developed XQ-58A , an uncrewed aircraft designed as a relatively affordable combat platform. Airbus is adapting the aircraft with its MARS mission system and presenting the combination as a way to provide Germany with a sovereign European capability without waiting for an entirely new airframe to mature. The U740 Valkyrie on its launch trailer. Airbus Published performance figures for the U740 include a maximum takeoff weight of around 3,000 kilograms (6,600 pounds). Airbus lists a range exceeding 5,000 kilometers (3,100 miles) and a service ceiling of 45,000 feet. It has an internal weapons bay and external payload stations beneath its wings. A U.S. Marine Corps XQ-58A Valkyrie conducts a test flight with a U.S. Air Force F-16. U.S. Air Force photo One distinctive feature is the U740’s rocket-assisted launch capability, which reduces its dependence on conventional runways. The original Valkyrie design is primarily recovered by parachute, but newer versions can take off with rocket assistance and land on a runway, offering greater flexibility in how and where they operate. That could help the Luftwaffe disperse operations or launch aircraft from locations where established airfields are unavailable or under threat. The XQ-58 family has also shown some potential for scaling to different requirements, as detailed in these earlier reports on runway launch and recovery and further platform development . In particular, the U.S. Marine Corps has been exploring ways to expand the XQ-58’s flexibility, including further development of the Valkyrie to meet its own mission requirements . If adopted, the rocket-assisted launch capability would provide an intriguing throwback to practical German studies during the Cold War, in which F-104G Starfighter fighter-bombers used the Zero-Length Launch (ZELL) system to take off from dispersed locations. Airbus says the U740 will be able to operate autonomously or under the direction of crewed fighters such as the Eurofighter . The company sees it as a means of increasing the reach, firepower, and survivability of existing combat aircraft, with uncrewed platforms undertaking higher-risk missions. With the MARS system, Airbus intends to give European customers control over mission applications, data, and key software functions, while enabling autonomous mission execution and coordination between aircraft. This is particularly relevant for Germany, which will likely want to integrate national weapons, sensors, and operational requirements without becoming dependent on a foreign-controlled mission architecture. The U740 Valkyrie. Airbus Since the underlying airframe is American, the degree of sovereignty Germany ultimately obtains will depend on the practical ability to control and modify software, integrate national systems, and support the aircraft throughout its service life. The European flight is an important step for the Valkyrie program, but substantial work remains before it can be considered combat-ready. Mission-system integration, further testing, and the demonstration of effective cooperation with crewed aircraft will be central to meeting the companies’ 2029 target. Another view of the U740 Valkyrie. Airbus The effort is also unfolding as Germany develops its requirements for what has been described in press reports as a Jagdbomberdrohne , or fighter-bomber drone. The precise operational concept has yet to emerge publicly, including whether the Luftwaffe primarily wants an uncrewed aircraft to accompany crewed fighters or a platform capable of conducting independent long-range strike missions. Germany has historically lagged behind several other major military powers in fielding armed uncrewed aircraft. Previous attempts to acquire larger reconnaissance drones encountered major technical and procurement difficulties, while political resistance to armed drones delayed the development of a strike capability for years. The U740 Valkyrie seen moments after launch. Airbus The Luftwaffe’s current larger uncrewed aircraft fleet remains limited to five leased Israeli-made Heron TP medium-altitude, long-endurance drones. Germany is also participating in the Eurodrone program, while uncrewed systems were expected to form part of the wider Future Combat Air System (FCAS), before that Franco-German-led effort hit the buffers earlier this year . A German Air Force Heron TP at Jagel Air Base in 2024. Bundeswehr/Ann-Kathrin Steinbring Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022 and Germany’s subsequent military buildup have intensified pressure to address these gaps. Berlin has set a goal of being ready for war by 2029 , and reports indicate that the Luftwaffe wants a new combat-drone capability on a similarly ambitious timeline. As well as Airbus and Kratos, the emerging competition reportedly includes Anduril, General Atomics partnered with Germany’s INTEC , as well as Lockheed Martin . Boeing and Rheinmetall are meanwhile pitching the larger, Block 3 version of the Australian-developed MQ-28 Ghost Bat , while Helsing and Hensoldt are pursuing the homegrown CA-1 Europa . The CA-1 Europa from the German defense startup Helsing. Helsing The various proposals reflect a broader shift toward uncrewed aircraft that can deliver additional weapons, sensors, and electronic warfare capabilities without putting a pilot at risk. But Germany’s terminology raises an important question about the intended role. A conventional collaborative combat aircraft, or CCA, would be designed to work alongside crewed fighters, extending their reach and providing additional combat mass. A platform intended to operate independently against targets deep inside enemy territory would place greater emphasis on range and survivability. These roles are not mutually exclusive, but the Luftwaffe’s final requirements will shape the aircraft it chooses. Germany may not be looking for a single drone to do everything. One option might be a split high-low approach that could pair more capable, longer-range systems for deep-strike missions with cheaper, attritable collaborative combat aircraft that can fly alongside crewed fighters. At this point, it should also be noted that CCAs could also give older fourth-generation fighters a new lease on life , boosting their lethality and survivability by extending their sensor reach, adding weapons capacity, and allowing uncrewed aircraft to take on more dangerous tasks. Meanwhile, Airbus is also working on its larger U760 Ravenstorm , intended for service in the early 2030s. The Ravenstorm gives Airbus a longer-term path toward a more advanced European-designed uncrewed combat aircraft as it pursues the nearer-term Valkyrie effort. The Airbus U760 Ravenstorm, a combat drone designed to operate alongside fighter aircraft in air-to-air combat, strike missions, and electronic warfare roles. Airbus In the short term, the Luftwaffe will need to determine which capabilities must be available in an initial operational fleet and which can be introduced later. Even an aircraft based on an established design requires substantial integration, testing, training, and infrastructure before it can be employed effectively in combat. Germany’s 2029 target leaves little time for a program that still has to integrate its mission system and demonstrate how the aircraft will be used operationally. That is a particular challenge for the Luftwaffe, which has little experience operating large uncrewed aircraft, let alone jet-powered systems intended for combat. A rear view of the U740 Valkyrie. Airbus The European flight gives Airbus and Kratos a head start in testing the U740 for German requirements, but the next major milestone will be flying it with the MARS mission system. How quickly that work progresses will help determine whether the Valkyrie can meet the Luftwaffe’s timetable. Contact the author: thomas@thewarzone.com The post European U740 Variant Of The XQ-58A Valkyrie Has Flown appeared first on TWZ .

title: Meta releases its first frontier model, Muse Wonder
body:
Meta’s Superintelligence Lab released a pair of new state-of-the-art models on Monday, Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, representing the company’s first attempt at a frontier model.
Where Muse Spark aimed to be a lightweight model that could perform at low latency, the Wonder models are larger and said to be more capable, with higher benchmark scores and better results on complex tasks like coding.
According to Meta’s testing (presented in the model card ), Wonder and Wonder Full achieve comparable benchmark scores to Fable 5.1 and GPT-6 Astra.
“Together, they mark the next step on our scaling ladder and a major leap toward personal superintelligence,” Meta’s blog post about the models reads.
That scale is reflected in the pricing: Accessed through the Meta Model API, Wonder will cost $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output tokens, making it roughly equivalent in cost to GPT-6 Sol or Opus 5.5.
Notably, Wonder Full will only be available to Muse Code subscribers and will not be served through the API. Both models will also be used to power the Muse agent.
In keeping with Meta’s interest in developing personal assistants that can perform tasks over a long period, the company placed particular emphasis on the new models’ ability to retain and synthesize information given by the user, a property Meta calls “active memory.”
To achieve better recall, Meta highlighted the MemoryBench benchmark , which challenges continual learning and memory construction frameworks. According to the company’s testing, Muse Wonder now scores higher on MemoryBench than Fable, Opus, or Astra.
“We put a tremendous amount of effort into making sure your model can remember what’s important to you over days, weeks, months, and beyond,” said research scientist Kavya Kopparapu in a video accompanying the launch.
The new models are the first frontier model release since Scale AI founder Alexandr Wang restructured Meta’s AI efforts in August of last year . Since then, Meta has released its lightweight Muse Spark model and Muse agent but has avoided the kind of state-of-the-art model releases OpenAI and Anthropic are known for.
According to the post, the models were trained at Meta’s Prometheus data center in central Ohio , which came online earlier this year.

title: Elon Musk Bragged About His Grok Lego Star Wars Haul. Then X Users Punked Him
body:
It seems that Elon Musk, while crowing on X about how useful his Grok Bot AI agent was in ordering some Lego Star Wars kits on Sunday, managed to reveal via a screenshot to his more than 240 million followers not only the 10-digit Lego order number of his purchase, but also what he paid for the sets, the delivery and billing addresses, the last four digits of his credit card, and the email address his bot used to buy the bricks from Lego.
Faster than the Millennium Falcon making the jump to light speed, the inevitable happened. An X account holder named Enderman posted screenshots of interactions with Lego's customer service chatbot on its website, where the user seemingly managed—using the email and order number Musk kindly, but recklessly, provided—to get the system to cancel Musk's order.
It’s a Trap!
Within a couple of hours—possibly to see whether Enderman's scheme was actually successful—Musk replied and said his order had not been canceled after all.
But by this point, the folly of posting the purchase details on his account must have been evident. For example, another X user went back to Lego's AI assistant, called “Sophia,” and supposedly used the same details to reopen the delivery, this time increasing the order count to 400 and changing the delivery address, all while using Musk's original payment method. “Perfect! I'll get your Lego adventure back on track,” Sophia replied, according to screenshots posted on X.
Upping the ante to 400 sets could be seen as conservative, as a glance at WIRED's Spend Elon Musk’s Money tracker reveals that if you wanted to blow $1 trillion of Musk's cash on plastic bricks, it might have been possible to buy one billion $1,000 Death Star sets, each with 9,023 pieces.
Lego declined to comment when WIRED contacted the company to confirm if such activity took place on Musk's personal Star Wars order. However, internal safeguards for Lego's AI assistant could have flagged unusual activity on the purchase, and so hopefully fleshy humans were tasked with checking the changes.
Attack of the Clones
On Saturday, Musk suggested that Grok could make purchases online with a simple prompt. In this post, Musk suggested that all brave users needed to do to let Grok buy stuff for them was upload a picture of their credit card so the bot could search the web for deals and then complete the purchase. AI companies like Meta and OpenAI have also highlighted the utility of using their respective agents for shopping tasks.
However, at the end of last year, Visa warned about fraud in agentic commerce, advising that bad actors were building legitimate-looking sites that could fool AI agents into purchasing fake items simply by offering gear at super-low prices.
“Once the AI agent completes the purchase … the malicious merchant can harvest payment data and instantly use it for unauthorized transactions,” according to Visa's blog. Visa added that it observed a 25 percent increase “in malicious bot-initiated transactions” in the latter half of 2025, but in the US, this figure jumped to 40 percent.

title: Fighting intensifies in Yemen as Houthis fire on Saudi Arabia
body: Yemen's Houthi rebels launched fresh attacks against Saudi Arabia on Monday, following deadly missile strikes on Riyadh's international airport that killed passengers, some of whom were preparing to board flights to perform Umrah. Saudi authorities extended the suspension of operations at King Khalid International Airport until midnight on October 17 following an attack on Saturday that killed 13 people and injured more than 300, and another on Sunday in which one person was killed. The King Fahd International Airport in Dammam was also hit on Sunday evening, Saudi Arabia 's General Authority for Civil Aviation said, with the damage being assessed. A missile launched at Riyadh by the Yemeni Houthi militia has been intercepted and destroyed, the Saudi-led coalition said. The interception was announced shortly after authorities sounded a threat alarm, followed by three explosions, in the Saudi capital on Sunday night. The strikes came as Yemeni government forces, backed by the Saudi-led coalition, clashed with Houthi rebels on the outskirts of the strategic south-western city of Taiz, repelling fresh attacks amid warnings that a tightening rebel siege is worsening conditions inside the Yemeni city. A military spokesman said on Monday that air strikes prevented the Houthis from sending reinforcements to Taiz. At least 20 people have been killed in a series of attacks since last week on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and the Abha international airport in Saudi Arabia’s Asir province. Saudi state TV broadcast footage of the moment a missile struck the passenger terminal in Riyadh on Saturday, with flashes of light filling the screen as travellers, including pilgrims in white robes, scrambled for cover. Ali, from Hyderabad, was travelling with his family on an Umrah pilgrimage when he was injured in Saturday’s attack. The Indian embassy in Saudi Arabia confirmed his death on Sunday and said it was in contact with his family to help arrange the repatriation of his remains. Etihad Airways cancelled all flights between Abu Dhabi and Riyadh until Monday, October 19, extending disruption to services between the UAE and the Saudi capital into next week. Flydubai has also cancelled Riyadh flights until Wednesday, October 14, while Emirates and Air Arabia services have been affected. The Saudi-led coalition said it responded to drone and cruise missile threats against the kingdom on Monday, as hostilities with the Iran-backed Houthis continued despite diplomatic efforts, including a phone call between the foreign ministers of Saudi Arabia and Iran, which supports the Houthis . The coalition said a missile launched at Riyadh by the Houthis on Monday night was intercepted and destroyed. The interception was announced shortly after authorities sounded a threat alarm, followed by three explosions, in the Saudi capital. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told his Saudi counterpart Prince Faisal bin Farhan that Tehran was ready to "provide assistance" to start talks between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis to reach a "political solution", Iranian state media reported. "The Foreign Minister of our country, expressing concern over the escalation of tensions, emphasised that insisting on a military approach and ignoring political solutions would complicate the existing situation," Mr Araghchi was quoted as saying. Amid the continued attacks on Saudi Arabia, Dr Anwar Gargash, diplomatic adviser to President Sheikh Mohamed, called for stronger Gulf security and collective defence . In his statement posted on X, Dr Gargash said the security of Gulf states as a whole was "indivisible". He stressed that attacks against Saudi Arabia also threatened the wider Gulf. “Targeting our sisterly kingdom of Saudi Arabia undermines the security of the UAE and all Gulf states,” he added. He warned that shortcomings in regional co-operation had contributed to the current challenges. US Central Command chief Adm Brad Cooper said the US and its regional allies were deploying the “largest air-defence umbrella in the world” to deter Iranian attacks, describing the effort as part of an “enduring security architecture” in the Middle East. “It was a vision we discussed with our regional allies and partners,” he told the audience in a recorded message at Trends Global's sixth annual conference in Abu Dhabi on Monday. “Earlier this year, during Operation Epic Fury, we validated at full scale and in actual combat the Middle East Air Defence network known as Mead. “Through our combined efforts, we transformed a concept into the most sophisticated and largest air-defence umbrella in the world,” he added. “For the first time in history, US air defenders stood shoulder-to-shoulder with allies and partners across the Middle East, linking national systems in real time. And so together we intercepted thousands of Iranian attack drones and missiles with an integrated shield built on mutual trust. This is partnership in action.”

title: Trump Defends Russia Diesel Deal as Zelensky Says Moscow Ignores Truce
body:
US President Donald Trump defended his diesel agreement with Russia on Monday, Oct. 12, despite condemnation from both US parties, European allies and Ukraine, latterly which remains under daily Russian terror.
Writing on Truth Social , Trump claimed that the EU had covertly acquired Russian energy valued at $250 billion. However, he did not specify the period or the source of the figure. Rather, he reiterated that he made the right choice striking a business deal with the Kremlin.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
“I made the right choice for the American People – ALWAYS, AMERICA FIRST!” Trump wrote.
By contrast, President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukraine had held off striking Russian energy facilities after Trump announced an energy truce on Oct. 11, while Russia kept attacking the country’s power grid relentlessly.
“I think this was [Russian President Vladimir] Putin’s response to President Trump. And the signals from Russia have been very clear: they know nothing about an energy truce. It is regrettable, because they always find reasons not to stop this war,” Zelensky said in an interview with Fox News on Monday.
The diesel arrangement, announced on Oct. 9 after a phone call between Trump and Putin, would allow Russia to supply up to 4.8 million tons of diesel to US and global markets.
To enable the deal, the US Treasury Department’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued General License 135 the same day. The license authorizes the sale, delivery and import of Russian-origin diesel through April 7, 2027.
Ukraine’s negotiating team, which held US-led talks in Miami on Oct. 9 aimed at ending Russia’s war against Ukraine, remains in daily contact with its American counterparts, Zelensky said .
He made clear that Kyiv expects Washington to step up pressure on Moscow, after recent US moves raised concerns about its strategy and its role in brokering an end to the war.
“As of now, there is no indication that Russia is complying with the conditions announced by the President of the United States,” the Ukrainian President wrote on Telegram.
Russian strikes on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure took place on Oct. 11 and continued on Monday . Air-raid alerts remained in effect nationwide throughout the day as Russia launched Shahed drones and dropped aerial bombs, he said.
“If these strikes are Russia’s response to the statement by the President of the United States, it means that the Russians have squandered another opportunity to bring peace closer,” Zelensky wrote.
In a Fox News interview, Zelensky said Ukraine did not strike any Russian energy facilities overnight because of Trump’s announcement. He declined to say whether that restraint would continue. “We never announce what we will do next as part of our operations,” he said, adding that “more pressure needs to be applied on Russia.”
Kyiv has said it is ready to halt refinery strikes if Moscow stops attacking Ukraine’s grid.
The Kremlin has neither confirmed nor rejected the truce. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said on Monday only that contact on the matter was ongoing. A White House official told Axios that the truce covers only oil refineries.
EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said such an arrangement would favor Moscow, since Ukraine has one refinery while Russia has many.
Meanwhile, US pressure has focused on Kyiv after days of rising tensions.
The Financial Times reported on Oct. 11 that US officials had threatened to suspend the Prioritized Ukraine Requirements List (PURL) – a mechanism for buying American weapons for Ukraine – unless Kyiv stopped striking Russian energy sites.
A day earlier, Trump said Ukraine should get a new president and demanded that Kyiv stop striking Russian refineries, which he blamed for high diesel prices. The global price spike has been widely attributed to the US-Israel war with Iran.
On Oct. 11, Republican Sens. Susan Collins, Lisa Murkowski, Thom Tillis and John Curtis joined Democratic Sens. Jeanne Shaheen and Richard Blumenthal in urging the administration to scrap the diesel deal.
They said the administration had neither consulted Congress nor submitted the justification required by law, the New York Times reported.
“The United States should not provide Putin with a financial lifeline while Russia continues to kill Ukrainian civilians. The Administration must immediately reverse course,” the senators wrote.
Sen. Tillis told NBC’s “Meet the Press” that there is “a legitimate case for saying the president’s not following the law.”
Republican Don Bacon called the deal “a grave error by the president.” Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer described it as a “deal with the devil to try to help his flailing political fortunes.” Lawmakers from both parties have warned that the deal could help fund Russia’s war.
In Europe, Kallas said lifting the sanctions “provides Moscow with more revenues to wage war,” AFP reported.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said on Monday that a similar deal was “out of the question” for Germany and Europe.
The EU also adopted its largest-ever addition to its Russia sanctions list on Monday, consisting of 1,646 new sanctions targeting Russia’s military-industrial complex , including missile supply chains, drone makers, and submarine shipyards.
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: Accessing OpenAI GPT models on Amazon Bedrock with global cross-Region inference in Thailand, Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia, and Taiwan
body:
Single-Region inference can throttle when demand exceeds local capacity. Teams in Thailand, Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia, and Taiwan need access to the newest OpenAI models beyond that capacity. Amazon Bedrock offers OpenAI GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna through global cross-Region inference from all five AWS Regions, and GPT-6 Astra from Asia Pacific (Singapore). This post shows you how to configure the call, set permissions, and monitor inference from your source Region. GPT-6 Sol, GPT-6 Luna, and GPT-6 Astra are all available through global cross-Region inference from the preceding Regions, on the bedrock-runtime endpoint. See Cross-Region inference in the Amazon Bedrock User Guide. For the full list of source and destination Regions in each profile, see Supported Regions and models for inference profiles . In this post, we introduce the global cross-Region inference profiles and invoke them from Asia Pacific (Singapore) using the Converse API, the OpenAI-compatible APIs, and coding clients. We then cover the AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) and service control policy (SCP) configuration, quota management, and monitoring. Global cross-Region inference profiles for OpenAI GPT-6 The GPT-6 family offers three models, each available through global cross-Region inference. GPT-6 Sol brings strong reasoning and coding capabilities to complex tasks performed throughout the week. GPT-6 Luna makes focused, repeatable tasks practical at high volume. GPT-6 Astra handles complex reasoning, coding, and long-document work. All three accept text and image input, client-side tool use, and prompt caching. They differ on reasoning effort. GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna accept none, low, medium, high, xhigh, and max. GPT-6 Astra accepts the same levels except none. For GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna, see Bring more intelligence to everyday work with GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna on Amazon Bedrock . For GPT-6 Astra, see Take on your most ambitious work with GPT-6 Astra on Amazon Bedrock . Global cross-Region inference routes requests across supported commercial AWS Regions where the model is deployed, giving you broad access to Amazon Bedrock capacity. You invoke it by passing a global cross-Region inference profile ID in place of a model ID. Your source Region is where you make the API call. Amazon Bedrock selects the destination Region for processing. Billing, quota tracking, AWS CloudTrail, and Amazon CloudWatch all stay in your source Region. The following table lists the global cross-Region inference profile IDs and the source Regions covered in this post. Global cross-Region inference profiles Source Regions Destination Regions global.openai.gpt-6-sol global.openai.gpt-6-luna Asia Pacific (Singapore) ap-southeast-1 Asia Pacific (Jakarta) ap-southeast-3 Asia Pacific (Malaysia) ap-southeast-5 Asia Pacific (Thailand) ap-southeast-7 Asia Pacific (Taipei) ap-east-2 Supported commercial AWS Regions where the model is deployed global.openai.gpt-6-astra Asia Pacific (Singapore) ap-southeast-1 Supported commercial AWS Regions where the model is deployed Inference profile availability and Region support change as AWS adds Regions and profiles, so confirm both on the model card before you build: GPT-6 Sol , GPT-6 Luna , and GPT-6 Astra . For per-token rates, see Amazon Bedrock pricing . Getting started with OpenAI models on Amazon Bedrock Start with the prerequisites, then invoke any of the three profiles through the Converse API, the OpenAI-compatible APIs, or your existing coding client. Prerequisites An IAM identity with permission to invoke the profile. The IAM policy in the Security and permissions section grants only what these examples need. Your source Region activated. Only the Region you call from needs activating. You do not activate destination Regions, which run on Amazon Bedrock managed capacity. Singapore ( ap-southeast-1 ) is a Region that is enabled by default. Jakarta ( ap-southeast-3 ), Malaysia ( ap-southeast-5 ), Thailand ( ap-southeast-7 ), and Taipei ( ap-east-2 ) are opt-in Regions you must activate first. For more information, see Enable or disable AWS Regions in your account . A current AWS SDK or CLI. The OpenAI-compatible examples also require the OpenAI SDK and the Amazon Bedrock token generator. Install them with pip install boto3 openai aws-bedrock-token-generator . The Amazon Bedrock console lists all three global cross-Region inference profiles under system-defined inference profiles. See Figure 1. Figure 1: The three global OpenAI GPT-6 inference profiles among the system-defined profiles in the Amazon Bedrock console Invoke GPT-6 models through Amazon Bedrock Runtime Each model supports three access paths on this endpoint: the Amazon Bedrock Converse API, the OpenAI Responses API, and the OpenAI Chat Completions API. The OpenAI-compatible APIs are called on the /openai/v1 paths rather than through the AWS SDKs, and the endpoint accepts either Signature Version 4 (SigV4) or an Amazon Bedrock API key. Pass the global cross-Region inference profile ID as the model in every case. Converse API. This example calls GPT-6 Sol from Asia Pacific (Singapore) and logs the response. Set BEDROCK_PROFILE_ID to global.openai.gpt-6-luna or global.openai.gpt-6-astra to switch models, or call converse_stream for streaming. import logging import os import boto3 # AWS_REGION overrides this default, so set it to your source Region or unset it. REGION = os.environ.get("AWS_REGION", "ap-southeast-1") PROFILE_ID = os.environ.get("BEDROCK_PROFILE_ID", "global.openai.gpt-6-sol") PROMPT = ( "In three bullet points, explain when a workload should use " "cross-Region inference instead of calling a model in a single Region." ) logging.basicConfig(format="%(levelname)s %(message)s") log = logging.getLogger("bedrock-cris") log.setLevel(logging.INFO) client = boto3.client("bedrock-runtime", region_name=REGION) # AccessDeniedException points at the IAM policy. ValidationException usually # means the model ID is not a global cross-Region inference profile. response = client.converse( modelId=PROFILE_ID, messages=[{"role": "user", "content": [{"text": PROMPT}]}], inferenceConfig={"maxTokens": 1024}, # GPT-6 Sol and Luna accept none through max. GPT-6 Astra rejects none. additionalModelRequestFields={"reasoning": {"effort": "low"}}, ) # Any effort above none can prepend a reasoningContent block, so pick the text # block by key rather than by position. text = "".join(b["text"] for b in response["output"]["message"]["content"] if "text" in b) log.info("Called %s from %s", PROFILE_ID, REGION) log.info("Stop reason: %s", response["stopReason"]) log.info("Response:\n%s", text) OpenAI Chat Completions API. Point the OpenAI SDK at the Regional endpoint and pass the same profile ID. import logging import os from aws_bedrock_token_generator import provide_token from openai import OpenAI REGION = os.environ.get("AWS_REGION", "ap-southeast-1") PROFILE_ID = os.environ.get("BEDROCK_PROFILE_ID", "global.openai.gpt-6-sol") PROMPT = "List three uses for a message queue." logging.basicConfig(format="%(levelname)s %(message)s") log = logging.getLogger("bedrock-cris") log.setLevel(logging.INFO) # provide_token mints a short-term key from your AWS credentials, valid up to 12 hours. client = OpenAI( base_url=f"https://bedrock-runtime.{REGION}.amazonaws.com/openai/v1", api_key=provide_token(region=REGION), ) response = client.chat.completions.create( model=PROFILE_ID, messages=[{"role": "user", "content": PROMPT}], max_completion_tokens=256, ) log.info("Called %s from %s", PROFILE_ID, REGION) log.info("Response:\n%s", response.choices[0].message.content) When migrating an existing OpenAI client: Set the model parameter on every request, including those referencing a previous response. Use supported tool types: function , mcp , custom , namespace , and tool_search . Configure the inference profile ID directly in your client rather than querying the models endpoint. Set up the ChatGPT desktop app and Codex CLI The ChatGPT desktop app and the Codex CLI share ~/.codex/config.toml , so one change covers both. Of the two built-in Amazon Bedrock providers, only amazon-bedrock-runtime accepts an inference profile. model = "global.openai.gpt-6-astra" model_provider = "amazon-bedrock-runtime" [model_providers.amazon-bedrock-runtime.aws] region = "ap-southeast-1" SigV4 signing means there is no key to rotate. Add profile = "
" for a non-default profile, and set region explicitly, because the client otherwise falls back to AWS_REGION . Substitute another profile ID for model to change models. Codex reports a 272,000-token window for these profiles, which is its own bundled figure rather than a service limit. Raise it with model_context_window . This configuration needs Codex CLI 0.148 or later. Figure 2 shows the result in the app. Figure 2: The ChatGPT desktop app running GPT-6 Astra on Amazon Bedrock Security and permissions Amazon Bedrock offers a range of controls over inference. Two of them matter here. AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) policies control which roles can invoke which profiles, and service control policies (SCPs) apply organization-wide controls, including Region scope. This section covers both, and where request data lands. IAM permissions for global cross-Region inference To call any of these models through a global cross-Region inference profile, your IAM policy needs four statements: Access to the inference profile and the project/default resource in your source Region. Access to the foundation model in your source Region, scoped to the inference profile. The Region-agnostic Amazon Resource Name (ARN) for the foundation model, arn:aws:bedrock:::foundation-model/openai.gpt-6-sol , with aws:RequestedRegion set to unspecified to permit cross-Region routing. bedrock:CallWithBearerToken for API-key authentication. This IAM policy grants permission to invoke GPT-6 Sol through global cross-Region inference from ap-southeast-1 . Replace with your AWS account ID and ap-southeast-1 with your source Region. { "Version": "2012-10-17", "Statement": [ { "Sid": "GrantGlobalCrisProfileAndProjectAccess", "Effect": "Allow", "Action": ["bedrock:InvokeModel"], "Resource": [ "arn:aws:bedrock:ap-southeast-1:
:inference-profile/global.openai.gpt-6-sol", "arn:aws:bedrock:ap-southeast-1:
:project/default" ], "Condition": { "StringEquals": { "aws:RequestedRegion": "ap-southeast-1" } } }, { "Sid": "GrantGlobalCrisInRegionModelAccess", "Effect": "Allow", "Action": ["bedrock:InvokeModel"], "Resource": ["arn:aws:bedrock:ap-southeast-1::foundation-model/openai.gpt-6-sol"], "Condition": { "StringEquals": { "aws:RequestedRegion": "ap-southeast-1", "bedrock:InferenceProfileArn": "arn:aws:bedrock:ap-southeast-1:
:inference-profile/global.openai.gpt-6-sol" } } }, { "Sid": "GrantGlobalCrisGlobalModelAccess", "Effect": "Allow", "Action": ["bedrock:InvokeModel"], "Resource": ["arn:aws:bedrock:::foundation-model/openai.gpt-6-sol"], "Condition": { "StringEquals": { "aws:RequestedRegion": "unspecified", "bedrock:InferenceProfileArn": "arn:aws:bedrock:ap-southeast-1:
:inference-profile/global.openai.gpt-6-sol" } } }, { "Sid": "AllowBearerTokenAuth", "Effect": "Allow", "Action": ["bedrock:CallWithBearerToken"], "Resource": "*" } ] } If you use streaming ( converse_stream or stream=True ), add bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream to the Action in the first three statements. Converse authorizes as bedrock:InvokeModel . If you only call Converse with SigV4 credentials, drop the fourth statement. To switch models, replace openai.gpt-6-sol with openai.gpt-6-luna or openai.gpt-6-astra throughout. For the complete reference, see IAM policy requirements for global cross-Region inference . Service control policy considerations for global cross-Region inference A global cross-Region inference request carries no Region name. Amazon Bedrock sets aws:RequestedRegion to unspecified , so a Region allowlist in an SCP denies the call, and the error names only the policy type, not which policy. That is a common reason a first call fails in an enterprise account. Rather than widening the allowlist, scope the exception. Amazon Bedrock populates the bedrock:InferenceProfileArn condition key during authorization, so an SCP can allow these profiles while keeping Region controls for everything else. The following SCP does that. { "Version": "2012-10-17", "Statement": [ { "Sid": "DenyOutsideApprovedRegionsExceptBedrockInvoke", "Effect": "Deny", "NotAction": [ "iam:*", "sts:*", "organizations:*", "account:*", "route53:*", "cloudfront:*", "waf:*", "wafv2:*", "shield:*", "support:*", "trustedadvisor:*", "health:*", "budgets:*", "ce:*", "cur:*", "tax:*", "billing:*", "bedrock:Invoke*" ], "Resource": "*", "Condition": { "StringNotEquals": { "aws:RequestedRegion": ["ap-southeast-1"] } } }, { "Sid": "DenyBedrockInferenceOutsideApprovedRegionsUnlessCris", "Effect": "Deny", "Action": ["bedrock:Invoke*"], "Resource": "*", "Condition": { "StringNotEquals": { "aws:RequestedRegion": ["ap-southeast-1"] }, "ArnNotLike": { "bedrock:InferenceProfileArn": [ "arn:aws:bedrock:*:*:inference-profile/global.*" ] } } } ] } The first statement enforces your Region allowlist for every service except Amazon Bedrock inference. The second denies that inference outside those Regions unless it routes through a global cross-Region inference profile. For geographic profiles, add their prefix (for example inference-profile/us.* ) to the ArnNotLike list, because geographic requests carry a real Region name. Keep your source Region in the allowlist, and add the global services your organization uses to NotAction . A blunter alternative is to add unspecified to your existing allowlist, which works but opens the same exception to every other service. For a ready-to-use policy file, see the aws-samples service-control-policy-examples repository . Data retention and abuse detection For automated offline abuse detection, classifier-flagged traffic is retained by AWS for up to 30 days and processed programmatically. Under cross-Region inference that retention happens in the destination Region, which for a global profile is any supported commercial AWS Region where the model is deployed. Eligible customers might request full zero data retention through their AWS account team. For more information, see Amazon Bedrock abuse detection and Data retention . If your organization has data residency requirements, take this to your risk and compliance team early. See the AWS Financial Services Compliance Center country pages for these five countries. We recommend you obtain your own advice on compliance with the requirements relevant to your business. Quota management GPT-6 quotas on bedrock-runtime are measured in tokens per minute (TPM), tracked against the source Region you call from. Input and cache-write tokens count 1:1, and each output token consumes 10 tokens of quota. For example, a request with 2,000 input tokens and 1,000 output tokens depletes 12,000 tokens from your quota. Amazon Bedrock reserves the full max_tokens up front, so set it close to the completions you expect. One quota covers InvokeModel , Converse, Responses, and Chat Completions. Review and raise it on the Service Quotas console from your source Region. Before production, request increases early and alarm on EstimatedTPMQuotaUsage in the AWS/Bedrock namespace at 70–80 percent of your allocation. See How tokens are counted in Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Bedrock endpoints and quotas for current values. Monitoring and logging Your operational surface stays in your source Region. Amazon CloudWatch metrics, AWS CloudTrail events, model invocation logs, quota accounting, and billing all remain in the Region you called from. You pay that Region’s rates, not the processing Region’s. CloudTrail records where each request was processed. AWS documents a global cross-Region inference profile’s destinations as its commercial Regions rather than enumerating them. GetInferenceProfile returns the Region-agnostic and source-Region model ARNs rather than a destination list. Your per-request record is additionalEventData.inferenceRegion in CloudTrail in your source Region. Inference on this endpoint is a management event, logged by default at no extra cost. CloudTrail Event History retains 90 days, so longer horizons need a trail or model invocation logging. Retrieve the CloudTrail events with this command. aws cloudtrail lookup-events \ --region ap-southeast-1 \ --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventSource,AttributeValue=bedrock.amazonaws.com \ --start-time
\ --end-time
\ --max-results 1 \ --query 'Events[0].CloudTrailEvent' --output text | python3 -m json.tool Set the window around a call you just made, because CloudTrail delivery lags by a few minutes. If the most recent event was a failed call, it carries an errorCode and no inferenceRegion . Raise --max-results and pick an event without errorCode . { "eventName": "Converse", "eventSource": "bedrock.amazonaws.com", "awsRegion": "ap-southeast-1", "managementEvent": true, "requestParameters": { "modelId": "global.openai.gpt-6-sol", "inferenceConfig": { "maxTokens": 1024 } }, "additionalEventData": { "inferenceRegion": "us-east-1" } } Metrics and coding-agent usage stay in CloudWatch. Where developers reach GPT-6 through a coding agent, CloudWatch Coding Agent Insights adds ready-made dashboards under GenAI Observability that break token use down by user, team, and cost center. The agents emit OpenTelemetry metrics natively. For Codex, see Set up OpenTelemetry for OpenAI Codex . Clean up This post adds an IAM policy and optionally an SCP statement and a logging destination. Detach or delete the IAM policy you attached, and revert the SCP entry if you added one. Delete the model invocation logging destination in Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) or Amazon CloudWatch Logs if you created one, to avoid storage charges. The global cross-Region inference profiles are system-defined, so there is nothing to delete. Conclusion This post showed how to invoke GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna from five Asia Pacific source Regions, and GPT-6 Astra from Asia Pacific (Singapore), through global cross-Region inference on bedrock-runtime . Pass a global cross-Region inference profile ID as the model parameter, and configure the IAM policy and SCP exception from this post. The same endpoint serves the OpenAI-compatible APIs, so an existing OpenAI integration moves across by changing a base URL and a key. To get started, attach the IAM policy from this post, and send a first request through global.openai.gpt-6-sol . Size your tokens-per-minute quota at the 10x burndown rate, and confirm in CloudTrail that additionalEventData.inferenceRegion appears on your calls. For more information, see the Amazon Bedrock User Guide , Route model inference requests across AWS Regions with cross-Region inference , and Amazon Bedrock pricing .
